Heading: German rape case: Goa Minister’s son arrested - Indian Express
Content:
A US based company is developing a vehicle that would require nothing but air to run on the roads, with Tata already buying the rights to make the car for the huge Indian market.

According to a report in Environmental News Network (ENN), Zero Pollution Motors is developing a vehicle that can motor around all day on nothing but air and a splash of salad oil, alcohol or possibly a pint of gasoline.

The science behind building the compressed air car, or CAV, is not new as off-the-shelf technology already uses compressed air to drive old-fashioned car engine pistons instead of combusting gas or diesel fuel to create a burst of air.

The air car can tool along at a top speed of 35 mph for some 60 miles or so, on a tank of compressed air, a sufficient distance for 80 per cent of consumers to commute to work and back and complete daily chores.

On highways, the CAV can cruise at interstate speeds for nearly 800 miles with a small motor that compresses outside air to keep the tank filled.

The motor isn't finicky about fuel, as it will burn gasoline or diesel as well as biodiesel, ethanol or vegetable oil.

Even if it used only regular gasoline, the air car would average 106 mpg, more than double today's fuel sipping champ, the Toyota Prius.

The air tank also can be refilled when it's not in use by being plugged into a wall socket and recharged with electricity as the motor compresses air.

The vehicles will be built in factories that will make up to 8,000 vehicles a year, likely starting in 2011, and be sold directly to consumers.

There will be plants in nearly every state of the US, based on the number of drivers in the state.

While California will have as many as 17 air car manufacturing plants, there will be around 12 in Florida, eight in New York, four in Georgia, while two in Connecticut will serve that state and Rhode Island.

Tata doesn't plan to produce the cars in the US. Instead, it plans to charge 15 million dollars for the rights to the technology, a fully built turnkey auto assembly plant, tools, machinery, training and rights to use trademarks.

Heading: Mine mishap kills one, 18 seriously hurt - Indian Express
Content:
Goa Education Minister Atanasio Monserratte's son Rohit was on Tuesday arrested in connection with the rape of a German teenager. Rohit, 21, who had deposed before the police on November 1 and went into hiding, surrendered before Calangute police station in-charge Tushar Vernekar in the afternoon.

"Rohit was placed under arrest as we have found variance in his statement on November 1 and today," said Superintendent of Police (North) Bosco George.

Rohit, an MBA student, was accused by a German woman of raping her minor daughter on October 2. Subsequently, she filed another complaint against State Public Works Department Minister Churchill Alemao's nephew Warren, charging him with sexually exploiting the 14-year-old girl.

The girl, who was initially reluctant to depose or get herself medically examined, finally broke her silence on November 1 before the Judicial Magistrate. The girl also got herself medically examined on November 2.

Police had launched a search operation for Rohit after he failed to appear before the police on Monday. After raiding two of his residences, Monserratte had assured the police that he would produce his son on Tuesday.

Accordingly, Monserratte, along with his lawyer and son, reached Calangute police station in a red beacon car.

"My son is paying the price only because I am a politician," Monserratte told reporters outside Calangute police station. The Education Minister, who is also booked for abetment of the crime, said he will the move heavens to prove that his son was innocent. "I am convinced that he is innocent," he claimed.

Monserratte said the entire rape case "is just a frame-up" to pin him down.

Heading: Andhra techie found dead in Seattle - Indian Express
Content:
One worker died while 18 others were seriously injured when a gaseous blast occurred inside a coal mine in the Ledo collieries of Coal India Ltd near Margherita in Upper Assam early on Tuesday.

The blast occurred about 1,000 metres from the surface level around 5.30 am, with officials describing it as a hot air explosion caused due to friction between fresh coal dust and air inside a mine called Lachit Khani. A side wall that caught fire also collapsed in the impact of the explosion.

"While all 19 workers injured in the explosion were rescued and rushed to hospital within an hour, all of them sustained burn injuries in varying degrees," Ranjit Dutta, a senior HR official in the Northeastern Coalfilds of CIL told The Indian Express over the telephone from Margherita.

While three of the workers were released after first aid, eight were referred to the Assam Medical College Hospital at Dibrugarh and two to the Indian Oil Corporation Hospital at Digboi. One of the two workers admitted to the IOC Hospital died later in the evening, Dutta said. Six others with lesser injuries are undergoing treatment at the CIL Hospital at Margherita.

The coalfields at Margherita and Ledo had a major accident in 1979 when at least 19 workers were killed while nine miners had died in another mishap at the Tipong mines in 1993.

Heading: Another airfield reopened on China border - Indian Express
Content:
Another Andhra American dream was snuffed out when 24-year-old Arpana, an exceptionally brilliant software engineer and one of the winners of the Microchip Technology Inc contest in 2004, was found dead by her friends on Monday morning in Seattle.

Daughter of Dr B C Jinaga, director in-charge of School of Information Technology at Jawaharlal Nehru Technology University, Hyderabad, Arpana was working as a software quality engineer at EMC Corp while doing her MS from Rutgers, the State University of New Jersey, Brunswick.

"We could not get in touch with her on phone since Friday so I called up a few of my former students settled there to find out if she was all right. They called back last night to inform that she was found dead in her apartment," Dr Jinaga said.

Arpana was living alone in a flat in Valley View Apartments in Redmond-Woodinville Road Northeast area near her office. Friends found the door of her flat broken and the girl lying on the floor with injuries on her throat. It is not clear how she died.

Dr Jinaga said that he was informed neither by the local police nor the company for which she worked. Family members said Arpana apparently died on the night between Friday and Saturday, but was found only on Monday.

Arpana did her B-Tech in computer science from VNR Vigyan Jyoti Institute of Engineering and Technology, Bachipally, Hyderabad before going to the US in April 2005. A bright student, Arpana was listed in the top 20 winning entries of Microchip Technology Inc contest for Digital Signal Control Design on December 12, 2004. The contest involved thousands of engineers across the world purchasing Microchip's Design Contest Kit and submitting models showing their design skills. Contestants like Arpana created product design, flow diagrams and circuits based on digital signal controller and she was among the 20 winners judged on the basis of innovation. Arpana's entry was a communications jammer.

Arpana's Facebook profile does not reveal much but shows a photo of hers clad in jeans and a blue T-shirt with a camera hanging around her neck, taken near a race track.

Arpana's sister Pavitra is doing second-year engineering in Hyderabad while her mother is a housewife. Relatives said the Jinaga family has gone into a state of shock and has no idea what to do.

"They do not have any relatives there and are depending on some friends to find out when the autopsy is being done and how the body can be brought to Hyderabad. Her body has been taken by police to King County Medical Examiner's Office on Monday evening. No one in the family has till now thought of going to Seattle. They are all in shock," a relative said.

Heading: TDP hopes to roar with Yuva Garjana - Indian Express
Content:
India has reopened another strategic airstrip along its unresolved border with China in Eastern Ladakh that will give it the capability to rapidly induct troops in the region.

The Fukche Advanced Landing Ground (ALG) was reactivated on Tuesday morning with the IAF landing a AN 32 medium transport aircraft on the newly refurbished airstrip.

The ALG, located at an altitude of 4,200 meters, is barely three kilometers away from the Line of Actual Control (LAC). It was being used as a helicopter base by the Armed Forces and had not seen fixed wing aircraft operations since the 1962 Sino-Indian war .

The reopening of the Fukche airbase comes months after the Daulat Beg Oldie (DBO) airfield, situated in the same region near the Karakoram pass, was reactivated by the Air Force earlier this year.

While the DBO is the highest airbase in the world and was reactivated for maintaining supplies to the troops posted on the border, Fukche is the second highest landing ground in the world.

IAF says that the airstrip will help carry out humanitarian missions in the region that is known to be prone to earthquakes and would also be used to promote tourism in the area. However, analysts believe that the airfield is a part of a series of steps being undertaken to improve connectivity along the China border.

India has been reviving advanced landing grounds and helicopter bases along the border from Ladakh to the North-East. Armed Forces have conducted status reports on reactivating airbases after directives from the PMO to promote tourism and to increase the reach of the army along the border.

"The airfield will be used for humanitarian relief work and evacuation in case of natural calamities," Air Marshal P K Barbora, Commander-in-Chief of the Western Air Command, told The Indian Express.

Work on the third major airfield in Ladakh along the Sino-India border, the Chushul Advanced Landing Ground, located at a height of over 5,000 m, is still to commence and the ALG is not likely to be reactivated in the near future.

Heading: Sadhvi, others undergo narco test - Indian Express
Content:
The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and Chandrababu Naidu are hoping to get back into the reckoning with 'Yuva Garjana' (roar of the youth), a massive public meeting, being organised at Nagarjuna Nagar in Guntur district on Wednesday. It's a do or die meeting for TDP, the success of which will set the tone for the coming elections.

Film star Chiranjeevi and his fledgling Praja Rajyam Party are making waves in the state. While the Congress appears unfazed, the TDP has been hardest hit with desertions and low morale in the rank and file. With the NTR clan in tow, Naidu is making a valiant attempt to restore the party's lost glory and regain lost ground.

Touted as the mother of all rallies, at least 15 lakh people, mostly youth, are expected to attend the meeting at the 150 acre land opposite the Acharya Nagarjuna University. The meeting, being held to mark 25 years of TDP, would be preceded by a motorcycle rally of more than 10,000 vehicles. Artists are working overtime to create a huge stage which would resemble a film set. The entire NTR clan is expected to be present at the meet except Junior NTR, who is apparently making some demands to make an appearance. NTR's sons, Balakrishna and Hari Krishna, and their sons, Kalyam Ram and Tarak Ratna, would be present at the meeting. The party has spent lakhs on preparing huge cut-outs of NTR and other TDP leaders.

Large scale preparations are on at the venue on the Vijayawada-Guntur highway. Four choppers have been hired, a dozen trains have been requisitioned and more than 900 state transport buses have been hired to ferry workers to Guntur from all parts of the state.

Senior TDP leader and Politburo member Y Ramakrishnudu who is in-charge of the arrangements said that Yuva Garjana would be the biggest public meeting ever in the state. The party has hired almost all hotels and guesthouses in Guntur and Vijayawada to accommodate its leaders.

The 'Yuva Garjana' meeting on which the party is banking so much hit some roadblocks initially. Junior NTR, grandson of NTR, considered to be the star attraction at the meeting, apparently came up with some demands for making an appearance. Party leaders said that the young actor is putting pressure on the party to give the ticket for Ganavaram Assembly seat in Krishna district to his close friend, Vamsi Mohan, who is making his maiden film with Junior NTR.

The party is in a fix because NTR's elder son and Naidu's brother-in-law, Harikrishna, is expecting that the ticket would be given to his close friend and educationist Bala Vardhan Rao.

Heading: Ahead of second list, Rajasthan Cong asks for police protection - Indian Express
Content:
Three of those arrested in the Malegaon blast investigation underwent narcoanalysis tests on Tuesday at Police Hospital in Nagpada. The narcoanalysis tests began at 11.45 am and went on till 7.30 pm.

The prosecution had informed the Nashik Chief Judicial Magistrate that the brain mapping and polygraph tests on the three had been positive and sought permission for their narcoanalysis. Sadhvi Pragya Thakur, ex-ABVP member Sameer Kulkarni and Major Ramesh Upadhayay (retd) have been charged under various sections of the Explosives Act among other serious charges. The prosecution had cited that the narcoanalysis tests were required to find out how the RDX was transported, the conspiracy and the funding of the operation. Investigators have so far seized a laptop and two mobile phones from Sadhvi Pragya and some crucial evidence against the other two accused, the prosecution has stated.

Meanwhile, Dombivali resident Jagdish Chintaman Mhatre, who was arrested by the Anti-Terrorism Squad on Friday for his suspected involvement in the Malegaon blast, has nine cases, ranging from petty assault to murder, pending against him in Vishnunagar, Manpada and Mahatma Phule police stations.

"He was an accused in a murder as well as extortion case and we are investigating the details. However, all these cases date back to the 90s and no fresh case has been registered against him in the past eight-nine years," said Ulhasnagar Deputy Commissioner of Police Sanjay Yenpure.

"There are three cases against Mhatre registered with us, the latest one being in 1999. While all are body offences, none of them are serious enough to merit an ATS arrest. In 1990, he was charged with minor assault and criminal intimidation. In 1994, he had been arrested for abducting a youth and bashing him up. In 1999, we had arrested him for threatening someone with a knife. However, he was not booked for any other crimes by us after that," said Senior Inspector D L Suryavanshi of the Vishnu Nagar police station.

Personnel from the Vishnu Nagar police station are also engaged in procuring details of Mhatre's criminal records from neighbouring police stations like Manpada, Dombivali and Mahatma Phule.

Suryavanshi added that while there were vague reports of Mhatre having been part of the KMC gang that operated in Dombivali over a decade back, they are yet to find criminal records that corroborate it. "In fact, Mhatre sustained a leg injury several years back and reportedly walked with a stick. His handicap reportedly prevented frequent trips out of the house," said Suryavanshi.

Heading: 'MNS violence reflects lack of political will' - Indian Express
Content:
If the declaration of the first 116 Congress candidates for the Rajasthan Assembly polls caused a furore amongst party workers, particularly the Jat community, the second list of 60 candidates, which is in the offing, has the state Congress unit on tenterhooks. So much so that senior leaders recently asked the Jaipur police for protection.

The Congress has to choose between the disgruntled but veteran Jat community leaders and former chief minister Ashok Gehlot's lobby on the one hand and the victory potential of the candidates on the other.

The request for police protection came on Sunday from the Congress headquarters in Jaipur, after which a temporary police outpost, manned by four policemen, has been stationed near the office. The request was made in the aftermath of protests by supporters of party leaders who were denied tickets, some whom even managed to break furniture and glass panes in the office.

Congress spokesperson Satinder Raghav justified the protection, claiming that inebriated miscreants and not party workers were creating ruckus. The agitations followed Congress and veteran Jat leader from Jodhpur Parasram Maderna slamming the first Congress list calling it anti-farmer, biased and reeking of sycophancy.

Senior Congress leaders in Rajasthan said 176 candidates had already been decided, of which only 116 names had been released to gauge reactions. A senior party leader said, "the remaining 60 names will be declared very soon and is bound to have repercussions as the party cannot possibly please everybody. We have concentrated on giving tickets to winnable candidates based on careful research."

He added that there would be protests from various quarters, but the high command's decision was final and no changes would be made. "The candidates contesting in Nagaur district, the Jat heartland and important Gurjjar- majority constituencies, including Dausa, will figure in the second list," he said.

However, political experts in the state believe that Maderna, who is expected to meet party president Sonia Gandhi about Jat representation, was a worrying sign for the Congress, particularly as disgruntled Jat leaders are known to break away from the party and contest as independents.

"The list will somehow have to pacify Maderna and the Jats and former chief minister Ashok Gehlot's lobby and also consider winnable candidates, instead of giving in to pressure from veteran leaders," said a senior leader.

He added that senior state leaders were also dropping names of Congress leaders in Delhi to avoid further revolts in the state.

Heading: Warning sign, Army needs to be alert: Ex-chiefs - Indian Express
Content:
Criticising the Government for lacking the required will to tackle the unabated attacks being carried out against north Indians by Raj Thackeray-led MNS in Mumbai, the Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear a PIL, seeking protection of life and liberty of individuals besides properties, on November 10.

Underlining that it (hate attacks) was more of a political matter, a Bench of Justices B N Agarwal and G S Singhvi observed, "It is a political matter and intervention by the court would not help."

After advocate Sugriva Dubey appearing for petitioner Salek Chand Jain, a businessman, urged the Bench to take up the matter "suo motu" on the lines of Gurjjar agitation, Justice Agarwal made it clear that a precedent was not set by that matter. "It is the lack of the political will, or else it would have been stopped. People have to be educated," the court noted.

Agreeing on the gravity of the issue, the Bench even grilled the counsel about his knowledge of Article 355 of the Constitution. The provision that mandates the Central Government to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbances, reads as: "It shall be the duty of the Union to protect every state against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that the Government of every state is carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution."

Observing that while the issue raised was "serious", the petition was "non-serious" in terms of material to support the arguments, the Bench told the counsel to amend the petition. After that, it would be taken up for hearing.

Dubey argued that attacks on north Indians by the MNS had led to a chain reaction elsewhere in the country and it threatened to destroy the unity and integrity of the country. Following the MNS attacks, the Jharkhand Chief Minister had announced that he would not permit the rich mineral resources of the state to be transported to any part of the country. The counsel claimed that the threat, if carried out, would seriously affect the country's development as 60 per cent of the mineral resources originated from Jharkhand.

Heading: Kerala militants buried in martyrs’ graveyard - Indian Express
Content:
The alleged involvement of retired and serving officers in the Malegaon blast is an "aberration", but the Armed Forces need to view it as a warning and remain alert for the future, feel former Armed Forces chiefs and senior retired officers.

With a retired Major in the Mumbai Anti-Terrorism Squad net on charges of providing training to the main accused in the blast, former chiefs have said that while an odd aberration can take place, the incident is not indicative of any larger trend in the Armed Forces. "If such an incident has happened it should be a warning to everyone that the Armed Forces should remain alert. It is more of a warning and the Army needs to be alert that such cases do not happen," former Army Chief General V P Malik said.

"The case is no cause for alarm and we have enough safeguards in the Armed Forces (to deal with such matters). This is one case in 60 years, anyone can go haywire. But by and large the ethos (of ex-servicemen) is sufficiently strong," former Navy Chief Admiral Arun Prakash said. Cracking down on extremism within the Armed Forces is part of the mandate of the Counter Intelligence Wing.

While the ATS is investigating retired Major Ramesh Upadhayay's links with the main accused in the Malegaon blast, the former officer had a clean record while in service and did not face any major disciplinary action.

After joining the Army as a soldier, Upadhayay undertook a special exam—aimed at identifying exceptional soldiers—at the Army Cadet College (ACC) to join the officer's cadre. The officer served in various streams of the Army and his final positing was with the Air Defence Artillery (ADA), a regiment that is assigned air protection roles of vital Army units and formations.

It was after he left the service in 1998 that the retired officer had a few brushes with the law and was even arrested by the police in Mumbai on charges of stalking a woman and posting indecent comments about her on a website. He was also convicted in a cheque bouncing case. The ex-officer had also joined the BJP as president of its ex-servicemen cell in Maharashtra and was actively involved with the RSS.

However, ex-servicemen believe his background as an ex-officer has nothing to do with the involvement in the blast. "He is not the first Armed Forces man to break the law. There will always be the odd element and this should not be taken as an indication of things to come," former Air Chief Marshal S P Tyagi said.

Heading: TN wall claims another life - Indian Express
Content:
With their families refusing to have anything to do with them, the four militants from Kerala who were killed in the Valley last month were buried in the 'martyrs' graveyard' in a village in Kupwara on Tuesday. After organising the last rites, the police handed over the bodies to the local Auqaf, which buried them in the graveyard where six foreign militants are also buried.

Around 400 villagers gathered for the funeral led by the local Imam, Qawamuddin. "All the four were buried by the local Auqaf members," Kupwara SSP Uttam Chand said. "The bodies were brought to Kupwara from Srinagar on Monday afternoon."

The bodies of the Kerala militants were kept at the police mortuary in Srinagar for almost a month. They were, however, not given any purifying bath as ordained by the religion. The deceased is not bathed only when he or she is regarded a martyr. "We did not perform the bath as the locals believed they were martyrs," said Diver village head Manzoor Ahmed. Ahmed, who attended the funeral prayers, said he was informed by the police about the burial.

There was, however, no sloganeering as happens with most of the funeral prayers of militants in the Valley.

In a letter, the families of the two slain militants, Mohammad Fayaz of Kannur and Abdul Raheem of Malappuram, had informed the J-K Police that they did not want the bodies of their sons.

Heading: In 2002, azadi, polls came together here, now Handwara rings with boycott - Indian Express
Content:
A dalit teenager was shot dead by police and several others injured after another round of communal protests gripped Uthapuram village in Madurai where a 'untouchability wall', which has for the past 19 years physically separated the communities, was partly demolished by the state a few months ago.

On Tuesday, a group of nearly 500 hundred Dalits, protesting the stoning of Puthiya Thamizhagam leader K Krishnasamy's vehicle on Sunday, attacked a police party, injuring several personnel including DIG S S Krishnamoorthy. According to officials, the police party lathi-charged and fired teargas shells to disperse the mob before firing at the "armed protestors". The shootout left 19-year-old K Suresh of Kottaipatti village dead, while two others have been admitted to the hospital with serious injuries.

According to the police, the DIG was on way to Ezhumalai where the situation was volatile after the attack on Krishnasamy's car. An early morning clash between the two communities had left five injured. The protestors, who have often charged the police of siding with the upper caste, blocked roads by felling trees and pelted stones at the police party, leading to the firing, claimed senior police officials.

However, Suresh's mother Murugeswari claimed her son had stepped out of the house after hearing the commotion when he was shot down. Her husband Karuppaiyya was also injured.

Ever since the demolition of the wall to make way for laying a road into the Dalit hamlet in May this year, Uthapuram and nearby areas have been tense with sporadic violence over small skirmishes between Dalits and upper caste Hindus. Following the demolition, a police outpost was set up at Uthapuram to prevent flare up of communal tensions.

Heading: Kashmiri youth in Tihar hopes ticket is his way out - Indian Express
Content:
If there is one constituency that sums up Kashmir's indifference to these Assembly elections, it is perhaps Handwara. In 2002, this place had emerged as the symbol of a new discourse in the Valley when a candidate — a cloth merchant, Ghulam Mohideen Sofi — contested the polls on a clear separatist agenda. For the first time, slogans of azadi and elections were heard in the same breath. When Sofi said he agreed with the separatists that the Kashmir dispute needed to be resolved through a tripartite dialogue, respecting the "aspirations of Kashmiri people", but "simultaneously sought a mandate to address the issues of local governance, development and other day-to-day problems faced by the people" through participation in the Assembly elections, even the Hurriyat Conference was forced to take note.

Sofi won, defeating a top National Conference leader and a senior minister in the Farooq Abdullah Government, Choudhary Mohammad Ramzan.

But if Sofi and his election in Handwara represented a new reality of Kashmir in 2002, his depleted chances this time tell the tale of Kashmir six years later. The recent separatist groundswell, the four-month-long protest over the Amarnath land controversy and the use of force by the Government to quell the protests have put a question mark on the peace process launched after Mufti Mohammad Sayeed took over as Chief Minister in 2002, and raised doubts about a campaign that talks of azadi and elections in the same breath. In fact, the separatists across the moderate-hardline divide have come together to call for a boycott of the polls now.

All this has left Sofi fighting with his back to the wall. Quite a change from that day of August 29, 2002, when thousands had joined him raising slogans for azadi and elections as he went to file his nomination papers. He was also riding the sympathy wave generated by the killing of top Hurriyat and Peoples Conference leader Abdul Gani Lone, who had been assassinated just a few months before. Sofi was known to be close to Lone. Though Peoples Conference denied Sofi was their proxy candidate, there were few takers for this.

The Hurriyat, which has a strong base across north Kashmir, particularly Kupwara district that includes Handwara constituency, had taken note of Sofi's campaign. While there was a split among the separatists over the issue of de-linking electoral politics from the larger question of the Kashmir dispute, it had piqued the interest of a section.

The Sofi phenomenon, in fact, worked in the broader context of the 2002 Assembly polls as well, with an otherwise exclusively "separatist" discourse becoming part of mainstream electoral politics. It was an election fought around the agenda of "the need to resolve the Kashmir dispute", "a velvet glove policy towards separatists and militants" and a "demand for Pakistan's active role in the resolution process".

This was reflected in the emergence of the Kashmir-centric Peoples Democratic Party, with its message of change and its separatist rhetoric. The ruling National Conference, which had particularly been shy of such a discourse because of its past experiences, suffered.

Sofi's victory over an NC stalwart in Handwara by merging mainstream electoral politics with the separatist agenda was reflective of the PDP gains against the NC and the change in the contours of mainstream politics across Kashmir.

After the 2002 polls, Sofi joined the coalition government and became a minister in the Mufti Sayeed-led government. The incumbency factor may also take a toll on Sofi's chances in the coming elections, as well as his strained relations with the Peoples Conference and the Lone family. Peoples Conference leader Sajjad Lone is among the most vocal supporters of a poll boycott.

This has brightened the chances of NC leader Choudhary Mohammad Ramzan, though a voter boycott may affect him as well. Handwara is among the four constituencies in Kupwara district where Peoples Conference has a substantial political base.

Heading: Kingfisher alleges assault, minister denies charge - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the separatist brigade is raising a poll boycott pitch, a young man from Bandipore has decided to jump into the fray for an unusual reason: a hope that the contest will help him come out of jail.

Mohammad Iqbal Jan (30) has been lodged in the Tihar jail since November 2006. He was arrested by the Delhi Police for his alleged militant links. The police had claimed to have recovered around Rs 5 lakh and a cache of RDX from him — a charge he and his family have been consistently denying.

"He is innocent. Everybody knows that. He had taken a loan of Rs 10.6 lakh from the J&K Bank for his new business. He had started a gas agency and was carrying Rs 5 lakh for payment," Iqbal's uncle Nazir Ahmad Jan — who is also his would-be father-in-law — told The Indian Express. "We have shown the bank documents to the court as well. We are hopeful that he will be set free."

He said Iqbal is getting desperate for his release from Tihar. "He wrote a letter to Panther's Party president Bhim Singh, who is also a good lawyer, and asked for help. He wants to contest the elections so that he can prove his innocence," Nazir Ahmad Jan said. "Bhim Singh has assured us that he will fight the case for his release and his innocence will be established once he contests the Assembly elections from Bandipore."

When Iqbal's nomination papers were filed from Bandipore, it took everyone by surprise. The Jammu-centric Panther's Party had specially dispatched its Delhi unit chief Sanjay Sachdev to Bandipore for the purpose. However, the Returning officer of Bandipore constituency, Ali Mohammad Dar, found an unusual anomaly in the nomination papers. Iqbal's affidavit had been filed in Delhi and Dar objected to it. He referred the case to Chief Electoral Officer B R Sharma for opinion because "only J-K affidavits were valid in the election process".

This led to a controversy and Bhim Singh called a press conference to lodge a protest against the Election Commission. "This young man is innocent. He was arrested by the Delhi Police, like several others, only because he had come from Kashmir. Now that he wants to contest the elections, the EC does not want to entertain an affidavit prepared in Delhi," he said. "In Kashmir, even Pakistani affidavits are being entertained. We don't understand why the Returning Officer refused to entertain our plea. He (Iqbal) is lodged in Tihar and he can only get an affidavit in Delhi," he added.

Singh said that Iqbal has not been convicted and he is not accused of a murder, so he cannot be denied the right to contest an election.

Iqbal's family, however, said that the EC had finally approved his nomination papers and now he was ready to contest the polls. "He (Iqbal) is the only son in the family. He was engaged and was to get married within a month. But then he was arrested. We tried everything to prove his innocence, knocked at every door, but nothing helped," Nazir Ahmad said. "He has eight sisters and every one of us will campaign for him. This election is our last hope for his release," he added.

There is a sympathy wave for Iqbal in his hometown. A science graduate, Iqbal first joined an insurance company and then started his own business. "I think people understand his (Iqbal's) desperation. He will get votes," Shabir Ahmad Bhat, a schoolteacher in Bandipore, said. "I will vote for him but only if the situation remains calm."

Heading: ARC for checks on foreign funding - Indian Express
Content:
Refuting allegations of misbehaviour levelled by a Kingfisher Airlines staff at the Patna airport after not being allowed to board the airline's flight for allegedly reporting late, Union Minister and RJD MP Akhilesh Prasad Singh on Tuesday said he had been framed in the episode. The airline stuck to its charges that it had reported the matter to the police authorities for investigation and appropriate action.

"There was no incident of any abuse or assault as alleged by the staff of the airline. The minister intends to take up the matter regarding the irresponsible action of the airline with the Civil Aviation Ministry," a statement issued by Singh's Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said.

The Kingfisher Airlines maintained that its airport manager at Patna had been "assaulted, abused and had to bear a barrage of foul language" from Singh "without any cause for provocation". In a statement, the airline said the flight was scheduled to depart at 8.30 pm and the airline staff were told by Singh's travel agent at 8.10 pm that he would not be travelling on the flight.

"By around 8.20 pm, since all guests were on board, the commander of the aircraft requested Patna ATC for start-up and push-back clearance which was given. The aircraft had just begun taxiing when Mr Singh reportedly landed up at the airport, 10 minutes before the scheduled departure of the flight," the airline said adding that given the circumstances, its airport manager told Singh that he could not join the flight. "That was when Mr Singh assaulted and abused our airport manager in the VIP lounge in the presence of several witnesses," the airline said.

Singh's statement, however, said, "The minister arrived at the airport at 8.15 pm whereupon he was informed that his ticket stood cancelled on the instruction of the travel agent. However, no such instruction had been issued by the minister. The duty manager was requested to issue the boarding pass."

Following this, Singh was taken to the VIP lounge where the duty manager told him that he would not be issuing the boarding pass to him. "The duty manager was not willing to listen to any amount of reasoning. The minister immediately apprised the Joint Secretary (Civil Aviation) about the unauthorised cancellation and the refusal of the manager to issue a boarding pass. The Joint Secretary also tried to reason with the duty manager who refused to listen. The minister told the duty manager that he would complain about the conduct and behaviour of the staff of the airline to the Civil Aviation Ministry on his return to Delhi," the statement said.

Heading: V-C who denied Rahul permission resigns - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Union Government continues to dither on the need for stronger laws to deal with terrorist and fundamental organisations receiving funds from abroad, the Second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) on Tuesday came out with its recommendations on the issue.

In its report on Social Capital, the ARC said amendments were needed in the existing law to monitor big-ticket contributions received by all organisations from foreign contributors. Releasing the 231-page report here, ARC Chairman M Veerappa Moily said in order to make the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976 more stringent, organisations getting over Rs 10 lakh a year as foreign contribution should be put under the scanner. However, ARC feels organisations receiving an annual foreign contribution equivalent to less than Rs 10 lakh should be exempted from registration and other requirements.

"They should be asked to file an annual return of the foreign contribution received by them and its utilisation at the end of the year," Moily said, adding that a law should be in place to ensure that in case there was reasonable suspicion of suppression or misrepresentation of facts, such organisations could be investigated and penalised, if found guilty.

The ARC report says the panel was aware that a large number of voluntary organisations were receiving donations from foreign sources. "As many as 99 organisations received contributions above Rs 10 crore in 2005-06 compared to 70 in 2004-05 and 57 in 2003-04," the report says.

Heading: Keep Mumbai cosmopolitan: Ansari - Indian Express
Content:
V K Suri, Vice-Chancellor of the Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology, Kanpur, on Tuesday submitted his resignation to Governor T V Rajeswar. Accepting the resignation, the Governor has asked the Registrar to take charge for now.

Suri hit the headline when he denied permission to AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi to hold a meeting in the university auditorium on October 24. The V-C cited security reasons for cancelling permission for the meeting. However, the Governor, who was supposed to attend the convocation of the university the same day, cancelled his programme.

The Governor had sought an explanation from the V-C on why he cancelled the MP's programme. The V-C replied that no formal permission was granted for Rahul's meeting by the university. The Raj Bhawan had said that the V-C acted under pressure from the Uttar Pradesh Government, a charge denied by the BSP Government.

Heading: Sena warns: Hindi channels defaming Maharashtra - Indian Express
Content:
In an apparent reference to the violence against north Indians by MNS in Maharashtra fuelling a blamegame across the political spectrum, Vice-President Hamid Ansari on Tuesday reminded the state Government of "scrupulous adherence" to its constitutional responsibility.

"The politics of our polity cannot be confined to the many little corners of India; and neither should our citizens be confined to their corners in this vast land," Ansari said during the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation awards ceremony in Mumbai. "What is demanded of every citizen, political actor and agent of the state is scrupulous adherence, in letter and spirit, to our Constitution — no more, no less."

Expressing his concern over this "propensity" in political quarters to explain such behaviour, he said, "This basic constitutional framework of rights and obligations is today under stress. Political parties and groups, operating within the ambit of the Constitution, tend to obstruct the exercise of fundamental rights by citizens. Equally disconcerting is the propensity in various quarters to explain such behaviour, or explain it away."

Pointing to the increasing urbanisation in modern India, the Vice-President wondered whether people had comprehended the implications of urban landscape, which would continue to attract people from across different geographical, linguistic and religious backgrounds.

"Today 30 per cent of our population lives in cities; it would be 50 per cent by 2050. Have the implications of this in social terms dawned on us? Cultural chauvinism and linguistic jingoism are inherently exclusionary. Would there be space for them in these urban conglomerates?" he asked, urging the people of Mumbai to take the lead in the emotional integration of India.

"Nehru had urged us 'to keep in mind the emotional integration of India'. The time has come to act upon it with a sense of urgency," said Ansari. "Would a lead in the matter be taken by Mumbai, India's premier city? Mumbai represents the cosmopolitan spirit of India. Any other depiction of Mumbai would be to lessen it and deny its history and its ethos."

Ansari's comments assume significance in view of the fact that it is for the first time a top constitutional functionary has expressed views in public on the issue.

Heading: Rane gives unity call for Maharashtra leaders - Indian Express
Content:
The Shiv Sena mouthpiece Saamna has warned Hindi news channels of retaliation if "the portrayal of the state and its people in poor light" was not stopped. "Some restraint should be exercised by the media and the criticism of politicians hatching plots to break the country must be stopped, at least in Maharashtra, or else some concrete steps will have to be taken against you in the interests of Maharashtra and then the stupid freedom of expression claimed by you will have to be set aside and the blot of defamation on Maharashtra will have to be washed away," said the editorial on Tuesday.

"Some sort of hatred is constantly simmering against Maharashtra in the minds of the North (Indians) and its sparks fly on the screens of the Hindi channels. These ravens did not dare to spit venom against the Assamese when there were violent attacks on Hindi speakers in Assam. Everyone was also quiet when Hindi speakers were attacked in Manipur. But when there is smoke somewhere in Maharashtra, these people call it a fire. What is this?" the editorial said in a strong criticism of the electronic media.

The mouthpiece supported NCP president and Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar's stance on not speaking to the media considering the manner in which it was defaming Maharashtra. It expressed anger at the way in which the law and order situation in the state was shown to have deteriorated and an impression created that non- Maharashtrians were not safe in the state.

"...the Maharashtrians in Maharashtra have some problems of their own and these questions are especially related to their employment as the sons of the soil. The Sena has been fighting on these issues," it said in a veiled attack on the MNS.

Heading: 45 dead as bus falls into gorge - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to counter the efforts by leaders from Bihar to put up a united front on the issue of MNS attacks on north Indians, it was the turn of Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane on Tuesday to forge unity among state leaders against what he called "politicisation of the issue". Rane was in the Capital to inspect the attack on Maharashtra Sadan on Monday here.

"Political leaders from Bihar are engaging in politics on this issue (anti-north Indian violence). I want to urge the political leaders from Maharashtra to stand united on this issue too. I said it earlier in Nashik as well," Rane said. Though he did not mention the MNS, Rane took a potshot at Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, saying he was even ready to resign from the Government on the issue.

"I am neither the chief minister of the state nor the party chief in the state. Still I am ready to resign from my post on this issue," Rane said in an apparent attack on Deshmukh's silence on the political heat being raised by leaders from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

He reiterated his earlier position that the "Marathi manoos" should get the preference in jobs located in Maharashtra.

Rane's statement followed Congress' defence of the "Marathi manoos" plank and the "son-of-the-soil" policy minus the violence against outsiders.

Heading: Cabinet nod likely for 2,500 model govt schools - Indian Express
Content:
Forty-five passengers were killed and five injured when the private bus in which they were travelling from Kotighat in Kumarsain tehsil to Shimla went off the road and fell into a nearly 600-foot-deep gorge at Lambidhar, near the tourist spot of Kufri in Shimla district on Tuesday morning.

Fourty-four passengers were found dead at the spot by the locals who rushed to rescue them. The six survivors were immediately moved to the IGMC Hospital in Shimla town, where a 35-year-old man was declared dead. The administration has decided to conduct postmortem of the dead.

Lalita Thakur, a survivor from Gullo village in Theog tehsil, who was sitting on front seat of the bus, said the driver was trying to change the CD on the music player when the bus went out of control. "He could not negotiate the curve though the road was very wide. Watching the bus go out of the road the passengers yelled, but by then the front tyres had gone off the road," she said. Lalita, who was thrown out through the broken windscreen, clung on to bushes on the cliff till help arrived.

Another survivor, 35-year-old Anita, who had boarded the bus from just a kilometre before the accident, corroborated Lalita's version. Her sister Draupdi Thakur died on the spot while her husband survived with minor injuries.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal visited the accident spot and also met the injured at the IGMC Hospital. He said a magisterial inquiry would be conducted to find out the actual cause of the accident. The Government has announced an immediate relief of Rs 50,000 and an equal amount to be given later to the families of the dead. The injured would be given Rs 50,000.

Heading: Ranthambore tigress plays cat-and-mouse game, relocation to Sariska put off - Indian Express
Content:
The UPA Government's promise to create model schools in the backward blocks of the country is finally set to be fulfilled with the HRD Ministry's school building mission likely to get Cabinet approval this week. While the state Government and the Centre will run 2,500 such schools, another 2,500 will be built on public private partnership. The 2,500 schools to be run by the Government will follow the Kendriya Vidyalaya model.

"The KV template will be followed in terms of the school area, size of the classroom, facilities like playground, library, medical check-up and training of teachers. The teacher-pupil ratio will be around 1:40. While the states will own and run these schools, the Centre will contribute Rs 4 crore to each school for its setting up. The decision regarding schools' affiliation to CBSE or with state boards will be states' prerogative," added an official.

The scheme aims to retain students in school through the secondary stage, more so with the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan bringing a large number of children into the primary education fold. The ministry claims there is nearly 97 per cent enrolment at the elementary level at present whereas the gross enrolment ratio for secondary education is around 52 per cent and still lower at the senior secondary stage. With a high-quality school in the most backward blocks of the country, the Government hopes to reduce and stop the drop in secondary stage enrolment and also hone talented children there.

The 2,500 PPP-based schools will, however, take a little longer. The HRD ministry is envisaging a flexible PPP format wherein private investment would be allowed on response and school-specific basis. The PPP-based proposal for 2,500 model schools awaits approval of the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC).

"The PPP framework we are working on will be a flexible and facilitative one and not prescriptive or suggestive in nature to ensure enough private investment. We are also open to the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) format, provided KV type academic quality and regulations are maintained," said an official.

Heading: Elections near, pink slips muddy rosy picture - Indian Express
Content:
The translocation of another tigress from Ranthambore National Park to the Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary in Rajasthan has been postponed to Wednesday with forest officials failing to sight and track the big cat since Sunday.

The four-year-old tigress was supposed to be tranquilised before being shifted to Sariska in an IAF helicopter. Sources in the forest department said if the tiger was not tracked even on Wednesday, the translocation would have to be deferred by a few more days.

"The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) experts and forest department officials have been trying to locate the tiger for two days now but the animal has not come out into the open," said Sariska field director P S Somashekar.

He added that localising a tigress was a cumbersome task as the animal was constantly on the move and tranquilisation was a precise science. "The Air Force and Sariska is fully prepared for the translocation, but it seems we will have to wait," he said.

A senior forest official in Ranthambore said they managed to spot the tigress on several occasions but only for brief spells. "We need to be around 20 metres away from the tigress to be able to tranquilise it. Also, tranquilisation is a tricky job and any miss could endanger the tigress," he said.

He also added that the drug worked for close to two hours, within which the tiger had to be shifted to the specially designed cage latched to a helicopter and flown to Sariska.

The Ranthambore National Park authorities, who had earlier tracked and translocated a tiger couple four months ago, said though the winter season was the best time for translocation, it was also the most difficult. "In winter, the tigress stalks more prey and is in a better physical condition," Somashekhar said.

After the monsoons, the grass in the national park had grown upto four feet making it difficult to sight the tigress for a sustained period, he added.

"The first tiger couple has settled well in Sariska," said Somashekhar.

Heading: ‘If not Om, then Allah, God will also do for Ramdev’s yoga’ - Indian Express
Content:
While the ruling Congress at the Centre is busy praising its rural employment guarantee scheme implementation and the BJP regime in Rajasthan is boasting of creating over half-a-million jobs, their claims seem to be melting down exactly four weeks before December 4 Assembly election.

At least 20,000 people are estimated to have already lost their livelihoods while a threat of unemployment is staring in the face of thousands of others in the desert state.

Pink City, the gems' capital of India, is reeling under this crisis as orders from the US, Europe and other countries have slumped by 20 to 40 per cent. Over five lakh people in Jaipur are directly or indirectly dependent on the jewellery business for their livelihood.

Rahim Ullah, managing director of the Vaibhav Gems Limited, a $250-million firm that has 20 gems and jewellery stores across America and 24-hour jewellery channels in London and Germany, rubbishes all rumours about the financial health of his firm after the retrenchment of some employees. His firm has around 2,000 employees. "We removed just five to seven per cent high-end employees and have curbed unnecessary expenses," he argued.

People in the streets are offering varied reasons for Subhiksha and India Bulls retail chains bringing down shutters on some of their stores here. The city is also agog with speculation about many top exporters and jewellers going bankrupt, although Jewellers' Association president Vivek Kala debunks them as "mere rumours".

According to Kala, while there is truth about the global economic slowdown hitting gems and jewellery sector badly, it is not Doomsday yet. They still get "orders" from abroad, although they are for "low quality and smaller items". Exports to the US from here constitute 40 per cent of the total trade.

"Last year, export of gems and jewellery to the global market from Jaipur was to the tune of Rs 2,200 crore. It should have increased this year because of the changes in dollar-rupee exchange rate. But, as it is, we will be very happy if we touch even last year's figure," said Kala.

Kala, a multi-millionaire gems and jewellery exporter from the Pink City, has always been an executive class traveller. But when he went to the US last month to get a first-hand account of the upheaval in the US economy, he chose to travel in economy class.

"It was symbolic. I wanted to convey a message to my people here that only the fittest will survive the crisis," he said.

He said that the UPA Government could have tackled the situation better. "As the Communist party was saying, the Government could have cut down excise duty on oil. Why is the interest rate still so high?" asked Kala.

Garment exporter Abhinav Sharma, who runs a company called Nirvana, is equally pessimistic about the current scenario. Since last July, the global demand for his garments has gone down by almost 50 per cent. He had hired a French designer to keep his company abreast of global fashion trends. He removed her recently.

"We still get some orders, but we are very cautious. We don't know if we will get paid later. What if the importer in Canada declares himself insolvent?" asked Sharma. According to him, thousands of sub-contractors, to whom he would pass on the additional orders and at least 10,000 labourers from neighbouring villages who worked for these sub-contractors, have been rendered jobless.

"There are not enough orders for the people working in my own firm. How would I sub-contract others? Almost half my people went on leave for Eid and then Deepawali. They should be coming back in a week's time. I don't know what I will do with them. I have to sit down and think," he said. According to Sharma, a karigar (skilled labourer) who earned Rs 400 a day until a few months back, now gets Rs 150-250 per day because of the slump.

There is equally grim scenario in tourism sector, the backbone of Rajasthan's economy, with both foreign and domestic tourists keeping away this year. "Our hotels would run to their optimum capacity at this time of the year in the past four to five years. Now, occupancy often comes down to 60 per cent. What is more worrying is the fact that Indian tourists seem to be reluctant to travel this year," said Tarun Bansal who runs a chain of budget hotels in Jaipur.

According to sources in gems and jewellery sector, jewellers are the worst-hit because they prefer to invest in high stakes. They would park their money in stock market or real estate. "So, while the gems and jewellery sector itself is hit, the double whammy comes for them from the stock market and the real estate. You call it triple whammy," said an eminent businessman in Jaipur.

Yet, the global financial upheaval does not seem to be bothering the political class in Rajasthan. If there is any impact, they seem to believe, there is always the 'others' to blame. Rajiv Arora, an eminent gems and jewellery exporter who is taking a plunge into electoral politics this year on a Congress ticket, sees anti-incumbency, corruption, and deteriorating law and order situation as his and his party's poll planks. He does not see the global financial upheaval and the resultant job losses here as a potential poll plank.

"If something like this (massive job loss) happens, it will be against the BJP Government here, and not against the UPA Government," he said.

The BJP appears to have a ready reckoner though. Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje believes India and China could have been able to "buffer" themselves to meet the current financial crisis. The UPA Government could have done some "out of box thinking and shown some determination" to cope with the crisis.

Asked if the job losses in the state could become an election issue, she said, "I think if you can't eat, that is something that affects the people the most."

Heading: Top Hizb militant escapes from court premises - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to popularise yoga among people other than Hindus, Baba Ramdev has said one can initiate the exercise without pronouncing the word 'Om' and can substitute it with 'Allah' or 'God'. Ramdev's Haridwar-based Patanjali Yogapeeth has asked its Christian and Muslim followers to begin yoga with a prolonged utterance of Allah or God.

"Our aim is to connect science with yoga for the betterment of mankind. Why should anybody not enjoy the benefits of yoga because of reservation to utter 'Om'," said Acharya Balkrishan of Patanjali Yogapeeth.

"Baba Ramdev believes that yoga might be a gift to mankind from rishis and yogis but it is not Hinduism. It is meant for everyone. Yoga cannot be restricted on the lines or religion and community. It is meant to enlighten the entire humanity," he told The Indian Express.

Acharya Balkrishan further pointed that the pronunciation of 'Om' causes positive resonance in one's body and 'Om' itself is not connected to any faith or community. "None of the religious images come to your mind when you say 'Om'. It's universal. Its prolonged utterance gives maximum benefit to scholars of yoga. However, it can be substituted with 'Allah' or 'God'," he said.

The Patanjali Yogapeeth has set up Yoga Samities in 560 districts across the country to propagate the ancient asanas and pranayaam techniques. "We have hundreds of yoga teachers in the country who are Muslims. They don't have any opposition to the word 'Om'. A large number of Muslim and Christian students are also learning various asanas and pranayaam in different states," said Balkrishan.

Heading: Chandrayaan-1 put into lunar orbit - Indian Express
Content:
A former divisional commander of Hizbul Mujahideen, Rayees Kachroo, arrested almost seven months ago, escaped from Pulwama court premises in south Kashmir on Tuesday afternoon. Police and security forces have launched a massive manhunt to nab the top militant commander.

"Kachroo was being taken to the district court in Pulwama for hearing from the Srinagar Central Jail and was being escorted by a havildar and three constables," said Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Niyaz Mehmood.

Mehmood said they were questioning the two constables to know exactly how Kachroo escaped, as he was brought to court handcuffed. Kachroo, a top IED expert of the Hizbul Mujahideen, was responsible for killing around two dozen securitymen in south Kashmir.

Heading: Chinese auto firm to look at Singur site - Indian Express
Content:
India's first unmanned lunar spacecraft — Chandrayaan-1 — entered the lunar space early on Tuesday after a successful fifth and final orbit raising manoeuvre and is likely to start circling the Moon by Saturday. The satellite is now orbiting at a maximum altitude of 380,000 km from earth.

Exactly two weeks after it was launched from Sriharikota, the spacecraft was in the last lap of its journey into the moon's orbit after it was injected into the lunar transfer trajectory by space scientists in a critical operation described by ISRO as one of the "crucial and important milestones" in the Chandrayaan-1 mission.

"It (Chandrayaan-1) is being tracked by Spacecraft Control Centre at ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) in Bangalore. Today we have done the last orbit-raising manoeuvre to enter the lunar transfer trajectory. If everything goes right, by November 8, Chandrayaan-1 will start circling the Moon," ISRO chairman G Madhavan Nair told reporters in Ahmedabad on the sidelines of a function.

Chandrayaan-1 entered the lunar transfer trajectory with an apogee (farthest point from earth) of about 380,000 km, the space agency said in a statement. "On Saturday evening, the lunar orbit insertion manoeuvres are planned to be carried out and the Chandrayaan will be captured in Moon's orbit," ISRO spokesperson S Satish said in Bangalore.

During the crucial manoeuvre on Tuesday at 4.56 am, the spacecraft's 440 Newton liquid engine was fired for 145 seconds. Since its launch on October 22 by PSLV-C11, all systems onboard Chandrayaan-I spacecraft were performing normally, Nair said.

The ISRO statement said Chandrayaan-1 would approach the Moon on November 8 and the spacecraft's liquid engine would be fired again to insert the spacecraft into lunar orbit.

It said the health of the spacecraft was being continuously monitored from the ISTRAC with support from Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) antennas at Byalalu on the outskirts of Bangalore.

Once the spacecraft is in the lunar orbit, it will stabilise in about a week's after which it will send a probe instrument to the moon's surface.

Chandrayaan-1 carries 11 payloads — five from India and others from abroad. During a two-year orbital mission, it will provide a detailed map of the mineral, chemical and topographical characteristics of the lunar surface.

Heading: Split over Andhra: little progress made as Karat meets Bardhan - Indian Express
Content:
Marxist West Bengal is now looking to Communist China to salvage the damage it suffered because of the pullout of Tata Motors from Singur. The state Government will show the abandoned site of the Tata Motors' Nano project of Singur to First Automobile Works (FAW), a major automobile manufacturing company of China which has agreed to build an automobile manufactutring factory in West Bengal in collaboration with automobile manufacturer Ural India Ltd. FAW which has presence in 19 countries has collaboration with automobile majors as Toyota, Audi, Mazda and Volkswagon to name a few.

On Tuesday, representatives of the company and Ural India Ltd chairman J K Saraf met Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. "They will be shown places like Kharagpur, Singur and some place in North 24 Parganas district. They may not be taken to Singur this time as the situation there is still volatile. But we will show them that site. They will manufacture minibuses and trucks here," an official told The Indian Express.

FAW is the first company to be shown the abandoned Nano site after the project was pulled out of Singur following violent agitation by the Trinamool Congress. The official said the joint venture company needed 600 acres for its project. Faw, which has 1.31 lakh employees, has a capacity of 20 lakh vehicles every year.

After the meeting, Saraf said they were quite enthusiastic about the proposed project.

"We got in touch with FAW for the joint venture and they got back saying they were quite interested. We will take them to places like Kalyani, Kharagpur, Haldia and show sites."

The Government is waiting for communication from the Tatas on when they were going to dismantle the structure in Singur and return the land to the West Bengal Government. None of the ancillary units that were supposed to set up shop at Singur has got in touch with the state Government after Tata Motors chairman Ratan Tata announced their decision to pull out of Singur.

Heading: Constitution bench starts hearing long-pending pleas - Indian Express
Content:
With differences persisting between the CPI(M) and CPI on the choice of alliance partners in Andhra Pradesh, the top leadership of both the parties on Tuesday began efforts to arrive at a common position, but could not make much headway.

CPI(M) general secretary Prakash Karat held detailed discussions with his CPI counterpart A B Bardhan and senior leader D Raja on the issue. While the CPI(M)'s Andhra unit wants to ally with the TDP, CPI prefers Chiranjeevi's Praja Rajyam.

Though both the parties have decided to fight unitedly in Andhra Pradesh, the differences in choice of alliance partners has complicated matters. With the CPI(M) insisting on remaining with Chandrababu Naidu, indications are that the CPI may ask its Andhra unit to have a re-think on its preference.

"It may take some time for both the parties to work out the tactics to be adopted in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu," a senior Left leader told The Indian Express. Karat and Bardhan agreed that both their parties should carry forward with the initiative to come up with a Left and democratic alternative.

Chandrababu Naidu is a key player in the Left plans to cobble up a viable non-BJP, non-Congress alternative and the CPI(M) central leadership is keen to have an electoral understanding with the TDP to keep the third front dreams alive.

Bardhan and Karat are also learnt to have discussed the electoral strategy to be adopted in Tamil Nadu. The state unit of the CPI(M) has already referred the matter to the Politburo with a detailed analysis of the options available before it, including aligning with either the AIADMK or Vijayakant's DMDK or going alone with the CPI. The CPI National Executive which met here over the weekend had also discussed the matter and decided to have consultations with the CPI(M) to arrive at a common position.

Heading: Milind Deora to marry Manmohan Shetty’s daughter - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court 's attempt to dispose of long pending matters, especially the ones involving significant questions of law, has taken off with a five-member Constitution Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan on Tuesday taking up first such matter. The bench also comprises Justices R V Raveendran, D K Jain, P Sathasivam and J M Panchal.

A batch of petitions, including one filed by K Krishna Murty, has challenged the constitutional validity of the 73rd and 74th constitutional amendments providing reservations to backward classes and women apart from SCs and STs in panchayat and local bodies elections. The hearing on the issue had last taken place in 2001 when another Constitution Bench had sought response from all states and Union Territories on the question raised before it.

The amendments brought about in 1993 were challenged in 1994 and the matter was referred to a Constitution Bench in 1995 as the apex court at that time was of the view that some of the provisions were open to interpretation.

Heading: Ganga declared National River - Indian Express
Content:
Congress MP Milind Deora will tie the knot with Bollywood producer-financier Manmohan Shetty's daughter, Pooja, later this month. Milind and Pooja have known each other for some time.

"I immediately said yes when the two approached me for my consent some months ago," the legendary Bollywood producer Manmohan Shetty told The Indian Express. Milind's father, Murli Deora, is Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas.

The two families are keeping the wedding date a closely-guarded secret, but those in the know say that the wedding will happen "in the next two weeks". It's going to be an extremely private affair, though. "It's only the two families and close friends who will be present for the wedding," said sources close to the two families.

When contacted, the 1976-born Mumbai-South MP said, "Pooja and I have known each other for some time now and we are looking forward to being together."

Apart from being one of the prominent Gen Next Congress faces, Milind has been a passionate campaigner on issues ranging from global warming to HIV. He is also considered close to Congress general secretary Rahul Gandhi.

Pooja, on the other hand, has been assisting her father in film production.

Heading: Maharashtra announces reward for whistleblowers - Indian Express
Content:
More than two decades after Rajiv Gandhi conceptualised the Ganga Action Plan (GAP), Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Tuesday decided to declare Ganga a 'National River' to achieve the objectives of the clean-up operation. The decision was taken during a review of the Ganga Action Plan by the Prime Minister.

The meeting also decided to set up a Ganga River Basin Authority, which will be entrusted with the responsibility of planning, implementing and monitoring projects regarding the river. The authority, headed by the Prime Minister, would comprise of chief ministers of states through which the Ganga flows.

Unlike the original Ganga Action Plan, which primarily focused on municipal sewage treatment, Tuesday's decisions are aimed at broad-basing the river management efforts, integrating pollution control with measures for sustainable use of water and flood management.

"It was decided that there is a need to replace the current piecemeal efforts taken up in a fragmented manner in select cities with an integrated approach that sees the river as an ecological entity and addresses issues of quantity in terms of water flows along with issues of quality," said a release issued by the PMO after the meeting. The funding pattern is likely to be finalised in two months.

Heading: Rajasthan moves SC over HC stay on BPL women scheme - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashra Government on Tuesday announced a reward scheme for whistleblowers who tip off the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on disproportionate assets of officials and public servants.

Accordingly, a person who tips off the ACB, with clues leading to the confiscation of movable or immovable properties, would be rewarded.

For discovery of disproportionate assets (DA) worth up to Rs 25 lakh the reward would be Rs 10,000; for DA over Rs 25 lakh and up to Rs 50 lakh, it would be Rs 25,000; for DA worth over Rs 50 lakh but below Rs 1 crore, the reward would be Rs 50,000; for DA above Rs 1 crore and up to Rs 5 crore , it would be Rs 1lakh; and for DA above Rs 5 crore, the reward would be Rs 2 lakh.

The scheme was announced by the Home Department on Tuesday. An official said the reward scheme was under consideration for a long time to take action against officials who amassed wealth by misusing their position. He said the name of the whistleblower would be kept a secret.

Heading: Gates to visit Pune, AIDS officials remain unaware - Indian Express
Content:
The Rajasthan Government has moved the Supreme Court challenging a High Court decision to stay the implementation of its "Bhamasha scheme", providing financial assistance to 50 lakh women from BPL families, as it "violated" the Election Commission's model code of conduct.

Following brief submissions by senior counsel Mukul Rohtagi, appearing for the state, a bench of Justices B N Aggrawal and G S Singhvi agreed to take up the matter for hearing on November 7.

On October 21, the Rajasthan High Court had stayed the implementation of the scheme on a writ petition complaining that the scheme announced by the state Government was violative of the election code of conduct as dates had already been announced for the Assembly elections.

Rohtagi termed the High Court order as being erroneous, as the scheme was announced in February this year much before the election dates were announced.

He said it was a Central Government scheme and the Reserve Bank of India had issued circulars as far back as in 2006 to banks for inclusion of 50 lakh beneficiaries in each state under the 'Bhamasha Financial Empowerment and Women Welfare Scheme'. The scheme envisaged providing incentive of Rs 1,500 to each of the families besides providing medical insurance cover to the tune of Rs 30,000 each.

Heading: 5-year-old loses battle for life - Indian Express
Content:
Bill Gates and his wife Melinda will visit Pune for the first time on Thursday, unknown to the people who are fighting in India the same cause that the Microsoft founder has taken up worldwide.

Gates and wife, who have been crusading against AIDS, will spend an hour with commercial sex workers at the red light area of Budhwar Peth. High-ranking officials dealing with AIDS awareness programmes are, however, in the dark. Officials with the Maharashtra State AIDS Control Society and scientists at National AIDS Research Institute had no clue of the high-profile visit, which is not being given publicity.

However, confirming the visit, Penny Richards, communications in-charge of the Gates Foundation in New Delhi, said Gates would assess two projects funded by the foundation at Budhwar Peth.

Bill and Melinda Gates are in the country with their children Jennifer Katharine, Rory John and Phoebe Adele, as well as Bill's father William H Gates. On Wednesday, Gates met Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss to launch a public healthcare initiative with focus on polio eradication.

The initiative will be under the Gates Foundation, which has committed about $ 9.9 billion in grants for global health till October. The foundation has committed more than $ 400 million globally to support polio eradication efforts. India, one of the four countries where the disease is still endemic, is among the recipients.

In Pune, though, Gates will review two projects on prevention of sexually transmitted infection and meet commercial sex workers. The Gates Foundation started its operations in India in 2003 and has committed over $200 million to HIV prevention in India, its largest commitment to the campaign in any country.

Heading: Assam blasts: suspect’s sketch released - Indian Express
Content:
Nilima Kalita will not have to call Roll Number 16 again. Five days was too long a fight that five-year-old Moromi Sharma, a nursery class student of Hengerabari P School near Dispur here, could put up against the impact of an explosion that was carried out by terrorists with a Maruti car that was packed with at least 30 kg of RDX and PE3 inside.

Thus, when Moromi's body arrived at the school, hardly 300 metres from the chief minister's office, not only Nilima Kalita, but the entire teaching staff broke down. Kalita was particularly inconsolable. "She was not just an obedient little girl, but also the most inquisitive. Moromi had a near-100 per cent attendance, and that despite her parents being daily wagers," the class-teacher later said.

"She suffered over 50 per cent burns apart from the shock which even adults could not take easily. We tried our best, but could not save Moromi," said Seemarekha Devi, associate professor in the plastic surgery (burns) department of the Guwahati Medical College Hospital.

While Hengerabari grieved for Moromi, several other localities in the Assam capital too were finding it difficult to cope with the massive damage that the serial blasts inflicted upon them last Thursday.

In Kahilipara, close to the state-owned Jyoti Chitraban film studios, Purnima Saikia, a 55-year old widow, has no words to describe the loss of her only daughter Dipamoni, a 29-year old singer and bihu dancer, who had only begun her career as a lawyer nine months back. "I have been reduced to a lump of flesh and bones," says Saikia, who kept repeating the story of how she had brought up Dipamoni after her father, a police inspector, had died when she was still in school.

The death toll in the nine serial blasts that occurred in three places in Guwahati and three other towns of Lower Assam, reached 86 on Tuesday. Over 300 persons are still in different hospitals.

Heading: Memories Remain - Indian Express
Content:
Full five days after nine explosions claimed 86 lives and left several hundred injured, the Assam Police released the sketch of one of the suspects on Tuesday on the basis of descriptions provided by eyewitnesses.

The sketch released was of a suspect in the blast that killed at least 15 persons, including three lawyers, in front of the courts of the Kamrup deputy commissioner and CJM on Thursday.

"We have hired a professional portrait artist who can draw pictures on the basis of descriptions provided by eyewitnesses. We are soon releasing some more sketches," Jayashree Khersa, additional SP, Guwahati City Police, said on Tuesday.

The additional SP said sleuths had estimated that he would be 35 years old, about 5 feet 7 inches in height and weighing about 68 kg. "The sketch released has been finalised after several rounds of verifications done by several eyewitnesses," Khersa said.

At least two eyewitnesses have come out in public giving descriptions of some persons they suspect to be the culprits in the blast that occurred between the DC's court and the CJM's court. While lawyer Pradip Konwar said he saw two suspicious-looking persons minutes before the blast, one person who had taken his sons to the planetarium claimed he saw two persons whose descriptions matched those of the lawyer's. Both have said they had seen two persons, one in kurta-pajama and the other in trousers and shirt, with one having a light beard. The face in the sketch released is one with a light beard.

Meanwhile, the police picked up four more persons on Tuesday, but refused to divulge any details.

Heading: Old lady visits the Bernabeu - Indian Express
Content:
Like they've done for so many years, fans once again walked in droves towards the 'old' VCA stadium on Tuesday. Its walls now blackened with age and disregard, this home of several commanding performances and notorious confrontations is also bidding farewell to Test cricket in this season of bye-byes.

Now a state-of-the-art complex has spawned on the outskirts of Nagpur, robbing the sheen of what was perhaps the last of India's simple, no-frills stadiums that ensured a great, up-close-and-personal view from anywhere in the ground. No gleaming corporate boxes, no glass facades, no macro patterns painted on the seats.

The new stadium, which contains all of the above, will make its Test debut on Thursday when the now-crucial fourth India vs Australia match kicks off. But before the focus shifts to that latest embodiment of modern technology (some last minute touch-ups are needed, and the practice facilities are not ready), the two teams went through light net sessions at the same old spot where their unforgettable skirmish had taken place four years ago.

Back in October of 2004, the green pitch at the VCA had been the centre of all sorts of speculation. Curator Kishore Pradhan had hurled a ticking bomb in the direction of the Indians, and the state association's boss Shashank Manohar — now BCCI president — had thrown the book in captain Sourav Ganguly's face by denying his request to have some of the grass shaven from the surface. At the height of the opposition camp's machinations to unseat BCCI chief Jagmohan Dalmiya, the Nagpur drama was seen as a ploy by the rival camp to show him in poor light.

Licking their lips at the sight of the wicket, and scarcely believing their luck, Australia had rolled on to victory, and with it captured the 'final frontier'. Ganguly and Harbhajan Singh had skipped the match because of injuries, but allegations run thick and fast to this day that they had been scared of failing on the ripe, green pitch.

The more things change

On Tuesday, the dullness during practice made the fires that had raged in the stadium four years ago seem almost unreal. In place of the green wicket in the centre were two barren, brown tracks separated by nets. Balls weren't darting off the surface, not moving prodigiously in the air. And VVS Laxman, getting ready for his 100th Test, was having a go in the middle, handling the measured accuracy of Munaf Patel with ease.

Sourav Ganguly, expected to be the centre of attention before his farewell match, took a day off, not emerging for practice from the larger-than-normal team bus with "Jumbo" emblazoned on it, which was misinterpreted by several onlookers as a tribute to Anil Kumble.
