Sandeep Thapar, a resident of Sector 27, said: "People come from the wrong direction all of a sudden. This increases the chances of an accident with the violator. The police should close the broken medians so that people can't cross over."

Superintendent of Police (Traffic) H S Doon said that the department had taken note of a few broken medians and written to the Engineering department to repair them and plug the gaps. "These broken road dividers are a potential threat. We will depute traffic cops on the broken medians and not let anybody cross over till the repair work is completed," he assured.

Heading: Panchkula gangrape: court cancels bail plea of an accused - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Police have arrested Ropar-based land developer Rajbir Singh, managing director of the Maharaja City, on charges of cheating and violating the provisions of the Punjab Urban Development Authority Act.

While a series of complaints were filed with Ropar police against Rajbir Singh and his wife Rajwant Kaur; the Ropar police on Tuesday arrested Rajbir and produced him in the Ropar court today. The court has remanded Rajbir to two-day in police custody for further interrogation. His wife's role is yet to scrutinised, the police said.

Rajbir, a resident of Phase-IV, Mohali and commonly known as Rajaji in Ropar, has allegedly defrauded various people to the tune of over Rs 60 lakh, the police said.

Spread over an area of around 18 acres, Maharaja City is located on the Ropar-Morinda road stretch, a few kilometres away from the Ropar city.

According to complainant Ajit Singh, a Ropar resident, Rajbir had entered into a sale-agreement with him for two plots in the Maharaja City, for which Rajbir allegedly accepted Rs 10.35 lakh.

The complainant alleged that despite repeated requests, Rajbir neither refunded his money nor got the registered deed executed in his favour. Following this, the complainant sought the help of the police.

Besides Ajit, there are around a dozen complainants who have submitted written complaints to the Ropar police against Rajbir and his wife. Almost all the complainants are related to duping investors, where Rajbir has accepted lakhs from the complainants in lieu of the plots in Maharaja City and then refused to get the registered deeds executed in the complainants' favour.

After receiving a pile of complaints against Rajbir, Ropar Senior Superintendent of Police R N Dhoke had marked all the complaints to the Economic Offences Wing for thorough investigations. After about a month-long inquiry, the Economic Offences Wing officials yesterday recommended registration of a criminal case against Rajbir.

The police investigations revealed that Rajbir got the approval-license from the Punjab Urban Development Authority (PUDA) for his residential colony – Maharaja City — on August 17, 2006; however, he had entered into sale-agreements with the complainants three months prior to the approval from PUDA.

SSP R N Dhoke said: "Rajbir committed serious violations as far as the PUDA Act is concerned. There are a series of complaints against Maharaja City and its directors --Rajbir and his wife Rajwant Kaur. While Rajbir's role was found substantial for registering a criminal case; his wife Rajwant Kaur's malafide involvement has not come forth as yet. We have registered one case against him; while seven more complaints are pending with us. It is quite likely that all those seven complaints will also lead to registration of seven more criminal cases against him, as the prime content of all the complaints is similar."

"I want to send a stern message to all such land mafias, who are alluring and duping innocent investors. We shall be launching a campaign against all such dubious land developers. People are free to approach the police on any such issue," Dhoke added.

Heading: PAU staff hold rally on campus to ‘get across the message’ - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the two main accused in the Panchkula gangrape case remain at large, the session's court on Wednesday dismissed the bail application of Jitesh, a co-accused. The bail application of Jitesh was cancelled on the plea that the phone set used to call the victim was his and recovered from his residence by the police.

Sources said the police are also planning to move court demanding the cancellation of the bail of another accused Aman Ahuja. While Aman was arrested on September 22, police nabbed Jitesh on September 26.

Meanwhile, an officer of the Haryana Women and Child Welfare department visited the residence of the rape victim in Sector 14 assuring her all possible help.

Suraj Lamba, the district programme officer of the Haryana Women and Child Welfare department, said: "After learning about what all happened with the minor girl, we have assured her family of full support. Besides, I not only made the Panchkula Deputy Commissioner aware of the status of the case, but also met DSP (city) Ram Chander Rathi and other police officers investigating the case. We were also informed that the police have moved court requesting cancellation of Ahuja's bail," Lamba said.

The police have also been asked to provide security to the family after it was alleged that they were receiving threat calls. A relative of the victim said: "The bail application of Jitesh was dismissed by Additional Sessions judge Sanjeev Jindal's court today. We will now move the Punjab and Haryana High Court against the orders of bail that Aman Ahuja has got in the matter."

Meanwhile, the victim was today taken to her school in Sector 11 to help her identify the Chhavi, one of the main accused in the case and five-year her senior.

"The victim, along with her mother, was taken to her school where she was asked to go through the previous records of the school students so that we have an idea about Chhavi," the relative of the victim said.

Heading: MC blacklists SK Constructions - Indian Express
Content:
Despite being served advisory letters and subsequent meetings with Vice-Chancellor M S Kang, the PAU Non-Teaching Employees' Union today held their rally on the campus. Though a majority of their demands have been accepted and implemented, the staff said that the rally was held to 'get across the message'.

Registrar Dr R K Mahey had called upon PAU NonTeaching Employees' Union president Harbans Singh Mundi and informed him that the V-C had rolled back his decision of appointing a teacher as his secretary and that the charge has now been given to Nahoria Singh, a non-teaching employee in the Dean Basic Sciences office. "We decided to go ahead with the rally as our two main demands — appointment of secretary to Vice-Chancellor (SVC) and withdrawing of the advisory letter — have already been accepted. But the other demands are pending. We have been told that these demands will be taken to the board of management and will also be accepted soon."

Owing to pressure from non-teaching employees, Dr Kang had withdrew the advisory letters sent out to various heads of departments and had even requested the non-teaching union not to hold the rally. The union had stuck to their guns claiming that the V-C still had to take a call on SVC.

While appointing Dr P P S Lubana as his SVC, the V-C said, "I have the right to chose my SVC." However, when the non-teaching employees mounted pressure and demanded that this post be held by their cadre, the V-C bowed to their pressure.

Heading: GLADA auction turns out to be a damp squib - Indian Express
Content:
The work carried out by the company in Barewal is not up to the mark: Ghuman

Taking serious note of the low quality roads constructed in the Barewal area, MC Commissioner G S Ghuman has ordered to blacklist the contracting agency SK Constructions from the corporation. Ghuman said: "The work carried out by the company in Barewal is not up to mark. Big potholes have surfaced."

In addition to this, even Rs 5-crore project of re-metalling on the Hambran Road was also not found satisfactory. Ghuman added: "I gave orders to stop the work three days ago because the contracting agency had not done thoroughly cleaned the road before metalling it. Moreover, road gullies for rainwater harvesting are to be made before remetalling the roads."

The Hambran road project had been sanctioned more than six months ago. Ghuman said that the company will not be able to apply for any works in the future but is bound to repair the broken roads at Barewal. While hitting at the MC's building branch Ghuman said: "Our building staff is responsible for not checking the work going on at the Hambran road. The owner had shown residential map in the corporation records but was making a huge commercial complex. The work has been stalled."

Heading: Four attack police bus to free 3 accomplices - Indian Express
Content:
No bidder attends the auction of 20 booths at Samrala

Officials of the Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA) were a disappointed lot as no bidder turned up at the auction of 20 booths at Samrala civil court complex.

The officials waited for bidders till evening and finally decided to postpone it.

This is the second such incident in the last one month. On October 8 too, no bidder had turned up for the auction of 16 shops opposite the Samrala civil hospital where the reserve price had been kept Rs 54,000 per square yard.

Estate Officer Jeet Ram said: "As we got no response today, we have decided to postpone the event."

The reserve price today was kept Rs 40,000 per square yard.

According to property dealers, the reserve price was too high. Moreover, being a small place, Samrala cannot give good returns to GLADA. GLADA authorities also feel that real estate market has slowed down due to the crash in the share market. Perhaps, this is the reason that property dealers did not come for the auction this time, said GLADA officials.

Property dealers claimed that even on the Jail Road, there was no scope of having a shopping compleax as the location is not strategic.

The inner city faces the problem of acute congestion.

Hence, buyers do not want to invest in the market.

Heading: How to improve education? Rescued child labourers give tips - Indian Express
Content:
CRIME IN CITY: Accused out on bail hurl bricks through windowpanes in the parking of the court complex

In an attempt to free their accomplices who did not get bail in a murder case, a group of accused on bail reportedly attacked a police bus carrying undertrials at local court here today. The four accused attacked the bus in the parking lot of the court complex.

Though the police thwarted the attempt, it failed to nab the accused.

The police have registered a case against all the seven accused, including the four who are already out on bail. Harpreet alias Vicky, Manvinder, Billa and Rampal had allegedly come to free Deepak and Sooraj who are lodged in Borstal jail and Gurcharan Singh who is lodged in the Central jail.

In a seemingly planned effort, the four accused along with some other accomplices, attacked the police bus as soon as it reached the judicial complex in the district courts parking. These accused pelted bricks at the bus thereby smashing the rear window panes of the bus.

To make most of the situation, the undertrials in the bus, around 24 in number, also tried to escape. The police had a harrowing time controlling the visitors, who began to run helter skelter and even damaged the furniture in the court complex.

"We have registered FIR against all the seven accused under Sections 307,353and 106 of the Indian Penal Code. We are investigating the matter and will take a stringent action to nab the culprits," said DSP Bhupinder Singh.

Heading: Even on the eve of Gates’ arrival, police clueless on security - Indian Express
Content:
For the 25 rescued child labourers who are now associated with Action for Rights of Children (ARC), it was once in a lifetime experience when they scrutinised the school system and gave suggestions to improve the quality of education. The children were participating at a meeting organised by ARC in association with UNICEF on the eradication of child labour and implementation of the right to education in the city on Tuesday.

Mini Srinivasan of ARC - Pune said that the children were asked to give suggestions in order to ensure that child labourers are attracted to school and do not quit to become a child labourer again. The children, who took part in the meeting, came up with suggestions like teachers must stop beating students in schools, schools must be spacious and clean, teachers must take genuine interest in teaching and spend more time with the students and surprise visits of supervisors should be surprise for the school management as well to understand the ground reality. These suggestions are forwarded for the state level consultation that will be held in Mumbai at the end of this month and will be attended by Commission of Women and Child Development.

Alpa Vora, national coordinator for the child labour eradication campaign, Vijayalaxmi Arora of UNICEF -Mumbai, Bhushan Nalge, education officer, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, representatives of non-governmental organisations and heads of two observation homes, brainstormed on ways to prevent children's migration, to make the rescue and rehabilitation process of child labourers less traumatic and related issues.

"I have mentioned in my recommendation that there is a need to address this problem case-by case with the help of voluntary organisations, students and government officials," he said. The children also put up a 20-minute play on child labour during this meeting. The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) is conducting these meetings at various cities in the state along with local voluntary organisations for the National Campaign on Child Labour Eradication that will be launched on Children's Day.

Heading: PMC issues notices to shops - Indian Express
Content:
On the eve of the arrival of Microsoft founder Bill Gates in the city, it was learnt that the entire trip has been arranged in such a manner that the entire police machinery and high ranking officers have been kept in the dark.

The Indian Express on Wednesday published a report on Gates' visit to Pune. The Microsoft founder who has funded HIV prevention projects via Pathfinder organisation wanted to visit two such programmes at Budhwar Peth in Pune.

However the visit has been kept such a closely guarded secret that even top police officials are not aware of it. Says Rajendra Sonavne, Joint Commissioner of Police, "I have no idea about security arrangements for Bill Gates.''

On their part, the Gates' have clearly said out that it was a personal and private 'learning' visit to Pune and they did not want publicity.

Penny Richards, communications-in-charge of Bill and Melinda Gates foundation when contacted in New Delhi about Gates' programme in Pune, said that it was a purely private learning visit and the Microsoft founder does not want publicity.

Till late Wednesday evening the organisers coordinating the visit were unavailable for comment.

Heading: NSUI leader was killed by cousin: Cops - Indian Express
Content:
Bogged down by the dues that are running into crores of rupees in the form of rent against the properties given on lease to various business houses and organisations in the city, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has recently sent notices to these properties asking them to vacate the shops if they are unable to pay the arrears and rent as per the existing ratable value of the occupied land.

The civic land acquisition department issued these notices. In the notices, the PMC has pointed out that the shops are occupied despite the lease period has come to an end and that these shops need to be auctioned, therefore action is being taken as per the government regulation regarding the land distribution. The notices also mention that if the shop occupants are ready to pay the rent as per the new ratable value of the land and pays the outstanding charges till the bidding process is over, the concerned shop owner could be given a continuation on the same location or else the occupant will have to hand over the occupied land to PMC.

Heading: HIV infection among high-risk groups has declined, say experts - Indian Express
Content:
Investigations have revealed that the murder of Pravin Jagdale, city vice president of National Students Union of India (NSUI) was the fallout of a petty dispute with his cousin Dinesh Jagdale. Police are also probing whether land dispute was the cause of his murder.

Jagdale was murdered at an open space on Shirole Road, Deccan Gymkhana on Tuesday evening. A complaint in this case was lodged at the Deccam Gymkhana police station.

Police said that the suspect Dinesh is absconding. Meanwhile, police have identified two more persons - Abhijeet Jadhav and Pramod Jadhav who are suspected to have involved in the murder.

Police said that Dinesh and Pravin had purchased a tempo three years back for business. There was dispute between them over distribution of profit and ownership of tempo. A few days before, Pravin sold the tempo to another persons. So the dispute between them had worsened. It is suspected that Dinesh along with the other two suspects stoned Pravin and assaulted him with sharp weapons on Tuesday, causing his death.

Heading: Fuming JCP makes dramatic exit from Janta Darbar - Indian Express
Content:
There is a declining trend in the prevalence of HIV infection among high-risk groups, Dr Prakash Sabade, project director of Maharashtra State AIDS Control Society (MSACS) said here on Wednesday.

The epidemic had stabilised but this did not mean that we should be complacent, Sabade said. He along with officials of the Geneva-based Global Fund for AIDS, TB and Malaria (GFATM) was in the city to review the ongoing HIV prevention projects funded by them.

Dr Suresh Gupta, additional director, MSACS, said that 'prevention of HIV' programmes had reached a saturation point among high-risk groups. So much so that from 88 HIV testing facilities in 2005, the state has set up a total of 678 HIV testing facilities. Also a total of 124 public and private partnership programmes are underway in the state to upscale efforts to prevent HIV.

The government has a budget of Rs 62 crore for HIV awareness and intervention programmes in the state.

The funds are provided by the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) and given to 33 NGOs in the state. According to MSACS officials there is a general decline of HIV among high-risk groups from 30 per cent to 14 per cent.

Sabade, however, emphasised that it was not the time to be complacent. Reiterating this viewpoint, Rekha Jain, western region coordinator of NACO for Maharashtra and Goa, said that a total of 36 link antiretroviral treatment centres are being set up in the state. Here people who have stabilised on treatment for HIV after six months or so need not travel to far-flung centres for their medication. In Maharashtra, a total of 1.2 lakh persons suffering from HIV have enrolled in the ART programme and around 43,000 are on treatment.

Heading: PMPML gets new chief - Indian Express
Content:
A 500-strong crowd was left speechless after an enraged Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonavne adjourned the first Janta Darbar, a platform where senior police officials address the problems of the public, held at Pimpri police station premises at 5.30 pm on Wednesday.

Sonavne left the stage in a hush under police security after politicians of various parties in Pimpri-Chinchwad tried to use the occasion as a political stage for accusing the police of harassing citizens and meting out injustice to them.

A lot of people present expressed their disappointment as Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh, who was supposed to attend the event, gave it a miss. It was he who conceptualised the idea of Janta Darbar and announced a week before his intention to start at Pimpri.

"Police are not recovery agents. So, it is not expected from people, to come to the police asking them to forcefully get a house vacated or recover money and settle financial matters. So people should not try give supari to police to solve such matter s. Instead, chairmen of societies should kick out those staying on rent if they are not ready to leave the house," said Sonavne, while answering a query before his dramatic exit.

Police officials present had to face a barrage of complaints of rising chain snatching incidents, increase in crime against senior citizens, harassment by police officials, fake currency circulation and increasing cases of loot in the industrial township.

During the interaction Sonavne said that from the year 2006 to October 2008 there have been 43 cases reported, where old woman have been tricked and looted but the cases have not been solved.

People also came up with complaints of indecent behaviour in public places from the part of college students in public places. Sonavne said in addition to policing and maintaining law and order they also have to solve social issues now.

Heading: APMC commissioning agents refuse to pay levy - Indian Express
Content:
Ashwini Kumar, former additional director general of Yashwantrao Chavan Academy of Development Administration will be the new chief of Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited(PMPML). He is replacing S B Patil, who will now be the additional divisional commissioner of Konkan.

The transfer order, which came in September, was stayed due to the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG). State government officials had felt then that it would be more useful to have Patil in charge till the CYG got over to ensure smooth operations during the Games.

"Fleet augmentation and route rationalisation continue to be the top priorities in improving the service," Patil said. Ashwini Kumar was not available for comment. However, in a written statement to the media, he said that he would strive to improve the PMPML service for the customers.

Patil joins the brigade of city bus utility's chiefs to be transferred within short duration. He has been the chief of PMPML for sixteen months. "Each new person who joins requires at least four to five months to figure out the nuances of the company. Then they are given such little time to work. It is not a good sign," said Vivek Velankar, PMP pravasi manch.

Patil's tenure in office was fraught with controversies because of the fare hike. Members of the youth congress had blackened his face last month demanding the cutting down of fares. Citizens groups have also been actively campaigning in this regard.

Heading: Women line up for low-interest loans - Indian Express
Content:
The last date for depositing the money was November 5

The levy charges to the tune of Rs 30 lakh, a contribution from Agriculture Produce Market Committee (APMC) customers, towards the PF, gratuity and other benefits for the 3,000 unorganised APMC labourers is yet to be deposited with the Mahtari Mandal Board. The last date for depositing the money was November 5.

This is because the APMC commissioning agents who are responsible for recovering the levy from customers have refused to do so, on the grounds that it would be difficult for them to implement. The levy is the additional fee of 30 per cent of the salary paid to the Mahtari Mandal by the commissioning agents towards the benefits of the workers.

"We will review the matter on November 7 and then decide the future course of action," said B J Deshmukh, administrator, APMC. On Tuesday, APMC administration had said strict action would be taken against those defaulting, including revoking of licenses.

"We did not pay the levy, we have called another meeting to decide the matter," said Shivlal Bhosale, president of the commissioning agents of APMC.

For the agents, the fear is that the customers will refuse to pay the levy and they themselves will have to foot the bill. "We are already paying the one per cent market cess from our own pockets, it should technically be paid by our customers," said an APMC agent. They have asked that the Mahtari Mandal Board ask their own labourers to collect the levy from the customers.

Pune APMC will be the second after Ahmednagar to tap the customer for the labourers' security net, for whom the additional cost will not be more than Rs 150 per tonne.

On October 19, the government appointed a committee headed by principal secretary of cooperatives S K Goel, which decided on an interim basis that the consumer would pay the levy to the commission agent, who in turn would deposit it with the board.

Till September, the farmers were paying the levy to the commissioning agents, who were depositing it with the Mahtari Mandal Board. But farmers decided not to pay, falling back on a 2004 Bombay high court judgement for an Ahmednagar court. The State government has decided in an interim order that the customer would pay for the levy. The agents have been authorised to collect the levy from the consumers, but they have not started recovering the dues yet. For the consumers, the effect of the levy over goods would be minuscule — only about 15 paise for every kg. But the aggregate cost per month in levy is to the tune of Rs 30 lakh.

Heading: EXPOSED: to radiation in France, to controversy near Pune - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 300 women from self-help groups (SHGs) have taken loans up to Rs 10 lakh from nationalised banks in the district since October 10, when President Pratibha Patil launched in the city a scheme bringing down the interest rate to four per cent.

Twenty-five SHGs have got the loan sanctioned while 15 are in the final stages of approval. Loan seekers have submitted proposals for poultry, organic, goat and dairy farming.

"The scheme will enable women to take on more entrepreneurial activities and repay faster," said senior district coordinator T L Shere of Mahila Arthik Vikas Mahamandal (MAVIM), one of the key agencies coordinating the scheme in the district.

Bank of Maharashtra, Bank of India, Central Bank, State Bank of India have provided loans ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh, he said.

All this has happened while awareness is still very low. Pune District Collector Chandrakant Dalvi has said he would organiae a meeting with bank representatives, followed by meetings in every taluka.

With banks so far having offered loans at 9-11 per cent, Shere said, the scheme will benefit nearly 17 lakh women from rural areas from a total of 1.42 SHGs.

"Around 45,000 SHGs will stand to get Rs 50,000, another 72,000 will get Rs 1 lakh and 18,000 SHGs will get Rs 2 lakh, with the state taking on an interest subsidy of nearly Rs 129.01 crore in three years," he said.

A senior officer with a nationalised bank said they are confident of repayment going by the past records of SHGs. "We will be only too willing to help these women," he said. Manisha Kale of Pune's Garib Nawaz Bachat Gat, who was given the first disbursal of Rs 2 lakh from the president, has speeded up planning for dairy farming. "It should start soon. We have mobilised our group," she said.

Heading: In hour of glory, Pandit speaks for chosen field - Indian Express
Content:
HITTING HOME: Radioactive trail from Otis lift buttons leads to foundry on city outskirts

Vipras Castings Ltd, tucked away in Khopoli, some 70 km from Pune, is coping with one bit of international exposure it could have well done without.

The source of its discomfort is a revelation last month that buttons installed in some 500 Otis elevators in France were radaioactive. The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) has traced the radioactive scrap metal to Vipras.

The buttons had been supplied to Otis by French firm Mafelec that, in turn, sourced the materials and components from four Indian companies.

It was at Vipras that the scrap containing radioactive metal was first melted and made into steel bars that were supplied to SKM Steels. SKM in turn supplied components to Bunts and Laxmi Electricals that finally sold to Mafelec. The source of the scrap, though, is yet to be ascertained.

"I received a call from my counterpart in the French regulatory board and was informed of their findings. We immediately set up an inquiry and traced the origin of the material to the Khopoli foundry," confirmed Dr Om Pal Singh, secretary of AERB.

Singh added, though, that this is a global problem that was neither restricted to India nor very uncommon. "What is vitally needed is a stringent check at every step to counter such incidents," he said.

Pranay Gordia, managing director of Vipras, admitted that the chain of events had ended at his foundry but said that it was a steel plant and had only made the steel bars, not the final lift buttons. Besides, the bars were made from scrap that Vipras imports from various sources, he said.

"We only recycle scrap, we do not generate any scrap. We are in the process of finding out where this particular scarp came from. It could be one of the many countries we import scrap from - it would not be proper to name any one right now," he said.

Vipras supplied about 10 tonnes of steel to SKM that further processed it for the lift buttons.

Goradia said that despite regulations being place for checking the materials for radioactivity, these had obviously not been adhered to either in India or abroad. "It's easy for the western world to say that the radioactive metals have been traced to India but the fact remains that the products went into France and also outside it to the US without any of the checks being conducted even at the most obvious points like ports. I have been in the business for 12 years and this is the first time I have experienced anything like this," he said.

Vipras has since installed a machine to check radioactive emission so that such an incident does not recur. "Henceforth we will carry out our own emission checks," said Goradia.

In France, 20 workers who had handled the buttons were exposed to radiation. After France's Nuclear Safety Authority detected this, Otis removed hundreds of buttons installed in about 500 elevators all over France and also the US.

The buttons contained traces of radioactive cobalt-60. The health risk to the workers exposed to the radiation, though, has been described as "extremely low".

Heading: Arrest of ‘patriot’ angers neighbours - Indian Express
Content:
Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, chosen for the greatest civilian award, describes the decision as an honour for Indian classical music.

"I accept this award on behalf of all those who have contributed to Indian classical music. This is the first time that someone from the kirana gharana has been honoured with the Bharat Ratna," the maestro said, a day after he had been named.

He went down memory lane: "I believe that all moments belong to the Almighty. There are many people who enriched my musical journey but I specifically remember harmonium player Thakurdas at this moment. I miss my wife who was the major source of inspiration. She was a true music lover and supported me in my musical journey."

He also remembered his guru Sawai Gandharva and the times he would to travel 10 miles just for the sake of listening to a three-minute record. "Today times have changed and it is difficult to identify good singers. I don't listen to most of the singers of this generation. The harsh reality is that most of the maestros are no more," he added.

Wednesday morning saw his house, Kalashri, flooded with well-wishers from various fields. "The phone hasn't stopped ringing since yesterday. In fact I got the news from one of my journalist friends. And by the time I came downstairs to inform my father about the good news, the phone started ringing," said Panditji's son Srinivas Joshi.

Among those who conveyed their greetings on the phone were Shiv Sena chief Uddhav Thackeray, artiste Prabha Atre, Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, Ustad Amjad Ali Khan and Pandit Jasraj. Among the maestro's visitors were Pune mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosle, Pandit Shounak Abhisheki, Sanjeev Abhyankar and tabla nawaz Ramdas Palsule.

Accolades and anecdotes
* Pandit Upendra Bhat congratulated Pandit Bhimsen Joshi and said: "This should have happened long time ago but then I must say that it is better late than never. I have never come across a progressive singer like Panditji. I remember him saying that in today's applause lies the challenge to be a better performer tomorrow."
* Shrinivas Joshi said, "Panditji is a cricket lover. Some years ago we were in Delhi for a function. We were waiting for it to start when suddenly he saw Sachin Tendulkar passing by. Panditji rushed to him and like a kid told him, 'I am Bhimsen Joshi and a great fan of yours'. I can never forget the shy expressions on Tendulkar's face."
* Pandit Shounak Abhisheki shared some of the interactions between his father Jitendra Abhisheki and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi. "My father would not hesitate whenever Panditji asked him to perform. He is the Bheeshmacharya of Indian music," he said.
* Pandit Sanjeev Abhyankar said, "In 1981 when Panditji heard me singing, he told my parents to nurture the singer in me. His words played an important role in making me a singer. He has inspired generations."

ENS

Heading: Couldn’t vote, but city’s Americans still hail the change in White House - Indian Express
Content:
Neighbours on Wednesday described Lt Col Prasad Purohit as "an innocent man who has been wrongfully arrested". He had done duty for the country both in Kashmir and the Nagaland and could not be painted a terrorist, they said.

"He is a very patriotic man. We are proud of him and will call a press conference to describe his heroics," said a senior citizen who claimed to be close to Purohit.

Purohit is a homegrown boy who studied at Abhinav Vidyalay, a local Marathi medium school, before graduating from Brihan Maharashtra College of Commerce. His home is at Susmruti, a bungalow in Shantileela Society off Law College Road. His mother and sister there while his wife and two sons were staying with him at Panchamadhi, where he was last posted.

"Prasad was trained at the Officers Training Academy, Chennai in 1995-96. As an officer in 15 Maratha Batallion, he has worked in sensitive areas of Nagaland and Kashmir. Then he was posted in military intelligence," the elderly neighbour said.

"He used to give lectures to youths to generate a sense of patriotism among them. He may have given a few lectures for Abhinav Bharat members too. That does not mean he is involved in acts of terror," he added.

A woman who lives near the bungalow agreed. "Prasad used to encourage youths to become patriots. Inspired by him, his nephew junked a lucrative job with a software company and joined the army," she said.

Neighbours took out their anger on the media for hounding Purohit. From early on Wednesday morning, journalists had hung around the bungalow. One neighbour went to the extent of calling the police to keep them at bay. Police sub-inspector Ravindra Patil and two constables of Deccan Gymkhana police station went to the bungalow and tried to soothe neighbours' frayed tempers.

Police inspector Peter Lobo of Pune's ATS unit said arms expert Rakesh Dhavde and Ajay Rahirkar were close friends of Purohit. "Rahirkar was a college friend. Purohit also knew other Abhinav Bharat members. He has conducted a few meetings with Abhinnav Bharat members in Pune," Lobo said.

Dhavde's wife Varsha went to the Pune ATS office on Wednesday and produced some documents. "Rakesh was not giving any kind of weapons training. He only used to give information on ancients weapons during open exhibitions," she said.

"Rakesh has a unique collection of weapons and we have the licences and the permission. I don't know how he was involved with the Malegaon blasts but I will support the police investigations," she added.

A team of Aurangabad police and Mumbai ATS officers were in Pune to probe terror links. The team interrogated senior Vishwa Hindu Parishad leaders in Pune in connection with Malegaon blasts and weapon training received by members of some radical Hindu outfits.

Heading: Way to GO-Bama! - Indian Express
Content:
For the 100-odd Americans in permanent residence in Pune, the general feeling is that the winds of change have started to blow the right way.

Barack Obama's win is a defeat not only for the Republican Party but also for all racial prejudices, said Arthur Mauser (45), an engineer who works for Suzlon. He feels there is now a new hope for change and prosperity.

Mauser, who has been in the city for three months now, said that he did not vote this year as he was traveling but everyone in his family in Ohio voted for Obama. "The victory of Obama is a proud moment for all of usWe are looking up to him as a man of potential who has the knack of making and executing the right decisions."

He praised Obama's emphasis on health issues. "There are many Americans who still don't have a health insurance; all of them would get one now!"

Architect Christopher Benninger, of Christopher Charles Benninger Architects Pvt Ltd, who has been in Pune since 1971, was another American who could not vote this year. Yet he too is celebrating.

"I have been following the results since morning. There are around 100 Americans with a permanent address in Pune, but I am in contact with only one. I can't have a get-together but will celebrate the victory with my friend. After eight years of a deceitful Presidency, we feel we are getting a straight-shooting, honest man in the White House. We are looking forward to a leadership not beholden to special interests like oil and Wall Street, but a leadership loyal to all the people of America," said Benninger (66).

"America needs to understand that we share this planet as one house, and must live in it like a Hindu undivided family. Openness, transparency and a process of change toward honesty is the promise that Obama has held out to us and we believe in him," he added.

Saith Sood, a medical researcher who earlier worked with WHO, said her brother had voted for Obama. Sood (7) had come to Pune from California in 1963.

Pam Stacey, who has been a member of the WIN club that works with expatriates, said, "Although I do not agree with Obama on some of the political issues he advocates, I feel he will make a great leader."

Heading: Modi to give Africa tour a miss for election campaign - Indian Express
Content:
African Siddi community in Gujarat celebrates Barack Obama's win in the US Presidential elections

We are proud of Barack Obama! An African winning in a discerning society of USA is a major victory for our tribe. I would like to congratulate him on behalf of the entire Siddi community of Ahmedabad. We kept watching the TV continuously till the results were announced," said a visibly happy Siddi Rumana Myawar, a Siddi residing in Pathar Kuva area of Ahmedabad.

Obama's victory in the US Presidential elections has brought a new ray of hope to the Siddi community in Ahmedabad. Siddis, also known as Habshis, originally belonged to the Bantu-speaking parts of eastern Africa. They were brought to Gujarat in the mid-15th century as slaves by the Arab and Portuguese traders. Later, they adopted Gujarat as their home state and even the Gujarati language, but with a distinct dialect.

In medieval times, they had a reputation as sturdy warriors and entered service of the Muslim kings. The 17th century saw Siddis enter India in large numbers. Later, they joined the Mughals in the latter's struggle with the Marathas.

Interestingly, the Siddis have still not discarded their native African customs. They reside in Ahmedabad as well as in Saurashtra in Gujarat. With their distinctive African appearance, the Siddis in Gujarat have been fighting both poverty and illiteracy in their bid to retain their unique customs. But on Tuesday, it was celebration time. The Pathar Kurva area in Ahmedabad, where the community resides together, was the scene of distinctive Siddi dance and music. Obama's victory apparently became their victory.

The Siddis in Ahmedabad celebrated the victory by organising a cultural festival, where they performed their traditional dance called Siddi Gaur or Siddi Dhamal, and the happiness of the people knew no bounds.

"He is our man. And we are sure that he will do a great deal for our community. We do aspire to join politics, but as we are overlooked by the government and struggle to make both ends meet, it appears as a distant dream. But we want to do something good for the betterment of our community," said Siddi Sikandar Mustafa.

"The change has come," said Obama to the media on his victory. The words transcended boundaries and echoed among the Siddis in Ahmedabad. They have pined their hopes on Obama to encourage and uplift their community in India.

According to them, it is the Indians in the US and India who supported Obama. And now, they hope that the Indian government would give some importance to Obama's people residing in various parts of the country.

A majority of the Siddis in Ahmedabad are engaged in small-time work with limited wages. They earn money by performing their tribal dance on festivals and other occasions. The education level among them is also low. The womenfolk are engaged in housekeeping and very few are literate.

"We want to come to the mainstream of society. We want some encouragement from the government. The authorities should give some scholarships and other benefits to our community also. We are totally abandoned, as we are outsiders for the government. With Obama winning the election, I am sure the government will start doing something for us," said Siddi Farzana Kamru.

"If not much, I feel he will do at least something for the Siddis in India. He is a youth icon and so he should encourage youth participation in industries and politics. We also want to become successful like him, if not a President than at least have a decent job and a good name in the society," said Nasreen Siddi.

They are not just excited but also worried about their fellow people in East Africa. With increasing number of criminal activities and terrorist attacks, they hope for a better security scenario in their native land.

"Obama has strong views on terrorism. I believe he will make all efforts to stop cross border violence. He should also work to bring more security to the eastern coast of Africa, especially Somalia. We hope that he will bring about the changes that all of us are eagerly waiting for," Sikandar added.

Heading: Modasa blast: DGP says no clean chit given to Sadhvi Pragya - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi will not go to South Africa, Uganda and Kenya to campaign for the Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit, scheduled in January 2009. For, the central BJP leadership wants him to campaign in the states where assembly elections will be held in November and December.

Sources in the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) confirmed on Wednesday that Modi was compelled to defer his plans to visit South Africa, Uganda and Kenya between November 16 and 25. They said he will be required to campaign for his party candidates in the impending assembly polls to be held in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Delhi and Jammu and Kashmir.

Since the schedule of his poll campaign in these states will clash with the dates of his visit to the African countries, there was no other option left for him but to postpone the tour, sources said.

"Now, only a team of senior bureaucrats will participate in roadshows to be organised in the African countries as part of an exercise to attract investments ahead of the Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit," sources added.

A senior BJP functionary said Modi will begin his poll campaign tour from Chhattisgarh on Saturday. After his two-day stay in the state, he will campaign for the party nominees in neighbouring Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. After a short break, he will move to Delhi to address election meetings.

The BJP functionary added that Modi, whose popularity chart has been growing especially after he brought the Nano car project to Gujarat, was expected to draw huge crowds at a series of public meetings he is scheduled to address in the poll-bound states over the next few days.

Besides the issue of terrorism, Modi will use development as a poll plank during the poll campaign in these states.

"Our party expects a good turnout at Modi's election meetings particularly in the BJP-ruled states of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh", said the BJP functionary.

Heading: Education Mobile Bus to offer  kids free ride on learning curve - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Director General of Police P C Pande has said the state police have not given any clean chit to Sadhvi Pragya Singh in the Modasa blast case.

Earlier, the Sabarkantha police, which is investigating the case, had interrogated Pragya and a few others accused in the Malegaon blast case, and said they were not involved in the September 29 blast at Modasa. But on Tuesday, Pande, while inaugurating four police stations in Surat, said that investigations were on and Pragya's role was being probed.

"The case is still under investigation. We are searching for clues against her (Pragya) and if her involvement is found in the Modasa blast, we will definitely grill her," Pande told reporters at Khatodara police station. He added: "We are in contact with the Mumbai police's ATS team. If we get some clue against her, we will take strict actions."

Pande said that Gujarat Police's functioning was being appreciated in other states, adding that the Karnataka Home Minister and DGP recently visited Gujarat to study the their work pattern. He said the visiting officials were surprised at the speed with which the Gujarat Police had cracked the Ahmedabad blasts case and the plantation of bombs in Surat. He said that a team of the Gujarat Police and Forensic Science officials are assisting the Assam Police to crack the recent serial blasts there.

Heading: State’s three biggest industries feel meltdown heat - Indian Express
Content:
Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) will be starting the first-ever Education Mobile Bus from November 15 to reach out to kids who have never been to school. It will start off initially as a pilot project for six months until April 30, 2009. The extension of the project will be decided later.

The project is a collaboration of the AMC, City Primary Education Committee (CPEC) and Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Service (AMTS) under the guidelines of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.

AMC has identified 140 children aged between six and 14 from the Gomtipur and Rajpur wards in the city, who have never been to school.

"We got the approval for this pilot project from our standing committee last week, and with the help of AMTS and CPEC. We will begin around November 15," said Lagdhir Desai, Administrative Officer, School Board, AMC. He further said, "In this education bus, apart from education we will be providing health kits to the kids. As promised by IP Gautam, Municipal Commissioner, we will be getting one AMTS bus free of charge. The salary of driver and fuel expenses will be borne by AMTS."

Under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), six teachers will be appointed on a pay of Rs 1,500 per month, Desai said. These teachers have already been given 60 days training for the purpose.

"After the successful completion of this project, these children will be transferred to AMC schools. Every student will appear in an examination and later absorbed in schools on the basis of the scores they obtain," said Desai.

After getting feedback from the teachers and evaluating the performance of the kids, the project will be taken to the next level and more wards and children will be identified, said Desai, who expressed hope that the project will be a success.

Heading: Ghalib Award conferred on veteran master of Urdu verse - Indian Express
Content:
Chandu Vaghasia, a 22-year-old youth from Amreli, has been desperately waiting for a call from his diamond unit employer in Surat, as this year, Diwali vacation has been longer than the usual 20 days. Moreover, uncertainty looms large over the re-opening of the diamond polishing unit where he works.
The worries of Manoj Chand, a labourer at a brass parts manufacturing unit in Jamnagar, are no different. He too fears losing his job. The unit where he works was supposed to reopen on Monday, after a week-long Diwali vacation. But even on Wednesday his employer did not intimate him when the operations would resume.

The three biggest industries in Gujarat — diamond polishing, brass parts and steel recycling — have been hit badly in the ripple effect of the global meltdown.

Decline in export and fluctuating raw material prices have taken direct toll on the manufacture of goods and their export order, putting a question mark on the employment of nearly 12 lakh labourers.

Over 10 lakh workers are employed in the diamond industry as polishers, 1.5 lakh are in the brass parts units in Jamnagar, and several thousands work at the Alang Breaking Yard and re-rolling mills in Bhavnagar.

In the last one month, rough diamond, steel and brass have registered drastic reduction in their prices in the international market. Furthermore, there has been a sharp decline in the demand for finished goods and scrap for steel.

"The price of rough diamond has hit a dramatic low. Many traders who had kept huge stocks of rough diamond bought at higher rates, are now finding it difficult to sell them at its original price, leave alone making a profit," said Chuni Patel, one of the biggest traders in Gujarat with polishing units in Surat and Amreli and offices in the US, Europe and Hong Kong.

He said, "It's not decided when the units will start functioning as usual." Even if the units re-open, he said, they would not function in full scale, which means that not all workers will get the call to resume work.

Worst hit are the small-scale units. Of the 8,000-odd units in Surat, Ahmedabad, Bhavnagar, Amreli and Rajkot, 5,000 fall in this category.

"We have been asked to stay back at Amreli until the next call from Surat," said Vaghasia. For him, this means a loss of Rs 200-300 per day.

The Factory Owners Association in Jamnagar has scheduled a meeting on Thursday to decide a course of action. "Brass prices in the international market have dipped to Rs 190 per kg from Rs 260 within a month. Now, the orders placed earlier have no takers," said Bharat Dodiya, secretary FOA, Jamnagar.

Fall in the prices of steel in the international market has turned Alang and Bhavnagar into a steel scrap storage area. From 650 dollars per ton, steel prices have come down to 300 dollars.

Financial crisis takes life of another trader
Express News Service
Ahmedabad, November 5
IN YET another incident of suicide owing to financial crisis, a 41-year-old debt-ridden businessman of Naranpura area hanged himself from a hook on the kitchen ceiling on Wednesday morning. Ghatlodia police have registered a case of accidental death.
Kalpresh Surti, a resident of Uday Apartment near Naranpura Telephone Exchange, had a wholesale shop of 'puja' items in the Manekchowk area of the city under the banner of Jashwantlal Hiralal Surti, the police said.
He is survived by wife Nila Surti, two sons and a daughter.
The police said that Nila found her husband hanging with a nylon string in the kitchen of her house around 5.30 am.
Head constable Jayanti Brahmbhatt, who is investigating the case, said: "Surti's business was not doing well for the last three years. Due to this, the family's financial condition had deteriorated. To meet household expenses, he had borrowed a lot of money on interest from different people."
Brahmbhatt said Surti had sold off his wife's ornaments, but still was unable to come out of the debt. "His wife told us that their hopes to overcome debt during Diwali vanished after they failed to buy new items on credit. Customers did not want old items during the festival," Brahmbhatt said.
No suicide note was recovered from the house.

Heading: Gujarat 10th state with low infant mortality rate - Indian Express
Content:
Vo raat jis ki sahar main na dekh paoonga; Vo raat aaye to ghee ke diye jalaoonga. Vaqt aane par Alvi ek ghazal na keh paaye, Itne saal Ghalib ko padh ke tum ne kya paya Andhera hai kaise tera khat padhoon, Lifaafe mein kuchh roshni bhej de.

(The night that shall never see light When it comes, I shalt light a lamp If Alvi can't phrase a ghazal

What hast he learnt from Ghalib?

In darkness how can I read thy letter?

If thou dost not send light in the envelope?)

These delicately framed lines of verse belong to noted Urdu poet Mohammed Alvi. Born in Ahmedabad in 1927, Alvi has mastered Urdu poetry over a span of five decades. For his distinguished service to Urdu poetry, the Ghalib Institute, New Delhi, has conferred on him the prestigious Ghalib Award this year.

A meeting of the institute held on October 10 in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Saiyed Ameer Hasan Abidi decided the awardees for this year.

The award function is likely to be held in New Delhi in the second week of December with former prime minister I K Gujral as the chief guest, said Idris Ahmed, the Programme Officer of Ghalib Institute.

In the later part of the 20th century, Mohammed Alvi became a significant name in modern Urdu writing. He has four volumes of poetry and an anthology to his credit so far. A deceptively simplistic way of conveying complex sentiments in an innocent manner has been his forte and his style has not found a match so far. In fact, Alvi can be safely counted among top three living Urdu poets in the world.

In 1992, Alvi bagged the Sahitya Akademi Award for Urdu poetry. Shortly after that, he bagged the Gujarati Urdu Sahitya Academy Award, too. However, as he himself admits, despite being recognised as one of the most adored modernists in Urdu literary universe, awards and accolades came very late in his life. "But that reflects more on the credibility of those awards and not on my merit," he says.

The Ghalib Award carries a cash prize of Rs 50,000, a citation, a certificate and a memento. Earlier, renowned Urdu critic, Waris Alvi, had received this award in 2004.

Other recipients of the Ghalib Award are as follows: Sharib Rudaulvi (Lucknow) has been awarded the Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed Ghalib Award for research in Urdu, while Valiulhaq Ansari (Lucknow) has received the Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed Ghalib Award for research in Persian. Mughni Tabassum has been awarded for Urdu poetry. Sagar Sarhadi of Mumbai has won the Ham Sab Ghalib Award for Drama. The Ghalib Atlas Award for overall contribution to Urdu literature has gone to Marghoob Banihali of Srinagar. Balraj Varma has won the Ghalib Award for Urdu journalism.

Heading: July 26 blast: 7 IM men sent to police custody - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat ranks tenth in the country in terms of Infant Mortality Rate (IMR), barely making it to the list of top ten states that have fewer number of infant deaths per thousand live births.

As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) bulletin released by the Registrar General of India, for October 2008 the IMR for Gujarat stands at 52. The IMR for the male child is 50 and for the female child it is 54.

The SRS is a large-scale demographic survey for providing reliable annual estimates of birth rate, death rate and other fertility and mortality indicators at the national and sub-national levels.

Gujarat stands 10th amongst the 19 states classified as 'bigger states' by the annual survey conducted across the country by the central government.

States such as Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal have done better than Gujarat, with lesser infant deaths.

Gujarat's IMP, however, is better than the national average, which according to the SRS bulletin is 55 — male IMR being 55 and female 56.

Professor Dilip Mavlankar of the Indian Institute of Management here believes that the cause of higher infant mortality in Gujarat is due to neglect of health services by the state government over the years. "There has not been any specific governmental intervention to check high IMR in the state," he said.

"Though there is some improvement in the IMR and Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) figures, the fundamentals required for a public health system are not in place," he said.

He said there is a need for more child health officers in the state who can monitor childcare system and provide interventions based on the information collected from across the state.

Maharashtra has two doctors per primary health centre, but Gujarat still has only one. Also, there is no proper data collection mechanism for the number of infant deaths in the state," Mavlankar said, adding that the government is highly dependent on the health staff at the field level for collection of health related data.

Additional director, family welfare, Vikasben Desai also admitted that the government has been slow in planning intervention to bring down the IMR. "But now we have identified the areas and are concentrating on it to bring down IMR in the state," Desai said.

Heading: Congress accuses state government of not allotting forest land to adivasis - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court, hearing the July 26 blast case, on Wednesday sent seven members of Indian Mujahideen to police remand till November 14.

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) produced the seven before justice G M Patel after bringing them to the city from Mumbai on transfer warrant on Tuesday.

The accused were identified as Afzal alias Afsar Usmani, Mohammed Sadiq Israr Ahmed Shaikh (both from Mumbai), Mohammad Jakir Abdul Haque Shaikh, Mohammed Arif alias Ladan Badruddin Shaikh (both from Thane), Asif Basiruddin Shaikh, Mubin alias Salman alias Sallu Qadar Shaikh and Mohammed Mansur Asgar Peerbhoy (all from Pune).

The Mumbai ATS had arrested them on charges of sending terror e-mails before and after the July 26 blasts in Ahmedabad.

Heading: Promotions made easy for govt education staff - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee (GPCC) on Wednesday accused the state government of not taking adequate steps to allot forest land to adivasis as per recommendations of the central government, while it held weekly meetings to decide about land allotment to industrialists.

GPCC chief spokesperson Arjunbhai Modhwadia said that by not taking effective steps to allot jungle land to adivasis, the state government has hinted at a design to keep adivasis backward and poor.

In a statement, he said that as many as 75,000 adivasis were entitled to jungle land under the Forest Rights Act 2006 enacted by the UPA government at the Centre.

But while the state government was busy allotting free-of-charge land to industrialists without following legal and administrative procedures, he said that not an inch of land under the act was allotted to adivasis.

Modhwadia said that the BJP had announced a Rs 15,000 crore plan for development of adivasi areas on the eve of December 2007 elections.

"But where are the development projects under the scheme in adivasi areas?" he asked.

Heading: All schools to re-open on November 17 - Indian Express
Content:
Now senior employees need not obtain CCC+ certificate made mandatory earlier

The Class one and two government employees working in education institutes now need not obtain the certificate of Course of Computer Concept Plus (CCC+) for promotions. They will be eligible for promotion by obtaining just the certificate of Course of Computer Concept (CCC).

The Gujarat government decision will help several senior employees in education department whose promotions and salary appraisals are pending for long.

"Now, Class one and two employees need to obtain CCC certificate which will be very easy for them," said a senior Gujarat government official.

A few years back, the state finance department had asked the government employees working in education institutes to obtain CCC+ certificates for being eligible for promotions. The decision was taken in view of the employees' salary scales.

"By mistake, they considered teachers, professors and principals into Class one and Class two categories, instead of Class three. Because of that they were required to obtain CCC+ certificate which was not easy for them," said a senior official from the state finance department, Gujarat Government on the condition of anonymity.

Secretary, Gujarat State Secondary Teachers Association, Ramesh Patel, said, "Because of the mistake done by the state finance department thousands of government employees working in education institutes had to suffer."

He said, "As instead of CCC certificate they were asked to obtain CCC+ certificates, these employees' promotions and salary appraisals were affected."

"Several employees who are on the verge of retirement have not been able to get promotions despite being eligible because of such policies," said Patel.

"Now, it will be easier for these employees to get promotion as they need not obtain CCC+ certificate and only CCC certificate will work for them," said RC Dave, a member of Gujarat State Secondary Teachers Association.

Heading: Diamond exporters happy at Obama’s win - Indian Express
Content:
The confusion over completion of Diwali vacation was cleared after a recent meeting between the trustees of non-granted private schools and Rajkot District Education Officer (DEO). In the meeting, it was decided that all the schools will reopen on November 17.

Earlier, over 450 private schools of Rajkot district had planned to reopen the schools one or two weeks before the date fixed by the DEO. After parents and some student bodies opposed the move, the education office instructed the private schools to follow the department's schedule.

However, many schools re-opened neglecting the DEO notice. But they were forced to close with the DEO issuing a warning to them following complaints received from NSUI members.

NSUI's Rajkot unit president Rajdeep Jadeja said: "We received complaints from some parents who could not dare to take up the issue before private schools' trustees. So, we had to ask the DEO to compel private schools follow the schedule set for all the schools."

This year, he added, the vacation started just a day before Diwali. "So, an early reopening of the schools could have disturbed the holiday plans of many families," he said.

Jadeja further said that realising the magnitude of the problem, the DEO convened the meeting of school trustees.

"However, on Wednesday some parents informed us that despite the DEO diktat, many schools reopened and hence we had to request the DEO to see that schools close down," he said.

Rajkot DEO KD Bagda said: "The trustees of all 450 self-finance schools have agreed to reopen their schools on November 17. But we gave relaxation to those schools who wanted to give coaching to SSC and HSC students."

He added: "I have asked all the schools to take prior permission of parents for carrying out this extra coaching."

Bagda said that after the NSUI complaint, he inquired and found that the schools were open to provide coaching to HSC students today.

"I have asked the school authorities to show me written permission of parents for this extra classes," he said.

He said the issue is over as all the 755 schools in the district, including 450 self-finance schools, have agreed to reopen on November 17.

Heading: Tutor held for ‘sexually exploiting’ 14-yr-old boy - Indian Express
Content:
They hope he will lift the four per cent import duty levied on diamonds

Gems and jewellery exporters in Surat have expressed happiness over Barack Obama's victory in the US presidential elections, as they expect him to take measures to boost the bilateral business in the years to come.

Sources in the industry said the imposition of 7 per cent import duty (which was later made 4 per cent) had affected the export business of gems and jewellery from India to the US. Some of its business was diverted to the Middle East and European countries.

Praveen Nanavati, convener of the Gem Jewellery Export Promotion Council, Gujarat, said: "I am seeing positive signs for the gem and jewellery industry over the victory of Obama. The diamond industry had been facing a slump in the recent years. Now, we feel it would become stable in the coming months."

Gem and jewellery exporter Chandrakant Sanghvi said: "Obama likes India and Indians. He also understands the diamond industry well. We expect his coming to power will be good for the industry as the US holds 55 per cent of the diamond market in the world."

"We believe Obama will lift the import duty of 4 per cent on diamonds and jewellery business. This will also play a role in strengthening the US economy," he said.

Another exporter Kirti Shah said: "The diamond industry, which is labour-oriented in India, is facing a great meltdown this year. Earlier, Diwali vacation used to be of 30 days. This year, it has been extended to 60 days. Lakhs of diamond polishers have become jobless in the last two months."

Shah said Obama's victory is likely to prove favourable for the industry as India exports most of its diamonds and jewellery to the US.

Heading: Rare collection of historical literature destroyed in Ajit Niwas Palace fire - Indian Express
Content:
The Sarkhej police arrested a private tutor for allegedly sexually exploiting his 14-year-old boy student, on Wednesday.

The arrest was made after the boy's father lodged a complaint with the police in this regard, wherein he has named Bharat Makwana, a resident of Fatewadi in Sarkhej, as the accused. Makwana runs a private coaching institute in the Sarkhej area under the banner of Suvidha Classes.

The boy's father told Newsline: "As my son will appear in Class X board exams this year, I had hired Bharat Makwana to personally teach him. On Tuesday, he took my son to his institute near Sarkhej railway station. He gave him some vulgar book to read and then tried to sexually exploit him. My son somehow managed to escape and rushed back home."

The boy informed his father about the incident, who lodged the police complaint. Makwana, however, was unaware of the development and came to teach the boy at his home on Wednesday and again asked him to go to the coaching class. At this moment, the boy's father nabbed the teacher and handed him to the police. The police said that investigations are on.

Heading: African students at MSU celebrate the victory - Indian Express
Content:
An entire collection of rare historical books and some records of the erstwhile Dhrangadhra state are feared to have gutted in fire that broke out at Ajit Niwas Palace in Dhrangadhra of Surendranagar district on Tuesday night.

A short circuit is believed to be the cause of the fire, according to the Dhrangadhra city police.

The police said it was a major fire and Army jawans were pressed into service along with the local fire brigade to douse the flames.

"It took them more than seven hours to bring the fire under control," said Yogesh Shah, Dhrangadhra Municipality Chief Officer.

According to a complaint lodged by Girish Vaghela, caretaker of the palace,

rare collections of literature and records related to the erstwhile state have reduced to ashes in the fire that broke out in the library adjacent to the main palace building.

Nearly 100-year-old furniture also reportedly gutted in the incident.

The heir of the royal family Shri Ram Meghraji and his younger brother Siddhrajsinhji stay at the century-old palace with their families.

Heading: Obama win brings new hope for ‘sceptical’ industry captains - Indian Express
Content:
AS Barak Obama became the first African-American president elect of the US on Tuesday night, his Kenyan roots set off celebrations among the African students at M S University (MSU).

Kenyan students along with other African students rejoiced Obama's historic victory as his father belongs to Kenya. "America has always been helpful to Kenya whether it is a natural calamity or any manmade disaster," said Jac Kihiko (27), who belongs to Kenyan capital Nairobi.

Kihiko, who is doing research in Applied Physics, added: "As soon as the poll results came last night, we celebrated and congratulated ourselves. Currently, there are more than 10 students from Kenya studying here."

It is not only Kenya, other African countries will also witness a change in the bilateral relations with the election of Obama, said Kihiko. "In 1995 when Kenya witnessed major bomb blasts, it got the maximum support from America. Now, we are hopeful of an even better relationship," he added.

Srida Malandi, an Arts student, said, "With his roots attached to Kenya, Obama will be able to strike the correct chord, which will lead to a better relationship between the two countries."

As a member of the Democratic minority in the 109th Congress, Obama had made official trips to Africa, Eastern Europe, and the Middle East.

Heading: Toast of Kolkata - Indian Express
Content:
Barack Obama winning the race for the White House has evoked hope among the captains of Gujarat's industry and commerce. They feel that despite his known stand against outsourcing, things after all would not turn out as bad as being feared all along.

Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GCCI) members said the industry will be able to concentrate on business instead of worrying over terror attacks. The Chamber is now critical of the Bush regime's hot pursuit of Iraq and attack on that country in search of weapons of mass destruction.

"We welcome Obama and believe it is important to directly attack Al-Qaeda and other terror outfits. If he adopts right policies on terrorism, we can concentrate on business," said GCCI president Rupesh Shah.

He added that the policies of the Bush Administration had pushed the world to the brink of an economic disaster.

CII Gujarat Council hailed Obama's victory as a positive signal to the world.

Asked if his stand against outsourcing would impact India's business with the US, its chairman

Vimal Ambani said it would not have a major impact "because there is a dearth of software professionals in the US".

Pointing out that opposing outsourcing and completely rejecting it are two different things, he said,

"India's outsourcing business would go on as usual."

Ambani said the development would change the way the US looked at the world and vice-versa. For Obama, it would be a long drawn process and an uphill task to put the US economy back on track.

Nirav Shah, president of Gujarat Electronics and Software Industries Association (GESIA), admitted to the fact that the software industry is a bit apprehensive about the future of outsourcing.

"People are jittery here. But outsourcing is a part of business and no industry can afford to lose cost effectiveness, they have to retain it. But still we feel the new regime will come with certain restrictions and regulations or some changes in policy on outsourcing," said Shah.

Shah went on to say that Gujarat had a wide gap to fill as far as outsourcing business is concerned. It has a small part in India's 70 per cent share in outsourcing from the US, he said.

Indian Drug Manufacturer Association (IDMA) is worried over the liquidity problem, which, according to its executive secretary R S Joshi, is felt everywhere.

"Gujarat and Maharashtra drug industries have no problem about quality. They are rated high by the US agencies. But our main concern is liquidity. We hope the regime change will bring about some positive changes in the liquidity crisis," he said.

Heading: Rizwanur case: Bail to top cops challenged - Indian Express
Content:
Black man in White House, I am happy: CM

As the Americans had their adrenal oozing during US presidential election results, a mock debate and polling conducted by the American Center in Kolkata had predicted Democrat Barack Obama bagging the White House even before the actual results were out.

The victory of Obama has drawn many praises. Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee said: "It is a good news that for the first time a black President will enter the White House. I am happy."

Director of the American Center, Douglas Kelly said: "Before the US polls declared Obama as the President, we conducted mock debates and voting, which spelt a clear victory for the Democrat."

Nearly 500 enthusiasts gathered early morning in Park Hotel on November 5 to watch the presidential election live. The poll results were tracked on television in an open-to-all event organised by the Center, which also asked the visitors to cast their mock votes.

Much before the verdict in US, results of the mock votes showed Obama as the winner with 154 votes against 45 votes in the favour of Republican candidate John McCain.

Draped in red, white and blue colours of the US flag, the venue saw life-size cutouts of the two candidates with their symbols of donkey and elephant, making the morning memorable. The event saw several foreigners residing in Kolkata and American students studying in the city.

"Once, we had shown the elections live but it was within the premises of the US consulate. This time we decided to do it big as we wanted to attract more people with this year's elections being a historic one," said Kelly.

"It is the first time that an Afro-American candidate was running for the Presidential post along with a woman running for Vice-Presidential elections," he added.

Earlier, an all-student mock debate organised by the American Center in the city on October 31 had hinted the preference of Kolkatans for Obama. Institutes like Presidency College, St Xavier's College, Loreto College, Bhowanipore Education Society and Calcutta International School participated in the debate, which saw Obama leading with 42 votes against 22 of McCain's.

This was the first such mock debate in nearly three decades. In 1980, the Center had held a similar debate ahead of the Presidential elections that had Democrat Jimmy Carter pitted against Republican Ronald Reagan, who had eventually won.

"The election results show that any person from any background can aspire to hold the highest office in the US," said Kelly. "I am glad that Obama won. He made history," said Simon Johnson, regional director, Western Australia trade office.

Heading: Buddha insists on new mining technology - Indian Express
Content:
The interim bail granted by the sessions court to the three police officers accused in Rizwanur Rehman case was challenged before the Kolkata High Court on Wednesday.

Counsel of the Rehman family, Kalyan Banerjee challenged the order of the sessions court that a magistrate can not dispose of a bail petition after granting an interim bail to the police officers. The order passed by the sessions court was not valid, he said.

Rukbanur Rehman, brother of Rizwanur Rehman, had filed a petition in the Calcutta High Court seeking cancellation of the interim bail. The accused police officers, former Deputy Commissioner (Detective Department) Ajay Kumar, Assistant Commissioner Sukanti Chakraborty and Sub-Inspector Krishnendu Das, had surrendered before the CBI court on September 30 and the court had remanded them in police custody. But the next day, the sessions court had granted them an interim bail.

On Wednesday, Banerjee pleaded before a Division Bench of the HC that the sessions court magistrate had granted the interim bail without going through the case diary. The magistrate should have fixed another date to hear the case but he disposed of the case. As a result the three police officers were released for an indefinite period, said Banerjee.

He, hence, pleaded that the Bench should cancel the interim bail.

Banerjee also pointed out that while Pappu, another accused in the case, was remanded in jail custody by the CBI court but the three police officers were released on bail.

Counsel of Ajay Kumar, Shekhar Bose pleaded that there was no ground to cancel the interim bail. He said Kumar had not intervened in the probe conducted by the CBI and the agency had not arrested him during the investigation.

Bose contended that the CBI had no right to demand the custody of his client after filing the chargesheet. Bose contended that Kumar had followed the court's order after the bail was granted by the sessions court.

Next hearing is fixed for November 11.

Heading: Government will now filter disease data - Indian Express
Content:
ninth four-day International Mining and Machinery Exhibition 2008

With the rising demand of coal in the country, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee insists that the mining sector uses new technology and innovative scientific measures to use the coal seams at greater depths.

At the ninth four-day International Mining and Machinery Exhibition (IMME) 2008, inaugurated in the city on Wednesday, the chief minister stressed that instead of mining the coal seams directly, new technologies might be introduced to extract the combustible gases present in coal, which could be used

as fuel or feedstock for chemicals.

"We have huge coal reserves in the state, which ranks fourth amongst the coal-bearing states of the country. There is, however, a need for augmentation of coal reserves in the state," said Bhattacharjee.

At present, there are five coal companies engaged in coal production in the state. Despite the West Bengal Mineral Development and Trading Corporation being allotted six coal blocks where pre-mining activities have commenced, Bhattacharjee claims that new coal blocks need to be allocated by the Union Ministry of Coal.

Organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry in association with the Ministry of Mines and Coal and Cola India Limited, the exhibition saw the participation of both domestic and international players.

Spread over an area of 50,000 sq m, with over 300 exhibitors from 15 countries, the exhibition has a 60 per cent presence of international players.

Germany — partner country at IMME this year — is expected to put up the largest ever exposition of latest equipment and engineering technologies for the mining sector.

Apart from Germany, the exhibition will witness participation from China, Canada, Greece, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, Poland, Singapore, Sweden, UK, Ukraine and US, among a host of others.

While special focus will be on mining construction, material handling and mineral processes, a number of new products for the mining construction and mineral processing sector will be launched during the exhibition.

"It is a challenge for the mining industry of our country to implement suitable technology so that deep-seated coal deposits can be exploited. The coalfields of Raniganj are predominantly deep-seated mostly exploitable by underground method but past performance of underground mining in India is rather poor," said Bhattacharjee.

Besides the exhibition, a Global Mining Summit, which will have 350 delegates, will also be held concurrently with the IMME. In addition, a buyer-seller meet has also been planned for manufactures and service providers to interact with potential buyers in the mining sector.

Heading: Bhuniya demands CBI inquiry into blast - Indian Express
Content:
In face of rising public indignation about the spread of vector-borne diseases, the Left Front government has officially asked the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) to hold back all data.

"Any information related to vector-borne diseases now will be provided by the information department of the state government as it has been asked by the state authorities," said Deb Dwaipayan Chattopadhyay, Chief Health Municipal Officer (CMHO).
