Party leaders said the move aimed to end any speculation about Raja Ram's possible appointment as the president.

At present, he is the party in-charge of Madhya Pradesh and his term as a member of the legislative council in UP expires in January.

Eight candidates from the state have so far filed their nominations for the RS polls. Samajwadi Party general secretaries Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav had submitted their papers on Thursday.

BJP candidate Kusum Rai is likely to file her nomination on November 10, the last day of filing the papers.

The deadlock within the Congress over the selection of the candidates, meanwhile, continued. Congress has 21 members in the state Assembly and will need 16 surplus votes of the Samajwadi Party. The SP, however, expects that the Congress support its third candidate.

The SP and the Congress sources indicated that the issue is likely to be resolved before next Monday.

Heading: Veryfilmy - Indian Express
Content: Healthy Hearing, Opening Eyes and Special Smiles. These are names of functions in a two-day programme being held on Saturday and Sunday under the aegis of Bharat Uttar Pradesh unit of Special Olympics, an organisation dedicated to bringing about improvement among mentally  children/persons through the discipline of sports. "With an eye on the next Special Olympics, we are holding an event in which athletic and sport events would be held," informed Rajeev Prasad, Coordinator-Healthy Athletes. "In between the sports events, a team of health experts will examine the participants for their hearing, sight and oral hygiene/health," he added. Children from various schools would attend the event to be held in the AMC Central School Stadium and would be familiarised with the special needs of the participants.

Heading: On HIV crusade, Gates takes in city - Indian Express
Content:
Perfect Bebo
It takes quite something to impress perfectionist Aamir Khan. So we understand how fit Kareena Kapoor actually is when Aamir compliments her on her great body. Bebo, who is a fitness freak, left quite an impact on Aamir with her well-toned body and her devotion to her workouts. He was also impressed by her professionalism as she shot in Ladakh's cold climate without a single complaint. The two stars are working together on Raju Hirani's Three Idiots. This is their first film together and unit members are already talking about how well the two have hit it off with each other.

Salman on a roll
SALMAN Khan was quite the charmer on the sets of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2009, where he appeared with the current love of his life, Katrina Kaif. The picture perfect couple appeared as an 'item' for the first time on Indian television and made everyone's day as they waltzed together to the song Teri Ore, from Kat's hit movie Singh is Kinng. But the star of the day was Khan, who was at his flamboyant best, dancing with the contestants, playing cupid between them.

Popcorn break
Himesh Reshammiya may have gotten tired of living on tandoori food but he ain't giving up his diet just yet. The actor, who lost over eight kilos for his recent release, Karzzzz, is working hard towards maintaining his physique. The singer-music-director-actor was seen munching on popcorn during the shoot of a popular reality show. Every time the camera was not on him, Reshammiya would get up from his seat and start hogging on the tub of munchies placed right next to him. The Bollywood hunks need to watchout — Reshammiya could just be the next six-pack guy.

Heading: Who’s that? Some Gate... Colgate, guesses crowd - Indian Express
Content:
Manju Kamble possibly did not realise the significance of the visit she was being paid on Thursday afternoon. She shyly offered tea and water to the third richest man in the world and then settled herself at the window of her kitchen. When her visitor left after spending ten minutes at her one-room home, she waved goodbye.

Manju Kamble (40) has been a sex worker for years. Her visitor was Bill Gates, Microsoft founder, who was in Pune on Thursday. Among the questions Gates asked her was, "How many clients do you get everyday? Do you use condoms?"

Manju and her housemates had a few clients a day, a translator informed Gates, assuring him about the use of condoms. Each client pays us Rs 60 or Rs 70, said Gauri (name changed), who like Manju has sent her two children to a village in Karnataka. Business is not always good, the women grumbled, sometimes as low as one or two clients a day.

Gates is carrying out a crusade against HIV. He was on a "personal learning visit" planned by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

It was a tightly packed schedule, with television and newspaper journalists turning up in huge numbers and occupying vantage positions at different locations for a photo-op and some sound byte.

For Gates, however, it was a purely personal visit that was not to be affected by the huge media presence. His guards ensured that Gates, his father and two sisters were not shoved and pushed by the huge crowd that surrounded the two Mercedez Benz cars that pulled into the narrow lanes of Budhwar Peth, where Gates interacted with the commercial sex workers at Manju Kamble's house.

Gates and his family also visited the Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) project of Vanchit Vikas, a clinic funded by the foundation, on his hour-long visit to Budhwar Peth. According to Darshana Vyas, project director of Pathfinder International, an NGO whose 'Mukta' project works in ten districts in the state to reduce the prevalence of STIs, Gates seemed to be happy with the work at the clinic.

Meena Kurlekar, director of the Vanchit Vikas project, said that the foundation has provided funds for the last three years and helped them reach out to over 4,000 commercial sex workers. "We have 35 to 40 women visiting our clinic daily and the level of STI infection has considerably reduced among them," Kurlekar said.

Gates refused to answer queries by The Indian Express. A press release stated that Bill Gates and his family were on a personal visit to India and though they may visit foundation grantees and other partners, they would not provide details about their plans.

Heading: Forging CM’s signature, to settle a score... - Indian Express
Content:
"Arre kaun aaya? Shahrukh Khan aaya kya? Arre nahi koi Gate — Colgate aaya."

Several residents of Budhwar Peth had never heard of Bill Gates and wondered what the fuss was all about when he came calling. The world's third richest man was taking stock of the progress of HIV prevention projects funded by the Bill and Melinda Gates foundation at Budhwar Peth.

With three hefty bodyguards scouting the lanes, a large media presence presented no obstacle to Gates. After The Indian Express had reported his plans to visit Budhwar Peth, his security personnel positioned themselves at Shukrawar Peth police chowky and were on their toes for the full hour that he was in Budhwar Peth.

The security personnel formed a small human chain to ensure that Gates, accompanied by his father and sisters, briskly walked to the brothel and back to their car. Their two Mercedez Benz cars blocked a sizable part of the lane at Budhwar Peth and traffic too came to a standstill till the police dispersed the crowd and restored some order. For onlookers who were unaware initially that Gates was in town, news reached them that the "computer guy" was visiting commercial sex workers and the crowd swelled around Vanchit Vikas Clinic at Budhwar Peth. Their efforts to meet him, however, went in vain; a local corporator who wanted to felicitate Gates had to back off too.

Journalists had a trying time. From 10 am, television reporters and photographers had parked themselves at vantage points at Budhwar Peth, but it was not till 2 pm that Gates turned up. He left after an hour. Some were at the Rameshwar market in the infamous Vaishya Galli, while others had set up their cameras and were ready for action at the Vanchit Vikas office. Gates did not respond. Later, the media was given a statement that it was a personal visit of the Gates family.

Heading: Rs 40-lakh subsidy: probe to find where money went - Indian Express
Content:
A 50-year-old man used forged rubberstamps and signatures of Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil to set the police behind his enemies.

The Crime Branch of Pune on Wednesday raided Sunil Jayant Pawar's house at Katraj for sending a forged letter to the cops. Forged letterheads and rubber stamps of the chief minister, deputy chief minister and other ministers and MLAs, including state Energy Minister Dilip Walse Patil and MLA Vilas Lande were seized. Police also got their hands on a dairy in which Sunil appears to have practised forging the signatures, some envelopes of government offices, letterheads of the Mantralaya and a letterhead of late minister Vasantrao Chavan.

What set the police on his trail was a letter received on October 27 at the police commissionerate with the CM and DCM's forged signatures. The letter stated that one Kamrunissa Shaikh belonging to Social Forum of Minorities had named two residents of upper Indira Nagar, Anil Kamble and Tukaram Kamble (they were named as accomplices of a deceased criminal Robert Salve) as members of the banned SIMI. The letter asked for a probe against the two.

Crime Branch initiated investigations during which sub-inspector Y K Nalawade found the Kambles to be auto-rickshaw drivers. As for Kamrunisaa Shaikh, he was nowhere to be found. Smelling a rat, the crime branch made a sketch based on the description of the person who had handed over the letter. From the sketch, the Kamble brothers identified him as Sunil.

It came to light that settling a personal score was the motive. The Kambles told police that they had a fight with Pawar over a financial dispute. They told police that Sunil had taken a bank loan of Rs 90,000 for which Kamble's father, Narayan, a government employee, had stood guarantor. After Sunil failed to repay the loan and the money was being deducted from Narayan's account, the dispute began.

Investigations confirmed that it was Sunil who had indeed submitted the letter at the police commissionerate.

Sunil was reported to be a historysheeter with complaints of cheating registered against him at Panvel, Vishrambaug and Bharato Vidyapeeth police stations.

Pawar was produced in court and remanded in police custody till November 13.

Heading: ...meanwhile, cops book man who exposed fake ration card scam - Indian Express
Content:
Following allegations by MPs and MLCs in the district that the subsidy of Rs 2,500 each for 1,600 farmers announced by the government had not been disbursed, District Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar has demanded an inquiry by the state agriculture commissioner.

Under the scheme, around Rs 40 lakh was earmarked to be disbursed to farmers to enable them to construct independent vermicompost units in their farms. For that, 1,600 farmers were shortlisted in the district.

But at a recent meeting of the District Planning and Development Committee (DPDC), former MP Sambhaji Kunjir alleged that a survey conducted in the district showed that none of the farmers had got the one-time subsidy.

"It is on paper but has not been implemented (on the ground)," he said. "I have proof and details that none of the farmers have got any benefits," he said showing the list of farmers who were to be covered under the scheme.

Farmers from Haveli, Bhor, Mulshi, Baramati and Indapur had not received any money, he said showing the list.

"There is no use of a scheme is it's not implemented in letter and spirit," he said. The scheme was to be implemented during 2007-08 but it had not been done, he said. He added that he had sought information on the scheme under RTI as well but got incomplete answers.

A farmer from Bhor, when contacted, said he had applied for the subsidy but no money had been paid to him though he had spent Rs 10,000 constructing the vermicompost pit. Kunjir said there were many such cases of which he had compiled a list.

District superintending regional officer Ravindra Bhosale refuted the allegations. He told The Indian Express that according to rules they were to provide 25 per cent of the cost of the vermicompost pit or Rs 2,500, whichever was lesser. "We also provided farmers with farm-based manure units with some of the amount as we were given the option of giving the subsidy in cash or in kind. We disbursed the entire amount to 1,900 farmers instead of 1,600," he said.

"The entire Rs 40 lakh has been disbursed and farmers have also been given manure," he added. Agriculture commissioner Prabhakar Deshmukh, said he would start a probe and call for details if any discrepancy was detected. The Agriculture commissioner would himself head the probe.

Heading: Discounts galore but no spark in electronics goods sales this Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
In a new twist in much-publicised case of a fake ration card issued in the name of Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, the Nigdi police have booked Anand Madhavrao More, assistant zonal officer at Nigdi rationing office.The ration card had been issued to a Dehu Road resident, Sanjay Dhutadmal, in August last.

Police have also booked Dhutadmal for taking up the issue with mediapersons, thus causing defamation of the state government. Dhutadmal had procured the ration card in the name of the chief minister and his family members on August 9 by allegedly paying a bribe of Rs 2,000. On September 17, he took up the issue with Divisional Commissioner Nitin Kareer and shared the details with mediapersons.

Food and Civil Supplies Minister Sunil Tatkare had ordered a probe and More, along with a clerk, Vidya Gangale had been suspended. Now, zonal officer Vaishali Waghmare at Nigdi rationing office has lodged a complaint against More and Dhutadmal.

When contacted, Dhutadmal said, "I procured the card in the name of Vilasrao Deshmukh and produced it before the mediapersons for exposing the bogus ration card racket." He alleged that Waghmare too was also involved in the racket. "More issued me the fake ration card as per her directions," he said, adding, "I have done nothing wrong. So I am not afraid of any police action. I am not happy with the investigations. Investigators did not call me once for hearing my side."

Heading: On second janta durbar, police commissioner calls for better public participation - Indian Express
Content:
All that glittered was not sold this Diwali. The flood of discounts and freebies, higher than last year, did not translate into increased sales because of the economic slowdown.

In many ways, this Diwali turned out to be less bright for dealers of white goods who found customers reluctant to buy, let alone splurge. "The sales were low this year, less by at least 10 per cent, compared to last Diwali. There were fewer purchases because of the global recession," said Tarvinder Singh, partner at the Maharashtra Electronics Corporation.

Entry of new players like Vijay Sales and e zone into the Pune electronic goods market probably explained the numerous discounts and freebies offered. Others like Croma Electronics had expanded and opened new branches. "The festival offers were similar to last year, but increased competition led people to believe that more discounts or choices were on offer," said Rajneesh More, Pune operations head, Dass Electric Trading Co. Pvt Ltd.

More said that increased competition had also divided the market. "Although Pune is growing compared to other cities, the sales potential during Diwali remains pretty much the same. Increased competition has reduced each dealer's share," he said.

Vijay Sales has been in Pune only for the last six months, but it has had a presence in Ahmedabad and Mumbai for nearly 40 years. "If the markets had not taken a downward swing, our sales would have increased by as much as 30 per cent in Pune. But without the offers, the customers would not have even come out to buy these goods," said Jyoti Mitra, operations head, Vijay Sales.

"Diwali boosts the market, but this time it was not up to the expected levels," Mitra said, referring to other cities as well where Vijay Sales is present. More added that the electronic goods segment was usually never affected by extraneous factors. "Initially I thought that people would spend on these goods with the money that they did not invest in the markets. But it did not turn out that way. Customers say that the market downturn has affected them," he said.

Heading: PMC needs 20 pc cut in development works - Indian Express
Content:
Now, citizens who file complaints can keep track of the developments in their cases every Saturday at the respective police stations, said Commissioner of police Satyapal Singh at the janta darbar organised at the Khadak police station on Thursday.

The janta darbar was initiated by the commissioner so that the common man can voice his problems — either regarding discrepancies in the working of the force or any complaint they have.

The proceedings of the day mostly saw irate citizens grumbling about traffic problems. Cases of manhandling and forgery were also discussed.

The commissioner also insisted that for civil disputes, land grabbing and encroachment cases, the citizens should approach the municipal officials.

Singh patiently heard out disgruntled citizens who voiced their concern about limited staff in the police department and promised to look into the matter.

He said, "If anyone commits any crime or if anti social elements try to disrupt peace, it is the duty of all citizens to inform their police nearest police station. The city police will ensure the security of such informers and will keep their identities confidential."

People from different backgrounds — freedom fighters to city-based associations — had assembled at the Khadak police station.

The commissioner appealed the presidents of various associations to actively participate with the city police and help curb the crimes. Singh also said that no discrepancy on the part of the police will be tolerated and that the city police will always be there to assist them.

The darbar went off smoothly as opposed to the first one where Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane had walked out in a huff.

Singh assured of more transparency in the functioning of his department. "Of all government deparments in the city, the police department has been the most efficient among all," he said.

Heading: Garbage disposal facility inaugurated at NCL - Indian Express
Content:
In order to cut down its operating expenses, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has issued a circular and directed the ward offices and department heads to prioritise the development works for the 2009-10 budget and said that the quantum of development works and monetary allocations should be at least 20 per cent less as compared to the 2008-09 budget.

The chief accountant of PMC, Virendra Jadhavrao has issued the circular on October 21. The circular directs the departmental heads, ward commissioner and ward officers to suggest only those works , which are essential, in the next budget. "The list of proposed works need to be prioritised and should be planned in such a way that these works are completed within a stipulated timeframe." The circular also makes it mandatory for the ward offices to mention the quantum of spillover works. A few months back, PMC had given nod to the ward offices to carry out the development works up to Rs 25 lakh without the permission of the civic administration. Now, the civic administration has directed the ward offices to keep the quantum of works within the limit of Rs 12 crore annually.

Talking to The Indian Express on this move, municipal commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said, "Till now, only commissioner used to plan the annual budget. But now, there is decentralisations of power and the ward offices have to plan for the development of the areas under their wards and suggest monetary allocations. Many important works like water supply and sewage remain neglected. If they do not prioritise, many important works might get chopped while planning the budget. " BJP corporator Ujwal Keskar, who made available a copy of this circular to media, however dumped this circular saying, "Asking the ward offices to reduce the quantum of development works next year is a backward step of the civic administration, even though the revenue as well as expenses should increase by the year."

Heading: Walchand Cup tennis: Seeds bite the dust, city lass in semis - Indian Express
Content:
S Sivaram, director, National Chemical Laboratory (NCL), inaugurated the garbage composting facility in the laboratory campus here on Thursday.

As per the new guidelines of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), garbage generated by institutions and housing societies should be segregated into wet and dry garbage and the disposal of the wet garbage should be done at the place of generation.

The NCL is spread over 475 acres and houses laboratory buildings, staff quarters, students' hostels, guest house, shopping complex and so on. The daily generation of garbage is to the tune of one tonne. NCL engaged SWACH, a Pune Municipal Corporation-approved cooperative of waste pickers for the house-to-house collection of garbage and to segregate the same into wet and dry garbage. SWACH personnel take the dry recyclable garbage away and the non-recyclable dry garbage is the only load for disposal on PMC.

NCL chose the mechanical composting system for its garbage disposal. An organic waste converter, manufactured by EXCEL Industries, Mumbai, is installed in a specially identified area spread over 10,000 sq ft. The composting machine processes 50 kg of wet garbage in one batch in 15 minutes. With the aid of this machine, the wet garbage — mostly from the kitchens of the NCL staff quarters, hostels, and canteen — is converted in to compost in two weeks. The compost will be used in the NCL garden area as manure.

Presently, out of the one tonne generated garbage, around 300 kg of wet garbage is getting converted into compost and the SWACH workers take away an equal amount of dry recyclable garbage. Thus, the total load on the garbage lifting and disposal system of PMC is reduced by two-third of the generated quantity.

An NCL team led by civil engineer Atul Mahajan created the garbage composting facility with suggestions from Dr Rajendra Joshi, ward medical officer of Aundh area and Jayant Bhosekar, Aundh ward officer.

Heading: Foreign players arrive in city for NECC-ITF tennis tournament - Indian Express
Content:
Karnataka's Vinod Gowda, Maharashtra's Rutuja Bhonsale, Andhra Pradesh's K Bhuvna and West Bengal's Amruta Mukherjee caused major upsets in knocking out their seeded opponents to move into the semifinal rounds at the Walchand Cup under-16 National Series Tennis Tournament organised by Deccan Gymkhana and played on their tennis courts.

City-based 12-year-old Rutuja Bhonsale, a seventh standard student of Nagarwalla School here, created two upsets in a day, accounting for third-seeded Iska Teertha of AP 6-3 6-2 in the pre quarterfinals and fifth-seeded Eetee Mehta of Gujarat 6-2, 6-2 in the quarterfinals to move into the last four in the girls' singles. It was a bad day for second seed Prathana Thombare and fourth-seeded Vaidehi Bhagwat of Maharashtra as they were shunted out from the singles' event.

In the boys' under-16 quarterfinals, seventh-seeded Vinod Gowda, a tenth standard student of the Vivekananda school, Bangalore, beat third-seeded Rohit Bisht of Delhi 6-3, 6-3 to move into the last four. Top seed Shahbaaz Khan, second seed Ronit Bisht and fourth seeded Vishwesh Sinha also made it to the semifinals with contrasting wins.

Meanwhile, seventh-seeded K Bhuvna of AP registered a shocking 6-4, 7-6 (13-11) win over second seeded and India junior team member Prathana Thombre of Maharashtra.

Sixth-seeded Kolkata's Amruta Mukherjee who won the Asian Ranking tennis in the city in April this year easily accounted for another member of the junior Indian team and fourth seed Vaidehi Bhagwat of Maharashtra 6-2, 6-2 to enter the last four. Top seed Ankita Raina Gujarat remained the only seed in fray scoring an emphatic 6-2, 6-1 win over Sabatini Ankaraju of Andhra Pradesh.

Heading: ABVP member spits at Geelani in DU seminar - Indian Express
Content:
For some of the foreign participants, preparations for the NECC-ITF women's tennis championships have already begun.

With four days left for the tournament to commence, Natasha Khan, Jade Windley, Jade Curtis from Great Britain and Korina Perkovic from Germany arrived in the city on Wednesday and have begun practising for the $25000 tournament at the Deccan Gymkhana tennis courts here.

Natasha Khan and Jade Windley are from Brighton, Sussex, and train at a tennis academy called Brighton Esporta, under Guy Galpin, former international tennis payer at the junior and senior level. Khan is currently ranked 641 in the world and has played in previous editions of the tournament. Windley, who is 18 years old, won the bronze medal in the women's doubles category of the tennis event at the recently concluded Commonwealth Youth Games. She is ranked 879th in the world.

Jade Curtis trains at a tennis academy at Saltash, Cornwall, under her coach and father Jason Spence. She is ranked 489th in the world and has participated in the women's doubles event of Wimbledon in 2007. German girl Korina Perkovic is from the HTV tennis academy in Frankfurt and is training under Mike Schiller and Mischa Gropper. She is ranked 471st in the world and is in good form after winning a $ 10000 tournament in Cremona, Italy.

The four competitors are currently practising with coach Guy Galpin and gearing up to play the qualifying matches that begin on Saturday.

Heading: Teen sisters fled home to meet man, shot dead by angry cousin - Indian Express
Content:
Members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), the students' wing of the Bharatiya Janata Party, disrupted a seminar in Delhi University where S A R Geelani, an accused in the Parliament attack case and later acquitted by the Supreme Court, was a speaker.

The protestors shouted slogans, hurled stones and one of them even spat at Geelani a few minutes after the Arabic lecturer entered hall 22 of the Arts faculty to speak on

'Communalism, Fascism and Democracy: Rhetoric and Reality'.

After police intervened and pushed the protestors out of the hall, Geelani commented: "This violent protest is a perfect example of the fascism and terrorism that we have gathered here to discuss." The police detained 14 ABVP members.

The party said they held the protest because the pamphlet for the seminar "was clearly pro-SIMI, which is a terrorist organisation". "We will not allow such anti-national people to come to DU," said Ashutosh Shrivastav, Delhi state secretary of the ABVP.

The protest began just a few minutes after the seminar started, when Geelani came into the room. A few protestors even broke the microphone. DUSU president Nupur Sharma and former vice-president Vikas Dahiya were also a part of the protest.

The Delhi University Teachers' Association has expressed its concerns regarding the event. Joint secretary Sanjay Kumar said they had approached the Vice-Chancellor to ensure punishment for those involved in the violence. "This is a disgrace. Everyone is free to voice his or her opinion but the method used by the ABVP was completely unjustified. This behaviour is an insult to teachers," said Kumar.

Students, too, thought alike. "They could have let him (Geelani) speak and then rebutted his arguments, instead of behaving the way they did," says Raghav Ahuja, a first year student.

Heading: Boy dies after surgery, Apollo faces criminal action - Indian Express
Content:
France has offered to upgrade India's 51 frontline Mirage 2000 fighters in a "compressed delivery time-frame", which could prove a boon to New Delhi in the backdrop of Indian Air Forces' force levels depleting to an alarming all time low of 32 Squadrons.

And as part of the upgradation deal almost at the final stages of conclusion, the new Mirages would come armed with longer range Air to Air Missiles to enhance the fighters capability in beyond visual range combat.

The fighters would be armed with new MICA missiles with a range of taking on targets almost 40 kms away, almost double the range of present missiles on Indian fighters.

"The time scale of upgraded fighter deliveries can be compressed and worked out according to IAFs needs," Francois Quentin, senior vice president of the European Aerospace, Electronics and services major, Thales, told visiting Indian newsmen in Paris.

The Paris-headquartered company is leading the consortium of four companies comprising Dassault, the manufacturer of the fighter, Snecma, the engine makers and European Missile leader MBDA, which would undertake the Mirage upgrade, estimated to cost over 1.5 billion Euros.

India and France have been in negotiations for the past two years on the Mirage upgrade and the deal almost now in final stages could be the last major defence contract to be concluded by the Government before the upcoming Lok Sabha elections.

Under the proposed deal, for which technical and weapon proposals have been finalised, 51 Mirages of the IAF will get a fresh lease of life for another 20-25 years, get an extended range of almost 800 kms without refuelling and longer range detection capability to confront and take on four to five targets simultaneously both on ground and in air.

The new fighters would be capable of carrying six MICA air to air missiles including two armed with infra red seekers giving them complete stealth capabilities.

Assuring a "easier and speedier" delivery schedule, Quentin said though under present negotiations, four upgraded Mirages are to be handed over to India in forty months, the delivery period could be shortened to 32 months.

The top Thales official said the upgrade deal could have other spin-offs, if New Delhi worked out its upgrade schedule to coincide with modernisation of 50 Mirage D fighters to be undertaken by the French Government soon.

Quentin said that the upgrade could accrue tactical advantage to IAF commanders as they would have to commit fewer fighters, while achieving a high success rate.

"A typical border protection mission involving two hours on station will require just two upgraded Mirages as compared with six current aircraft," he said.

Another company official said due to its high availability and low attrition rates, the Mirage 2000 remained one of IAFs key assets, which had proved its mettle in the Kargil conflict.

Under the proposed deal offered by the French companies, two Mirages would be upgraded in France and the rest 49 under technology transfer by Hindustan Aeronautics limited in Bangalore.

For the upgrade deal, a thirty per cent offset package by the French industry is proposed and Thales officials said these would be undertaken through five to ten Indian partners, both in private and defence public sector undertakings.

Heading: CPI outs name of its candidate for Okhla - Indian Express
Content:
In '05, 8-yr-old died of internal burns and infection after a 'rare' fire in a laser machine, treating a tumour in his larynx, burnt his airway; HC finds hospital negligent

The death of an eight-year-old boy due to an "accidental" laser spark during a surgery at the Indraprastha Apollo Hospital has left the company that runs the country's leading healthcare centre facing criminal action. Charges made out against the Indraprastha Medical Corporation Limited are "culpable homicide not amounting to murder" and "causing death by negligence".

Aditya Pal died of internal burns and infection in October 2005, 23 days after a "rare" fire in a laser machine that was used to treat a recurrent tumour in his larynx (voice box) burnt his entire airway. After the surgery on October 3, the boy was kept in the ICU under intensive paediatric care till he died there on October 26, his ninth birthday, said his maternal grandfather Tej Singh, who is fighting the case against the hospital.

It was Aditya's fifth visit to the hospital where he had been undergoing treatment since November 2004 for 'recurrent laryngeal papillomatosis'.

The postmortem conducted the very next day by a specialist board of doctors from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) had found it a "case of gross criminal negligence, and the burn injuries that were the primary cause of death were unwarranted and speak of failure of taking required precautions, care and skill in adopted procedure".

In a recent order, the Delhi High Court agreed with the postmortem report and refused to quash a metropolitan magistrate's direction issued in March 2007 to the Sarita Vihar police to investigate the hospital authorities and the doctors concerned under Sections 304 Part II and 304 A of the Indian Penal Code.

The boy's family named the company running the hospital, its managing director, medical superintendent Ritu Rawat and the ENT consultant who had conducted the laser surgery on October 3, as accused in the complaint.

Rawat and the ENT consultant had moved the HC, seeking to quash the criminal proceedings.

The punishment under Section 304 Part II is imprisonment up to 10 years, but under Section 304 A it is a maximum of two years in jail.

"Aditya's father had died of kidney failure in February 2005, but my daughter continued to stay with her in-laws in Meerut. Whenever it was time for Aditya's treatment, I would pick them up from Meerut and later drop them back," recalls Tej Singh, a resident of Loni.

The hospital authorities defended in the court that the postmortem report was "preliminary" in nature, and brought the judge's attention to the November 2005 findings of an AIIMS medical board that had inspected the same laser machine and found it "working normally".

Appearing for the hospital, senior advocate Siddharth Luthra argued that the Delhi Medical Council, on inquiry in 2006, had already given his client a clean chit and absolved the hospital of any negligence.

The council's inquiry report termed the laser spark that claimed the boy's life as "rare, and known to occur with the incidence of 0.5 to 1.5 per cent in the USA".

Dismissing Luthra's pleas, the Bench threw its weight behind the postmortem report.

It said the board that conducted the postmortem "had the body of the deceased who is alleged to have died on account of medical negligence with them while the other boards did not have the advantage of examining the body".

Besides, the court observed that the inspection of the laser machine was done "considerably after the incident", rendering the exercise far less conclusive.

The Apollo management, meanwhile, said it regretted the unfortunate incident, calling it "rare but not a case of medical negligence".

"We have extended full cooperation to the investigating agency and will continue to do so," their statement read.

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Pooja Deshwan - Indian Express
Content:
In-laws to the rescue
With all his Cabinet colleagues now in the safe zone, Delhi health minister Yoganand Shastri, a victim of delimitation, is now looking for hope some 40 km away from his present constituency, Malviya Nagar. With this constituency going to Hauz Khas MLA Kiran Walia, Shastri is hoping to find support in his sasural, Narela. Sources close to the minister said Shastri has been given only two options, Mehrauli or Narela, and given that he could use the clout of his in-laws, he is seriously contemplating contesting the elections from there.

Who's laughing now
BJP MLA Vijay Jolly's mimicking might be amusing for the media and other spectators but not for senior BJP leaders. On Thursday, as Jolly tried to warm up to BJP leader Arun Jaitley, the latter rebuffed him for claiming that he jogged early in the morning with a fracture in his leg. "How can you jog with a fracture?" Jaitley exclaimed and murmured that Jolly come up with better ideas to attract attention.

Heading: Kiran Walia woos ‘new’ voters in Malviya Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
Constituency: Ashok Vihar

Pooja Deshwan is a Hindi MA final year student at Delhi University. All of 21 years, 2008 is special for her, as she will be voting for the first time because she is "grown up and feels it's time to start voting". Born and brought up in Ashok Vihar, Pooja feels Delhi is the best city for young people. The speed of progress in the last few years along with the Delhi Metro and clean roads make Sheila Dikshit and the Congress favourites. "I just do not see a better alternative," Pooja says candidly.

On Ashok Vihar
"It's a relatively new locality, so the roads are extremely bad. The electricity supply is also erratic," she says. She feels that while the rest of Delhi has developed, her area remains neglected. Pooja says there are potholes in her colony and driving there is a nightmare.

On Delhi University
Few books and bad food in the canteen tops her list of complaints. "The libraries and the food are bad but I guess that's the situation everywhere," Puja says. She admits that while the problems persist, "it is not enough to create a ruckus".
"I love my campus as it is generally nice to its students," she says.

Heading: Catch them early: BJP mixes morning walk with political talk - Indian Express
Content:
Congress leader Kiran Walia was out wooing new voters on Thursday, a day after she was chosen to represent the party from Malviya Nagar.

Her constituency, Hauz Khas, was dissolved and a huge segment was incorporated into the Malviya Nagar constituency. Starting early this morning, she visited parts of Malviya Nagar that are new to her.

"People in Hauz Khas already know me well, so the real challenge is to meet the new voters. More effort needs to be pumped into the newer areas," she says.

All this follows the fierce struggle between Walia and Yoganand Shastri over the Malviya Nagar ticket. Till Tuesday, the area was untouched by any excitement about the upcoming elections, as the Congress could not reach a consensus on its candidate.

On the other hand, Ram Bhaj, the veteran BJP leader, has been campaigning since Sunday.

Walia, however, remains unfazed by the challenge the BJP leader offers. She says: "If he was such a veteran, why did he leave his area around Nizammuddin and chose to fight from a new constituency? I am confident that voters will vote for the Congress because its developmental work has been very visible."

Residents say whoever contests from the area will have to address parking issues and the problem of sealing. Khem Chand, president of the E-Block resident welfare association, says many people will lose their shops if the sealing drive begins and that would be a concern during election campaigns.

He, however, says the people cannot trust any of the candidates, as they will never refuse them anything during campaigning. "All candidates, be it from the BJP or the Congress, will say yes to everything but when the time comes, it is the courts that decide everything," he says.

Heading: Man held for blackmailing girl after filming obscene video - Indian Express
Content:
In the backdrop of the imposing tombs in Lodhi Gardens — shimmering in the light mist of a nippy Thursday morning — Bharatiya Janata Party's Vijay Jolly could be seen running the talk with fellow joggers.

Jolly, slightly limping at present because of a hairline fracture in one foot, is carrying the BJP's hopes for a close fight with reigning Congress MLA and two-time winner from this New Delhi constituency: Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit.

Regulars at the park, some jogging and some in the middle of a workout, were approached by Jolly, since 6 am sharp. The leader was in casuals — a brown, striped T-shirt and bermuda shorts. He stirred up some interest extolling the virtues of his party, and denouncing the Sheila Dikshit years.

But funnily enough, he ran out of words in the middle of it all when he bumped into another regular at the park — Dikshit's son and Member of Parliament from East Delhi Sandeep Dikshit. Jolly later said in the evening: "We exchanged pleasantries and wished each other luck for the elections. There was no negativity or bitterness."

But Jolly is pleased with the effect he had on morning walkers. "My novel method of canvassing stumped them. This way, I can reach out to senior citizens staying in the New Delhi constituency and hear their problems at length," he said. However, Jolly is not the only one talking to morning walkers. BJP seems to have adopted this as an effective campaign strategy.

O P Babbar, MLA from Tilak Nagar, has also followed the routine since his name was announced on November 1. "I have been doing yoga for a long time, the only difference is that I try to visit more parks these days so that I can reach out to more people," Babbar said.

The younger generation is not behind either. Yogesh Attre, a first-time BJP candidate from Mongolpuri against Congress minister Rajkumar Chauhan, has weaved a morning walk into his daily routine. "In the Rohini area, many residents come to parks for exercises. Their minds are open in the mornings, and it is the best time to talk to them about the issues concerning Delhi," Attre said.

Heading: Centre opens up water table, draw as you please - Indian Express
Content:
The Northwest district police have arrested a 24-year-old man and his two friends who had allegedly made an obscene video of a girl and were blackmailing her for money.

The Ashok Vihar police said the girl initially gave in to their demands but when Vinod Kumar, the main accused, and the two others started asking for more money she lodged a police complaint against them, after which the three were arrested.

Police sources said the girl had met Vinod at a private institute in Ashok Vihar, Phase I, and that they had been in a relationship till he filmed her.

"In 2007, the two had gone out of Delhi with others. In a hotel room there, Vinod, with the help of his friends Ashish and Rajan, made her consume sweets and drinks laced with sedatives, which left her unconscious," said a senior officer.

According to the complainant, she was undressed and filmed in an obscene manner. After she gained consciousness, Vinod allegedly showed her the video and brought her back to Delhi. Once in the Capital, the three started asking for money from her, failing which, they threatened, they would air the film on a local cable TV channel.

They initially asked for small jewellery items and cash, but their demands started getting heftier, the police said.

Fearing a scandal, the girl narrated the entire incident to her parents earlier this week after which they lodged a complaint with the police.

"The accused have been arrested under Sections 375 (rape) and 383 (extortion). Further investigations are on and relevant sections of the IPC will be added after we get more details in the case," said a senior officer. According to the police, Vinod is the son of a popular restaurateur in the area.

Heading: Bee Complex - Indian Express
Content:
In what appears to be a please-all move ahead of the elections, and one that will certainly help the state leadership, the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) has opened up the groundwater table for free domestic use.

While the move is meant for the entire country, Delhi — which is going to polls later this month, and is perennially parched — can now have a private borewell for each family. The effects are likely to be felt most in South and South-West districts.

In 2000, the CGWA had notified the two districts and also the Yamuna floodplains as critical areas where the use of groundwater had to be controlled and regulated. In a meeting in August, however, it decided that each house, even in notified areas, could withdraw free groundwater for domestic purposes.

While this may lead to severe depletion in the water table in South and Southwest districts, the situation may turn out to be more exploitative in non-notified areas comprising the rest of the city. The new guidelines issued by the CGWA specify that "there is no restriction" on the construction of tubewells for drinking and domestic purposes.

The only catch for notified areas is that the well should be of a maximum diameter of 100 metres, and the CGWA or the Deputy Commissioner of the area needs to be informed ten days before the construction began.

Environmentalists, meanwhile, point out that this step will lead to overexploitation of the groundwater resources. The water table will dry up faster than it gets filled, they add.

Obtaining a permission to dig a borewell was earlier a difficult and lengthy process.

In Vasant Kunj, a mad rush to dig borewells seems to have already started. "Contractors are making money and telling everyone that wells up to 800 feet in depth can be dug. At least 200 borewells have already been dug. This will dry up the entire city," says Jyoti Sharma, a resident of Vasant Kunj and president of FORCE, an NGO. "A borewell is not a permanent solution to water crisis. In Jaunapur, where I stay, borewells have already dried up," says Vinod Jain, an environmentalist.

Heading: Comedy Centre - Indian Express
Content:
Spelling Bee comes to the Capital and has children tied up in knots over "rendezvous" and "kleptomania"

What's wrong with "manoeuvre"? Oh, it is the letter 'O' and the '-re' ending. When the American Spelling Bee comes to Delhi, leave your British-bequeathed English at home and pronounce maneuver, like the Yankees do, that it can pass off as a brand of Chilean wine — and spell it likewise. So this reporter felt quite foolish when she realised that she, along with approximately 100 school kids across the National Capital Region, added that extra 'O' and ended up with a blooper. Welcome to the first ever Spelling Bee in Delhi where the alphabet is alpha, beta and omega.

The Spelling Bee, for the uninitiated, is an American institution. Primarily a spelling competition, it is open to students who have not yet completed the eighth grade or have turned 15 or won a previous National Spelling Bee. The first ever Spelling Bee was organised in 1925 in Louisville, Kentucky, and had just nine contestants. "The Scripps National Spelling Bee is enormously popular and most of the finalists are Indian-Americans. So this year, we decided to bring the competition to India," says Ann Seshadri, cultural affairs officer, American Center, Delhi, who has organised the competition for students in the NCR and Kolkata.

Thursday morning saw a flurry of activity at Delhi Public School, Mathura Road, as students of Class IX-XI from over 100 schools across NCR attended the preliminary round, attempting to spell common and not-so-common words and trying to remember the rules of American English. "When we did a dry run last year, we found that the usual Bee words were too difficult for students here. So we've slightly increased the age limit," says Seshadri. Indian-American kids might be poring over dictionaries to get their "guerdon" and "prosopopoeia" right and asking politely "Can I have the language of origin, please?", but in a country without a Bee tradition and where English is not quite the first language, children were tied up in knots as "rendezvous" turned into "rondeywoe" and "prodigious" became "prodigas".

However, for the winners of the elimination round, Sushmita Sarkar and Nitika Khaitan of the Convent of Jesus and Mary, finding their way around multiple pronunciations and spelling variations was not a problem. "This cannot be done overnight. I set aside time everyday to learn the words in the spelling pamphlet that was given to us a month in advance of the competition. There are words that can't be recalled easily, like the one which means contemplation of one's belly button," said Khaitan. It is omphaloskepsis and you need to be a genius to get that one right.

Thirty-four finalists are set to battle their wits at the American Center on November 20. The winners of the Delhi round then face the winners of the Kolkata round. The final will take place at the Kolkata Book Fair next year.

Heading: Shoe Fling - Indian Express
Content:
In an interview with Dipti Nagpaul-D'Souza, Sanjeev Bhaskar talks about his new show Mumbai Calling that blends call centre, race relations and serious comedy. Excerpts:

* How did Mumbai Calling happen?
Producer Allan McKeown was interested in setting a comedy in a call centre in India. I had started writing a movie about a call centre some years ago, which I abandoned to pursue other projects. I dusted those ideas and developed a situation comedy. Actor Nitin Ganatra and writer Simon Blackwell are friends. I brought them on board and they added to the series.

* What's your character Kenny Gupta like?
Kenny Gupta is a British-born Indian who comes to Mumbai to manage a call centre.
Although he looks like everybody else, he's a fish out of water and is constantly looking forward to the day he can return to his cold, rainy, depressing bit of London.

* Is this yet another attempt at speaking about race relations?
From Goodness Gracious Me through The Kumars at No. 42 to a documentary series on India, my work has always been about playing with people's perceptions and stereotypes. I hope to do the same with Mumbai Calling.

* How is the race scene in the UK now?
Better than it was when my parents came here. After President Obama, who knows, we might have an Indian prime minister of the UK.

* Do you fear that given the current economic scenario and the western take on outsourcing, the show might face criticism in the UK?
Mumbai Calling is entertainment and thus employs dramatic licence. It isn't a documentary, so any criticism other than from an entertainment point of view is pointless.

* Your wife Meera Syal has not been a part of Mumbai Calling. What is she up to?
Meera has been writing movie scripts and acting in a comedy on British TV, called Beautiful People, so she is busy.

* What makes a good joke — a situation or a punch line?
Both make a good joke. A combination of the two makes a great one.

* Who are your favourite comedians?
The Marx brothers, Woody Allen, Monty Python, Peter Sellers, Robin Williams... the list goes on. At the moment my three-year-old son Shaan makes me laugh more than anyone else.

The show will be on HBO from November 8

Heading: BSP presence will hit Congress: Arun Jaitley - Indian Express
Content: On a wintry Tuesday evening, British High Commissioner Sir Richard Stagg threw open his residence on Rajaji Road to welcome 200 guests for the launch of a British footwear company in India, Pavers England. Currently, their shoes are available at all Shoe Tree outlets in Delhi. "I visited India in 2002 and found a serious lack of comfort footwear," said Stuart Paver, chairman of Pavers England, before the show. A modest Catherine Paver, founder of the 36-year-old brand, who conceived the project in a coffee-room while bringing up three kids, said, "I never dreamt in a million years that I would come to India. I hope they like our shoes." An hour-long fashion show saw models walking down the ramp in chic pumps, leather boots and some lethal-looking wedge heels, while guests nibbled on a sumptuous spread that included a very British stewed lamb and kebabs. Pavers England shoes begin at Rs 900 and will soon be available at Lifestyle and Pantaloons.

Heading: Poonam Azad hands in resignation - Indian Express
Content:
Senior BJP leader Arun Jaitley on Thursday highlighted the role the Bahujan Samaj Party could play in ensuring victory for his party in the Delhi Assembly polls. He was speaking to the party's 69 candidates at a meeting organised for the distribution of the party symbol.

"The BSP has a strong presence in Delhi for the first time and our surveys indicate that at least 10 per cent of the seats will be won by them. This will hit the Congress campaign in a big way. We should utilise this opportunity and ensure there are no vote-spoilers in our case," Jaitley said to the candidates.

This is the first time that a senior party leader has spoken openly about the 'key role' the BSP could play in the elections later this month.

Jaitley also emphasised the need for all campaigns to concentrate only on two issues — terrorism and price rise. "We should play the match on our pitch and try to stick to our own agenda, as closely as possibly. Talk about terrorism and price rise does not get entangled in a personal fight," he said.

The party also decided to use the slogan "Mehengi padi Congress" in a big way. Both Jaitley and BJP chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra called on candidates to ensure the party slogan reaches every house.

Also, after the Election Commission banned the use of posters, the party has decided to publish 10,000 stickers for each candidate with the slogan on them.

The BJP has witnessed much infighting and dissidence ever since the first list of 53 candidates was announced on November 1.

Speaking on the issue, Jaitley said: "Talk to party insiders who are opposing you, if necessary visit them, but make sure they are on your side."

Delhi BJP unit president Harsh Vardhan told candidates they should prepare a private note about the dissidents and to pass this on to senior leaders.

The candidates had assembled at the Delhi BJP office on Ashoka Road to collect the party symbol before beginning the nomination process.

To ensure that no last-minute errors in filing of nomination forms could play spoilsport, the Delhi unit president and legal cell briefed the candidates, and also issued a list of instructions.

V K Malhotra will be filing his nomination on Saturday, while party president Harsh Vardhan would file his on November 10.

Heading: Bank de-seals four of the five flats ‘owned’ by murdered trader - Indian Express
Content:
Poonam Azad says the BJP has broken her trust and that of all Poorvanchalis

Poonam Azad, the Delhi BJP vice-president and head of the party's Poorvanchali unit, gave her resignation to BJP national president Rajnath Singh on Thursday. Azad had been canvassing for the Patparganj ticket, which was eventually given to student leader Nakul Bhardwaj.

Azad announced her decision soon after a list of 12 candidates, which included the Patparganj seat from East Delhi, was declared late on Wednesday.

She and some of her supporters held a protest in front of Rajnath Singh's house. He was, however, not in town and Azad left her resignation with Singh's staff.

"When they want to choose a candidate for sacrifice, they choose me. And now, when I have an opportunity to win, the party decided to ignore me. The party has broken my trust and the trust of all Poorvanchalis," Azad said. She also criticised the party for giving very few seats to women and Poorvanchali candidates.

Azad contested against chief minister Sheila Dikshit in the last Assembly elections and lost with a huge margin.

Heading: BMW case: Bhasin bail plea rejected - Indian Express
Content:
Canara Bank, which had taken physical possession of five apartments on the ground floor Sharan Apartments in South City Enclave on Tuesday following a Rs 2.25 crore loan default, de-sealed four flats on Thursday.

Ombir Sharma, a resident of DLF Phase-I, who was shot dead on October 6 this year by his business partner in his office in Noida, had bought a ground-floor flat (G-5) in the building in 1999. He then forged the documents of the remaining four flats on the same floor to avail the bank loan. The bank had later issued a notice on November 24, 2006, for the repayment of the outstanding amount within the next 60 days.

Ombir, the owner of Golden Rathi Saria in Noida, and his brother-in-law Vicky were shot dead on October 6 over a shareholding dispute.

Canara Bank manager Mukesh Goel said: "We agree it was a mistake on our part and therefore have de-sealed the four other flats after verifying all the details."

Goel said the bank was planning to recover the loan amount by taking physical possession of Sharma's property and then auction it. "It would be done after we get court orders," added Goel.

R S Grover, owner of the building said: "I received a letter from the ITO office in September this year seeking information on details of the properties owned by Ombir. I have submitted the bill details of all five apartments on the ground floor. Three of the owners have got the property registered and one has the power of attorney," he said. He, along with other flat-owners, had filed an FIR against the bank at the Sector-40 police station after the flats were sealed. Though the bank returned the properties, residents are aggrieved by the awkwardness and humiliation they had to face.

Urvashi, a Class IX student and a resident of G-2 said, "I am happy that the bank has de-sealed our house but we had to undergo a lot of mental harassment during the episode. When I returned home from school on Tuesday, I found my home sealed. We had to spend the night sitting in the corridor. I faced embarrassing questions from my classmates and juniors the next day. We even missed school on Thursday as we couldn't wear dirty uniforms to school."

Heading: Alumni Karat, Digvijay criticise SC order on JNU union polls, MNS - Indian Express
Content:
A city court on Thursday dismissed the fresh bail application of Utsav Bhasin. Nineteen-year-old Bhasin allegedly killed one and injured another with his BMW car near Moolchand flyover on September 11.

Dismissing the bail plea, Additional Sessions Judge Brajesh Garg noted that the offence for which Bhasin was under trial was "grave". He further said that as Bhasin was charged under Section 304 of the IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), he could not be granted a bail.

Arguing on his bail plea, Bhasin's counsel contended that as the chargesheet had been filed in the case, the investigation was certainly over and hence, there was no valid ground to continue keeping Bhasin in custody. The prosecution, however, claimed that extreme rashness was involved in the act as the victim was dragged over a distance before the accused stopped his car.

Bhasin has been in jail since September 27 after he surrendered before the police, following the Delhi High Court's refusal to grant him anticipatory bail.

Heading: Two arrested for running fake NGO, false claims of Congress link - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court stay on JNU elections and the regional chauvinistic politics followed by the Raj Thackeray-led MNS in Maharashtra came under attack at the Jawaharlal Nehru University on Thursday as former students, CPI (M) General Secretary Prakash Karat, Congress leader Digvijay Singh and president of Youth Congress Ashok Tanwar took turns to discuss "Politics in India — Today and Tomorrow".

The leaders were speaking at a seminar organised by JNU as part of its three-day alumni meet, being organised for the first time in the university.

Addressing the gathering, Karat said, "In 1971, JNU had started a democratic process of elections, but the Supreme Court has disrupted it. I suggest the former office-bearers of JNU form a delegation and submit a memorandum to the court." Ashok Tanwar criticised the ban on candidates re-contesting elections and said that true leadership requires stage-wise grooming.

The leaders also blamed the Centre for making pro-elite policies. "After the US was hit by financial crisis, the PM called a meeting of corporations, but left out trade unions and farmers," said Karat. On Friday, a panel discussion will be held to discuss the challenges faced by the world economy.

Heading: Guard faces 10 years in jail for selling govt files to junk dealer - Indian Express
Content:
The crime Branch has arrested two men for running a fake NGO and falsely claiming association with the Congress party. The accused, identified as Baba Gauri Shankar Verma and Suresh Kumar allegedly cheated people into paying them huge sums of money after promising them allotments of petrol pumps and gas agencies.

Crime Branch officials have estimated that the accused cheated people of over Rs 21 lakh.

Police said the two accused ran the NGO, registered in Janakpuri, in the name "All India Minority Sadbhawana Congress". Verma identified himself as the national president of the NGO.

"On the letterhead of his NGO, he printed photos of Sonia Gandhi as chief patron of the trust and Rahul Gandhi as the National Yuva Leader. He duped people into paying huge amounts of money to secure a high post in his NGO and also promised to allot them petrol pumps, CNG pumps, or kerosene oil depots after showing them fake documents," DCP (Crime) Neeraj Thakur said.

Police said the accused had also opened an ICICI Bank account where he asked his victims to deposit the money.

The fraud came to the police's notice when an Agra resident lodged a complaint that Baba Gauri had lured him into paying over Rs 1.32 lakh. When the victim asked for his money back later, Gauri threatened to implicate him in a false case.

"The accused was arrested from a Paharganj hotel on November 5, where he was to meet one Vaibhav Goyal," a senior police officer said. Co-accused Suresh Kumar had met Baba Gauri in 2002 and acted as his personal assistant.

Heading: Court denies bail to man held for selling endangered turtles - Indian Express
Content:
Selling off over 500 files from his office to a junk dealer had earned Main Pal, a security guard, Rs 320 in 2003. Five years later, he is facing trial and can be awarded an imprisonment of up to 10 years for trespass and theft.

The files belonged to the Land and Buildings department of the government where Pal was employed.

In April 2003, when the department reopened after five days of holidays, the officer-in-charge realised that as many as 564 files were missing from the record room.

An FIR was registered and the police found out that Pal had sold off the files to Shamsuddin, a junk dealer, between April 11 and 15, when the office was closed. Further, when he realised that a case had been registered, Pal allegedly went to Shamsuddin, requesting him not to disclose anything to the police in case they approached him.

Observing that there was ample prima facie evidence against Pal, a Sessions judge has now sent him back to the metropolitan court where he will undergo trial.

Quashing a revision petition filed in the case, Additional Sessions Judge P K Saxena held that the charges framed against Pal did not call for any "interference".

Pal's counsel had earlier filed a revision petition on the grounds that Pal had not been named in the report lodged by the department.

Moreover, he had argued, nothing had been recovered from his possession and hence there did not arise enough

suspicion against Pal to nail him as the accused.

Heading: Noted Urdu, Gujarati ghazal lyricist Adil Mansuri passes away - Indian Express
Content:
A wildlife offender attached to a pet shop in the Sushant Lok area of Gurgaon was on Thursday denied bail at the Tis Hazari Courts, after he was arrested for trading in live Indian Tent Turtles, which enjoy the same amount of protection as the tiger.

Ritin Mehrotra was apprehended late on Tuesday by the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau for trying to sell four Tent Turtles. On Wednesday, he was sent to judicial custody.

"Mehrotra is a resident of Dhankot, and was caught in Mahipalpur by a decoy customer. He had the turtles in a car. It is illegal to possess these animals and he did not have any kind of documentation on him," Ramesh Pandey of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau said.

Trade in all turtles is illegal but they are popular in the poaching and wildlife crime networks. Officials said pet shops might often trade in these animals, supplying them to well-heeled customers.

"Tent Turtles, Star Tortoises and Indian Roof Turtles are most in demand in the international and national markets. This is a silent trade and these animals are used in aquariums and water bodies as pets. Since they are cold-blooded, they suffer as a result of climate change as well and protecting them becomes an even more important task. We are keeping a sharp lookout in all pet shops," Pandey said.

"It's time we understood and recognised that all turtles are protected species and buying them and keeping them without permission is illegal. Anybody who spots a turtle in a shop must immediately report this. If you already possess a turtle, please inform the Forest Department. Thousand of Starred Tortoises are smuggled out of India to be kept as pets. Their shells are also used to make ashtrays and trays," Kartick Satyanarayan, member, advisory board, Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, said.

Heading: LPG distributors to go on indefinite strike from November 10 - Indian Express
Content:
The one last dream of Adil Mansuri, who passed away in New Jersey, will be buried with him. The legend of modern Urdu and Gujarati ghazal once wrote a couplet in Gujarati, his mother tongue: Marya pachheej aa sapnu phale Adil, Vatan ni maati ma dharbayela rahevanu (One has to die to realise the dream of being buried in his native land.)

When he left for the US about two-and-a-half decades ago, he had a premonition that made him write his famous ghazal that starts with: "Nadi ni ret ma ramtu nagar male na male…"

The freshness of his thought won instant attraction from all sides both in Gujarati and Urdu.

In fact, Gujarati ghazal will always remain indebted to him for guiding its poets out of the traditional mould and giving them the courage to break free from the shackles of tradition.

A calligrapher par excellence, Mansuri has left behind more than 3,000 works.

To use the words of Chinu Modi, Mansuri was the biggest experimenter in Gujarati poetry and was the one who initiated the Re-Math movement, a landmark phenomenon in Gujarati literature.

Calling him the compendium of courage (sahas ni samhita) Modi

admits that it was to the credit of Adil Mansuri that he and others had dared to think differently.

"Otherwise we would still have been writing in the same old traditional style," he said.

Mansuri never cared for criticism just for the sake of it and taught his peers as well to experiment with words and thoughts.

He wrote ghazals like Jyare pranay ni jag ma sharuaat thai hashe, Tyare pratham ghazal ni rajooaat thai hashe (When love first blossomed in the world, the first ever ghazal would be presented then). His dexterous handling of varying thoughts made him immensely popular among all generations in equal measure.

Known Urdu critic Waris Alvi acknowledges him as a brilliant and excellent poet who was one of the most important avant-garde poets and harbinger of new ghazal that is identified with Mohammad Alvi in India and with Zafar Iqbal in Pakistan.

It was only recently that Zafar Iqbal had penned Tarkeeb, 121 ghazals in Urdu with ending of

couplets (qafiya and radeef) in Gujarati supplied by Adil Mansuri. It was again a bold experiment that only the likes of Iqbal and Adil could accomplish and Adam Tankarvi in his preface calls it a scoop in Ghazal poetry.

Heading: Nine months on, AMC schools yet to get funds for telephone lines - Indian Express
Content:
Claim state govt officials misuse LPG Licensing Order to harass and extort money from dealers

Furious over not being taken seriously, LPG distributors in the state have started mobilising support for an indefinite strike from November 10 through their associations. The distributors are incensed with officials who misuse the law to harass them and extort money from the dealers.

P M Patel, president of All India LPG Distributor's Federation (Gujarat), has been holding meetings with dealers in different parts of the state. He was in Rajkot on Thursday to garner support for the strike. He has already visited Surat, Vadodara and Ahmedabad in this connection and spoken to member dealers. Patel said there will be no alternative but to strike work for an indefinite period if the government fails to meet their demands.

There are 546 LPG distributors in Gujarat, who cater to 5.5 million customers by providing 3.3 million refills. This leaves a gap of 2.2 million refills, "but we still manage to retain the supply flow without having any complaints from any side", Patel said. He also said that nobody in the government had so far listened to their grievances despite several attempts.

"We avoided the Diwali period, so that people do not suffer due to the strike, but now strike is the only way to voice our demands," he said, adding that there was no official communication from the government so far.

Patel said the LPG Licensing Order was passed in1981 and has been in force since 1985 "only to harass dealers and extort money from them. We want a terror-free atmosphere". According to him, with LPG being available through the pipeline grid and the number of dealers increasing, there is no reason why officials should threaten dealers with closure by misusing the law.

The state government officials are busy finding ways to cope with the situation that may arise in the wake of the strike from November 10. The government has officially admitted that if LPG dealers go ahead with their strike, LPG supply and distribution in the entire state will be affected badly, causing severe problems to consumers.

The government has instructed collectors in all the districts to take stern measures against elements trying to hinder the smooth flow of distribution channels. Meanwhile, Gujarat State Civil Supplies Corporation chairman Rajesh Kishore did not answer phone calls when he was approached for the official version.

Heading: GSRTC breaks its intraday earning record - Indian Express
Content:
Even as nearly nine months have gone by since the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) passed a budget for installing telephones in all of its schools, they continue to run without this service.

Habib Mev, AMC School Board member, said though the Corporation allotted Rs 5 lakh to the board for this purpose, till date they have not received "a single penny".

"There are around 450 schools under the AMC with nearly 1.64 lakh students and 4,500-odd teachers. But it is strange that there is no telephone service to convey messages to schools," he said.

He said the board faces several difficulties when it wants to convey some message to the school authorities on an urgent basis. "We either have to call principals or teachers to our office or send our staff members there, which is not an easy task," he added.

The budget for the AMC school board is divided into two parts — grantable and non-grantable. Around 80 per cent amount of the allotted budget is grantable which is taken care of by the state government and 20 per cent is non-grantable, which is borne by the civic body.

"The allocation of Rs 5 lakh was made under the non-grantable budget. We wrote a letter to Municipal Commissioner I P Gautam in this regard long ago, but are yet to receive a reply from him," said Nilesh Patel, another AMC School Board member.

He added: "There is an urgent need for installing telephones at these schools so that we can keep a tab on principals, teachers and peons. We have received several complaints that many principals, teachers and peons are never found at their place or do not come to school on time."

He went on to say that senior officials were "not very keen" on working on this and "try to run away from their responsibilities". "They are not serious about any kind of emergency or security related to kids," he added.

Gautam could not be contacted despite several attempts.

Heading: 56 Pakistani fishermen caught near Jakhau let off - Indian Express
Content:
The prevailing global economic crisis seems to have no effect on the profit of the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC) which recently registered income of Rs 5.54 crore in a day — the highest since its foundation.

According to GSRTC secretary P D Patel, the revenue was generated in one day of Labh Pacham. On Diwali, the corporation recorded a total income of Rs 4 crore. "This has been one of the most remarkable Labh Pacham for the GSRTC. From Ahmedabad alone we received nearly Rs 45 lakh," Patel said.

He added: "We are expecting good response on Dev Diwali on November 13. We have arranged for more buses and hope to cross the Rs 6-crore mark that day."

The previous highest earning was to the tune of Rs 5.11 crore last year and Rs 5 crore in 2006. Nearly 35 lakh people travelled in GSRTC buses on Labh Pacham to famous pilgrim sites like Dwarka, Ambaji, Somnath and Sreenathji.

GSRTC buses make a whopping 42,000 trips every day, covering approximately 28 lakh kilometres, ferrying around 24 lakh passengers. GSRTC officials believe that the travellers prefer the state transport as it is cheap and convenient for them.

Heading: Duo held for transporting cattle to illegal abattoir - Indian Express
Content:
Fifty-six Pakistani fishermen, who had inadvertently strayed into Indian waters near Jakhau coast on Tuesday, were let off by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG), as a goodwill gesture under the confidence building measure between New Delhi and Islamabad.

Indian Coast Guard ship Tarabai intercepted eight Pakistani fishing boats that had reportedly strayed more than 10 nautical miles into Indian waters across the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL).

"All the 56 crew members onboard were immediately let off along with their boats after giving them a warning," defence spokesperson Wing Commander Satish Menon said.

According to experts, post-monsoon season is most conducive for fishing. Fishermen from either side make maximum catches during this period of the year.

"Because of a non-demarcated IMBL, the chances of fishermen straying into each other's territorial waters inadvertently are also more during this season," an ICG officer said.

Heading: Court summons V-C, top cop to appear on Nov 10 - Indian Express
Content:
The Sola police on Thursday arrested two persons for allegedly taking seven buffaloes and 10 bullocks to an illegal abattoir in Ahmedabad. The accused, identified as Razaq Majetha (35) from Bhuj and Dawood Gagda (22) from Dhandhuka, were arrested under the provisions of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and the IPC.

According to the police, an animal welfare organisation caught the duo near Sola Bhagwat on the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway while they were transporting the animals.

The NGO then handed over the duo to the Sola police.

The vehicle has been confiscated and the recovered animals have been sent to a cattle shed in Odhav. Further investigations are on.

Heading: In the backyard of law, notes of a scandal - Indian Express
Content:
The Metropolitan Magistrate on Thursday ordered the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone I) and Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor Parimal Trivedi to remain present in the court on November 10 in connection with a criminal case registered against the latter.

Pankaj Shrimali, a city-based professor, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste, has lodged a complaint against Trivedi under the provisions of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for allegedly making derogatory remarks about his caste. The Ahmedabad city police had filed a summary report in the case, which was challenged by Shrimali in the court. "In spite of the court notice, the DCP was not present in the court during the hearing," said Shrimali.

Heading: Books donated by Gaekwads lie in neglect at Central Library - Indian Express
Content:
Rare musical instruments donated by Gaekwads gather dust in police department

While many of the artifacts gifted and donated by the erstwhile Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad find place in the Vadodara and Fatehsinh museums, over 30 musical instruments are gathering dust in small rooms of the rural police department.

Shockingly, senior police officials there are said to be paying no heed to the requests made by the members of the police bands regarding the maintenance of these instruments.

"There are several musical instruments which are rare. But those at the helm of the affairs are not bothered about them. Since there are a limited number of band members, many instruments are not used regularly," said a band member requesting anonymity.

Some of the instruments are being repaired by the band members themselves, he added.

The instruments include Bells (a set of long metal pipes), Brass (an instrument whose tone is produced by the vibration of the lips as the player blows into a tubular resonator), Bass trumpet, B-Flat Clarinet, Alto Saxophone, and Euphonium among others. These were purchased by Sayajirao from different countries, which were donated to the police after Independence.

"The repairing of these instruments is difficult as it is done only at some places in Pune and Indore. The sponge, which is placed below the valves, if not used regularly, gets damaged. In many instruments, it has already been damaged. Also, the body of some of the clarinets had damaged which we have repaired locally," said a member of police band.

According to an official, the kind of musical notes which come out of these instruments are unmatched. "The new-age instruments do not have the quality and sweetness which these instruments have. Moreover, it is our duty to preserve the rich heritage gifted by the Maharaja. Unfortunately, sanctioning fund for their maintenance seems to be a difficult task for the government," the official added.

When asked about the condition of the instruments, Narendra Chaudhary, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Rural Police headquarters, said the department has some plans for their upkeep.

"We are going to have a new headquarter in the Chhani area for which the work is going on. Once we shift there, we would certainly ensure that these instruments are repaired and kept in proper condition," he said.

Heading: Cambridge University forms council to spread awareness about CIE - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Library of Vadodara may boast of a collection of 2.14 lakh books in its shelves, but there are 20,000 other historical books which lie in the state of neglect due to government apathy.

While on one hand the state government has its ambitious plans to have one library in each taluka of Gujarat, on the other hand, the antique collection is on the verge extinction due to the lack of proper equipment.

To save this collection — kept on the top floor of the library — from complete extinction, the library authorities had approached the state government for digitalisation of these books. But their effort seems to have gone in vain.

Talking to Newsline, library director Dr A F Sheikh said: "The process of digitalisation had to be postponed because we do not have the proper equipment for undertaking the project. Any concrete picture on the digitalisation can be drawn only after the next budget."

Even the library workers are apprehensive about handling these books.

"These books are not at all in a readable condition. Most of them crumble to dust even with a touch. No scientific preservation will be of help as some of them are not even in a condition to be photocopied. The only way to preserve them is a proper digitalisation," said a library worker.

While the library has a collection of 2.14 lakh books in six languages, including English, Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Urdu and Sindhi, these 20,000 books are not included in the library's book records.

"Maharaja Gaekwad was a voracious reader and a traveller, which helped him collect these books. All these books have been brought straight from the Maharaja's library," said a library official.
