Heading: International Congress calls for merging open, institutional mapping - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to spread awareness about its teaching in India, the University of Cambridge International Examination (CIE) has formed a Higher Education Advisory Council (HEAC).

The council comprises representatives from the National Council of Education and Research Training (NCERT), the Knowledge Commission besides 15 vice-chancellors of M S University and Sardar Patel University.

The HEAC recently made a two-day visit to the Cambridge University after it was invited to advice on the matter pertaining to CIE qualification, which is equivalent to HSc level in the Indian education system.

Ian Chamber, regional manager, South Asia, CIE, whose head office is in Delhi, told Newsline over telephone: "Two hundred schools across the country are affiliated to the CIE. Of these, 25 are from Gujarat. HEAC has been formed to advice CIE on all matters pertaining to CIE qualifications and Indian universities' acceptance to the provisional grades (of CIE pattern)."

He added: "An increasing number of NRI students affiliated to CIE are coming to India for higher education. Over the years, Indian students have been going abroad for further education. If students complete their higher secondary level education with schools affiliated to CIE, it will become easier for them to get access to other countries which follow a similar pattern."

CIE, a part of Cambridge University, was formed in 1988 to provide international qualification with their uniform level of teaching patterns in the UK, Europe, South Asia, Asia Pacific, North America, Central and South America, and Africa. The qualifications are mostly equivalent to the HSc pattern in India, which also provides access to students in other countries for higher education due to uniformity in its approach.

CIE has also written to the Gujarat State Education Department member secretary to create awareness in the administrative sections of universities as well training teachers at the HSc level so that they can opt for teaching in CIE affiliated sections.

Whereas institutes such as All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) have minimum criteria of 35 per cent for admission, some autonomous universities have not accepted it due to their autonomous nature of functioning, said B G Patel, Vice-Chancellor of the Sardar Patel University.

Patel added: "Some universities in Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Kolkata, Madras, as well as higher institutes such as Indian Institute of Management and Indian Institute of Technology that recognise the grades pattern. But some universities, also from Gujarat, do not enrol CIE students in professional courses such as medical, architecture and engineering."

Heading: Traffic Education Trust to solve city’s traffic problems - Indian Express
Content:
Three-day event organised by INCA, SAC concludes in Gandhinagar

Delegates at the 28th International Congress on 'Collaborative Mapping and Space Technology' have emphasised on the need for merging 'open' and 'institutional' mappings.

Open mapping refers to the concept of total public participatory mapping or 'crowd sourcing' as it is called in business terms, where each and every user is free to create, modify and rectify maps. On the other hand, institutional mapping is the generation of maps by various enterprises like Survey of India, National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation by using secure data transfer and grid computing.

The three-day Congress organised by the Indian National Cartographic Association (INCA) and ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC) Ahmedabad, concluded in Gandhinagar on Thursday.

P K Srivastava, Deputy Director Signal and Image Processing SAC, who is also the current President of INCA, said: "This congress has deliberated upon new modes of mapping in a collaborative fashion using the technology of Web 2.0. It concluded that the oven fresh theme is generating a Geomatics application for providing accurate, efficient, robust, and affordable orthorectification solution."

He also outlined cartographic research, creation of map awareness among masses, promotion of geo-spatial industry and securing legitimate place for cartography as some of the major aims of INCA.

A K Das Gupta of Bhaskaracharya Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics, Gandhinagar said: "We should realise that a major revamp is required in the geo-spatial industry. Institutional mapping is fine but availability to masses must be ensured."

Gupta stressed that open mapping models like Google Earth succeeded because it fulfilled a latent need felt by the masses.

Brig Manoj Tayal of the Survey of India said the Public Private Participatory model of mapping is the inevitable need of the industry. "The convergence model of mapping must be introduced now," he said.

Tayal was supported by Prof Armin Gruen of Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, Zurich who also delivered a key-note address on '3D Mapping from Space.'

Gruen said: "Data merging by the two modes of mapping is not recommended, but data sharing is a must. With the availability of advanced technology, even generating highly accurate 3D maps has become possible now."

Heading: Mumbai ATS picks up active member of Hindu Jagran Manch - Indian Express
Content:
Perfect Bebo
It takes quite something to impress perfectionist Aamir Khan. So we understand how fit Kareena Kapoor actually is when Aamir compliments her on her great body. Bebo, who is a fitness freak, left quite an impact on Aamir with her well-toned body and her devotion to her workouts. He was also impressed by her professionalism as she shot in Ladakh's cold climate without a single complaint. The two stars are working together on Raju Hirani's Three Idiots. This is their first film together and unit members are already talking about how well the two have hit it off with each other.

Salman on a roll
SALMAN Khan was quite the charmer on the sets of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2009, where he appeared with the current love of his life, Katrina Kaif. The picture perfect couple appeared as an 'item' for the first time on Indian television and made everyone's day as they waltzed together to the song Teri Ore, from Kat's hit movie Singh is Kinng. But the star of the day was Khan, who was at his flamboyant best, dancing with the contestants, playing cupid between them.

Popcorn break
Himesh Reshammiya may have gotten tired of living on tandoori food but he ain't giving up his diet just yet. The actor, who lost over eight kilos for his recent release, Karzzzz, is working hard towards maintaining his physique. The singer-music-director-actor was seen munching on popcorn during the shoot of a popular reality show. Every time the camera was not on him, Reshammiya would get up from his seat and start hogging on the tub of munchies placed right next to him. The Bollywood hunks need to watchout — Reshammiya could just be the next six-pack guy.

Heading: Readymade Printed Circuit Board may provide clue in Modasa blast - Indian Express
Content:
Sunil used to act as Sadhvi Pragya's chauffer during her stay at Sabrikumbh fair in 2005

The Mumbai Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) picked up an active member of the Hindu Jagran Manch from Vapi, who was earlier associated with Swami Ashimanandji Maharaj at his Ashram in Subir village in Ahwa Taluka of Dangs district. Sources said the ATS has now taken him to Mumbai for further interrogation.

The ATS picked up Sunil Dhawade (30) from a packaging factory in Vapi GIDC on Wednesday afternoon, after keeping a watch on him for three days. Sunil, a resident of Ambapada village in Ahwa Taluka of Dangs district, was earlier working at Sabrikumbh with the Maharaj, who runs the Vanvasi Kalyan Ashram at Subir village.

Sunil left his job with Swamiji and started working in a packaging company at Vapi GIDC, for the last three months. The reason behind him leaving the job is not known though.

Apparently, Sunil is an active member of Hindu Jagran Manch and Vishwa Hindu Parishad in Dangs.

Sources said that Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur had stayed at the Sabrikumbh fair for a couple of weeks in 2005. Sadhvi was close to Swamiji and Sunil used to act as her chauffer during her stay here.

Sources said that Swamiji had left the ashram and had gone underground after the arrest of Sadhvi Pragya. While searching for Swamiji, the ATS picked up Sunil as he was considered closest to him.

After taking Sunil's address from Swamiji's ashram in Subri, the ATS went to his house in Ambapada village. The officers identified themselves as hotel businessmen from Mumbai and told Sunil's father Arjun Dhawde that Sunil had earlier shown them a land to start a hotel business. Arjunbhai gave Sunil's mobile number and address at Vapi to the officers, after which the ATS picked him up with help of their Vapi counterparts.

The ATS officers interrogated Sunil for a couple of hours at the Vapi police station and later left for Mumbai with him.

Valsad District Superintendent of Police D J Patel said: "Our officers assisted the Mumbai police in picking up Sunil. We are working out to find Sunil's history and his contacts."

Meanwhile, Sunil's father said: "We have not been informed by the officers about my son's whereabouts. We don't even know the reason why he was picked up. The police contacted me identifying themselves as hotel businessmen and they took the phone number and address of my son."

Heading: High voltage destroys 100 fridges, 50 TV sets in Vadodara - Indian Express
Content:
The Sabarkantha police, who are yet to find a lead in the September 29 Modasa blast case, may get lucky finally, if they manage to track the origin of a readymade Printed Circuit Board (PCB) used in the timer circuit of the bomb. Unlike assembled PCBs, the manufacture of a readymade PCB, according to forensic experts, can be tracked with the help of its specific manufacturing design and serial number.

Experts in the Physics Department of the Directorate of Forensic Sciences (DFS) at Gandhinagar say the readymade PCB consists of two Philips Integrated Circuits (ICs), and some capacitors and resistors mounted on a circuit board in a particular order (which is quintessential of a manufacturing unit).

"It was a readymade multi-purpose PCB that could be used as an oscillator, a counter or a timer. The non-programmable Philips ICs used in the circuit are respectively 4060 and 4040 types," said an expert.

He added: "We have short-listed the names of some companies that manufacture PCBs of these types. The list had also been handed over to the Sabarkantha police and they are trying to track the final recipient of the PCB under examination. Though this can be a difficult task, it is not impossible."

Deputy Superintendent of police K K Mysorewala, who is heading the investigations into the case, did not divulge any details, saying "these are operational secrets."

Earlier, chemical experts of the DFS had confirmed the use of only gunpowder, and had completely ruled out the use of RDX or ammonium nitrate in the Modasa blast samples collected from the site. The timer circuit, which had split into five parts in the explosion, was being examined in the Physics laboratory in the DFS. The DFS is likely to hand over its complete report to the Sabarkantha police soon.

Unlike the bombs that exploded in Ahmedabad on July 26 and those found un-detonated in Surat, the Modasa bomb, according to DFS experts, was a simple Improvised Explosion Devise (IED).

"Gunpowder, packed tightly inside a cast-iron container, was the main explosive. While a simple detonator was used as the primer that initiated the ignition, a ready-made PCB was used as a non-programmable timer. An ordinary motorcycle battery was used to complete this circuit," said a senior scientist supervising the forensic examination.

The Modasa police, who were disappointed on the inability of the forensic experts to decipher the original chassis number of the stolen Hero Honda Passion motorcycle used in the blast, are now counting on finding the manufacturers of the PCB to get to the final buyer.

Heading: Asaram gurukul case: Parents, NGOs opt not to submit affidavits before Trivedi Commission - Indian Express
Content:
Much to the shock of the Ambikanagar society residents at Gotri Road, nearly 100 refrigerators and 50 television sets burst due to voltage fluctuation after two conductors got stuck with each other on Thursday.

While the Madhya Gujarat Vij Company Limited (MGVCL) authorities shrugged off the responsibility to the sudden rise in the electricity voltage, residents said they would take up the issue with the MGVCL office, if they were not paid compensation.

Rakesh Patel, Ambikanagar Society president, said: "Most of the people in the society belong to the middle class and they cannot afford such a major loss. So, we intend to take up the issue with the state Power Ministry and MGVCL."

K I Dalwadi, Junior Engineer, MGVCL, Gotri zone, told Newsline, "A spark occurred between two conductors at Gotri when they came in contact with each other after a kite twine got entangled with the wires."

When inquired about the regular monitoring which the MGVCL is supposed to do, he said, "We will inquire into the issue."

Residents, meanwhile, said they have been facing the high voltage problem for the last many days, but no one paid heed to this. Alkesh Patel, a resident who works as a medical assistant in an ambulance, said, "Initially I thought it was the sound of firecrackers on Dev Diwali, but to my surprise, it was my TV set which was in rubble and covered with smoke."

Heading: No student in Asaram Bapu’s congregation in Vadodara this time - Indian Express
Content:
In a surprising development, the parents of the two minor boys at the Asaram Ashram gurukul who were found dead in the Sabarmati riverbed on July 5, as well as the NGOs which actively agitated for securing justice for the family of the victims, have not submitted their affidavits before the Justice D K Trivedi Commission.

The Justice Trivedi Commission was appointed by the Gujarat government on July 21 to inquire into the facts and circumstances leading to the deaths of the two boys and the police investigations into the case.

The commission was appointed following a massive public agitation against the investigations and the Ashram run gurukul at Motera from where the two boys went missing under mysterious circumstances on July 3. Praful and Shantilal Vaghela, the father of the two boys, had then sat on an indefinite hunger strike.

An official associated with the commission said: "It is very shocking and surprising that the people who were quite vocal during the massive public agitation to get justice for the two deceased boys, have not come forward when a judicial inquiry has been set up for the same. Even the parents of the two children have not provided the commission any information in the case."

On being asked why he had not filed any affidavit before the commission, Praful Vaghela said, "Mentally, I am yet to come out of the shock of losing two sons of the family."

Elsewhere, Ashok Jain, an office bearer of the Akhil Bhartiya Mahajan Parivar, an NGO, purportedly said: "The mysterious act of the two Vaghela brothers to break their fasts before the chief minister and discontinue the agitation is very objectionable. Therefore, we have detached ourselves from them. We are not concerned with the issue anymore, and do not want to submit anything before the commission."

Prakash Kapadiya, the president of Jagega Gujarat Sangharsh Samiti, an NGO, which actively participated in the agitation, said he is not an eye-witness to either the missing act of the two boys or the subsequent recovery of their bodies from the Sabarmati riverbed. "Therefore, we cannot submit anything before the commission," he said.

Sources said the commission has received more than 500 affidavits ever since it was set up. The initial time frame for the commission ended on October 20, though it has been given a six-month extension till April 20, 2009.

Sources also said that now the commission is planning to issue summons to the Vaghelas and the organisations associated with the agitation to appear before it.

Heading: Cops detain 4 protestors of Asaram’s discourse - Indian Express
Content:
The usually jam-packed congregations of Asaram Bapu will see empty spaces this time when he comes to the city between November 9 and 13, after the District Education Officer (DEO) reportedly refused to permit students from attending the same.

Throughout the day, Vadodara DEO R K Patel played hide and seek with the followers of Asaram, who were desperately seeking permission to allow schools to send their students to the discourse.

After two followers of Asaram Bapu approached the DEO on Thursday, and sought his permission to allow school children to attend the congregation, they were not just refused permission, but were also turned down from meeting R K Patel directly.

The reason given to them by the DEO was that the on-going Diwali vacation has made it difficult to gather the students. But, the unsolved controversy over the death of two minor boys at the Ashram run gurukul is being cited as a possible deterrent.

A similar invitation was sent across to school students the last time he was in the city and a number of students were sent to the congregation then.

Heading: RBI detects Rs 95.40-crore scam after SBI-SBS merger - Indian Express
Content:
The Raopura police have detained four people, including two women, from Vadodara and Ahmedabad in a bid to prevent any sort of disturbance during Asaram Bapu's five-day discourse starting November 9.

Those detained are Amrut Prajapati and his wife Saroj Prajapati (residents of Prathmesh Plaza, Kirti Stambh), Hansa Patel of Haatkeshwar area, and Rohit Rajput of Atladara near Vadodara.

Prior to the congregation, the followers of Asaram Bapu had organised a 'bhajan kirtan yatra.' The four had threatened to immolate themselves if the yatra or the discourse took place.

"We were already informed that the four would protest against the congregation. When the yatra was near the Mama ni pol in Raopura area, we detained them," said a Raopura police station officer.

Heading: Rural projects worth Rs 32 cr in doldrums - Indian Express
Content:
Currency chest was operated by cashier and accountant, but case registered only against cashier

Two months after the grand merger of over 420 branches of the State Bank of Saurashtra with the State Bank of India, the Reserve Bank of India has unearthed a Rs 95.40-crore scam from the Bhavnagar branch of the former, when it was the headquarter of the erstwhile SBS.

A case of fraud and cheating has been registered against head cashier Kirit Purohit for misappropriation of cash even as the police have not ruled out the possibility of involvement of more people in the crime.

The currency chest was operated under the joint custody of the cashier and the accountant, but the case has been registered against Purohit only. Incidentally, the bank authorities have also made Purohit file an affidavit to the police accepting responsibility for the scam.

According to reports, an inspection by an RBI vigilance wing revealed that the scam began in April at the Nilam Baug branch, and continued till November 6, when cash was withdrawn in installments from the currency chest.

The seven-month old scam remained under carpet even when the merger took place in August, the report said.

The complaint registered by SBI Nilam Baug branch assistant branch manager Anil Mule accused Purohit of illegally using withdrawal slips and not depositing money submitted in the bank deposited by a current account holder. The complaint has been lodged under Sections 420, 409, 406 and 403 of the IPC.

Deputy Superintendent of Police P Bharada said "investigations are on and Purohit has been subjected to interrogation."

The A-Division police, with whom the complaint has been lodged, said that Purohit siphoned off cash to the tune of Rs 82.5 lakh during April-November, through 40,000 notes of Rs 100 domination, 4,000 notes of Rs 500 domination and 2,250 notes of Rs 1,000 domination. Besides, he also withdrew Rs 6.60 lakh through withdrawal slips.

It has also been accused that Purohit did not deposit Rs 6.3 lakh to the account of current account holder Asian Gems, though a receipt in this regard has been issued.

SBS was one of the associate banks of SBI. The State Bank of Saurashtra started as Bhavnagar Darbar Bank, which was established in 1902. Bhavnagar was one of the princely states of the Saurashtra region of Gujarat. In 1948, when the princely states were integrated to form the Saurashtra state, a need for the state-owned bank was felt. Accordingly, the Bhavnagar Darbar Bank was formed into a statutory corporation, called the State Bank of Saurashtra. Four Darbar Banks — Rajkot State Bank, Porbandar State Bank, Palitana Darbar Bank and Vadia State Bank were merged with it. In 1960, the State Bank of Saurashtra joined the State Bank family as one of its fully owned subsidiaries. This enabled the State Bank of Saurashtra to expand its operations by using the network of the State Bank Group to further its business activities.

Heading: BJP leader arrested in six-year-old corruption case - Indian Express
Content:
Files await clearance from Congress-led District Panchayat where BJP forms the body

Rural development projects worth several crores in Rajkot are awaiting implementation as they are yet to get the green signal from the District Panchayat general board.

The files of these projects worth Rs 32 crore are gathering dust because of a complicated power sharing situation in the district panchayat — the Congress heads it while the BJP forms its body. Even routine works in the panchayat have now been jeopardised as the two parties pull in different directions.

In January, the BJP applied brakes on the Congress rule by snatching away six of its councillors. The reverse horse trading saw the Congress drawing in seven BJP councillors into its fold in May.

The result: the Congress with 22 members in the house of 37 has its president in Bhavna Balgha and also a clear majority in the general board. But the executive committee and six other vital committees are under control of the BJP.

This has been the apparent reason for the lack of coordination in the executive committee that forwards development projects for clearance to the general board. With the BJP having an upper hand in building construction and water supply committees, these committees are almost dead for quite some time now.

In May, when the Congress regained majority, a stay was ordered by the state Planning Commission Office on a resolution passed by the general board to dissolve the executive committee with all the BJP members and form a new one.

While the Congress has moved the Supreme Court in this regard, the state government is now gearing up to find a legal solution to clear the projects.

District Development Officer Jayprakahs Shivhare said: "A meeting was called on Wednesday in Gandhinagar to discuss the problem. Members of the Planning Commission; secretary, water supply and secretary, building construction attended the meeting. Legal help would be sought in this regard."

The BJP had taken over the control of all the seven committees in January when six Congress members crossed over to it soon after the December Assembly elections. The Congress, which had come to power in 2005 with 22 members, lost control over all the committees when six of its members, including state unit vice-president Hardevsinh Jadeja joined the BJP.

Before the BJP could topple Balgha, nine BJP members — P G Vaghasia, Bharat Parmar, Banuben Jetapara, Jagdish Koria, Deepa Kumwaria, Jasu Kakrecha, Navghanu Meghani, Ushaben Vachani and Sobhana Ramolia — joined the Congress in April. With the majority again by its side, Balgha announced voting over resolution number eight which was about dissolving the existing committee and forming a new one.

Heading: SP leaders file nomination for RS poll - Indian Express
Content:
In an embarrassment to the Bharatiya Janata Party in Saurashtra, party leader Hasmukh Gambhva has been arrested by the Jamnagar Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on charges of corruption filed against him six years ago while he was the director of the Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank.

Also a member of the working committee of the Aamaran-based Aadarsh cooperative society, Gambhva is accused of having duping the state government of Rs 28.94 lakh after producing fraudulent documents. Besides, he was also found to have involved in corruption in the 2001 earthquake relief schemes.

Gambhva was arrested on Wednesday and sent behind bars. ACB Inspector (Jamnagar) J J Dhranga said: "He was produced before the court and has now been sent in judicial custody in the Jamnagar Jail."

Apparently, Gambhva had fought a by-election from the Jodiya-Dhrol Assembly constituency on a BJP ticket and

lost it.

The Jamnagar ACB police said, Gambhva, a resident of Aamaran village, faces corruption charges in two cases (no. 09/ 2002 and 04/2003) under Sections 120(B), 196, 197, 198, 199, 407, 417, 419, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian penal code and under Sections 13 (1) (C) and 13(3) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

ACB officers said, after the 2001 earthquake, Gambhava and his associates withdrew subsidy amount, loans and compensation amount, provided to shopkeepers by the state government as part of the earthquake relief scheme.

Besides, he had also produced fake transportation bills for removing debris from earthquake hit areas. Gambhva was found to have played a pivotal role in these corrupt practices, they said.

On being asked, why Gambhva was being arrested now though cases were registered against him in 2002 and 2003, Dhranga said the investigation was under progress till now.

Heading: Kept waiting for his paan, Lucknow cop shoots vendor - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday raised its objection to providing reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) besides Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in elections to panchayats and municipal bodies, without having adequate data on OBCs and the intended beneficiaries.

A five-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, examining the Constitutional validity of the 73rd and 74th amendments, sought to know from the Government's counsel how the scheme could be carried forward in the absence of data for OBCs and without excluding the creamy layer. These amendments provide for reservation for backward classes and women in addition to the SCs and STs for the local bodies' election.

Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramanium referred to the Mandal Commission report to prove the existence of backward classes which he said had been recognised by the apex court in the Indra Sawhney (Mandal case) and Ashoka Thakur (OBC quota in educational institution) judgments.

However, the Bench observed that if reservation was extended without excluding the creamy layer, it would mean that the scheme was caste-based.

Heading: Amar Singh declares assets worth Rs 37 cr - Indian Express
Content:
Reiterating that the hate attacks on north Indians in Maharashtra were an internal disturbance which the state had failed to contain, the Supreme Court on Thursday underlined that it was a serious issue and it would like to consider it for passing appropriate directions. However, for the want of a "serious" petition, the Bench headed by Justice B N Aggarwal gave the petitioner time to amend the petition and come next week.

The petition by advocate Sanjeev Kumar Singh, which came up on Thursday, will now be tagged along with another petition by advocate Sugriva Dubey on the same issue on November 10. However, before agreeing to post the petition for hearing next week, the three-member Bench expressed its annoyance at the unabated attacks against north Indians. "What is the difference between north Indians and Indians?... We are all Indians," asserted the Bench as the advocate was trying to convince the Court to pass some directions, which shall put an end to the attacks.

The PIL had sought a judicial inquiry into the killing of Patna youth Rahul Raj in an alleged police encounter and the murder of another north Indian in Mumbai last month.

However, like in the previous petition, the apex court again felt that the petitions were not drafted "seriously" and it would entertain a petition, which raise this issue "seriously". "The petition you have filed is very light (in terms of contents)," observed one of the judges, suggesting the counsel amend the pleas in the petition.

The Constitutional provision of Article 355 caught the attention of the Bench even on Thursday. It asked the advocate if he knew what the provision meant. He was asked to read from the statute, which he promptly did in the court, appearing particularly interested in the provision which empowers the Central Government to give necessary directions to the state to prevent such incidents.

Heading: BJP youth wing to be trained by RSS seniors - Indian Express
Content:
Samajwadi Party (SP) general secretary Amar Singh has revealed that he and his family members have movable and immovable properties and valuables worth Rs 37 crore.

On Thursday, Singh filed an affidavit of his properties and other assets along with his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha elections. Singh said that he had already paid an income tax of Rs 1.99 crore during the current fiscal year along with Rs 60,735, as wealth tax to the government.

An income tax of Rs 11.93 lakh, however, was still pending, the affidavit read.  Singh also did not have any valuables or funds in the name of his twin daughters Disha and Drishti except for a LIC of Rs 2.5 lakh each.

According to the affidavit, Amar Singh and his wife Pankaja have Rs 10 lakh cash in hand. While bank deposits of Singh figures at Rs 3.47 crore, his wife's stands at Rs 2.25 crore.

The family has bonds, debentures and shares worth Rs 16.60 crore, while they have PPF, NSS and LIC worth Rs 7.06 lakh.

The SP general secretary owns two vehicles, including a Toyota Land cruiser, while they have jewellery including diamonds worth Rs 3.32 crore. They have also got watches, furniture's, mutual funds and others amounting to Rs 8.23 crore.

As per the details about the immovable assets given in the affidavit, they have agricultural land worth Rs 50 lakh, a plot in Noida's sector-44 worth Rs 1.75 crore, two flats at Greater Kailash of Rs 1 crore each, one flat each at Bangalore and Koltaka valued Rs 7 crore, a commercial building at Kasturba Gandhi Marg Delhi valued Rs 1crore, a bunglow in Lucknow of Rs 2.8 crore and a house in Azamgarh worth Rs 9 lakh.

Ram Gopal Yadav, another general secretary of the Samajwadi Party — first cousin of party president Mulayam Singh Yadav — has properties and valuable worth Rs 71 lakh. 

Yadav possesses land worth Rs 32.43 lakh, a plot in Vrindavan housing scheme in Lucknow and a house each in Sefai in Etawah and Agra having a total worth of Rs 23.69 lakh.

He also has three firearms worth Rs 1.20 lakh and air conditioners valued Rs 2.83 lakh.

Heading: Police yet to identify the man they shot - Indian Express
Content:
With the Lok Sabha polls round the corner, it's time for the juniors of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to get back to basics.

The party's youth wing, Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), will be organising a two-day training camp at Mirzapur. This camp will witness senior party leaders, who have been associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh (RSS), delivering lectures about the RSS views and its association with the national political party.

In order to regain the lost ground in the state, the party has come out with a new strategy. While the BJP senior leaders will be a part of all the RSS meets — scheduled from November 21 in Lucknow — the RSS leaders will be training the party youngsters.

The two-day camp will see 350 workers of the BJYM being trained by eminent RSS leaders. According to party sources, such a camp is being organised after six years with the aim to increase the awareness among the new and young members about the ideologies preached by the RSS and BJP.

Speaking to The Indian Express, the state president of the BJYM and former member of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidhyarthi Parishad Dayashankar Singh, said: "Since the elections are approaching, the need was felt to train all the young members about the basic ideologies of the party."

Those who will be delivering lectures include Ram Pyare Pandey, national coordinator of BJP training wing; Rakesh Jain, former RSS prant pracharak; BJP state general secretary Nagendra Nath and state spokesperson and vice-president H N Dixit.

Heading: Tech institute ready to fly on GARUDA - Indian Express
Content:
The identity of a person gunned down within an hour of the robbery at the residence of jewellery shop owner in Thakurganj is yet to be established.

The police maintain that the deceased was a member of the gang that had conducted the heist and the recovered items, including jewellery, were part of the loot.

The police are digging out the details of the miscreants involved in similar incidents. The burglary had taken place at the home of Om Prakash Aggarwal, owner of Khunkhunji jewellers, in the early hours of Wednesday. Aggarwal's wife Usha Rani (65), who had tried to resist, was beaten up and she died later in hospital.

"While conducting searches near the house, we spotted some people, who on seeing us, began running away," said K P Singh, in-charge, Thakurganj police station. "When we asked them to stop, one of them fired at us. We were forced to retaliate and the man was killed." He added that Aggarwal had identified the jewellery recovered from the deceased.

The police maintain that the incident was planned, as the miscreants were well aware of the layout of the house.

"We have evidence that they escaped by the rear entrance, but it is still not clear how they managed to enter," said a senior officer attached with the Thakurganj police station.

Circle Officer, Chowk, Vinay Chandra said, "We suspect that three to five persons were involved in the theft". The statement of two watchmen and a domestic help has been recorded.

"They denied seeing any of the miscreants," Chandra said, "they claimed that on hearing some noise, one of the watchmen called up Om Prakash's son". The postmortem report of the person gunned down by the police states that death occurred due to fire arm injury, while Om Prakash's wife died of a head injury.

Heading: Doctors trained in systematic use of drugs - Indian Express
Content:
THE researchers at the Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology can now use GARUDA - the state-of-the-art computational grid project linking prestigious research and academic institutions across the country.

The institute will be the first in the state to have this computational facility, which links 17 top research institutions of the country. Highly secure Virtual Private Network has been installed for data protection.

"A grid allows us to solve complex problems that may take long otherwise. It provides high speed and seamless access to other supercomputers," said Prof Krishna Kant, who played an important role in bringing the facility to the institute.

It is an aggregation of heterogeneous and geographically distributed resources - computing, storage and special equipment.

Its aim is to share research resources to facilitate their optimal utilisation, said Prof AK Misra, Dean (Planning and Development) and Head of the Computer Science and Engineering Department.

Through GARUDA, the participating institutions can access 48 nodes, including super computers. "The intricate analysis required in chemistry, biology and computer sciences can now be performed easily through GARUDA," said Prof Kant.

According to him, countries like India are in

dire need of such computational grids, as no institution can individually bear the cost of their installation and operation .

The project was funded by the Department of Information Technology and was developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, Pune.

The institute already has the state-of-art super computer, Param, and with the addition of this computational grid, revolutionary changes in research are on the cards.

Heading: UPTU to send report of ward’s attendance  to guardians - Indian Express
Content:
Recognising the rampant wrong treatment of tuberculosis patients, around 400 doctors were trained in systemic use of drugs at the 10th conference of National College of Chest Physicians and Indian Chest Society on Thursday.

According to a study of "Prescription Patterns of Second-Line Drugs in Chronic Pulmonary Tuberculosis" conducted by CSMMU doctors, lack of awareness among the private doctors about the proper use of first and second line treatment of TB has resulted in extreme drug resistant cases. There are also

indications of misuse of drugs increasing the risk of TB drug resistance.

The experts say that such resistance occurs either due to patients leaving off the treatment in the middle or due to wrong presciption by the doctors — giving higher intensity of drugs at initial stages.

Often false medication and half treatment leads to Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB) — a strain of tuberculosis — which is resistant to at least two main first-line TB drugs — isoniazid and rifampicin.

Such MDR cases are given a second-line treatment. But, when MDR-TB cases become resistant to second-line drugs, they are put under Extreme Drug Resistance (XDR-TB) cases. These cases are extremely difficult to cure. There is still no standardised mechanisim in the country even to monitor XDR cases.

The first study conducted in 2007 on first-line drug use revealed that around 50 to 70 per cent of private doctors in Lucknow and adjoining areas were prescribing wrong drugs for first-line treatment of TB.

Following this study, the CSMMU doctors conducted another three-month preliminary study for the second-line drug use.

The study brought out some alarming facts about doctors once again prescribing wrong medication in the second-line drug treatment.

"In the days to come, extreme drug resistance TB will be a major threat for the country," said Dr Rajendra Prasad, President of the Indian Chest Society and also the Head of Department of pulmonary medicine at CSMMU.

"It was alarming to find that a large number of suspected MDR patients were given second-line drugs for a period of more than a month. Thereby increasing the risk of more severe type of resistance to TB drugs — XDR-TB," he added.

Prasad said that multi-drug resistance cases should be given the second-line treatment in order to avoid XDR cases. In the recent study, the researchers included 45 cases of chronic pulmonary tuberculosis. It was found that of these, while there were 9 confirmed cases of MDR, there were 36 cases of suspected MDR.

Of these 36 suspected cases of MDR, at least 26 patients were already given second-line of drug treatment for over a month.

As per the World Health Organisation guidelines, those multi-drug resistant patients who have taken the second-line treatment for more than a month are not included in the DOTS programme of Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme.

Heading: BSP names 6 candidates for Rajya Sabha polls - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure a minimum of 75 per cent attendance of all the engineering as well as management students, the Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU) has decided to apprise the guardians every month about the attendance of their wards. 

The institute has issued circulars to the principals and directors of all the affiliated technical and management colleges in this connection.

The circular also directs the college authorities to ensure regular attendance of the students. An official said in the first two months of the ongoing academic session, it has been found that a number of students remained absent without taking any prior leave from the college.

"As per the norms, classes should be held at least 90 days in any academic session. For students, it is mandatory that they attend 75 per cent of the lectures in one academic session," said J P Pandey, Additional Controller of Examination, UPTU. "This step has been taken to avoid guardians' complaints that their wards have been regular in college, when the reality is that they often skip classes," he added.

Pandey said those students whose attendance is found to be less than 60 per cent in the first two months of the current academic session, would be listed with their attendance record sent to the parents.

Officials said that taking advantage of the short attendance, college employees exploit the students before their examinations. According to Pandey, this system can be successful only when the university and the guardians monitor the attendance record of the students.

UPTU Vice-Chancellor Professor Prem Vrat said the decision to inform the guardians about their respective ward's attendance was in the interest of the students.

"When students become aware that their attendance report could be sent to guardians, they will automatically be regular in attending classes."

Heading: Karchana power project: lowest price higher than first bid - Indian Express
Content:
The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati announced the names of six candidates on Thursday for the biennial elections to the Rajya Sabha slated on November 21.

The candidates will file their nominations on Friday.

Of the candidates, four are from the Scheduled Castes and two from upper castes — one from the Bania community and the other a Brahmin.

The candidates are Veer Singh from Moradabad, a sitting member of the Rajya Sabha and party in-charge in Maharashtra, Avtar Singh Karimpuri, the state president of Punjab, Rajaram, the sitting member of the state Legislative Council whose term ends in January, former parliamentarian from the Lok Sabha Brijlala Khaabari, former Congress union minister Akhilesh Das and Lok Sabha member from Unnao Brijesh Pathak.

With its strength of 216 members in Uttar Pradesh assembly, the five BSP candidates are expected to sail through.

The party will have 31 spare votes and for the victory of its sixth candidate, it will need six more. It hopes to mobilise the additional votes from Independents.

In her statement, Mayawati said Das will be contending for the Lucknow Lok Sabha seat in the next parliamentary elections.

Brajesh Pathak is currently working to bring the Brahmins in UP, Delhi and Uttarakhand into the party's fold. The party, Mayawati said, will field another Brahmin candidate from the Unnao Lok Sabha seat in place of Pathak.

Rajaram was caught in a controversy in August, when the media concluded that he was the successor of Mayawati. Rajaram, who was the party's vice-president, was immediately shown the door. He is currently the party in-charge in Madhya Pradesh.

Heading: UP gets 3 point in a drawn match - Indian Express
Content:
It was an expensive search for the state government, which was on the lookout for a private sector company offering low tariff for the 1,200 MW Karchana thermal power project in Allahabad.

After the third bidding on Thursday, the lowest price quoted for the thermal power project was found to be far higher than what was quoted the first time.

The first global tender for the Karchana project was floated in December 2007. Five bids were received for the project, of which, Lanco emerged as the successful bidder with the lowest tariff of Rs 2.83 per unit. This round of bidding was

cancelled by the state government, as the price was found to be too high.

The bids were floated for the second time in June 2008, where Reliance Power emerged as the successful bidder with a tariff of Rs 2.60 per unit. The state government once again scrapped the bidding process without assigning any reason.

For the third time, the bids were floated in September. The Jai Prakash Associates emerged as the front-runner to grab the power project offering a tariff of Rs 2.97 per unit.

The levellised tariff of JP Associates for 25 years was found to be the lowest by the consultant Feedback Ventures Pvt Ltd, followed by the Adani enterprise at Rs 2.98, Lanco Infratech Ltd at Rs 3.18 per unit and Reliance Power Ltd at Rs 3.98 per unit.

According to an official release issued by the UP Power Corporation Limited, the consultant will soon submit its report to the bidding evaluation committee. Later, they will submit its report to the state government for further action.

Heading: Sizzling Stuff - Indian Express
Content:
Meet a Japanese national who is a Hindi-bhashi

It's heart over technology. Hailing from the tech capital of the world, Fuminori Yokote, First Secretary, Political Affairs, Embassy of Japan, surprises you with his fluent Hindi, a language he mastered putting his heart into it. "English is a chord that binds people of the world, but a local language is a rooted in culture and traditions. Yeh dilon ko nikat laati hai," he says with a smile.

"Way back in 1991, I was sent by the government of Japan to learn Hindi, keeping in mind my subsequent posting in India. What better place could there be than Allahabad for anyone pursuing an education in Hindi. So, there I was, enrolled in the Allahabad University. Under the wings of masters like Dr Ram Swarup Chaturvedi and Meera Srivastava, I began learning Hindi right from 'ka, kha, ga'," fondly recalls the envoy.

His first lessons were actually in Kobe, his native place in Japan, thanks to "helpful friends like Mr & Mrs Kukreja and Ashwini Mishra, a Doordarshan employee who was in a deputation to Japan to learn some techniques from NHK, the Nippon broadcasting agency."

In India, he was put up in the International Centre of the Allahabad University, where he learnt not just in the classroom but on the streets too. "I couldn't have chosen a better destination. The people were so warm, friendly and helpful. Even my teachers allowed me to take the lessons at their residence when the university was closed during the Mandal Commission protest," recalls Yokote.

Japan, he says, holds India in high regard, since its culture and traditions are rooted here. "The government is extending aid for road development in Shravasti, Buddhist Circuit and also in poverty elimination," he says, explaining how/where his knowledge of Hindi comes in handy.

Has his family learnt a word or two? He chuckles. "I have two kids and they are too young to learn new languages. My wife is just about comfortable with English."

Asked if the exchange is mutual and if he teaches Nihong, his mother tongue to his teachers of Hindi too, he answers in affirmative. And goaded to part with a nugget, he gives the meaning of Takashi, the name of his son. "It means respect. My daughter's name, Yui...well, I am not very sure how it can be translated."

He is on a Hindi trip, after all!

Heading: Seriously funny - Indian Express
Content:
The production of 600-MW power at Rajiv Gandhi Thermal Power would start three months before its schedule, said Haryana Power Minister Randeep Singh Surjewala.

Heading: Funny side up - Indian Express
Content:
How did you work out the theme for Mumbai Calling?
Producer Allan McKeown was interested in setting a comedy in a call centre in India. I started writing a movie some years ago set in a call centre, which I had abandoned to pursue other projects. I already had some homework done. It all seemed a natural fit to dust off those ideas into this new project and develop a situation comedy. Nitin Ganatra as an actor and Simon Blackwell as writer are both friends and colleagues, so I was able to bring them on board and they added to the series.

What's your character Kenny Gupta like?
Kenny Gupta is a British born Indian who has never been to India and, although he looks like everybody else, he's still a fish out of water and is constantly looking forward to the day he can return to his cold, rainy, depressing bit of London.

Yet another attempt at speaking out against racism?
My work has always been about playing with people's perceptions of stereotypes from Goodness Gracious Me through The Kumars at Number 42 through to the documentary series India with Sanjeev Bhaskar, and I hope also with my contribution to Mumbai Calling.

How different is the racism scene in UK now?
Better than it was when my parents came here. After President Obama, who knows we may have an Indian Prime Minister of the UK too.

Given the current economic scenario and the international take on outsourcing to India, is there not a possibility that the show might face criticism?
Mumbai Calling is entertainment and thus employs dramatic license. It isn't a documentary so any criticism other than from an entertainment point of view I think is pointless.

Your wife, Meera Syal, has not been a part of Mumbai Calling. What is she up to?
Meera has been writing movie scripts and acting in a comedy on British TV, called Beautiful People, so she's kept busy.

What do you think of comedies from India?
As mass appeal, comedy in India struck me as sometimes lacking in sophistication but this certainly seems to be changing in recent times, particularly in the films. We have a generation in India now that can not only compete with the West in terms of commerce but also entertainment.

The adaptation of international formats of laughter shows has triggered many series here. Comment.
I can't comment on any specific one except perhaps The Kumars format that was tried in India. In my experience the problem with buying the format is that what one buys is the end result not the experience that goes with it.

What makes a good joke—a situation or a punch line?
Both make a good joke, a combination of the two, make a great one.

Who are your favourite comedians?
Marx brothers, Woody Allen, Monty Python, Peter Sellers, Robin Williams, and the list goes on. At the moment my three-year-old son, Shaan makes me laugh more than anyone else.

(Mumbai Calling airs on HBO from November 8)

Heading: Acts of Grace - Indian Express
Content:
Azhar Usman is called Osama Bin Laughin' for a reason

He's the man who had Pervez Musharraf in splits at a sit-down dinner in Dallas in September 2006. Azhar Usman, a 32-year-old, Chicago-based, stand-up comedian whom CNN recently named "American's Funniest Muslim", is preparing for his first professional outing in India and he is excited: "When I walk down the streets of Chicago I get dirty looks for being a Muslim. So in India, it'll be so nice to finally be hated for being an American. I feel so patriotic."

A Muslim and a comedian — it is an image that breaks away from stereotypes. Usman sticks to his carefully cultivated Muslim look — read heavy black beard — during performances. His brand of comedy is obvious in his wildly popular show "Allah Made Me Funny: The Official Muslim Comedy Tour" though he is sure he doesn't want to be "stuffed into some rigid box called Muslim comedy". "I am a comedian and I am Muslim and I think I understand what people mean when they call me a Muslim comedian. I hope that doesn't mean I can't be funny for funny's sake," he says.

On Saturday, Usman will hold fort at the American Center in Delhi. "The objective of this tour is quite simply to make people laugh," he says.

It is a homecoming in many ways: Usman's parents moved from Bihar to Chicago in the 1970s, a few years before he was born. He went on to get a law degree and run his own dotcom before venturing into comedy. He was a hit from the word go — in one of his first shows, the emcee introduced him as the Ayatollah of Comedy and the name sticks to this day.

"Now, I've been a full-time comedian for years and have performed in over a dozen countries in five continents," he says. In November 2005, he was called on to perform at the US-Islamic Word Forum in Doha. "My agenda has always been to wage peace through humour," he adds.

And about how Muslim clerics react to his jokes, Usman says they love it. "Every single Muslim cleric, scholar and imam who has watched my show has had nothing but praise," he says. This American traveller to India has packed his luggage, and airport security be warned — they could die laughing if they peep into his bag of tricks.

Heading: 2 die in Kolkata, one in Howrah - Indian Express

Heading: Who cares about WHO guidelines - Indian Express
Content:
With two deaths in the city and one in district, the official toll due to vector-borne diseases in the state has reached around 30.

Tufani Bhuniya, a resident of Christophar Road, Ward 59, died of dengue and Madhabi Patro (42), a resident of Belgachia Main Road, Ward 34, succumbed to malaria in Beleghata Infectious Diseases Hospital. According to a hospital official, both were admitted in a critical condition.

Patro's death certificate stated that he died of "severe malaria". Subodh Dey, MMiC, Health said the hospital did not get enough time to conduct tests in Patro's case. "The cause of the death mentioned in the death certificate is the result of the clinical diagnosis the doctors had made by seeing the patient's symptoms. She has tested negative for both malaria and dengue in the KMC malaria clinic," he added. Jhuma Das, Councillor of ward 34, however, said Patro has died of vector-borne diseases.

As for Bhuniya, Snehanshu Roy, the councillor of Ward 59 appeared clueless and least interested in the matter. "I am busy in an important meeting. I do not have any information about the death," he said.

Raju Das (40), a resident of Dakshinapur Katapur in Jagacha (Howrah) also succumbed to malaria on Thursday morning. "He had been suffering from high fever for the last few weeks. He was at first admitted to a local nursing home but was later shifted to Jain Hospital. Blood tests confirmed that he was suffering from malaria. Yesterday, he was admitted to Howrah General Hospital where he died," said Mayor Gopal Mukherjee, Howrah Municipal Corporation.

Vector-borne diseases, including unknown fever, have already claimed 22 lives in the city this year. While 10 have died of malaria, six have succumbed to dengue. Three others have succumbed to unknown fever while Japanese Encephalitis, Meningo Encephalitis and Viral Encephalitis have claimed three more. According to a civic health department official, 41,223 people are afflicted with malaria in the city with 4,781 being plasmodium falciparum cases. There have been 105 cases of dengue this year, he added.

State Congress supporters, meanwhile, held a protest in front of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation to protest against the outbreak of vector-borne diseases on Thursday.

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee also blamed the state for the outbreak. "The state health department has asked state-run hospitals and the civic body to suppress data to cover up its failure. Several people are dying of unknown fevers but the department has not taken any initiative to find the cause," she said.

Heading: Cops failed to dig deep, avert Salboni blast - Indian Express
Content:
What lies behind the sudden spurt of the vector-borne diseases in Bengal?

It turns out that the health authorities have been consistently ignoring the recommendations of the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the National Vector-borne Disease Control Programme (NVDCP).

Hobbled by years of neglect, not only in the hinterlands, but also in the core-city area, medical facilities remain woefully unprepared for the outbreak.

For the state health department and local urban bodies, political considerations always outweigh scientific facts.

A case in point would be fogging, which has long been banned by the WHO as it is ineffective in killing adult mosquitoes and pose serious health hazards for humans.

Still, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) continues with fogging, as the Councillors of some wards demand it.

Sahidul Islam, joint commissioner, KMC, said: "We understand that fogging does not help kill mosquitoes and the fact has been reiterated by the WHO. But some councillors nag us for fogging in their wards. If we try to explain, they say the people want it. The councillors simply do it to get public support during election."

As per the WHO guidelines, during the mosquito breeding season, a number of anti-vector measures should be implemented — including the strengthening of vector surveillance measures.

Guidelines say civic bodies have to distribute family-size insecticide impregnated bed-nets to the families living in slums or congested areas.

Besides, the Ministry of Health has to stockpile anti-malarial treatments in hospitals in the affected areas. Immediate treatment can help stop the infection.

"The WHO warned us about the rising risk of vector-borne diseases like malaria and dengue across the state," said a senior health official, "but due to lack of infrastructure, we have been able to do little about it."

Providing support for vector-control strategies — including establishment of a proper drainage system and engineering methods — are key components of WHO's long-term strategy to refurbish public health infrastructure.

According to the guidelines of NVDCP, cities like Kolkata that are endemic to malaria and dengue, the department of health has to conduct its routine vector-control activities throughout the year by collecting active data.

"We asked all urban bodies and the state health department to distribute insecticide-treated mosquito nets in slums. We also emphasised on procuring rapid diagnostic test kits for malaria and dengue," said H G Thakor, consultant, NVDCP. But the preventive measures have not been implemented properly.

"We are looking into the matter. Tomorrow, we will meet some senior officials and discuss this issue," he added.

Besides, NVDCP has recommended the constitution of an Emergency Action Team and Rapid Action Team under the municipal commissioner comprising administrators, entomologists, epidemiologists, clinicians and laboratory specialists during an outbreak.

"We could not formulate such action teams as we are short of manpower. Earlier, the authorities said health workers will be recruited urgently, but that is yet to be done," said Subodh Dey, MMiC, Health.

Heading: Cop posted near Tata factory found dead - Indian Express
Content:
Had policemen dug deeper, literally, they could have "unearthed" the explosives used in Sunday's blast in Salboni.

It now comes to light that metal detectors used by the police had "beeped" during a security check on Saturday at the very spot where the blast took place.

The policemen had dug up the spot. At a depth of six inches, they found two iron rods planted vertically. They looked no more. If they did, they would have found the improvised explosive device (IED) buried right beneath.

"They did it to confuse the police," an officer who has been showcaused, reportedly said. " The Maoists probably completed the electric circuit of the IED, ready for explosion, on Saturday night. Had it been a jungle road, the police might have been more vigilant."

Rajesh Singh, SP, West Midnapore, said there were two iron rods. "I am not an expert. The picture will be clearer after the investigation by the experts."

As the CID took up the blast investigation on Thursday, three more persons were arrested on Thursday from various villages of Binpur in West Midnapore.

The arrested people were Bhagabat Hansda, a panchayat member of Jharkand Party, Sunil Hansda and Sunil Mandi from Binpur.

Singh said two foreign-made pistols were recovered from Hansda and Mandi. The blast, he said, was carried out by the Lalgarh Squad of Maoists and Sasadhar Mahato is the leader of the group.

Police continued the search operations in various villages at Lalgarh and Binpur to trace the suspected Maoists.

Jharkhand Party (Naren) MLA Chunibala Hansda alleged that the police have been harassing the tribals, suspecting their involvement with the Maoists. Their villages were being raided at night.

On Thursday, hundreds of villagers held a road blockade at Lalgarh protesting against the police action of the police.

Villagers also claimed that police had misbehaved with the women during raids.

Also, seven police officers got the showcause notice, which asked them to reply within five weeks.

Heading: Citizens can criticise court judgments, says Biman - Indian Express
Content:
A policeman posted outside the Tata Motors' Singur factory was found dead near the factory on Thursday morning.

The cause of death is not apparent and the body has been sent for postmortem.

Police said that 50-year-old Bidhan Patra had joined duty on Wednesday. He was posted on the western side of the factory.

Patra was a resident Keshabgram in Khatra area of Bankura. It is, however, not clear whether he was on duty on Wednesday night.

In the morning, locals of Hora Kalimandir area saw his body lying beside a canal. There was no injury, but eyewitnesses said blood was oozing from his nose and ears.

The body was sent to Walsh hospital for postmortem.

"We cannot say whether it was a murder or natural death until the postmortem report arrives," said Chandernagore Sub-Divisional Police Officer Amitava Maity.

Heading: BESU erupts again, students asked to vacate hostels - Indian Express
Content:
Contempt case against CPM leaders in Calcutta High Court

The CPM state secretary, Biman Bose, admitted that he had criticised the judgment delivered by the Calcutta High Court on the police firing at Nandigram on March 14, 2007. He, however, denied that he had attacked the judiciary during his speech at a rally in Esplanade on November 17, 2007.

In his affidavit placed before a Division Bench of Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose today, Bose said every citizen has the right to criticise court judgments. Moreover, his criticism had been reasonable.

He added that he had critically analysed the judgment vis-a-vis the Constitution and keeping in mind the limitations of the honourable court, healthy criticism can only strengthen the constitutional machinery.

He had no intention of obstructing the administration of justice, he said.

Besides Bose, two other CPM leaders, Shyamal Chakraborty and Binoy Konar, also placed their affidavits before the court through their counsel Rabishankar Chatterjee.

The next hearing will be held on November 27.

On November 16, 2007, the Calcutta High Court had declared that the police firing at Nandigram on March 14 was unconstitutional and illegal. Bose, Konar and Chakraborty had allegedly criticised the judgment as well as the judiciary while addressing a rally in Esplanade on November 17.

Bose had reportedly said: "We feel the court has interfered in the state's domain. If the High Court has the last word on everything, what is the use of having a legislature and an executive? Will the court decide the government's course of action?" Konar and Chakraborty had also echoed Bose.

The Bar Association and the Bar Library Club of the Calcutta High Court had filed a petition last December, alleging that the remarks amounted to contempt of court. The High Court had issued contempt notice against the three leaders in February.

During the last hearing on August 5, the court had asked the trio to file affidavits.

Heading: UGC asks Calcutta University to identify colleges with ‘potential for excellence’ - Indian Express
Content:
With the Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) again on the boil and clashes among student groups and the police continuing unabated, the university has suspended undergraduate classes and asked over 1,000 students to vacate their hostels.

According to the police, Deputy Superintendent of Police Anjan Chakraborty, Howrah Town, and some students were injured on Thursday after a group of students attacked the police personnel in front of the main administrative building of the university. Eight students have been arrested in connection with the attack.

Earlier, sporadic clashes took place between the Independent Consolidation (IC) and the Students Federation of India (SFI) inside the university campus.

Meanwhile, a team of the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) of the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE), the statutory body of the universities and colleges providing

technical education, is expected to visit the university on Friday.

"We are not going to take any chances. Since the NBA team is expected in the university on Friday and clashes inside the campus are still on, we have decided to suspend all the undergraduate classes," said registrar of the university Biman Bandopadhayay. Since classes have been suspended, the students will have to vacate their hostels, he added.

"We are not going to hide anything from the NBA. Accreditation is necessary for the students and if they do not cooperate with us then we cannot do anything to help them," said a BESU official.

"Whenever a small incident occurs in the campus, the university authorities hand over the matter to the police, instead of handling it themselves," said Rajorshi Dutta, a fourth-year student and an IC supporter.

He added that such sporadic violence were common before students' union election. "A group of SFI students tried to create problems in the campus by inciting students," he alleged.

Subhasis Bhattacharjee, SFI secretary of Howrah, however, said that none of his supporters were involved in the violence and accused the IC for causing unrest inside the campus. He said the SFI has filed an FIR in the Shibpur police station against those who were involved in the violence.

This is the second time this year when the students are asked to vacate their hostels after violence erupted in the campus.

Heading: Trinamool renews demand for return of land in Singur - Indian Express
Content:
In order to provide financial assistance to colleges making significant contribution in imparting higher education, the University Grants Commission (UGC) has asked the University of Calcutta to identify colleges affiliated to it that can be granted the status of "potential for excellence".

In a meeting held earlier this week, the syndicate of the Calcutta University has decided to form a committee to identify such colleges.

"A committee will be constituted by the vice-chancellor to identify colleges for the UGC assistance," said Dhrubojyoti Chattopadhyay, Vice-Chancellor (Academic). According to Chattopadhyay, colleges need to fulfill certain criteria for the status. The university can identify eight colleges for the financial assistance by the commission. There are 137 colleges affiliated to the University of Calcutta.

Under the UGC initiative, if colleges with potential for excellence status are autonomous and have the accreditation by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) then they are given a one-time grant of Rs 1 crore.

However, if the colleges are not autonomous, the grant by the UGC is Rs 65 lakh.

In case a college does not have NAAC accreditation and autonomy, the grant is Rs 35 lakh.

Presidency College, St Xavier's College and Loreto College have already achieved this status. Lady Brabourne, Bethune College, Ramakrishna Mission College at Narendrapur, Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandir Belur, Scottish Church College and Goenka College of Commerce are in the queue to achieve this status.

"The process is like another NAAC accreditation where performance of a college is judged on various parameters. Earlier, when we had applied for the same, the college did not have the NAAC accreditation," said Sanghmita Mukherjee, principal of Lady Brabourne College.

"In certain states, the concept of autonomous colleges does not exist. More funds are allocated to the colleges which are autonomous, but autonomy is not a pre-requisite for the status," said a UGC member.

Last week, an expert committee of the UGC conducted a meeting with 25 vice-chancellors of the eastern and north-eastern region to deliberate on making the affiliating system stronger. The participants agreed on making the NAAC 'A' grade colleges autonomous. The recommendation will be made to the UGC by the end of this year and the commission can decide on the recommendations from the next academic session.

Heading: CPM calls Mamata an ‘ally of Maoists’... - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee renewed her demand for the state government to return 400 acres from the small car factory project area in Singur.

"We want the state government to abide by the agreement that was signed on September 7 in the presence of Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi. We agreed to the meeting only on the request of the governor," Banerjee said on Thursday.

She alleged that though the agreement had clearly stated that "maximum land" will be given from within the project area, Commerce Minister Nirupam Sen had later informed the party that they will receive only 70 acres.

"During the talks, the Tatas suddenly decided to pull out. Mysteriously, within four days, they found a new site in Gujarat," she said. The Trinamool chief further alleged that even after the pull out, the copy of their agreement with the state has not been made

public. According to her, the whole mystery of the Tatas pulling out and moving to Gujarat will be solved once the agreement is made public.

Senior Trinamool leader Sougata Ray said: "The CPM needs to remember that the agitation in Singur was suspended and not withdrawn. If need be, we will revive the agitation. The state government cannot just show the site to investors and think of alternative projects to come up in the area."

Banerjee also said that at least four potential investors had contacted her. "Before investing, they wanted to discuss the matter with me," she added.

Heading: ...Mamata says Maoists are CPM cadres in disguise - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM top brass at Alimuddin Street has drawn up a blueprint to launch a statewide campaign targetting Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee as an "ally of the Maoists".

After the attack on Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's convoy in Salboni, the party is sure that now it will be easier to label Banerjee a "destructive" force.

"Both Mamata and the Maoists are against the state's development. It is clear that the Salboni incident was a veiled threat against the mega steel project coming up in that area," said a senior CPM leader, while emerging from a two-day meeting of the party's state committee. The meet ended on Thursday.

In the meeting, the chief minister blamed Banerjee and her alleged Naxal allies for Tata Motors pulling out of Singur. "We are sure that the Maoists are linked with the Trinamool Congress. It was evident in Nandigram and Singur as well," Bhattacharjee reportedly told his party colleagues.

State party secretary Biman Bose said the opposition parties are united in their opposition to any development projects, be it the expansion of the national highway or setting up a chemical hub.

"The issues should be dealt with courage. Sometimes our members are confused whether the Opposition is fighting for the cause of the poor farmers or not," said a source, quoting Bose.

Heading: Paswan was the target of Salboni blast, says LJP - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee alleged that "Maoists in the state were actually CPM cadres in disguise".

She was speaking at an open conference to mark "Save Democracy Day", organised by the party on Thursday to protest against the alleged police atrocities on Trinamool supporters in Singur. "Many states have banned these organisations. But strangely, while the state government keeps talking about Maoist attacks, it has never taken any initiative to ban them," Banerjee said.

Referring to Sunday's blast at Salboni, she added: "It appeared to be much of a coincidence that the blast occurred quite some time after the chief minister's convoy had passed the incident spot and soon after the CPM started propagating that he was ready to give his life for the sake of industrialisation."

If the attack was meant to target the chief minister, then it would have occurred while his convoy was passing the area and not half-an-hour later, Banerjee added.

"Whenever CPM leaders go to Purulia, Bankura and West Midnapore, they are faced with Maoist attacks. But during elections, they sweep these areas," she said. Her comment was in tune with the recent statement of Congress leader Manas Bhuniya who had said that none of the Opposition parties had any presence in the area where the blast had taken place.

Banerjee also demanded a Central investigation into the blast. "The chief minister's security is not a matter of joke. But in several previous cases of landmine blasts, investigations have revealed that they were fake," she added.

The Trinamool chief further said that in the name of identifying Maoist activists, the police are now questioning and harassing innocent people. "The CPM calls us pro-Mao, they label theatre personality Bibhash Chakraborty and singer Kabir Suman as Maoists," she said.

According to Banerjee, the blast at Salboni showed that the common people are against industrialisation and the incident has created panic among the investors. The party plans to demand a probe into the Salboni blast on November 18.

Heading: Presidency, JU students accuse cops of harassing villagers - Indian Express
Content:
The Lok Janshakti Party claimed on Thursday that Sunday's blast in Salboni was aimed at killing Union steel minister Ram Vilas Paswan — the last dignitary to pass the spot.

Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee was in the front of the convoy. The blast occurred just after Paswan's car had passed.

The party workers will stage a demonstration in front of the residence of Bhattacharjee on Friday to protest against the state government's failure to provide security to Paswan.

"Paswan feels that the blast was directed at him. We will demand a CBI inquiry into it," said Subrata Mukherjee, vice-president of the party unit in Bengal.

"The state government is also shirking responsibility," said a party spokesperson.

"The senior police officers who were responsible have been spared while pawns are being punished."

The party has demanded the immediate suspension of the Inspector General of South Bengal and the Superintendent of Police, West Midnapore.

Heading: Govt aims to raise contribution of mining sector to country’s GDP, says minister - Indian Express
Content:
The students of Presidency College and Jadavpur University have criticised the police for arresting innocent villagers in and around Salboni for their alleged involvement in the blast on the chief minister's convoy last Sunday.

In a statement, the students said that innocent students studying in Classes VIII and IX and school teachers are being labelled as Maoists and being harassed by the police. They alleged that the police have failed to provide security to the VIPs and now they are targeting the poor villagers.

The Independent Consolidation (IC) at Presidency College and the Faculty for Arts Students Union (FAS) at Jadavpur University, have urged Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee to stop further arrests. They have also urged the people across the state to protest against the issue.

Heading: Paschimanchal funds remain unutilised - Indian Express
Content:
The Union Ministry of Coal wants the Indian mining sector to contribute more towards the country's gross domestic product (GDP) and is keen on purchasing latest equipment for the purpose.

Speaking at the first global mining summit in the country on Thursday, Santosh Bagrodia, Union Minister of State for Coal said: "Indian economy is fighting against the global meltdown because of its sound economic policies. It is due to its strong economic base that India is one of the preferred investment destinations in the world."

Talking about the mining sector, the minister said that although Indian mining sector contributes just three per cent to the country's total GDP, the ministry has plans to take it up to 9 per cent in the near future. The minister said that after the government opened up the mining sector for foreign investment, the government is considering several joint ventures between Indian and foreign companies.

"India's economic growth has been considerable in the last few years, but it has been limited to the service and IT sector. India's mining sector has enough potential, but lack of planning, long-drawn official procedure of procuring licence and to some

extent insurgency are major obstacles in its growth," said Russell King, chief strategy officer of the Anglo American Plc, which plans to invest nearly $40 billion globally in the next five to 10 years.

Coal India Chairman Partha Bhattacharya said that keeping in mind the energy requirement of the country, it is important to take up the growth of coal mining sector to 9 per cent from present 5.5 per cent, which has been the average growth rate in the last 35 years.

Heading: US academy has restored Ray films, see them at film festival - Indian Express
Content:
While the districts of West Midnapore, Bankura and Purulia are reeling under Maoist threats, the Paschimanchal Unnayan Board has failed to utilise the funds allocated by the state government.

The board, headed by Sushanta Ghosh, Minister for the Department of Paschimanchal Unnayan, is responsible for the development of the three districts along with Bankura and Birbhum.

In the financial year 2006-2007, Rs 19.90 crore was sanctioned while the amount released was Rs 17.79 crore. Out of that, only Rs 10.94 crore could be utilised. In 2007-2008, Rs 46.39 crore was sanctioned, but Rs 17.79 crore was released, of which Rs 14.82 crore was spent. "Some of the areas are inaccessible. Infrastructure is very poor in those areas," said A B Bhattacharya,

the department's Principal Secretary. The department, in fact, is going ahead with the development of the area, based on an action plan prepared by IIT Kharagpur.

The institute had formed a nine-member committee which had submitted its report in November last year. According to the action plan,

areas marked for improvement included agriculture, transport, health, education, infrastructure, industries and information technology.

The committee gave an estimate of Rs 16,000 crore to be spent in a span of 10 years for the development of the districts.

Heading: Blame game on at airport after collision averted - Indian Express
Content:
Here is some good news for Satyajit Ray fans in the city. From Monday, they will be able to see some of his masterpieces that have been restored by the US Academy of Motion Pictures.

"The academy has preserved and restored 18 of Ray's masterpieces, which had deteriorated with the time. We will screen some of these films for the first time in the Kolkata Film Festival beginning next Monday," said Josef Lindner of US Academy of Motion Pictures.

For the first time, the US consulate's public affairs office has dedicated two special film packages to Ray for this year's Kolkata Film Festival.

While one of the packages will have selected Hollywood movies of the maestro, the other will have Ray's preserved films from the archive of the US Academy of Motion Pictures.

"For the first time, the American Consulate will contribute to the Kolkata Film Festival," said American Centre director Douglas Kelly. "Besides seven popular Ray films, five of his restored movies will also be screened during the festival," he added.
