Experts from the US participating in the film festival will visit Jadavpur University, Calcutta University and Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute.

Besides Lindner, film critic Peter Rainer of The Christian Science Monitor will oversee the screening of Ray's Hollywood films.

Ray's film Aparajito will be screened for the first time after its restoration by the academy.

Apart from Aparajito, the second package of Ray's films restored by the Academy will include Teen Kanya, Parosh Pathar, Joy Baba Felunath and Two, which is a short film.

The Motion Pictures archive which has a target of restoring or preserving one Ray film every year is at present working on the preservation of Chess Player, which will take two years to complete.

The academy is waiting for funds to work on Kanchenjanga too. It has also worked on Ray's films like Apu trilogy, Devi, Charulata, Mahanagar, Jalsaghar, Teen Kanya, Jana Aranya, Monihara, Parash Pathar, Jai Baba Felunath, Kapurush O Mahapurush, Nayak, Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne, Abhijaan and Shimaboddho.

Efforts are also being made to screen Ray's documentary film Sikkim.

"The restoration work on Sikkim will not be completed before the next year. But we are trying to screen it in the video format at the festival," said Lindner.

Some of Ray's popular Hollywood films are The Southerner (1945), Trouble in Paradise (1932), A Night at the Opera (1935), The Maltese Falcon (1941), Citizen Kane (1941), Double Indemnity (1944) and Rear Window (1954).

Heading: Mahindra Utd looking to tame East Bengal in their own den - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a major collision was averted at the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, the blame game has begun between officials of the Airport Authorities of India (AAI) and the Air Traffic Control (ATC).

On Wednesday, a Kingfisher aircraft, waiting at the taxi point for its turn to take off, rolled onto one side of the secondary runway where an aircraft of Jet Airways was about to land.

"It is not clear why the ATC failed to alert the Jet Airways pilot and why they did not notice that the Kingfisher flight had rolled onto the runway when it was supposed to wait," said an AAI official.

AAI Regional Director P K Singhal said: "The Director General of Civil Aviation is the only authorised agency that can conduct an investigation into the incident. The probe is on and we are waiting for the report."

He added that the accident was averted because of the Jet pilot's alertness.

The Kolkata-bound Jet Airways flight was carrying around 100 passengers.

ATC officials, however, pleaded innocence.

"It seems there was a mistake on part of the Kingfisher pilot. You are

supposed to wait within a certain safety mark and the aircraft went beyond that.

It was not cleared to hit the runway and was asked to hold (stop and wait) at the taxiway," said an ATC official.

Heading: Walking the Line - Indian Express
Content:
On the eve of the much-awaited big match in the I-League Premier Division between Mahindra United and East Bengal, coach Dereck Pereira is eager to make the most against his fancied opponents.

The Mahindra United coach is brimming with confidence despite going into a tough away-match at the Yuba Bharati Krirangan, simply because the players are on a high after an impressive victory in their last outing. The Jeepmen scored a dominating 2-0 win over Vasco SC in their last Premier Division encounter. And more importantly, the team is upbeat over the welcome return to form of their Nigerian striker Edeh Chidi.

Understandably, the visitors went through a rigorous two-hour-long training session at the venue of the match in the sweltering Kolkata heat, following which, coach Pereira gave the impression that he is a relaxed man going into tomorrow's big match.

Mahindra United are in an uncomfortable position in the points tally, having garnered a modest 6 points from 6 matches. Hosts East Bengal are just a shade better off at this stage, sitting on a none-too-inpressive 8 points from 6 outings.

However, the stalwart Mumbai side's coach put up a brave face after the day's gruelling practice session. "It's not that we are failing to perform. We are only failing to score goals despite dominating in the matches and we are also coming up with chances. The good news is, Chidi seems to have regained his old form, which we discovered in our last I-League match, against Vasco. I have this feeling that the confidence level of the boys has shot up after the win against Vasco and they are looking forward to perform well against East Bengal tomorrow. I am expecting a good show from my boys, and I will be happy even if the boys manage to force hosts East Bengal to share points."

The Mahindra United coach Pereira is keeping a close watch on their new Nigerian defender Lamine Tamba, who is recovering from injury. "He is good considering the qualities a good defender possesses. I hope he will be seen in action a week from now," Pereira said.

The East Bengal camp, too, is quite wary going into tomorrow's match. And coach Stanley Rozario isn't relaxing. The bad news for the red-and-gold brigade is that the Kolkata team's man in form, Nigerian striker Yusif Yakubu, looks doubtful for tomorrow's match since he is still down with fever. The East Bengal think-tank however has decided to list the in-form Yakubu in the reserves going into the match.

The East Bengal coach is likely to start with Sunil Chhetri and Parveen Kumar upfront, and Mehrajuddin Wadao could be given the usual role of playing as a defensive screen in the midfield.

Coach Rozario said: "Yakubu's fever and the doubt over his participation in tomorrow's match has already put the team in quite a difficult situation. The Nigerian striker has been in tremendous form. Let us see, if he can recover, then he may play also. And Mahindra United, despite a mediocre run in the I-League so far, is a well-balanced side. They have a perfect combination of players in all the segments. Tomorrow's match will be a tough tie for us."

Meanwhile, East Bengal Club is likely to obtain the All India Football Federation's (AIFF) nod in getting another foreigner as a replacement for the team's Brazilian striker Edmilson, who has been ruled out of the I-League due to Hepatitis B. Edmilson is set to be out of action for the next two-and-a-half months.

Heading: End of an Era - Indian Express
Content:
Background scores, for Salim-Suleiman, would remain as special as their latest as music directors – Aditya Chopra's gigantic Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi

When a certain Aditya Chopra decides to step behind the camera, with Shah Rukh Khan in his frames, we don't expect sparks, we bet on fireworks. And if anything leaves music director duo Salim-Suleiman with goose bumps, it has to be this. "I am usually nervous when I do music for a film," laughs Salim Merchant right before the music release of Aditya Chopra's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi. Expectations, are often unreasonable feels Salim. "There seems to be popular demand for thumping, racy dance tracks. There has to be at least one such track in a film," says Salim.

Rab Ne…, however, chooses not to trek the beaten path. Chopra wanted the music to completely feel like it belongs to the spirit of the film, and not just full of random chartbusters. "People often have funny expectations but we have tried to make the music true to the film," says Salim. So, the music director duo, who have worked wonders with the music for films like Dor, Chak De! India, Roadside Romeo, and most recently Fashion, decided to keep Rab Ne… simple. "The film is based in Amritsar. The sounds reflect the same," says Salim.

While Fashion had been a delightful experiment with relatively new voices, Rab Ne… would stick to old favourites — Sukhwinder Singh and his ilk. But new voices still remain in the priority list of the duo. And reality shows are most likely to be their favourite hunting ground for fresh talent. "We are waiting for an opportunity to put all the talent we spot on these shows to good use," says Salim, who with his brother has been judging the two seasons of Chak De on 9X channel.

However, being in the big league of music directors wouldn't mean that the duo gives up doing the background score for films —where it all started. "In fact the experience of doing the background score comes very handy in gauging the pulse of the film, while making music," says Salim. It's difficult to forget the haunting background score of Nagesh Kukunoor's 3 Deewarien, and Salim wishes there were more people who acknowledged the importance of the background score of a film. "The background score is all-important in creating the mood in a film. It's strange how it gets a step-motherly treatment in the country," laughs Salim. Things, hopes the music director, would surely look up in future. "It's very difficult for us to stop doing background scores because that is we belong to it. There are very few composers who both want to and can create quality background music," adds Salim. We are not complaining.

Heading: SOPU member thrashed outside V-C’s residence - Indian Express
Content:
The irony wouldn't have escaped Bollywoodphiles. Noted filmmaker BR Chopra, who passed away on Wednesday at the age of 94, may have launched younger brother Yash Chopra as a director with the 1959 film Dhool Ka Phool, which like other BR Chopra films was a reformist tale about an unmarried mother, but his later films, most notably Baghban and Babul, borrowed heavily from the Yash Raj sensibility of chiffons and satins. Yet, in a career spanning more than five decades, this legendary filmmaker took risks, broke boundaries and redefined both Indian film and television industries. A list of his most notable endeavours.

Naya Daur
In this Dilip Kumar-Vyjanthimala, the compelling storyteller in BR Chopra uses the rustic backdrop to narrate a tale about the aspirations of an emerging nation. This reformative drama was a trendsetter and inspired many other gaonwalla versus shaherwalla dramas. The most recent being Ashutosh Gowariker's Lagaan.

Kanoon
An edge-of-the-seat courtroom drama, with a flawed, fragile protagonist, Kanoon was one of those edgy, psychological thrillers, which most of us would happily lap up today. This songless Sunil Dutt starrer may not have been a commercial success, but it took Hindi cinema a step forward.

Waqt
A happy family is torn apart by a natural calamity. Brothers become enemies. Love triangles emerge and complexities arise. Until fate intervenes to sort things out. This 1965 film happens to be the mother of all family dramas and spawned many copies. So much so that a term called the 'Waqt formula' became a part of the film lover's lexicon. Countless Bollywood potboilers borrow their basic premise from this classic, namely Yaadon Ki Baarat, Locket etc. With legends like Balraj Sahini, Raj Kumar, Sunil Dutt, Sadhana, Sharmila Tagore and Sashi Kapoor in its cast, Waqt was also the first Indian multi-starrer.

Insaaf Ka Tarazu
While Bollywood was only too happy to make kanjeevaram-gajra sporting stereotypes out of its women in the 1980s, BR Chopra came up with this potent drama where pertinent feminist questions were asked without resorting to preaching. Zeenat Aman was the liberated, young protagonist, who is raped by a powerful sociopath. Her fight for justice is marred by society's preconceived notions about "modern women". Yet justice prevails.

Mahabharat
If you happen to be in your twenties or more, you will probably associate the term "good television" with Sunday mornings in the late 1980s when streets of the country wore a deserted look as families settled down in front of their newly-acquired colour televisions to watch this BR Chopra classic. A year before Mahabharat was launched, Ramanand Sagar's adaptation of another Hindu epic, Ramayana, ruled the TRP charts. But this BR Chopra project brought true professionalism to Indian television with its ambitious sets and shrewd casting.

Heading: Gangsters brandished swords to scare family; - Indian Express
Content:
A member of Students of Panjab University (SOPU), Barinder Dhillon, was beaten up by nine youths outside the residence of Panjab University Vice-Chancellor R C Sobti late on Thursday evening.

Dhillon was rushed to a private hospital. Doctors attending to him said that the victim had to be given 45 stitches at three points on his head.

A case of assault, rioting and intimidation has been registered against three youths, Simranjeet Singh Sandhu (a law student in PU), Narinder Gujjar and Sanjay Kumar (members of Haryana Students Association (HSA), and other unidentified accomplices. ASP Madhur Verma raids are on to nab the accused.

"Security around the university will be tightened to avoid such clashes," he added.

Dhillon, along with Govind Khatra, Sahil Nanda and Vijay, had gone to the V-C's house to invite him for a cultural programme. "When the four were leaving the premises, the eight youths came out of two cars (a white Swift car and a silver Skoda) and started beating them with sticks. While Barinder was beaten mercilessly, Govind, Sahil and Vijay escaped with minor injuries. Govind threw a flowerpot, which was placed just outside the Vice-Chancellor's house, on one of the cars," sources said.

The V-C heard the uproar and came out of his house. "I saw a few people beating Dhillon with batons. When I tried to intervene, they ran away," he said. Denying he was manhandled, Vice-Chancellor R C Sobti said he was injured while trying to catch hold of a miscreant.

SOPU members alleged security guards deputed outside the Vice-Chancellor's residence remained mute spectators to the incident.

Heading: Haryana Pollution Control Board seals hotel kitchen, allows it to function by evening - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve muffled faces haunt this 15-year-old girl, a resident of Bhagomajra village. She has not dared to step out of her small rented house ever since a dozen goons took turns to rape her for two hours on Diwali night.

"Around 8.30 pm on October 28, I was picked up from the courtyard where I was washing dishes," recollected the visibly shocked teenager.

The gangsters brandished swords, rods and batons to intimidate the victim, her two elder sisters and maternal aunt. While the others were held hostage in a room, the minor girl was gagged and assaulted in the adjoining room. Two gangsters stood guard at the main gate, which they earlier scaled to trespass, while four held down the girl as the other six took turns to rape her.

"They kept hitting the swords, rods and batons against the walls and the main gate to keep us under duress," said the girl's aunt. The teenager's ordeal ended only when her parents returned home around 11 pm and raised an alarm. The goons fled under the cover of darkness, leaving the victim unconscious. The girl's father is unemployed after he lost his legs in a road accident.

Thereafter, the family was put under immense pressure to reach a compromise as the accused were residents of the same village. But five days later (on Monday), the teenager dared to walk to Mohali.

She met the Superintendent of Police (Headquarters), who ordered the Kharar Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Raj Balwinder Singh Marar to conduct an inquiry . A case of gangrape, wrongful restraint and rioting has been registered against the 12 accused. The medical examination report of the victim has confirmed rape, said the Kharar Station House Officer.

Heading: MC to start drive to check fire safety norms in city - Indian Express
Content:
Officials of the Haryana Pollution Control Board sealed the kitchen and laundry units of the four-star hotel, KC Crossroad, in Panchkula around 11.30 am on Thursday.

The four-member team, led by Regional Officer Bhagwan Singh, also disconnected the water and electricity supply to the hotel.

According to senior officials, the units were sealed as the owners had failed to submit the required affidavit for an effluent treatment plant and a bank guarantee of Rs 2 lakh within the stipulated time of three months.

By evening, however, the units were allowed to function again. "I gave orders to remove the seals after the Head Office received all the due documents from the hotel representatives," said A S Chahal, chairman of the Haryana Pollution Control Board.

On the other hand, general manager of KC Crossroad, S K Mehta, completely denied the incident. "This is completely false. No officials came to the hotel for inspection and no units were sealed. Everything is normal and in place," said Mehta.

Incidentally, a dispute over payment of bills between the hotel authorities and a Board official, who had held a marriage function at the hotel, was also reported recently.

Heading: Rs 4.73 lakh siphoned off from trader’s bank account - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation in Chandigarh has decided to start checks on the buildings which are violating fire safety norms within a fortnight. In a meeting of the Fire and Emergency Services committee held recently, it was decided that notices would be pasted on the buildings where violations are found during the checks conducted earlier.

In case the violators do not conform to the requisite norms, stringent action would be taken at the earliest. The Fire and Emergency Services Committee had conducted numerous checks on buildings including schools, offices, hotels, coaching centres, eating joints, malls, etc and issued notices. But even after five months no action has been taken yet.

Among others notices have been issued to Vivek High School, a few government schools, Aerizzona, Noodle Bar and Swagat Restaurant. Various coaching centres were also found without fire safety equipment.

At Aerizzona, Sector 9, all safety norms were found to be violated. It was found that in case of a fire, even the staff would not be able to escape the premises. It has now been sealed by the Administration.

The most common violations found were the cylinder not being in place, staff not trained enough to handle equipment, extinguishers were found to be not working or expired, lack of proper exit gates and case of emergency.

An official of the Fire Wing of the MC said that the main aim of civic body is to create awareness rather than taking stringent action. "We find that people are not aware about the norms. We issue notices and after the time period lapses another check is conducted. In case violations persist more time is given."

Chairman of the Fire and Safety Committee M P S Chawla said: "We would soon be conducting checks. The places where more public is involved would be given priority. These include hospitals, schools, malls, etc. Public safety would not be compromised. In case need arises we would not hesitate in sealing buildings."

Heading: Forget washing woes, city to have more laundry marts soon - Indian Express
Content:
In the second of its kind theft in the city, an unidentified person managed to withdraw Rs 4.73 lakh from the savings account of a Mohali resident through stolen cheques and forged signatures.

According to G S Tulsi, owner of PNS Leathers in Phase-V, Mohali, he has a savings bank account (100802000001232) with HDFC in Sector 9. On September 13, he found two cheques (33770 and 33771) from his cheque book issued against the account missing. He verified the records and discovered he had never issued the cheques.

A police officer said: "He immediately informed the HDFC authorities and asked them to stop the payment against the cheques. The bank, however, told him that Rs 4.73 lakh have already been issued against one of the cheques (33771) about a week ago. The cheque had come in clearing from the State Bank of India in Sector 10 Panchkula branch. The cheque bore the forged signatures of Tulsi."

Tulsi approached the SBI officials and found one Krishan Prabhu, holding a savings account (20016467627) in their bank, had deposited the crossed cheque with them and they had forwarded it to the HDFC bank. The HDFC bank, after verifying the signatures, issued the money to SBI and credited it in Krishan's account. The entire money was withdrawn the same day.

The SBI officials later provided the residential address, PAN identity and other documents of Krishan Prabhu to Tulsi. All documents were found fake.

Tulsi told the police that he had asked HDFC bank manager Rohit Bhateja to report the matter to police but he refused.

"We are now investigating who had stolen the blank cheques from the cheque book. The entire staff of TNS Leathers would also be questioned especially those who are in direct contact with the complainant," police said.

Last month, Rs 2.8 lakh were withdrawn from the IDBI savings bank account of one Maninder Singh by using the same modus operandi. A blank cheque from his cheque book was stolen and the amount was transferred from IDBI to Bank of Baroda. The address given by the accused was also found to be fake. Police are now investigating if the same person was behind both the crime.

Heading: Immigration firm to pay up for shattering dollar dreams - Indian Express
Content:
With the Architecture department approving the proposal of the Municipal Corporation to transform existing dhobighats into laundry marts, the city could soon have seven such modern facilities.

In the next step, the estimates to set up the modern laundry marts would be taken to the Finance and Contract Committee meeting and the House Meet for clearance.

At present, such machines have only been installed at the dhobighat in Sector 15. Meanwhile, the new washing machines would be accommodated in dhobighats in Sectors 7, 15, 19, 20, 22, 27 and 32 and an extra floor would be added to the building for the same.

The proposal for new laundry marts was mooted a few months ago mainly after the mart in Sector 15 gained popularity. The first mart, set up at a cost of Rs 35 lakh, had been set up here due to the proximity with Panjab University. A large number of students stay in the sector as paying guests and the laundry mart is a boon for them.

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra said: "The coin-operated washing machine that was set up is popular with the residents of the area. We are hopeful that the new marts would also be welcomed."

At the existing laundry mart, as many as 15 clothes can be washed by paying Rs 20. In the new marts, coin-operated washing machines would be set up.

With the machine taking half an hour to wash one lot, around 10 to 15 people are accommodated in a day. The laundry marts also provide lines to dry clothes.

Heading: HUDA asked to pay interest on refunded amount - Indian Express
Content:
The district consumer forum has directed an immigration company to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation for failing to send the complainant to Canada. They have also been directed to refund Rs 60,000 paid to them by the complainant to process his immigration.

Ravinder Singh Dhaliwal said in his complaint that in response to an advertisement of Canadian 4UR Immigration Services in 2005, he approached the company seeking permanent immigration to the country.

He produced original certificates as demanded by them and after entering into a service agreement, paid Rs 60,000. The rest of the payment was to be deposited at the time of the nomination.

The company then informed him that due to backlog of cases, his immigration process was taking a reasonably longer time. He was then shocked to receive a letter in April from Overseas Immigration from Canada that his case was not processed as the Immigration Services at Chandigarh has not taken any action despite reminders.

It was further averred that the complainant had been making preparations simultaneously, and was also not accepting the job offers that came by.

Canadian 4Ur immigration services said in its reply that they never promised to clear the process within six to eight months as alleged by the complainant.

It was submitted that they had a contract with Overseas Immigration from Canada but it started corresponding directly with the clients to mislead them. In the best interest of its clients, therefore, all dealing with said Overseas Immigration company were withdrawn, hence the delay.

The forum said that that the company was entitled to receive Rs.2.50 lakh on receipt of nomination and Rs.4.50 lakh on receipt of immigration visa. The forum said no affidavit of any authorised person from the Service India Centre has been filed by the company to authenticate any of these letters or to prove that employment has been arranged for the complainant.

"He also procured a loan of Rs 62,550 and is repaying it through installments. The complainant had been waiting for two years to get immigration, but the company did not do anything and shattered the dreams of an unemployed youth, besides plunging him into debt. The contention of the complainant that in the hope of immigration to Canada, he did not do any work or left the assignments also appears to be plausible," said Jagroop Singh Mahal, district forum president.

Heading: From fashion king to aspiring engineer - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) to pay 18 per cent interest to the complainant for the deposited amount for a plot which was later refunded without interest.

The interest is to be paid on Rs 3,34,548 for the allotment of one-kanal plot in Urban Estate, Faridabad, in 2006.

Darshan Singh said in his complaint that he deposited Rs 3,31,548 through Oriental Bank of Commerce, Manimajra, along with application for allotment of a one-kanal plot in Urban Estate.

Later, the draw was not held on its scheduled date. The complainant alleged that by non-consideration of his application, he lost an opportunity to apply in other sectors in which plots of the same category were floated. It was also averred that HUDA did not mention in the brochure what will be the action if the draw was nit held. The grievance of the complainant raised failed to evoke any effective response.

In its reply, HUDA said that the scheme was closed in the meeting under the chairmanship of the Haryana chief minister and Rs 3,31,548 was refunded to the complainant within 6 months from the date of brochure. Also, there were only eight plots of one-kanal in Faridabad's Sector 46 which were allotted.

It was further submitted that the brochure was published only for the remaining plots in various sectors of Urban Estate. The forum said the complainant has lost his opportunity to apply in other sectors in which the number of plots of the some category were also floated and this caused financial loss to the complainant as well as mental agony.

The forum said that not only was the complainant deprived of owing a one-kanal plot but also lost a chance to apply for a suitable plot in some other sector.

The interest is to be paid from the date of deposit of the amount which was July, 2006.

Heading: Lawyers’ chambers to cost over Rs 56 crore - Indian Express
Content:
In July last year, 18-year-old Karan Chhabra shot to instant fame after he won the title of Mr Personality at the Hindustan Super Model Contest 2007. In fact, this Class XII YPS student heralded a new trend - he thrived at a time when turbaned models were a rarity.

"Today, there is no dearth of turbaned models. Films like Singh is Kinng have been successful in enhancing the image of Sikhs as models and actors. But when I won the title last year, they were nowhere to been seen in the arclights. I am proud that I proved that Sikhs look good in everything and traditional wear works best for them," says Karan.

Now, the youngster is back to studies. Keeping in view the uncertainties in choosing modelling as a profession, he is pursuing engineering at Rayat College near Kharar. "I need a backup in life and wanted to complete my education first," he says.

"I am into cardio and regular gymming but don't have much time for exercise as studies are a priority," he adds.

A stylish dresser himself, Karan feels 'clothes maketh the man'.

"Traditional dresses suit me best. The judges told me they selected me for my confidence and my eyes. I am an optimistic and feel life has so much to offer and one should always make use if it," he says.

Earlier, fashion magazines were full of his interviews and leading fashion designers sought him for his style. Today, Karan does local print shoots and ramp shows in Chandigarh. "But I am always open to any lucrative offers that come my way. Modelling is my first love," he adds.

Heading: Vascular surgery offers hope to counter diabetic foot amputations - Indian Express
Content:
Court lauds the effort of the Chandigarh Administration, but advises it to cut the cost

It might sound astounding but it's true. Chandigarh Administration is likely to invest Rs 56.46 crore to construct 440 chambers for lawyers in the new judicial complex being set up in Sector 43.

The estimate along with other decisions regarding ownership of land was on Thursday submitted in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Justice Jasbir Singh expressed surprise over the amount that the Administration is going to invest on construction of the lawyers' chambers. "Try to make it cheap," was the advice Justice Singh gave to the Chandigarh Administration.

However, the Division bench of the court headed by Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur, lauded the effort of the Administration. He asked the District Bar Association to rise to the occasion and ensure full support to the Administration for speedy construction of the new judicial complex.

According to the detailed affidavit submitted by the Executive Engineer (W & E), Secretary Engineering, Chandigarh, the ownership of the land as well as the building will remain with the Chandigarh Administration while the District Bar Association shall have only limited right of usage of the chambers by its members for their professional activities.

The construction of the building will be undertaken by Chandigarh Administration. The cost of the construction including any escalation or revision will be borne by the District Bar Association.

It has been decided by the Administration that the tentative time schedule for the completion of the project is three years. Once completed, the building will be handed over to the District Bar Association for further allocation of individual chambers to the members of the Association.

For the first 10 years from the date of start of work at the site, the District Bar Association is exempted from paying the ground rent to the Chandigarh Administration in respect of the land.

It has been decided that the District Bar Association will also be liable to pay any other charges, taxes, duties or any such dues which any authority including Chandigarh Administration, the Municipal Corporation or the Government of India may levy under any law applicable at the relevant point of time. In addition to this, the individual lawyers will also be personally responsible for payment of the electricity and water charges etc, in respect of their respective chambers.

The original plan of the building will not be altered without the prior written consent of the Chandigarh Administration.

Heading: HC asks NGO to point out grey areas in Punjab Police Act - Indian Express
Content:
While the ominous threat of amputation of the diabetic foot looms large on patients, the small community of specialised vascular surgeons says that the burden can be reduced substantially through surgical techniques. According to the surgeons, if proper diagnosis is made on time and the correct surgery is performed, several legs and feet could be saved.

Talking to Newsline, on the sidelines of the annual conference of the Vascular Society of India, being organised at the GMCH, Sector 32, the secretary of the society and senior adviser at the Army Hospital, Captain V S Bedi said, "Just like the procedure in heart surgeries, the blocked blood vessels in the legs are surgically treated to avoid amputation. We have been performing these surgeries for a few years and amputation have been avoided."

Bedi added that strict surveillance of patients and early diagnosis are vital in treating the patients. Citing the example of the Kargil War, Bedi added: "Following the new techniques, the amputation in the Kargil War were just in single digit, much less than those in the earlier conflicts."

Estimates suggest that of the nearly 40 million people suffering from diabetes in India, 15 per cent of the patients are likely to develop diabetic foot and 40 per cent of these are likely to go in for "lower extremity amputation" — amputation starting from the toe.

Other estimates indicate that of the nearly 40,000 legs amputated every year in the country, most of them result from an infection in a diabetic foot. While the surgery offers hope, the extreme shortage of vascular surgeons in the country stands as a big challenge. "There are just 40 to 45 vascular surgeons in the country, which is a woefully small number compared to the burden of complications and the diabetic load of the patients," said Dr Ravul Jindal, Fortis Hospital Mohali.

Heading: Soon, city homes to get LPG through piplelines - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure that the common man does not suffer due to any wrong policies or norms adopted by the Punjab Police or its excesses, the Punjab and Haryana High Court will decide on significant issues raised in a public interest litigation (PIL) by Resurgence India, an NGO from Ludhiana.

The NGO has been directed to prepare a list of suggestions and grey areas in the Punjab Police Act or its functioning and submit it to the High Court, after which the Punjab government will file its reply. Before passing the directions, the HC questioned the motive of the petitioner in filing the PIL.

Rubbishing the claim that the PIL has been filed on the motivation of certain IPS officers, Advocate A P S Shergill, counsel for NGO, submitted that the PIL was filed in 2003 and was not motivated at all.

The petitioner submitted that the case was relegated back by the Supreme Court to the High Court.

"Any issue which the Supreme Court has not examined, we are not inclined to examine. Where is the issue of public interest? If IPS officers are affected then they can always come to High Court. All India Service Rules is not an issue, which an NGO will raise. The IPS officers can themselves come, why the NGO needs to represent them, where is the question of NGO raising an issue," the Bench observed.

Replying to the query, Shergill submitted that the posting of non-cadre officers on cadre posts results in violation of D K Basu judgment, which aims at protecting human rights.

Heading: Redundant syllabus or chasing money — PU students shun Sanskrit - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of the city will soon be able to escape the hassles of booking and waiting for LPG cylinders. In a pilot project by the Indian Oil Corporation in the city, cooking gas will soon be supplied through pipelines.

The IOC has, at present, set up the project at the Indian Oil Colony in Sector 44 in collaboration with the Sunshine Gas Agency. A bank of cylinders has been created in the colony and pipelines have been laid connecting the bank with each household.

Ravleen Uppal of the Sunshine Gas Agency said the bank is catering to around 23 houses in the colony. "It is for the first time in the city that gas is being supplied through pipelines. A meter has been provided in each house and monthly bills will be taken from the residents. In case the number of households is more, an underground tank can be set up," she said.

The cost to install the equipment cost each house around Rs 15,000. This will go down as the number of houses increase. The set up is equipped with an auto cut system as well as a number of gauges. In case of leakage, the gauges indicate the reduced pressure and the auto cut system snaps the supply. The residents also have the provision of cutting off their individual supply in case a leak is detected.

Jagdeep Rana, senior area manager, IOC, said: "This is a pilot project. We are holding talks with builders in Zirakpur, Panchkula and Mohali to extend this facility to other colonies and areas. A large number of high-rise residential buildings are coming up and this would be an additional facility for the residents."

He adds: "With gas being supplied through pipelines, the residents would not have to wait for days for the cylinder to arrive and of course the problem of receiving cylinders of inadequate weight would be solved. It certainly has its advantages."

Heading: ‘Library services need to be made user-friendly’ - Indian Express
Content:
At Panjab University, the department of Sanskrit appears to have lost its sheen over the years with the number of students seeking admission declining by the year. For the authorities, the entire blame for the development lies with the changing trend that sees more students opting for money-making options.

While the department offers 60 seats for MA in Sanskrit every year, not even half the number are filled as there are hardly 20 to 25 takers for the same.

Talking to Newsline, Prof Shankar Jha, chairperson of the department said: "We are losing our heritage and the government needs to take immediate steps to restore the same. There are no incentives available for students studying Sanskrit at the higher level and, thus, the government needs to start thinking on those lines."

While adding that students over the years have started finding the language boring and useless, Prof Jha suggested that more scholarships need to be made available to students to retain their interest in the language.

The dismal picture continues at the doctorate level as well with hardly four or five students doing their

PhD every year from the department.

A majority of those who choose to stick to the subject comprise the civil service aspirants, for whom Sanskrit serves as a scoring subject.

For the students, it is the "age-old syllabus" that has caused them to loose interest in the subject.

Sunil, a student from the university added, "Anything and everything becomes boring if we don't change it.

The syllabus for all the subjects should be revised regularly."

Heading: ‘Women more superstitious than men, mostly due to lack - Indian Express
Content:
Scholars of Library Science need to re-orient and re-design the mechanics and dynamics of their approach, aimed at diversification and spreading knowledge among the masses. They should also develop a continuous interface with librarians and experts from the industry. This would, inter alia, help in generating better employment opportunities for the forthcoming generation of library scientists.

These views were expressed by Punjabi University Vice-Chancellor Jaspal Singh, while presiding over a UNESCO-sponsored 'Training

-the-Trainers' workshop on Information Literacy in South and Central Asia at the university senate hall on Wednesday.

Singh advocated the cause of using new media and information technology as a result-oriented mechanism for enlarging the vistas of knowledge and breaking the dogmatic mindsets.

Amrik Singh, former Punjabi University vice-chancellor, in his inaugural address, observed that the information scenario — in schools, particularly in Punjab was in a shambles. "Only the right kind of training in digital technology in schools, which should be made mandatory, can help achieve the desired goals in the field of education," he said. Referring to the present policy of the state government, he said that "it talks of a dozen issues relating to school education but computers are not mentioned anywhere rendering the exercise as political rather than academic."

Earlier, Pradeepa Wijetunge, director of the National Institute of Library and Information Sciences, University of Colombo, highlighted the need for implementing the new information literacy models for better results. Harish Chandra, a librarian at IIT Madras, stressed upon developing a flexible and adaptable attitude to make the library services more user-friendly.

Both Wijetunge and Harish Chandra underlined the need for establishing the UNESCO Information Literacy Centre at Punjabi University.

Heading: SAD-BJP wrests control of Kharar MC - Indian Express
Content:
"Women are far more superstitious than men. This has a lot to do with the lack of education among women," stated Sarjit Talwar of the Rationalist Society of Punjab on Wednesday. He was conducting a workshop on explaining scientific miracles at the Commonwealth Youth Programme Asia Centre. More than 30 teachers from schools all over the city participated in the seminar which was organised by the Environment Society of India.

While addressing the teachers, Talwar said that since women are suppressed in every sphere, it has made them prone to superstitions. "We live in a male-dominated society. Also, women are usually not self-dependent. This is more prevalent among womenfolk in rural parts of the country. But their urban counterparts too are equally blindfolded," stated Talwar.

For the last twenty four years, Talwar has been working to create awareness among people regarding superstitions. "I had seen my friends and relatives believing the so-called godmen blindly. This is the reason that I took up this cause. My aim is to expose those people who take the gullible for a ride and to inculcate a scientific temperament among the masses," said Talwar.

His belief, as he states it, is that "everything has a scientific explanation to it". Being possessed by an evil spirit, walking barefoot on burning coal and other such notions all have logic behind it, he says. "For example, our skin has a tolerance power of not more than three seconds. Following this principle, these godmen are able to perform such feats," explained Sarjit.

In his effort to awaken the scientific temperament in people, Talwar also organises counselling sessions. "I have people coming to me who say they are possessed. After listening to them, they are generally found to be suffering from some kind of psychological problem and we help them overcome it," said Talwar.

He is also working towards creating awareness about female foeticide through street plays and seminars. "It is essential to check this problem in time. We should not forget that women are generators of the society," said Talwar.

Heading: Industrialists upbeat about new policy - Indian Express
Content:
Amid high drama, the ruling SAD-BJP combine finally wrested control over all the three coveted posts of the Kharar Municipal Council (MC) at a special meeting on Thursday.

Sukhwant Singh from Ward 8 was elected the new president while Roshan Lal from Ward 9 and Jai Bhagwan Singla from Ward 15 became the senior and junior vice-presidents respectively.

After waiting for 53 days since their election on September 14, all 15 municipal councillors were administered the oath of allegiance by Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who was convener of the maiden meeting of the present MC House.

No sooner did Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh's son Jasjit Singh Bunny, along with Morinda SAD MLA Ujjagar Singh Badali, put forth some slips to pick the name of new city chief and two deputies, Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu, who being ex-officio member has the voting right, and two Congress councillors Kamal Kishore and Sarabjeet Kaur walked out of the meeting.

Calling it undemocratic and illegal, Sidhu accused Capt Kanwaljit of resorting to unfair means to grab the MC top posts.

In the presence of remaining 13 councillors, however, including 10 of the SAD-BJP combine and three independents, the SDM called for a proposal to elect new president.

On this, Bunny asked councillor Darshan Singh from Ward 1 to pick up a slip from a few put forth by him. The slip, which Darshan picked, bore the name of Sukhwant, whose name was seconded by councillor Jai Bhagwan Singla while all other present councillor agreed on him as new president.

Ward 4 councillor Gurprem picked another slip, which bore the name of Roshan Lal, whose name was seconded by councillor from Ward 12 Jagjit Singh and supported by the other councillor to take over as senior vice-president. For electing junior vice-president, Sukhwant picked a third slip bearing the name of Singla, who got the support from the House.

Heading: Protest against GMADA, Admn against hike in conveyance deed registration - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed new industrial policy will not only revive the existing industry but will also attract new industry in the state, say the industrialists of Mohali.

According to sources, the new policy, expected to be released shortly, will supersede the policy released by the Housing Department in January 2008. The major relaxations in the new policy are likely to include reduction in the requirement of the size for commercial conversion and reduction in fees for commercial conversion of the plots in the existing industrial areas. The charges for commercial conversion are likely to be reduced considerably from the rates fixed earlier.

The new policy, said sources, will allow setting up of a multiplex on an industrial plot measuring 4,000 square yards in the existing industrial area.

Setting up of cafeteria and ATMs on such plots has already been permitted by Punjab State Industrial Export Corporation.

A cross-section of industrialists in Mohali, told Newsline that the move will relax the norms and make setting up of new industry more attractive in Punjab.

"It is high time such moves are introduced to revive industry in the state," said Sukhbir Singh Shergill, general secretary, SAS Institute of Information and Technology, Mohali. Shergill said the policy should be made applicable to the entire industrial area of Mohali and not be confined only to Phase VIII-B.

Industrial areas should be provided with better infrastructure, said Sanjay Gupta, director, Spray Engineering Devices Limited. This will help Mohali industrial area become a hub of the BPO industry, he said.

The 200-foot wide road connecting Kharar to Airport and Banur will give a boost to the Mohali industrial area, said Rajiv Syal, a renowned structural designer of the city.

The road will be completed in the scheduled time of nine months, said Avtar Singh Walia, the managing director of the construction company which is allotted the project.

Sources said the industrialists have also been demanding permission to allow warehousing in the industrial area for long.

"We need a positive and quick response from the government about giving permission to set up business here, said NRI Shishu Bedi, who is also founder chairman of e-billboard.com.

Bedi has recently started his business of electronic advertisements in Mohali.

State Industries Minister Manoranjan Kalia had recently promised that the new industrial policy will fulfill the demands of the industrialists.

Heading: Love & Longing - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of Mohali have united against the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) and the district administration to protest the hike in the rates for registration of conveyance deeds of plots in Mohali.

Under the banner of the Joint Action Committee (JAC) of all the Residents Welfare Associations of Mohali, the residents have launched a mass public protest against the "arbitrary" decision to register the conveyance deeds of plots at the prevailing collector rates instead of their actual allotment price. In a statement issued on Thursday, Baljeet Singh Kumbra, general secretary, JAC, announced to lay siege to the GMADA and Deputy Commissioner's offices in Mohali on November 26.

"We have called local residents to gather outside the GMADA office in Sector 62, from where we will take out a protest march to the DC office in Phase I," said Singh.

Citing the system being followed in Chandigarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and other neighbouring states, where conveyance deeds of plots are registered at the actual allotment price, the JAC urged the state government to order the withdrawal of the fresh order and revoke the system of registration at actual allotment rates.

The JAC has threatened to intensify the stir if their demand is not met soon.

Heading: Designer notes - Indian Express
Content:
It cannot be quantified or locked in a time capsule. Love transcends everything, romances Sooraj Barjatiya's new Prem, Sonu Sood

Sonu Sood is quite familiar with loss. It's the inheritance from it that he has found his answers in. And so, he holds long conversations, with the self, and with his mother who passed away last year. "She used to say no sms or phone call can match up to the warmth a letter provides, and I treasure hers to date," Sonu makes it a point to write one, pen a diary entry every day. It's one of these endearing qualities that Sonu brings out in his characters, especially the latest one, Sooraj Barjatiya's Ek Vivah Aisa Bhi. Playing the romantic lead as Barjatiya household's new Prem, Sonu's quite confident carrying the film on his well worked out shoulders. "In an industry that's churning out thrillers and action, a soft romance might come as a fresh breath of air," he smiles, in town for an ICL match and yes, to talk about his film that releases this Friday. "Barjatiyas need no promotion, they are a brand in themselves, an institute which is passionate about whatever it does. As for the film, I play what I am best at and still connected with - a small town boy who embarks on a journey from Bhopal to Mumbai to pursue his dream, music. But little does he realise that it will take 12 years to reunite with the love he left behind." But does love, in restless, frivolous times like these survive 12 long years? "True love can survive a 100 years, and if it's not, it won't even last a 100 seconds! For love, time has no meaning, it transcends all these physicalities," says the romantic who has strummed the guitar for the film. "I used to play it in my engineering days in Nagpur, and it came in handy in the film," he sure has touched all the right chords!

From struggling as an actor, doing south films to winning the National award for Bhagat Singh, Sood has come a long way. As Surajmal of Jodhaa Akbar, he got the audience up and take notice. Now, after Ek Vivah, Dhoondte Rah Jaoge will make them spin around him. "I'm looking forward to this one," Sonu's playing 11 different characters in the film. "Big B from Deewar, Shah Rukh from DDLJ, Sunny in Gadar, Aamir in Lagaan...you name it and I've played and dubbed it!"

Had he not forayed into acting, cricket would've been taken seriously by Sood. "But I never got a chance...nobody gives one to small town guys!" C'mon, films have been fair enough!

Heading: Speak out! - Indian Express
Content:
After designing JJ Valaya's Lifestyle studio, Manjeet Bullar wants to leave his mark on the city

Anything can be a fashion item, as long as the object has been sufficiently overlooked to merit a re-interpretation," says interior designer Manjeet Bullar, here to study the city and design a collection especially for it. In the profession for over 25 years now, Bhullar's file flaunts names like Victoria and Albert Museum, London, and JJ Valaya's Lifestyle studio. "It just happened over time. I defied all trends, worked with history and people liked it," he sums up his journey in two lines and says that his furniture and designs USP is that they have a soul. "House lives with us and each and every part of it has to be dealt with carefully," Bhullar goes beyond the conventional list of what's in and what's out. "Style by its very virtue is timeless and classic and fashion is sweeping," he states his signature style.

The designer, having been amongst the first ones to bring in the concept of 'Retail Destination', discloses that history and culture are his muse. "Themes, references and concepts that are from an ancient era appeal to me," chirps Bhullar, reeling that for now sufism, Indian history and Islamic thought are his inspiration. Viewing products beyond their form, "I like to bring in cultural aesthetics in my artifacts and believe that design and culture are constantly interacting," Bhullar sees every object as symbolic and weighs it on its practical rendering. As his gaze moves around the city roads and ticks off elements, his observations are no different. "The sharp and cutting lines of the city would be hard to match. The organic geometry will have to be kept in mind," Bhullar asserts that to compliment the "wholesome character" of the city, he will have to use all elements in the design dictionary. "Just like every alphabet of vocabulary is used to make a complete story, here too all sensibilities will have to come together," he draws a rough sketch of his collection that will be customized for Chandigarh and will be showcased in December. For now, he'll host an interaction at the Government Museum and Art Gallery, Sector 10, on November 8 at 5:00 pm.

Heading: Will power - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra may be miles away but Youth United vows to make themselves heard

It's not just about feeling the heat, it's about standing up and making a difference. "India's beauty and strength lies in its diversity, when one part of the country burns in 'hate crime' every region is bound to be affected," tells Jyotindra Nath, President, Youth United. The group is holding a signature campaign 'United we Stand' at the Sukhna Lake on November 7, 5.30 pm onwards. This will be followed by a candle light vigil. "The idea is to extend our support in favour of the people who are suffering in Maharashtra due to regionalism," Love Upadhayay shares.

"We urge people to join this campaign to bring peace in Maharashtra and other parts of country. We are not raising our voices against any particular section of society but a specific attitude that leads to hate crimes. Our constitution allows us to move freely in the country and seek employment. When the law is supporting free movement, such politically motivated actions hamper national integrity," chips in Aman Ahuja. Youth United has also written to letters to the Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister and President of India requesting them to bring harmony and fraternity back to the state. As students, the group's concern is all the more stronger. They feel that such activities will limit the growth of youngsters all over the country who look up to certain career destinations. Himanshu Gupta believes, "It's illegal to curb freedom this way, more than that it's unnatural. But the sad part is that the Maharashtra government is doing little for change, we do hope our efforts will make a difference." Join the cause.

Heading: Life in colour - Indian Express
Content:
If you like Salsa, then you will love the Bachata tells Hong Kong based DJ and dancer Will who is in the city to conduct special sessions

All of last year Salsa was and continued to be the toast of the town with back to back workshops, contests and performances. It had much to do with the formation of Club Salsa India spearheaded by city based dancer-couple Barsha and Varun D S Rana. While the two twirled their toes overseas bringing home awards and accolades, they also managed to convince Salsa dancers of repute to come and conduct workshops for dance enthusiasts on our home turf. After Alex and Kim who came in from San Francisco, this year's 2nd Annual International Salsa Bootcamp brings in DJ Will from Hong Kong. But, hey what's a DJ doing on a salsa dance floor? "I DJ only on Salsa songs," smiles the affable William who back home in Hong Kong is a financial advisor by day and dancer-DJ by night. Originally from Toronto, Canada, DJ Will has won many competitions and is also the official DJ for Hong Kong Salsa Congress and the Hong Kong Salsa Festival. But as much as he likes Salsa, it's another dance form that DJ Will swears by. "It's called the Bachata and hails from the Dominican Republic," tells William who first saw the very sensual dance on a visit to Cuba with a friend. "Bachata isn't as fast paced as Salsa, rather it's slow and sexy," tells Will as he takes to the floor showcasing some moves for us. The music is in sync. "You will be surprised to know there are so many Salsa singers out there cutting albums by the minute. With Salsa workshops and contests, I saw a need gap for a DJ," tells Will who regularly steps in to spin the Salsa special nights back home. "One of my favourites are Celia Cruz, Tito Puente and Oscar Deleone. Not only are their superb Salsa singers but dancers too," mentions the DJ who is on his first trip to what he calls, "Incredible India".

"I have heard so much about your country," spoke Will who will be stepping in as judge for the Open Salsa Championship to be held on November 7 at Hotel Shivalikview. "He will also be conducting two-day 'Groovy Latin Workshop' at Ozone on November 8 and 9 followed by a Salsa party at Arabia on Saturday where he will play a role of DJ," listed out Varun who is keen to take Salsa to the next level in the city. "Sponsorship is an issue and we hope sponsors get magnanimous," he says. As for now, we can make the most of the man who is much "willing" to take us on to the dance floor. Over to you.

Heading: The Right Moves - Indian Express
Content: The agony, the ecstasy, struggle, success...the making of a man, painter, artist, MF Husain, was charted in Ekjute Theatre group's Pencil Se Brush Tak, staged on Wednesday night at the all-new Tagore Theatre. Houseful, the play directed by Nadira Babbar based on MF Husain's memoir and written by Varun Gautam gave an absorbing insight into the lesser-known facets of the life of the painter. Peppered with music, visuals of Husain's paintings, humour and a huge cast, the play effortlessly brings forth the intricate details of what makes Husain the phenomenon he his. Portrayed by three actors, Pawan Uttam, Anup Soni and Tom Alter, the play from the early years to present day deals with not just Husain's art, but his growth and journey as a son, husband, father, artist, film-maker and celebrity. Born in a small village in Maharashtra, Husain's talent was both recognized and encouraged by his family despite the hardships. His short tryst with a tailoring class, falling in love with Jamuna and losing her, joining the evening art school, innumerable attempts to find his feet in Mumbai, facing discouragement, his undying spirit and belief in his work and art, love for India, its culture, heritage...in just over two hours you Fida up, close and personal. The last part of the play is about Husain as a brand, a celebrity, his fascination with Madhuri, his numerous shows, studios abroad...Tom Alter plays the present-day Husain to perfection and all the three actors come together on stage to recount the colourful journey.

Heading: Pursuit of Happiness - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when career course options are aplenty, what gives students an edge when they step out in the fast paced world is that little bit extra information and finesse up their sleeves. "Education in whatever field it might be has to be all rounded," mentioned Vandana Worrell, the centre head at Sky Hawks Institute in Sector 35 which conducted a unique seminar on cosmetology and gynecology for its aviation and hospitality students on Thursday. Sky Hawks, a part of the Career Weavers Consultants Group, imparts training in aviation and hospitality management coupled with personal and corporate training. Taking the students through the seminar was Dr Krishan Mohan Kapoor, senior consultant and head of department, cosmetic surgery, Fortis Hospital, Mohali and Dr Swapna Misra, consultant, obstetrician & gynecology, Fortis Hospital, Mohali.

Dr Kapoor stressed that since in aviation and hospitality sectors, an immaculate look is a basic necessity, students should have healthy and beautiful skin. Hence the need for developing vital skin care habits early and making them part of the daily routine for the long term. Dr Kapoor educated the students about basic body chemistry, the pH scale, skin histology, hair trichology, sanitation techniques and hygiene etc. Dr Misra stressed on certain health and gynecological problems that flight attendants themselves, their flight passengers or hotel guests could face, especially during the flight, and how they can cope with these problems effectively. "At Sky Hawks, we pride ourselves at imparting the students with the best, all-round training in aviation and Hospitality. Hence, besides regular classroom theory and mock-training sessions, we keep organizing such seminars for the benefit of our students," mentioned Worrell who finds that since this particular sector has a glamourous side to it, there has been undue focus on the same in such bad economic times.

Heading: Up, where we belong - Indian Express
Content:
His characters are strictly Biblical, yet bear an eerie resemblance to himself. He paints them dark, gloomy and mysterious but that's no way like him. He brings out the negativity in him through his art and clears the space within for a composed self. Meet Avijit Roy through his paintings, but be warned. The portraits are not what he is but what he is not. 24 hung paintings give you an insight into the mind of the artist and the way he sees the emotions that rule us.

Dark colours rule the canvas conveying essentially dark moods. Buddha and Christ's shut-eyed portraits invite you into meditation and spirituality. One comes across spiritual symbols, chakras and motifs in all the frames. To cleanse the soul, he pours milk over the Christ portrait. The saintly figure is depicted in a myriad of moods, his expressive eyes melting with wisdom. Adam finds himself at the centre of conflicts of violence, love and passivity reflected by a gun, knife, flower and a butterfly. Personifying autumn the artist paints a sombre and lonely lady looking for a bright red flower amidst the dense paleness of the forest. Adam and Eve figure in many frames, in state of separation, complexities of personas, winged in beauty. Shiva's trance closes the chapter for the time being.

On at Art Folio, 351- Sector 9D, Chandigarh till November 14.
