Heading: Cabinet nod to Rajpura thermal plant - Indian Express
Content:
Chances of release for fifteen-year-old Pakistani boy Naseer Sultan, lodged in a jail for the the past two months, brightened today after senior Pakistan High Commission officials met him in the jail for his consular clearance and promised every help in facilitating his return home.

Pak High Commission official Zulfikar Gurdazy said that ever since the case relating to his 'unintentional' entry into India came to their notice, they were verifying his credentials. Naseer was arrested near Ferozepur border. He had said that he had entered India to meet Bollywood star Shahrukh Khan.

The officials spent over three hours with him, interviewed him and were convinced that he hailed from Dir district in North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) in Pakistan. They said his travelling documents would be ready shortly to send him back to Pakistan. "It is a clear case of inadvertently crossing the international border and we are satisfied with his credentials. I will be submitting my detailed report to the High Commission and then we will request the Indian authorities to release him on humanitarian ground," said Gurdazy. He said he hoped Naseer would be freed in a few days but a lot depended on the Indian security agencies.

Naseer is lodged in the Faridkot juvenile home and was brought here yesterday for his consular access to the Pak High Commission officials.

Naseer had told his parents that he was going to school on August 16, but actually set out on the journey to meet hi favourite film star, Shahrukh Khan. "I took a bus to Lahore and then to Kasur and then walked on foot to reach the Indo-Pak border in two days. I kept moving ahead and was surprised when the Border Security Force rounded me up," he said.

After questioning, he was handed over to the Punjab police who registered a criminal case against him for entering India without valid documents. When he was taken to the local court he said that he wanted to see Shahrukh Khan in person and wanted to go to Mumbai.

The Punjab police have even stated that if he was sent back home they would have no problem as his intentions seem to be innocent.

"I never thought that a passport or visa is required to cross over to India'', said Naseer, a student of Class X. His family had also initiated a hunt for him and with the help of an Islamabad-based NGO, they had taken up the case of his release with Pak authorities.

Heading: WB halves user charges - Indian Express
Content:
Maharaja Ranjit Singh Police University to come up in Ludhiana

The Punjab Cabinet today gave its approval in principle for setting up a 1,200-MW thermal plant at Rajpura. Work on the project is likely to be inaugurated on December 8.

A decision to this effect was taken at a meeting of the state council of ministers here this evening. The meeting was chaired by Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal.

Giving details of the decision taken at today's meeting, CM's Media Advisor, Harcharan Bains, said the coal-based power project would be set up at Rajpura over 1078.16 acre on Build Own Operate (BOO) basis. It may be recalled that the construction work on Talwandi Sabo Power Project and Goindwal Sahib Thermal Plant with an installed capacity of 1980 MW and 540 MW respectively is on already and those two projects are likely to be operational by December, 2011.

The Cabinet also gave a green signal for establishing the Maharaja Ranjit Singh Police University at Ladhowal, near Ludhiana, for study and research in police-related subjects. The university would also carry out police education programmes for police personnel as well as for non-police persons. The state government would make a provision of recurring expenditure of Rs 5 crore per annum for the university, besides mobilisation of capital expenditure of Rs 50 crore from sources including the PIDB.

A new policy for opening private veterinary sciences colleges also got the nod. A screening committee, comprising of the directors of animal husbandry, fisheries and dairy development and registrar of Punjab Veterinary Council, has been constituted under the chairmanship of Secretary, Animal Husbandry, to interview prospective applicants and inspect the sites to assess the financial status, interest and capability of the applicants. The committee would send its recommendations to the state government.

The Cabinet also approved the acquisition of about 120 acre land in Attari and Roranwala village for setting up and integrated check post at the Wagah border in Amritsar.

The Cabinet also gave its approval for amending the Punjab Agricultural Produce Market Act, 1961, to enhance the period of super session of market committees for a period of two years. It would enable the state government to reconstitute the superseded market committees by May 17, 2009.

The CM Parkash Singh Badal also directed his cabinet colleagues to remain available to general public for three days every week in Chandigarh. Bains said the ministers would remain in Chandigarh on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

The Cabinet also approved the Punjab Works of Licensees Rules, 2008, prepared by the department of power on the basis of the rules framed by the Government of India in consultation with the PSEB, State Electricity Regularity Commission, Chief Electrical Inspector, Department of Personnel and Local Government Department.

Heading: Armed men loot Rs 40 lakh from Jalandhar GPO - Indian Express
Content:
Household user charges that were levied in rural areas as a pre-condition to avail World Bank aid have been halved.

Addressing mediapersons, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal said the WB has conceded to the long-pending demand of the state government. The CM said general category beneficiaries of the water supply scheme will now have to pay Rs 750 per household, while the SCs and those living in kandi belt, border and water-logged areas would have to pay Rs 400 and Rs 200, respectively. He said the World Bank has a Rs 1,280-crore aided water supply scheme for rural areas and as many as 612 villages had been covered under it up to September last.

The decision will benefit over 6.7 lakh rural households in 3,161 Punjab villages.

Meanwhile, Cabinet minister Bikram Majithia accused the previous Congress government of "stabbing the rural population in their back" by hastily signing the loan agreement with the World Bank without critically examining the implications of various conditions. Majithia said he received a communication today from the Country Director of the World Bank, conveying amendments in the beneficiary contribution. He said it has been decided that each Scheduled Caste household would derive benefit irrespective of the percentage of their population in that village.

Earlier, SC households used to get the benefit if their population in a particular village was over 40 per cent.

Badal said the process of re-organisation of blocks and tehsils in the state has been initiated and is likely to be complete in the next two months. Badal said all the 141 blocks, 77 tehsils and 76 sub-tehsils would be revamped to ensure all-around and balanced growth in the new model of rural development.

The CM announced that the state government had taken an in-principle decision to develop Attari as a new block. He said Rs 300-crore funds would be given to the 128 municipal committees and nagar panchayats within 15 days to undertake development schemes to upgrade the existing infrastructure of streetlights, tubewells and roads.

The CM said 26 municipalities under category-I would be provided Rs 3 crore each and the others a little less. Referring to the allocation of the Rural Development Fund, the CM said Rs 4 crore would be disbursed in each assembly constituency shortly.

The CM said he would call on the PM and Union Civil Aviation Minister Praful Patel shortly to apprise them of the impending crisis that has badly hit the trade and commerce in the region on account of flight cancellations at Rajasansi airport. The CM said the payment of 7 per cent DA installment to the employees would be released soon. Expressing satisfaction over the 98.3 per cent procurement by the state agencies, he said it was sad that merely 1.7 per cent was picked up by the Food Corporation of India against its target of 10 per cent.

Reacting to a query on Manpreet Badal's statement opposing subsidies, the CM said subsidies were being given across the world and would continue in the state as well.

Heading: 3 diarrhoea deaths in Tarn Taran village - Indian Express
Content:
Four armed persons looted Rs 40 lakh from the General Post Office (GPO) in the wee hours here today.

Security guard Ashok Kumar heard voices coming from inside the post office and before he could do anything, he was attacked by the armed men, who later tied him in a corner along with a labourer, who was also present on the spot.

Then, the robbers went to the strong room of the GPO and looted Rs 40 lakh. At 7 am when other employees came to join duty, they found that the office was locked from inside and cries could be heard, said sources. The staff members then scaled the wall, opened the door after and freed the two.

Senior Superintendent of Posts (SSP) N R Meena said the strong room was safe, and only a box was broken from where Rs 40 lakh were stolen. Fingerprint experts were summoned and a red alert has been sounded in the city, said SSP Pawan Rai.

Police are also investigating the role of employees. Sources said it seems that the looters were present on the premises last evening.

Heading: Parliament standing committee to visit Rajasansi, says Sidhu - Indian Express
Content:
Deaths of a two-year-old child and two adults, and increasing number of diarrhoea cases being reported in Wein Poin village in Tarn Taran district are giving sleepless nights to the residents as well as the health officials.

The authorities today took water samples from across the district and distributed chlorine tablets.

The deceased have been identified as two-year-old Arshdeep Singh, 40-year-old Hardev Singh and 60-year-old Jagir Kaur. Sources said the area was dotted by pools of dirty water that have not been cleared since long and these were contaminating the potable water supply.

Sources said earlier, diarrhoea had gripped Naushera Pannuan village too. Harjinder Singh, a resident of the area, said, "In the absence of a proper potable water supply channel, people have no choice but to consume contaminated water."

Balwinder Singh, another resident, charged the government with turning a blind eye towards the area.

Dr Gagandeep Singh, district epidemiologist, said the Health Department was working to study the real causes behind these deaths, as the cause may not necessarily be diarrhoea or gastroenteritis. "We have summoned the records of the patients from hospitals. Patients have been coming to us with complaints of diarrhoea, but it is not an outbreak."

Dr Singh said the Health Department had initiated awareness programmes in which the residents were being advised to consume boiled water, use chlorine tablets and keep their surroundings salubrious.

Heading: Bumper paddy to add Rs 400 cr to VAT kitty - Indian Express
Content:
BJP MP Navjot Singh Sidhu today met Union Minister for Civil Aviation Praful Patel in Delhi to discuss various airlines' decision to call off flights from the local Rajasansi International Airport.

Sidhu said members of the standing committee of Parliament on Civil Aviation would soon visit the airport. He said he told Patel that the airport was the backbone of this neglected border area and the Central and the state governments should do everything possible to save it.

"He told me that the difference of landing charges was not solely responsible for the airlines suspending their operations. There were

other reasons as well and the Centre will do its best to address the problem," said Sidhu.

He said the 18-member standing committee would assess the situation and press the government for remedial measures.

Sidhu said apart from the non-occupancy of first class seats from this airport in the international flights, the absence of facilities and infrastructure for cargo operations were also the reasons behind the airlines showing disinterest.

"I also requested Patel to resume the flight to Nanded either from Amritsar or Chandigarh, and he promised to look into the matter. I will not sit silently till the airport bounces back," asserted Sidhu.

Heading: Sinking feeling: earth-level goes down, houses develop cracks in Bathinda village - Indian Express
Content:
Basmati arrivals witness five-fold rise

A bumper paddy harvest in Punjab will not only add to buffer stocks of the country, but also make the state richer by Rs 400 crore. The Excise and Taxation Department is expecting a jump of Rs 75 crore over last year's purchase tax on paddy due to a good minimum support price (MSP), Excise and Taxation Commissioner A. Venu Prasad said.

Paddy arrivals in Punjab have already crossed last year's figure of 136.63 lakh MTs as on November 5 and procurement by state agencies has witnessed a jump of 15 per cent so far, as private purchases are down by 38 per cent from last year, according to the figures available with the Punjab State Agriculture Marketing Board.

Interestingly, basmati arrivals have registered an almost five-fold jump as compared to the corresponding period last year.

Against 1.46 lakh MTs last year, the arrival to date was 5.9 lakh MTs. Since arrival of basmati and other late-sowing fine varieties is picking up in the state mandis now, their total arrivals are expected to touch an all-time high.

Heading: Daily-wage employees seek regularisation, meet CM - Indian Express
Content:
A case of the level of earth going down has surfaced in Bathinda district with at least two houses in Chakk Fateh Singh Wala village developing major cracks.

The civil engineering department of Giani Zail Singh College of Engineering and Technology (GZSCET), that visited the site on Wednesday on the directions of Bathinda SDM K P S Mahi, has asked the residents of houses to vacate the houses immediately to avoid any untoward incident.

Led by the village sarpanch, a delegation had brought the matter to the notice of Bathinda administration. The adjacent houses of Jasvir Singh and Beant Singh have developed cracks and both have vacated the houses after the recommendation by the technical team. Adjacent to Jasvir's house on other side is the house of Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's in-laws.

"On October 30, I noticed that doors and windows were getting jarred. I also noticed some cracks at different places in the house as a result of the level of earth going down," Jasvir said, adding that the cracks were getting widened with each passing day.

Dr D Singal, head of the civil engineering department at GZSCET, who inspected the site along with Dr Sanjeev Aggarwal, said the inspection had revealed that the soil settlement had taken place on a specific area only. "The exact cause of the settlement would be known only after testing the soil profile. He added that change in the moisture content in the soil could be one of the reasons for the earth level going down. When contacted, SDM K P S Mahi said he had directed the civil engineering department of GZSCET to look into the matter. "The inspecting team is yet to submit their report to me," said Mahi.

Heading: Warning to Gurdaspur mining contractors - Indian Express
Content:
Daily-wage employees engaged with the Punjab Hospitality department, some for the last 15 years, are yet to be regularised by the State government. There are over 70 such people who have served between 10 to15 years with the department and are getting a meager Rs 132 every day as wages. A delegation of the employees met Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today.

The cash-starved state government, however, argues that since there are no sanctioned posts for these employees, it is hard to regularise them. There are nearly half-a-dozen such workers engaged at the Chief Minister's residence as well.

We had got some respite from the HC in 2003, however, after the government moved a special leave petition in the Supreme Court, the matter was sent back to the state government for re-examination, an employee said.

"The government had made a policy in 2006 wherein it said that all those who have served for ten years stand a chance to be regularised. This has not been implemented," he quipped. They urged the government to consider the case on humanitarian ground. "A permanent cook gets about Rs 14,000 a month against barely Rs 3,100 that is given to a daily-wage cook," they said.

Heading: Mandi gets ESI medical college - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government issued a strict warning to mining contractors of Gurdaspur to break their cartel and charge reasonable prices for sand and gravel, else their contracts would be cancelled.

Director-cum-Secretary Industries and Commerce VK Janjua said, "A show-cause notice has been issued to contractors of 52 quarries of Gurdaspur and they have been given a month to file replies." Last auction of quarries of Gurdaspur was held in 2002. After a lot of efforts, auction of 56 quarries was fixed for March 24 last and a committee was constituted with Deputy Commissioner as the presiding officer, besides other members, including SSP, geologist, tehsildar and mining officer. However, no bidder came forward. The auction was again fixed for July 11 and 111 bidders deposited the earnest money. On the basis of these bids, 52 contracts were allotted. This auction fetched a hefty amount Rs 4.17 crore per year. Increase in price of sand can also be attributed to the fact that the royalty rate has increased from Rs 20 to Rs 30 per tonne from April 2008, he added.

Heading: Govt steps up action against pvt buses; Minister too steps in - Indian Express
Content:
Both BJP govt, Cong claim credit for public sector institution

Mandi will finally have a medical college and multi-speciality hospital in the Central government sector, instead of the private sector, as proposed earlier by the BJP government.

To be set up by the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Corporation at a cost of nearly Rs 500 crore, the project will be completed in two years. The first batch of MBBS course, having 50 seats, half of these reserved for Himachalis, will begin in 2010-11.

The development, which comes in the backdrop of the BJP government and Congress' tussle over the medical college issue, has once again brought Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal and PCC president Kaul Singh Thakur on a collision course. The two spoke out about the project separately during the day.

The Chief Minister today said an ESI team headed by its Director General Prabhat Chander Chaturvedi, which had reached Mandi on Wednesday, has already selected a site proposed by the government. Health Minister Rajeev Bindal and Principal Secretary (Health) Deepak Sanan were with the team and finalised all modalities of the project, including selection of the land.

"It was at the initiative of the government and after a series of meetings with Union Labour Minister Oscar Fernandes that the Central government approved the medical college and hospital project," he told a hurriedly-called press conference here.

He stuck to the government stand that the previous Congress government had misled the people about sanctioning a medical college in the government sector after the Assembly elections had already been announced. He said, "There is nothing on record to show the government's approval.

A back-dated notification was issued in violation of the election code to hoodwink the Mandi people."

On return to power, the BJP government had proposed not one but two medical colleges for Mandi in the private sector. Some leading doctors working at Fortis and a few other hospitals, who hailed from Mandi, had approached him recently, expressing a desire to form a Trust to set up a medical college in Mandi. "The proposal is welcome," he added.

Dhumal said, "Right now, the government is very keen to see that work on the ESI medical college and hospital project is started on a war footing and Mandi's dream project is completed in time. I appeal to the Congress to shun politics over the issue and help the state and Central agencies to set up the medical institution."

Hours before him, Kaul Singh Thakur, who hails from Mandi, announced that the Congress' efforts to set up a new medical college have paid off. "After the BJP government had scrapped the earlier government proposal and announced the project in the private sector, the party had approached Sonia Gandhi and the Union Labour Minister to sanction an ESI hospital and college. We are grateful to the Centre, especially Oscar Fernandes," he said.

The PCC president accused the government of playing in the hands of private players, including Jaypee associates. "The decision to scrap the Congress proposal for Mandi college was done on political considerations. I have asked the Union Labour Minister to lay the foundation stone for the project at the earliest," he said.

He also hinted that the ongoing agitation on the medical college, started by Mandi Sangharsh Samiti, may be called off soon.

Heading: Kullu’s ‘bekaar ghaas’ may prevent superbug deaths in UK hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
Follwing Monday's accident in Kufri, the government's drive to check violation of transport rules by private bus operators today peaked, with 40 local buses in Shimla being challaned and Transport Minister Krishan Kapoor himself taking to the roads for surprise checks.

Highly agitated with today's government action, the local private bus operators resorted to a temporary chakka-jam near the Inter-State Bus Terminus, which resulted in chaos all over the town as the circular road got blocked for traffic. Students of schools and other passengers were also put to inconvenience as the bus operators refused to ply buses in protest.

It may be mentioned that the Minister himself checked various buses crossing the Secretariat near Chota Shimla for their permits, other records, over-speeding and music systems. Some buses were also impounded for not having complete documents, but looking at the situation where passengers had to suffer, the police released the buses with a warning after challaning them.

Meanwhile, president of the Shimla Local Bus Operators' Union Kamal Thakur termed this action of the government a mere "eyewash". "The police even challaned the vehicles that had violated no rules. The checking drive should be systematic as by swooping down upon operators in a single day, the police cannot ensure long-term safety of passengers," said Thakur.

However, to the pleasant surprise of passengers today, the local buses in Shimla were not overcrowded, with no one hanging out of the doors. The conductors and drivers ensured that the doors of the buses were closed, no music was playing and that the passengers were given tickets. In the past there have been several accidents as a result of buses with open doors. A school student had died in a similar manner a few years ago.

Heading: BJP gears up for Lok Sabha polls - Indian Express
Content:
A variety of grass considered 'Bekaar Ghaas' (useless grass) in Himachal Pradesh is likely to help prevent the death of thousands of British patients who die due to a superbug in hospitals here every year. Researchers in Bristol have discovered that a natural oil extracted from the 'bekaar ghaas' found in the state may eradicate the superbug — Meticillin-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus (MRSA) — from hospital wards. In 2007, nearly 1,600 patients died due to an infection by MRSA. Hospital authorities in Britain have been grappling with the superbug for years, but they now see a ray of hope in Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh. A team at the University of the West of England (UWE), Bristol, has found that essential oil from Himalayan oregano kills MRSA and is carrying out tests to determine how it can be used to fight the infection.

Preliminary research shows that small doses of the oil was needed to wipe out the bug. Experts found that the vapour also kills MRSA bacteria and may be useful in cleaning hard-to-reach areas. The oil even works at boiling temperature, so it could be used for disinfecting hospital sheets. "We have done a few preliminary tests and have found that the essential oil from the oregano kills MRSA at a dilution 1 to 1,000. Tests also showed that the oil kills MRSA both as a liquid and as a vapour and its antimicrobial activity is not diminished by heating in boiling water," UWE's project leader Professor Vyv Salisbury said.

The project was part of an initiative to provide rural communities with sources of income generated from sustainable collection of non-timber forest products in Kullu district.

"This is exciting as it also means that we could consider using the oil to develop disinfectant washing powders. We now aim to conduct a focused academic study in partnership with SGS Labs in Delhi that we hope will give the project the academic credence needed to market the oil," Professor Salisbury said.

Origanum vulgarem, referred to as 'bekaar ghaas' or 'useless grass', is a relatively common herb that grows in high-altitude meadows throughout the Himalayan region. It is perceived by many villagers to have no culinary, medicinal or economic value. "Once we are able to start providing a sustainable income for villages in Kullu, the scope for up-scaling and replication in other parts of the Himalayan region is enormous," added Professor Salisbury.

Ben Heron from Biolaya Organics, which is closely involved in the project in India, said, "We started working with oregano because it is a species that, if managed properly, can be collected year after year without depleting the population in the wild. Our aim is to be able to pay the local herb collectors the equivalent amount that they would normally earn from collecting endangered medicinal herb species, so that they become less dependent on the extraction of these plants for their livelihoods."

The scientists have won the SEED award for the project, which involves working with a laboratory in New Delhi, a community-based organisation and an environmental research institute in Himachal Pradesh.

The team will be presented the award at the SEED award conference on November 17 at the German Embassy in New Delhi by the German Minister of Environment, Sigmar Gabriel.

Heading: HPCC skips top names from election-duty list - Indian Express
Content:
Stepping up an exercise to gear up the rank and file of Bharatiya Janata Party in view of the coming parliamentary elections, senior leaders of the party have asked the workers to take a pledge for eliminating the prevailing notion of anti-incumbency in their respective regions.

The frontline leaders of all five Assembly segments, who discussed the issues of developing differences between workers and party leaders and their failure in educating the masses concerning the achievements of the government, pledged to show the door to the Congress in the coming Lok Sabha elections.

These discussions were done in a two-day meeting held under the chairmanship of district unit president H.N. Saini. The meeting, which ended on Wednesday evening, was inaugurated by state party chief Jai Ram Thakur and attended by Narender Bragta, Renu Chadha and all sitting MLAs, including Dr Rajeev Bindal. Sources in the party revealed that though the meeting was also attended by Shanta Kumar loyalists, a large numbers of his supporters were sore over the lack of proper coordination between the government and party rank and file.

Heading: INLD flays Hooda govt for Bhiwani killing - Indian Express
Content:
Names of some of the top state leaders are missing from the list of party leaders who will carry out the campaign in Delhi and Rajasthan for the forthcoming assembly elections, released by the Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee.

The names missing from the list includes MPs Selja, Dr Arvind Sharma and Atma Singh Gill, Finance Minister Birender Singh, Power Minister Randeep Singh Surjewala and Haryana Deputy Chief Minister Chandra Mohan.

The list of party leaders for the campaign was finalised by the HPCC president Phool Chand Mullana two days ago in the All India Congress Committee office at New Delhi. While the leaders assigned duty in Delhi start their tour from November 10, those in Rajasthan will start campaigning from November 17.

Majority of the party leaders were present in the HPCC meeting. On asking why some important names had been left out, Mullana said the HPCC had intimated all the state leaders to send a consent note to intimate which state they wanted to campaign in and they all had been asked to be present at the HPCC meeting in Delhi. Some of the leaders did not intimate, he said.

"Birender Singh has been assigned special election duty by the AICC in Rajasthan. He expressed his inability to attend the HPCC meeting in Delhi since he was attending the All India Finance Ministers' conference at that time. Selja is on a tour to China and will be back only by November 13. Some leaders who have not been assigned election duty had not replied to the HPCC letter,'' said Mullana.

Talking to The Indian Express, Randeep Surjewala said his name was not in the list since it was specific to Delhi and Rajasthan. I would go to the other states.

Dr Arvind Sharma has been at loggerheads with Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda in the past and had made a futile bid to join BSP just before the UPA government's trust vote in Parliament, a few months ago.

Mullana said the campaign leaders would be divided in two categories. One category will include main speakers of the party such as Bhupinder Singh Hooda, MPs Dr Ram Prakash, Rao Inderjit Singh, Avtar Singh Bhadana, Navin Jindal, Deepinder Hooda and ministers Capt Ajay Singh Yadav, Kiran Choudhry, Meena Mandal, MLAs Balbir Pal Shah and Anand Singh Dangi, Political Advisor to the CM, Professor Virender Singh, who will be sent for campaigning initially. Heading: ‘State would be power-surplus by 2011’ - Indian Express
Content:
Senior INLD leader and former Haryana finance minister Sampat Singh today demanded probe by a sitting judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in the recent killing of a student in Bhiwani by the Haryana police. Singh said the government should announce a long term policy on paddy. "There should be no ad hoc policies on MSP, export, classification as basmati and non-basmati and other related issues concerning the paddy crop," he said. Heading: Hello, brother - Indian Express
Content:
Sanjeev Bhaskar returns with Mumbai Calling to take forward his war against racism

How did you work out the theme for Mumbai Calling?
Producer Allan McKeown was interested in setting a comedy in a call centre in India. I started writing a movie some years ago set in a call centre, which I had abandoned to pursue other projects. I already had some homework done. It all seemed a natural fit to dust off those ideas into this new project and develop a situation comedy. Nitin Ganatra as an actor and Simon Blackwell as writer are both friends and colleagues, so I was able to bring them on board and they added to the series.

What's your character Kenny Gupta like?
Kenny Gupta is a British born Indian who has never been to India and, although he looks like everybody else, he's still a fish out of water and is constantly looking forward to the day he can return to his cold, rainy, depressing bit of London.

Yet another attempt at speaking out against racism?
My work has always been about playing with people's perceptions of stereotypes from Goodness Gracious Me through The Kumars at Number 42 through to the documentary series India with Sanjeev Bhaskar, and I hope also with my contribution to Mumbai Calling.

How different is the racism scene in UK now?
Better than it was when my parents came here. After President Obama, who knows we may have an Indian Prime Minister of the UK too.

Given the current economic scenario and the international take on outsourcing to India, is there not a possibility that the show might face criticism?
Mumbai Calling is entertainment and thus employs dramatic license. It isn't a documentary so any criticism other than from an entertainment point of view I think is pointless.

Your wife, Meera Syal, has not been a part of Mumbai Calling. What is she up to?
Meera has been writing movie scripts and acting in a comedy on British TV, called Beautiful People, so she's kept busy.

What do you think of comedies from India?
As mass appeal, comedy in India struck me as sometimes lacking in sophistication but this certainly seems to be changing in recent times, particularly in the films. We have a generation in India now that can not only compete with the West in terms of commerce but also entertainment.

The adaptation of international formats of laughter shows has triggered many series here. Comment.
I can't comment on any specific one except perhaps The Kumars format that was tried in India. In my experience the problem with buying the format is that what one buys is the end result not the experience that goes with it.

What makes a good joke—a situation or a punch line?
Both make a good joke, a combination of the two, make a great one.

Who are your favourite comedians?
Marx brothers, Woody Allen, Monty Python, Peter Sellers, Robin Williams, and the list goes on. At the moment my three-year-old son, Shaan makes me laugh more than anyone else.

(Mumbai Calling airs on HBO from November 8)

Heading: Close range? Encounter? Docs hint, then back off - Indian Express
Content:
Varying floor space index a possibility following World Bank study on area-specific construction limits

The future of Mumbai's skyline may resemble that of Manhattan's today. In a decision that could have far-reaching implications for the city, the state government is taking a relook at the present restrictions on the vertical limit for buildings in Mumbai.

The Mumbai Transformation Support Unit (MTSU), state government advisory body, has undertaken a World Bank-funded study that would ultimately lead to a Floor Space Index (FSI) mapping for the city.

Explaining the concept, MTSU project director UPS Madan said, "Unlike Mumbai, most developed cities of the world do not have the concept of uniform FSI. An exercise in FSI mapping would be a more rational approach wherein different areas will be granted varying FSI. It would depend on factors such as whether the area is residential or commercial, its proximity to business districts, public transport corridors or green areas."

The report, which is being prepared by a team of planners and economists led by World Bank appointed urban planner Alain Bertaud, will be ready in another couple of months. According to Madan, the World Bank team will submit the basic formula for area specific FSI and mapping while local planners with knowledge of the situation on field will carry out the detailing.

The Floor Space Index (FSI) — the permissible built up area on a plot — is 1.33 for most of Mumbai. Over and above this, constructions in suburbs can load transfer of development rights and can consume a maximum FSI of 2. The concept of additional FSI in Mumbai at present is scheme-specific rather than area-specific. For instance, projects under the Slum Rehabilitation scheme, Urban Renewal scheme, the proposed cluster redevelopment scheme, townships, MHADA colonies and redevelopment of old buildings under Development Control Regulation 33/7 enjoy higher FSI than other areas.

"Depending on how the study reviews FSI use in the city, we will make necessary amendments to the Development Control Rules," said TC Benjamin, principal secretary for the state Urban Development department.

Madan added that the study will take a look at FSI usage in cities such as Singapore, New York and Seoul. "The norm for residential FSI across most cities if 0.5 to 4 depending on factors such as size of apartments. In case of bigger apartments, more FSI is granted considering low density in the area. For commercial districts the FSI is as high as 10 to 25," said Madan.

Developers in Mumbai have for long being demanding higher FSI in order to correct the demand-supply mismatch.

"Where even cities like Chennai and Hyderabad have a high FSI of 2.5, Mumbai was too conservative in its FSI policy. A differential FSI hand in hand with infrastructure development is a good idea. However with most projects in Mumbai being redevelopment projects, there won't be an immediate decrease in prices unless there is government intervention on resettling existing tenants or clear land titles as in the case of Dharavi," said developer Mayur Shah from the Marathon group.

Urban planners have welcomed the move albeit with some reservations. "Cities should be planned with varying FSI, like high FSI for low density higher income group colonies or low FSI to protect historic areas like Khotachiwadi. But any such study on FSI should also address the issue of affordable housing and infrastructure development through some regulatory mechanism," said Anirudh Paul, director, Kamala Raheja Vidyanidhi Institute of Architecture.

Heading: How IM used would-be grooms - Indian Express
Content:
JJ Hospital officials on Thursday set off a debate on Rahul Raj, suggesting initially that the police bullets that killed him could have been fired at close range, and then doing a U-turn denying it.

Raj had taken over a BEST bus at gunpoint before being shot dead by policemen. The post-mortem was done at JJ Hospital.

First, Dr B G Chikalkar, associate professor for forensic medicine, told NDTV 24×7, "After the firing the gunpowder gets stuck on the skin inside. If there is tattooing around the entry wound, it indicates close-range firing."

The denial came from Dr B M Subnis, dean of the Sir JJ Group of Hospitals. "Details of the post mortem are not available with me as it is a medico-legal case. The report has been submitted to the judge. Besides, the said doctor denies giving any such statement to the press."

Dr Chikalkar refused to comment any further. So did the head of his department, Dr A Nandedkar. The hospital issued a press statement saying the post mortem was done by a team of four qualified doctors in the daytime.

Later, the Mumbai Police crime branch denied there was any blackening around the wounds. "I received the post-mortem report this afternoon. There is no mention of any blackening. We will find out why Dr B G Chikalkar made a statement contrary to the report. He was one of four doctors who conducted the post-mortem," said JCP (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

The report identifies five entry wounds, two on the scalp and one each on the ear, chest and torso. "There is no way yet of knowing the distance from which he was shot. We will send specimens of the skin around the entry wounds to the Kalina Forensic Sciences Laboratory. Only an analysis can determine whether the shots were fired from close range, intermediate range or long range," said Maria.

Close range means anywhere up to six feet, experts say.

The post-mortem report would also be considered by the one-man inquiry being conducted for the state by the chief secretary, said government sources. "When the inquiry started, the police had not given the post-mortem report. Now they are expected to do so," a source said.

The state is independently recording statements of witnesses that will be cross-checked with statements received from police.

"Basically the statement of Manoj Bhagat is going to be most essential. He was the only person who saw what actually happened. He was shot and sitting there," said the source.

Heading: Sea link gets into land row - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Mujahideeen (IM) had surfed a matrimonial website for identities they could assume. The crime branch said IM men took details from the website and used these to forge documents. The idea was to get their hands on SIM cards.

Interrogation of arrested IM suspects reveals that one of them used to submit forged documents using photographs and ID details of men named on the site.

The police have now notified the website of the misuse. Two of the men who had posted their profiles on the website were, in fact, questioned after it was learnt that SIM cards in their names were used by the suspects.

"Over the last couple of years, the suspects had procured and used around 30 to 40 SIM cards bought in various cities. Anique Shafiq Sayyed, who ran a cellphone shop in Pune, was the one got the connections," said JCP (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

"Anique used to prepare the documents using identities of men who had posted their profiles. Depending on the city where the connection was required, Anique chose the people and procured SIM cards for Hyderabad, Secunderabad, Ahmedabad, Surat, Bangalore, Mangalore, Delhi, Mumbai." A resident of Mumbai and one of Bangalore were questioned when SIM cards in their names were found to have been used by the suspects.

Heading: Rewards over Raj controversy - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai Port Trust, MSRDC want same piece of land

A five-hectare piece of land has started a tug-of-war between the state government and the Mumbai Port Trust (MbPT). The state government wants the land to be allocated to the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) for the 22-km Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL) project, but the Trust is not willing to part with it.

The government wants the land to serve as the casting yard for the project at the Sewri end of the proposed bridge and the MBPT insists it needs it for a container freight station, part of its offshore container terminal project.

With work on the eight-lane, Rs 8,000-crore MTHL project, which will link Sewri in mainland Mumbai to Nhava across the creek, due to start on January 26, officials are trying to sort out the problem.

The land had been earlier allotted by MbPT to the Food Corporation of India for its godowns, which are now abandoned.

Senior state government officials said the MbPT had informed them that the land was meant for a container terminal project planned by the port authority, but they see no problem because the state would need the land only for three years (from 2009 to 2011) and the MbPT was to start its work on the container terminal 2012 onwards.

For the sea link, the MbPT has already given 2.9 hectares near an abandoned kerosene wharf and an adjacent triangular plot, which will be used for launching pre-cast beams to the construction site in the sea at the Sewri end.

The project still needed around 70 hectares for the pre-cast component and the City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) had handed over 50 hectares at the Nhava end. To reduce cost of construction and get the logistics in place for the ambitious project, the state needs around five hectare of land at the Sewri end.

Principal Secretary, Urban Development Department, T C Benjamin, had on Wednesday written to MbPT Chairman Rahul Asthana seeking a reconsideration of the decision so that the five-hectare land could be allotted to MSRDC for three years from 2009.

Senior officials said the issue would not hold up the MTHL work set to start in January. The piling and other civil works would be undertaken first, which would ensure the land for the casting yard would be needed only after that.

However, senior MbPT officials said they had already given some (the 2.9 hectare) land for the casting yard, but the state government wanted more. The land being sought was earmarked for a container terminal facility, they said and suggested that the state should instead look at the salt pan land in the city as an alternative. The state urban development department, however, maintains that salt pan land would not be feasible as it was under litigation and it was not easy to settle the dispute in a short time.

A senior MbPT official said, "If we don't have that (the land sought by the state government), we will be in trouble as there will be no place to keep the containers." The official added that the dredging work for the container terminal project was almost over.

The much-touted MTHL is aimed at providing better connectivity with the proposed international airport at Navi Mumbai and the growth centres in Raigad district. The sable-stayed bridge would also cut 15 km from the distance and save two hours of travel time. The state is not only planning to link MTHL and the Eastern Freeway through an approach road, but also setting up a monorail on the bridge.

Heading: Patient’s kin accuses hospital of selling babies; allegations baseless, says ACP - Indian Express
Content:
BEST to reward conductors, driver for 'presence of mind'
For showing their 'presence of mind', when Rahul Raj, a Bihari youth, had held passengers hostage in a Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) bus, the BEST committee passed a proposal to reward two bus conductors and bus driver.
Mahendra Ghule, one of the conductors who was on the upper deck when the incident occurred, will be receiving a reward of Rs 10,000 while the other conductor Shivaji Borade and driver A S Khan will get a reward of Rs 5000 each.
On October 27, Rahul Raj (23), a youth from Bihar had hijacked BEST bus no 322 on the pretext that he wanted to kill Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray for his anti-north Indian campaign. The youth who was later killed in the police firing also fired at a passenger and tried to strangle Ghule with a chain. Gule was on the upper deck of the bus.
In the melee, when Borade who was at the lower deck came to know that his colleague's life was in danger, he directed the bus driver Khan to halt the bus near a stop. After stopping the bus, Borade rushed to a police chowky to inform the cops about the incident.
"It was a good coordination work among these men and it helped to avert a major tragedy," said BEST committee chairman Pravin Chedda.
"They showed presence of mind for which they should be rewarded. In case of any promotions, they would be given a priority," said BEST committee member Ravi Raja who supported the proposal in the BEST committee meeting.
The BEST also announced a compensation of Rs 50,000 to Manoj Bhagat, the injured passenger in the incident.

Autopsy 'confirms' Rahul Raj was murdered, says father
PATNA: THE father of Rahul Raj, the Patna youth who was killed after attempting to hold a bus hostage, said on Thursday that his son's autopsy report confirmed his doubts that Rahul was "murdered" by the Mumbai Police on October 27. Meanwhile, a complainant has lodged another case regarding the incident against Raj Thackeray and others in a Patna court.
An enraged Kundan Prasad Singh told reporters that the autopsy report confirmed that bullets were fired at his son Rahul from a distance of less than 2 feet. "How can an encounter take place from such a close distance? He was shot at almost point blank range," said Singh.
Mumbai doctors said there were five entry wounds in the chest and head region of Rahul's body. There were only four exit wounds. A senior doctor had interpreted that the bullets were fired from close range, causing gunpowder to burn the skin around the wound.
Singh, who has decided to meet the President shortly to demand justice for his son, said: "My son was surely overpowered by the police and then shot dead so that it would like an encounter."
He added that the "fair report" prepared by medical experts of JJ Hospital, Mumbai, should open the eyes of the Maharashtra Government to the "bestiality" of its men in uniform. "I have been also seeking legal opinion to move the Supreme Court," he added.
Meanwhile, complaints continue to be filed against MNS chief Raj Thackeray and others in Bihar. One Vinay Kumar alias Bihari Bhaiya on Thursday filed a case against Raj and nine others accusing them of murder, criminal conspiracy and tampering with evidence in a Patna chief judicial magistrate court.
Vinay Kumar accused Raj Thackeray, Bal Thackeray, Maharashtra Home Minister R R Patil, the Chief Secretary and Vinoba Bhave Nagar police station in-charge of murder and criminal conspiracy.
In a fresh twist, Kumar also lodged a case against Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Sushil Kumar Modi, minister Ashwini Choubey and Patna DM Jitendra Srivastava and Patna Senior Superintendent of Police Amit Kumar, accusing them of tampering with evidence.

Heading: Thane, Gujarat,  MP police  gang up against robbers - Indian Express
Content:
A patient's husband on Thursday accused the staff of a suburban hospital in Jogeshwari (west) of medical negligence. He also accused the hospital of regularly selling babies. He has complained about medical negligence when his wife Tahira Sheikh (30) had undergone two operations in Mallika Hospital since March. In one of these operations when she was getting her uterus removed, her urinary tract was slashed. As a result, she was in great pain so she underwent a third operation where a plastic tube was placed without informing her after which she started falling sick. After visiting a private hospital she was advised to get her sonography done. The sonography showed the plastic tube and the doctors told the couple that this was the reason for her deteriorating health, he alleged.

They were also told that this was very serious as this was done without their knowledge. Tahira's husband Sahiblal Sheikh (40) then complained to the police and after seven days approached some mediamen to meet Dr Priti Shah who conducted the operations.

According to the Amboli police Sahiblal and a few miscreants also went to the hospital, started protesting, and created ruckus at the hospital. Among other allegations, Sahiblal also said that the hospital regularly sold babies. The Emboli police, however, state that his allegations are baseless and have filed a case against the men who forcibly entered the hospital along with him.

"I have been visiting this hospital for the past eight months and during that time a lot of employees here told me that babies were being sold," said Shill. He also says that they police did not take action immediately, "I made a complaint seven days ago and still nothing happened, that is why I have approached the media now," he added.

The local corporate Spayed Bargeman also investigated into the matter and her workers have been protesting at the hospital.

"We had heard that there were around 15-20 babies in a room up there. When we questioned the hospital authorities about them they refused to tell us anything and stated they would only talk to the police," said Changes Multani, brother of corporator Bargena.

 The Amboli police are now conducting enquiries into whether these babies were being sold in the hospital or these allegations were baseless. "As far as we know the babies belong to Bal Vikas Kendra which is an orphanage in Goregaon. I even spoke to someone from the orphanage and they say that the babies are in the hospital as they are sick and it is very difficult for them to take care of these babies when unwell," said Senior Police Inspector Ramesh Gavande from Amboli Police Station.

"These are just baseless allegations levelled by the patient's family to get money from the hospital. After he got nothing by filing a complaint on October 30, he decided to threaten the authorities by calling the media and a few people to create chaos in the hospital. He also fabricated stories about the sale of babies in the hospital. We have filed a case against 20-25 people who created chaos, including him," said Assistant Commissioner of Police Dilip Suryavanshi from the DN Nagar Division.

Heading: Metro project: change in plan to overcome design clash - Indian Express
Content:
'Conventional' methods of tackling crime is not enough to control them: SP

 

With a view to combat the threat of robber gangs who operate with a unique modus operandi of migrating from one state to another and committing armed robberies, the police from Thane rural have started collaborating and sharing intelligence with their counterparts in Madhya Pradesh (MP) and Gujarat.

Superintendent of Police Thane (Rural) Naval Bajaj said, "According to our intelligence, there are at least more than 100 such gangs operating in villages of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. They have the modus operandi of migrating from state to state and committing robberies, which normally frustrates the efforts of local police."

Bajaj added, "After committing the robbery, the gang would migrate to a different state without leaving any clue about to their original whereabouts, unlike local criminals whose backgrounds are known to the local police." Bajaj feels that sharing information and intelligence with the neighbouring states would help the police keep track of such gangs' movements and they can apprehend them as and when the information about their entry in the Thane area is received.

Though Bajaj claims that the gangs' activity in the rural parts of Thane is at a bare minimum, he accepted been in regular touch with his counterparts in MP and Gujarat.

The SP added that "conventional ways of tackling crime is not enough to bring such gangs to task".

"Recently, we had busted the dreaded Raja Kale gang of Pardhis from Osmanabad which had been involved in around 11 dacoities in the past 3-4 months in the Vasai-Virar and the Mira-Bhayandar area. This was the biggest success of our department as the Kale gang topped the hierarchy list of such gangs in the state. They operated not only in Maharashtra but also in Karnataka and Surat," Bajaj said.

Heading: Right to Education Bill of paramount importance to women: Saeeda Hameed - Indian Express
Content:
One of the major impediments to the construction of the city's first metro rail corridor—clearance from the railways for the design of the section over the railway tracks at Andheri — is expected to be resolved soon, the Metropolitan Commissioner has said.

According to Ratnakar Gaikwad, metropolitan commissioner, the issue of the general agreement drawings (GAD) for a viaduct section across Andheri railway tracks, pending approval from the Railways, was discussed at a high-level review meeting of the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar metro corridor.

"After discussions, the issue is by and large resolved and the height of the section would be brought down from its designed 14 metre," Gaikwad told Newsline. It is expected that the height would be brought down to nine metre.

The railway authority, after giving approval in principle, had not cleared the GAD for the section since October 2007 and asked the Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd (MMOPL) to modify the design, owing to the Union Railway Ministry's grand plan for an elevated railway corridor between Churchgate and Virar.

Gaikwad added that since the proposal of an elevated rail corridor came up the Railways had asked the MMRDA to elevate the metro viaduct to 23 metre so that the elevated corridor could go under the Metro corridor.

"It wasn't possible to take it that high as there was no scope for a ramp, therefore now the elevated corridor would go over the metro corridor," Gaikwad added.

Meanwhile, the MMOPL is hopeful that clearance would be given at the earliest without hurting the construction schedule. K P Maheshwari, Director, MMOPL, said, "A meeting was held to discuss the issue. It's in an advanced stage of discussions and would be resolved soon."

The section over the railway tracks is one of the most daunting challenges for the MMOPL. One challenge would be a cantilever bridge spanning 98 metre across busy railway tracks at Andheri — balanced on a pier on either side of the tracks. The two piers will themselves be tricky to build since the area outside the railway stations, especially on the western side, comprises narrow, crowded lanes with small, tightly-packed buildings. In fact, the pier on the western side of the tracks is located right outside a religious place.

Heading: New pumping stations to solve city’s woes during floods: BMC - Indian Express
Content:
When Dr Saeeda Hameed, the only female member of the Planning Commission, was born, her relatives sent their condolences to her father mourning the birth of a girl child. On Thursday, addressing school and college girls at the National Symposium on Girls and Girlhood organised by Vacha, a resource centre for Women at the SNDT University for Women, Dr Hameed could not help but reminisce the herculean efforts made by her parents to help her reach where she is today.

The first day of the three day event saw participation of eminent researchers and scholars from across India as well as girl students from schools and NGOs across eight states of the country.

Dr Hameed stressed on the significance of the Right to Education bill, recently cleared by the Cabinet, for the education of girl child in India. "We need support from all quarters to ensure that the Right to Education bill is passed so that the current 'apartheid' education system is done away with. We need to question the current system of schooling that is divisive in nature" said Dr Hameed. Dr Anita Rampal, member of the 11th plan Working Groups for Elementary Education and a professor at the Delhi University concurred, "There is an urgent need to restructure our education system which does not necessarily stand for social transformation but instead produces inequalities at various stages. School curriculum should empower students. That is why the need for Right to Education bill is of paramount importance especially to the girl child." Hameed also expressed her disillusionment at being the only female member of the Planning Commission. Hameed, who strived to introduce schemes for women, hoped that the next Planning Commission would have at least two more women members 'to strengthen the voices of women of this country.'

"The effort of the 11th plan is to ensure that women's issues are not neglected. Women make up almost half of the population of the country contributing in every sector. But what are the resources allotted to them? What are the efforts made to include them?"

Hameed asked the gathering school girls and professors. She stressed on the central government schemes like the Nutrition Programme for adolescent girls and the Kishori Shakti Yojana and the need for the government to allocate more funds for development of adolescent girls.

"During meetings of the Planning Commission, I have always tried to sensitize ministers of different states about various issues of women instead of the stereotypical ones," Dr Hameed concluded.

The three day symposium, being held at the SNDT Churchgate campus will also host lectures on issues ranging from violence against girls, 'Demography of Girls, 'Legal System' and 'Strategies for Change.'

Heading: New monorail between Mumbai, Navi Mumbai on anvil - Indian Express
Content:
Givan the much beleaguered storm water drainage system in the city and the consequent flooding that residents of Mumbai face each year, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) is hoping that the flood water pumping stations being constructed at Haji Ali and Versova are completed by May 2009.

Part of the Brihanmumbai Storm Water Drainage (BRIMSTOWAD) project, the two pumping stations are being built at key catchments areas at Haji Ali in Worli and Irla nullah in Andheri. The civic body has roped in a South Korean firm to provide them with necessary equipments.

Civic officials state that if these two projects are completed, the city will have some respite from the problems due to floods that it faces each year. For the Haji Ali project, the civic body is spending Rs 58 crore on the construction and maintenance up to seven years. SWD deputy chief engineer, V S Karombelkar said, "We are building this pumping station on an area of 4000 hectare. This pumping station is expected to relieve flooding from areas like Nanachowk, Slater Road, Tardeo Road, part of Pedder road."

Civic officials added that with this project, they are also undertaking the work of nullah widening and nullah tilting. "All this will help in easier transport of water system," said Karombelkar. However, he added that there may be a delay in the completion of the project. "We are facing problems due to a number of utilities like gas pipelines, electric lines etc lying underground. It is a huge task to remove them. We are yet to get all the permissions. Added to this, is the problem of traffic diversion. We have spoken to the police authorities and we hope to get permission to start the work on a larger scale soon. Owing to these problems, the work is running behind schedule," said Karombelkar. "The pumping station will also house six set of pumps with a total capacity of 36 cubic meters per second," he Karombelkar.

The people residing in Andheri and nearby areas under the JVPD scheme had to battle it out the hardest during the 2005 deluge. Civic officials said that if the work on the Irla nullah flood pumping station is completed, this will not happen again.

"Work on this area is going on in full swing. This is built on BMC owned land so we don't have any problems of land acquisition for traffic diversion, the problem of shifting underground utilities etc. Hence we are very sure that work on this stretch will be completed by next year," said SWD deputy chief engineer and project manager, SP Prasade. For this particular stretch the civic body is spending Rs 77 crore. Civic officials added that this project will bring respite to areas like Milan Subway, Andheri (East), Santacruz (West). Irla nullah is notorious for causing flooding problems in the nearby areas. "With every high tide during the monsoons, flood gates will open. Water from the Irla and Abhishek nullah will be thrown to the beach through inlet channels. This will prevent a deluge like situation in the area," said Prasade.   According to him, the Irla pumping station will have eight sets of pumps with a total capacity of 50 cubic meters per second.

BMC officials further said that work on the Cleaveland Bunder station at Senapati Bapat Marg in Dadar and Lovegrove pumping station at Worli has been completed. In Cleaveland, BMC has installed seven sets of pumps with a capacity of 42 cubic meters per second while in Lovegrove, they have installed 10 pumps to pump 60 cubic meters.

The pumping stations were proposed in 1993, after the appointment of Watson Hawksley International as consultants to study necessary improvements for the city's storm water drainage system. They had submitted the BRIMSTOWAD report.

Heading: Notary found guilty of forging documents - Indian Express
Content:
The Urban Development department is deliberating on the idea to link the Mumbai and Navi Mumbai airports via a monorail along the proposed Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL).

According to T C Benjamin, Principal Secretary, UD, discussions were held at a high level meeting over possibility of the 22.5 km sea link between Sewri and Nhava accommodating a monorail corridor. "We discussed whether the MTHL can accommodate a monorail corridor which can take people across the creek to Navi Mumbai airport," Benjamin told Newsline.  

According to him, the monorail would be structurally fit to go across the creek without a major change in the designs prepared by the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC).  "A monorail corridor along the MTHL is feasible according to MSRDC engineers without much change in design as it doesn't weigh more than a bus," Benjamin said. The inclusion of the monorail would raise the cost of the MTHL by 10 per cent. At present it is estimated to cost Rs 6000 crore.

The officials are also contemplating on linking the Mumbai airport with the proposed one in Navi Mumbai. The linking of the two airports would be possible with the extension of the Jacob Circle-Wadala-Chembur monorail which was recently awarded to a consortium of Larsen & Toubro and Malaysian firm Scomi. "Subsequently it can also link the two airports but that would involve proposed mono rail on one side and an extension from Nhave to the Navi Mumbai airport," Benjamin said.

"It is desirable if it connected by mass transit system which can increase the airport's utility manifold. It would help better coordination between the airports," Benjamin said.

Heading: Cong corporator in the dock over false caste certificate - Indian Express
Content:
The certificate of practice of a notary has been cancelled after the law and judiciary department found him guilty of forging documents.

The action was taken last month following an inquiry by Arvind Rohee, joint secretary to the department, in which advocate-notary Nandlal Dave was found guilty of gross misconduct.The inquiry found that Dave had certified more than 70 forge documents of various private family trusts without a proper identification. Dave's name has been removed from the register the notary register.

His misconduct came to light after one Direndra Sheth lodged a complaint alleging that Dave indulged in professional misconduct by certifying documents without identification and presence of the executants, which is in violation of the Notaries Act, 1952. Sheth, therefore, sought that these documents be treated as cancelled as they were not properly certified.

The subsequent report has observed that Sheth is one of the trustees with more than 22 trusts among the 42 mentioned in the document.

Dave had pleaded that he did not commit any breach. Rohee, however, expressed surprise when Dave stated that the document executed by one person and attested by him can subsequently be cancelled by some other person by executing 'Deed of Cancellation' that can be done after intimation to the person who has executed the original document.

"It is very strange and erroneous to say that a third person can cancel a document which is executed by some other person," the report observes.When contacted Dave said he did not commit any violations and he has written a letter to the Law Minister in this regard.

During the inquiry, Dave admitted that 96 signatories on the document were not present before him at the time of its execution and all the documents are signed by the constituted Power of Attorney in his presence.

None of the documents are signed by any advocate endorsing the identity of the executants, the report states."Thus there are serious lapses on Dave's part, which amount to professional or other misconduct," the report says.

"In fact when important documents are executed and notarised affecting rights and liabilities of other trustees, the notary should be very careful and cautious and such document should be executed in presence of the executants after verifying his identity and other documents concerning the trusts," it observes.

Heading: Engineer, wife die in accident - Indian Express
Content:
The RCF police have registered a case of cheating against a Congress corporator for allegedly furnishing fake documents to attain a caste certificate.

The accused Kisan Raju Mistry who is a corporator of Ward no 144 in Chembur has been booked for cheating and forgery.

The complainant in the case, Sainath Mangaonkar, is a tehsildar from the District Collector's office. According to Mangaonkar, Mistry had applied for a caste certificate claiming to be a Yadav on October 18, 2006. He had procured the certificate but on realising that the Yadav caste does not merit any reservation or special privileges he applied for another caste certificate, this time claiming that he belongs to the 'sutar' caste and was successful in procuring an OBC certificate.

Mistry had used the certificate to contest from ward 144. According to inspector Shailesh Pasalwar, RCF police, in February 2007, Rajesh Patange filed a complaint with the caste verification committee, Belapur alleging that Mistry had procured bogus caste certificates and was using them to contest the election as a reserved category candidate.

The committee then launched an inquiry into the matter and found that while Mistry's caste certificate as an OBC was valid, his earlier certificate acknowledging him as a 'Yadav' was false.

The Collector's office was notified about the aberration and Mangaonkar was instructed to initiate criminal proceedings against Mistry.The RCF police registered a case under sections 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 but Mistry who has already procured anticipatory bail claimed that he was innocent and attributed the case to an act of his political rivals.

"Three generations of my family have lived here and the election rolls of 1965 show that my father was from the 'sutar' caste. I have always fought my elections on the basis of my OBC caste certificate and all these allegations of me having applied for a 'Yadav' caste certificate are utterly baseless," said Mistry.

He added that Patange, a BJP candidate had contested the election against him and had lost.

"He began harassing me after his defeat due to which I was forced to approach the RCF police, which registered a non-cognisable offence against him a year back," alleged Mistry.

Heading: Businessman attacked by armed assailants - Indian Express
Content:
An executive engineer with the Punjab state electricity board and his wife died and another man was injured in a road accident as two cars collided head on at Heddon village near Samrala on Ludhiana-Chandigarh highway on Thursday.

The deceased were identified as Jaswinder Singh (40) and his wife Harpreet Kaur. The injured, Rajinder Singh, is a resident of Ludhiana. He was rushed to civil hospital Samrala and was later referred to Ludhiana.

Jaswinder was posted at civil lines Ludhiana and the couple were on their way to Chandigarh from Ludhiana.

Harpreet Kaur died on the spot while Jaswinder succumbed to injuries at civil hospital Samrala. The postmortem was conducted at civil hospital Samrala.

A police team led by Samrala DSP Ravinder Loomba reached the spot.

According to sources, Rajinder Singh was on his way from Ludhiana to Chandigarh and met with the accident as he tried to overtake another car.

Jaswinder who was injured seriously was taken out of his car by breaking the window of the car half-an-hour after the accident.

Heading: Two Sutlej Club members engage in brawl - Indian Express
Content:
The 12 assailants did not allow the three victims to move out of their car

Three youths were injured, one of them critically, as nearly one dozen assailants carrying sharp-edged weapons attacked them on the Pakhowal road late last night.

The injured youths have been admitted to the DMC hospital and the police have registered an attempt to murder case against unidentified assailants.

The injured persons have been identified as Vishal Joshi, Vaibhav Sharma and Rajinder Singh. The condition of Vaibhav is stated to be serious.

According to sources, the youths were attacked by about 12 assailants when they were travelling in a car near the Green Field area on the Pakhowal road at night. Sources said the assailants, who came in a car and on two motorcycles, did not let the victims move out of their car. After injuring them, the assailants fled from the spot as people started assembling there.

A police team reached the spot on receiving the information about the incident. The injured were initially rushed to a nearby private hospital from where they were referred to the DMC hospital. Sources said that Joshi, a resident of Sukh Ram Nagar who owns a finance business, was the main target of the assailants.

The Division number 5 police have registered an attempt to murder case against unidentified assailants and have started search for them.

Heading: Students of three commerce colleges go on strike - Indian Express
Content:
Once again, the prestigious Sutlej Club is in news for bad reasons as some high profile members of the club got engaged in a brawl on Wednesday night.

After the incident, people from both sides have registered their complaints with the club authorities and the police.

According to some club members, requesting anonymity, around 11 pm last night former general secretary of the club G S Laddi and another reputed member Mahesh Goyal entered into heated arguments at the club bar. Both were accompanied by some of their supporters.

Goyal, a colony developer, said, "I had given a contract for the development of a colony to Krishan Kharbanda and had paid a big amount to him for the work. Kharbanda did not do much work on the project and rather asked me to pay Rs 3 lakh more. Yesterday, Laddi called me up and in a threatening tone asked me to pay this money to Kharbanda. He also dared me to come to the club to face them."

He said, "I reached the club around 11 pm along with some of my friends and met Laddi at the bar. Laddi was accompanied by Krishan and his brother Pawan."

I was threatened at the spot by Laddi and his companions, Goyal told Newsline.

Goyal further said that he had given written complaints to Senior Superintendent of Police R K Jaiswal and Deputy Commissioner Sumer Singh Gurjar, who is also an ex-officio president of the club.

"I have demanded action against these persons," said Goyal. On the other hand, Laddi said, "It was not me but Goyal who had called me up and threatened me and Kharbanda."

Krishan Kharbanda also denied the allegations levelled by Goyal. Kharbanda claimed he had to take some money from Goyal.

He said, "When I told Goyal that we were in the club, he rushed to the place with his supporters and started abusing us in the bar."

Laddi said that he had also given a written complaint to the club authorities.

"We are also going to lodge a complaint with the police about the threats given to us by Goyal."

Meanwhile, general secretary of the club, Yogesh Bansal, said, "We came to know about the incident from some of the members who were present there at the time."

Bansal said they have received complaints from both the sides and that they will take appropriate action.

Heading: GLADA may reduce prices of plots - Indian Express
Content:
Blame authorities for keeping them in dark about fee-hike

The ongoing student agitation over hike in fees in commerce stream has spread to three more colleges of the city as students of these colleges went on strike calling the hike "unacceptable".

The commerce students of first, second and final year in Gujranwala Guru Nanak Khalsa College, Civil Lines, Guru Nanak Khalsa College for Women, Gujarkhan Campus, Model Town, and DD Jain Memorial College for Women, Kidwai Nagar, went on strike.

The agitating students alleged the fees have been doubled. Moreover, they were not informed about the hike at the time of admission or even later, claimed the students .

The college managements on the other hand said the fees were being demanded as per Punjab University guidelines. They said the students had been apprised about the fee structure well in advance.

The protest held by the students of DD Jain Memorial College for Women continued on the second day today. The situation at the college turned unpleasant as parents of three students representing the protesting students were called for by the college authorities.

Today's protests came two days after the students of Guru Nanak Girls College (GNGC) took on the college authorities for allegedly overcharging them.

"The fee has been charged as per the structure devised by the university. We held two meetings with class representatives of the commerce department. Three of them said they would not accept any university circular and hence we had to call their parents to sort out the matter," said Dr Surinder Dua, principal of DD Jain Memorial College.

"These protests are sparked by GNGC," said a college professor. "But students should know that the fee has been charged as per the Punjab University guidelines."

"Since we are raising our voice against the rise in fees, the teachers have started threatening us saying they would deduct marks in the assessment or practicals," said some students at GNKCW.

However, Gurbir Singh Sarna, general secretary of the management team at GNKCW, said, "The fee is charged according to PU guidelines. But no student will be victimised for taking part in the protest." He said they will communicate with the protestors to end their resentment.

The students boycotted classes throughout the day. Some students threatened to continue protests until the college managements came clear on the issue. "We want a dialogue with the management or we will continue with the protests," said a student of GGN Khalsa College. "Last year we paid an annual fee of nearly Rs 10,000, but this year the total fee is about Rs 20,000," said a final year commerce student of GNKCW.

Jagpal Singh, a professor at SCD Government College, who is a senator in graduates' constituency from the city, said he will raise the issue in the senate meeting to be held in December.

"The fee structures for regular and self-financed courses are different. The fee for self-financed course is bound to be higher. But colleges can be blamed only if they charge more than the prescribed fee structure," he said.

Heading: Ayodhya temple construction in 2006: VHP - Indian Express
Content:
Following two flop shows at Jail Road and Samrala within a month, Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA) is considering to re-determine the reserve prices of the plots.

Earlier, no bidder turned up at the auction for 20 booths organised at Samrala and for 16 booths held at Jail Road in Ludhiana a month ago.

GLADA had organised the auction twice at both the places but had failed to get even a single bidder. The authorities now believe that perhaps they need to consider reduction in the reserved prices of these booths.

The reserved price at Jail Road was Rs 54,000 per square yard of the booth at Samrala, it was Rs 40,000.

The local office will not be writing to higher authorities about the poor response so that the booths can be sold after reducing the reserve price per square yard, said sources.

Sources revealed that recession in the market has forced the GLADA to consider revision in the prices. Slowdown has affected even the real estate also and rates in posh localities like Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, Sarabha Nagar, and BRS Nagar have also remained stagnant.

Heading: V-Day: Proposal passport or mkt byproduct? - Indian Express
Content:
Champat Rai, Joint General Secretary of Vishwa Hindu Parishad, talked at length with Ashok Kumar of Express Online disclosing the plans of the rightist organisation in relation to the construction of Ram temple in Ayodhya to their relationship with BJP, Congress, Commies and its outlook towards the Muslims.

I never said that we are going to start the construction of temple in 2002 but yes the construction of the Ram Temple at Ayodhya may very well start before the end of the year 2006.

The Canadian expert, who worked on behalf of the Tojo Vikas International solicited by the Govt on the direction of the court in his GPRS survey report hinted out at the remains of the huge building. It was later confirmed by the ASI committee constituted under the directions by the court, which verified the experts theory on the maximum number of points.

The report has been submitted to the court, which accepted as it said the same would be taken on record subject to objections by oral evidences. Once that process is over the judgment will be delivered.

Currently the case is with the courts and hopefully soon they will come out with the judgment. But we are not a party to the case in the courts. According to my knowledge there are 25 parties involved with the suit but VHP is not one amongst them.
