Those making profits include, B&R, Hindustan Salts Ltd, BBJ Construction Co, Braithwaite and Co and Andrew Yule and Co Ltd. Those which have met their respective targets are Cement Corporation of India, Heavy Engineering Corporation and Bharat Pumps and Compressors Ltd.

In the case of Bharat Heavy Plates and Vessels, the revival process began only this fiscal, while Bharat Wagon and Engineering Co Ltd has now been handed over to the Railways.

PSUs like HMT (Machine Tools), Praga Tools Ltd and HMT (Bearings) remain loss-making units. In fact, the Commission's caution is believed to have stemmed from the fact that despite the cash infusion these PSUs were not able to sustain themselves.

What is more, banks are understood to have expressed their reluctance to fund bailouts of more PSUs in the queue for revival through interest waiver and infusion of fresh capital. The UPA dispensation has recommended 26 PSUs to the Board for Reconstruction of PSUs, which subsequently examines them and gives its recommendations.

However, the government decided to revive 13 PSUs while remaining indecisive on four of them. The revival has, of course, led to the number of PSUs defaulting on payment of salaries coming down to 10 from 24 in 2003-04.

Heading: IMF cuts India’s growth forecast - Indian Express
Content:
The European Central Bank (ECB) cut its key interest rate by half a percentage point to 3.25 per cent on Thursday and the Bank of England made an even more aggressive reduction of 1.5 percentage point in an effort to ease the financial crisis and boost their flagging economies.

The Bank of England's cut to a 3 per cent base rate — the biggest trim in 27 years — took markets by surprise, reflecting fears that Britain is headed for a deep recession.

ECB president Jean-Claude Trichet said the central bank to the 15-country euro zone had discussed a bigger, three-quarter point rate cut, but "after having checked and discussed the pros and cons of those different options, we decided unanimously that it was appropriate to decrease by 50 basis points", or a half percentage point.

Trichet said the decision to lower its rate was made in light of inflation that, while still above its preferred level of at or about 2 per cent, had shown signs of slackening.

Others banks followed suit. The Swiss National Bank cut its key interest rate by half a percentage point to 2 per cent, only its second reduction since March 2003. In Prague, the Czech Republic's central bank cut its interest rate by three-quarter percentage point to 2.75 per cent.

The BoE and ECB, which followed the Fed and other banks in a coordinated cut on October 8, have been criticised in some quarters for being slow to respond to the sharp economic slowdown this year amid fears about inflation. The ECB actually raised rates a quarter-point in July as inflation spiked sharply higher.

Heading: Yahoo shouts out to MS: Buy me! - Indian Express
Content:
The International Monetary Fund has revised its global economic outlook. In its World Outlook Report, the IMF has predicted that global growth would slow down by 0.2 per cent in 2008 and 0.9 per cent in 2009, thus leaving the revised growth figures at 3.7 per cent for this year and 2.2 per cent for 2009.

The outlook is not too different for India as well. The IMF sees the country's economic growth going down to 6.3 per cent — 0.6 per cent less than what it had projected last month.

The US would contract by as much as 0.7 per cent in 2009, while the Eurozone has been forecast to shrink by half-a-point next year. For advanced economies, IMF sees a negative growth of 0.3 per cent and 5.1 per cent for emerging/ low-income countries.

Heading: US jobless claims show slight dip - Indian Express
Content:
Yahoo chief executive Jerry Yang said on Wednesday that Microsoft should buy his pioneering Internet firm despite failed takeover talks between the companies earlier this year. "To this day, I would say the best thing for Microsoft is to buy Yahoo," Yang said. "Did we want to do the deal? Yes."

Microsoft has said repeatedly that it is no longer interested in buying the floundering firm.

"Our position hasn't changed," Microsoft said in a statement released in October. "Microsoft has no interest in acquiring Yahoo. There are no discussions between the companies."

The company issued the statement after Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer commented that the business reasons for a Yahoo acquisition still make sense.

Microsoft on January 31 offered to buy Yahoo for $44.6 billion in a half-cash, half-stock deal. Microsoft walked away from negotiations on May 3 after Yahoo rejected an offer it raised from $31 to $33 per share, which amounted to $47.5 billion.

Heading: SBI chief warns of a bad loan pile-up this year - Indian Express
Content:
New claims for unemployment benefits in the US dropped slightly last week, while the number of people continuing to receive benefits reached its highest level in more than 25 years, the government said on Thursday.

The US Labor Department reported that initial claims for jobless benefits dropped 4,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4,81,000 for the week ending November 1.

But the number of people continuing to receive unemployment insurance jumped by 1,22,000 to 3.84 million, the highest since 1983, when the nation was coming out of a deep recession. The figure for continuing claims lags the initial claims report and is for the week ending October 25.

The increase indicates that unemployed workers are taking longer to find new jobs and is more evidence of recessionary conditions in the job market.

The number also may affect the political debate, as Democrats in Congress are pushing to include an extension of unemployment benefits in a new stimulus package, which could be taken up this month.

Heading: More banks cut lending rates - Indian Express
Content:
The banking system which had been flush with cash in the last few years, and extended credit to whosoever wanted a loan, will see a growth in non-performing assets (NPAs) this year. "Stressed assets in the banking system could push up the NPA levels of banks," said State Bank of India chairman O P Bhatt.

India's largest bank also cut its prime lending rate (PLR) by 75 basis points with effect from November 10, home loan rates are also expected to come down soon. The PLR will now be 13 per cent from the present 13.75 per cent. The bank also reduced interest rates on deposits by 50 basis points across maturities from 91 days up to five years. For maturities of five years and above, SBI has cut its interest rates by 25 bps. The deposit rate reductions come into effect from December 1.

Bhatt said that increase in NPAs would be caused majorly by debtors in the textile, gems and jewellery, pockets of the real estate sector and auto component industry. However, he also said that banks would continue to see robust credit growth even this year at around 29 per cent. He was speaking on the sidelines of a Ficci-IBA organised banking seminar on Thursday.

Bhatt said there was a huge demand for credit by corporates as in the last three months global sources of funds for business houses have dried up. "We are feeling pressure as there is suddenly a great demand for credit from corporates, infrastructure and agri-sectors too need loans and liquidity continues to be a big issue," Bhatt said.

"We need liquidity not only in the short term but in the long term as well," Bhatt said. "There is a need for structural liquidity in the system which is sustainable in the long-term," he said, adding that the regulator was aware of the prevailing liquidity situation in the system and was ready to act according to the requirements of the situation.

On economic growth, the SBI Chairman said that it continued to be in the range of 7.5-7.9 per cent.

Heading: Output cut, 3-day week at  Ashok Leyland - Indian Express
Content: Taking cue from RBI's signals, which had cut the cash reserve ratio by 3.5 per cent and the repo rate by 1.5 per cent points in recent weeks, many banks cut their prime-lending rates (PLR) today.  Oriental Bank of Commerce, Central Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank reduced their PLRs by 75 basis points to 13.25 per cent each. OBC also reduced interest rates on housing loans up to Rs 30 lakh, and education loans. The interest rate on retail loans linked to BPLR stands reduced to the same extent, Central Bank said. Other banks that cut their PLR on Thursday were: Allahabad Bank (by 75 bps effective November 10), Dena Bank (by 75 bps effective November 10), Citibank (by 50 bps) and Corporation Bank (by 75 bps).

Heading: Sensex falls below 10,000-mark as it goes the way of the world - Indian Express
Content:
Demand slowdown has started taking a toll on India Inc. Close on the heels of Tata Motors' decision to close the Jamshedpur plant for three days, Hinduja-owned Ashok Leyland today said it would cut the production of its commercial vehicles in the next two months and its manufacturing plants will work only three days a week till December on account of decrease in demand.

"Taking into account the inventory in pipeline and the suppressed market demand, Ashok Leyland has decided to moderate the production plan for the next two months," the company said. Its manufacturing facilities would also reduce the number of working days to three a week till December this year, it added. "This decision has also been partially influenced by the problems encountered by the suppliers as a result of power shortage in some parts of the country," the company said.

Lately, medium and heavy commercial vehicles market had been facing problems of inadequate funding and high interest costs resulting in reduction of market demand, it added. Meanwhile, the company today reported a 50.23 per cent decline in vehicles sales in October.

Heading: BJP’s Raje formula a mix of development, regional pride - Indian Express
Content:
Plunging global markets and high inflation number sent bulls packing from Dalal Street once again. The Sensex tumbled below the 10,000 level in a highly volatile trading session as an unexpected increase in inflation shattered hopes of further interest rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of India.

The benchmark index, which fell 511 points on Wednesday, plunged another 386 points or 3.81 per cent to 9,734.22 even as a sell-off in global markets over deepening US recession also weighed on the domestic bourses on Thursday. "The markets had opened in red following the global peers which had slid on the back of US economic data showing higher job cuts in the month of October and also due to the comment by the Institute of Supply Management that the US services sector contracted sharply in October. Further the Indian inflation number for the week ended October 25 was at 10.72 per cent which was higher than the previous figure of 10.68 per cent added to the slide in the afternoon," said an analyst with Geojit Securities.

Index heavyweight Reliance Industries (RIL) made a roller-coaster ride and closed with a loss of Rs 7.7 per cent, causing volatility in key benchmark indices. The fall in European as well as the US index futures also supported the bears. On the sectorial front, the losers were metal (down by 8.41 per cent), oil & gas (down by 4.83 per cent) and technology (down by 4.71 per cent). Tata Motors fell 12.2 per cent after it said it was shutting down its commercial vehicle plant in Jamshedpur for three days to avoid a build-up of inventory. Tata Steel, the world's sixth-largest steel maker, fell the most among frontliners with the stock closing 13.7 per cent lower.

"When you are in the grip of full-fledged bear market, you see sharp rallies. But that does not mean that things have turned around," said Daljeet Kohli, head of research at Emkay Global Financial.

"Markets work on both fundamentals and sentiments. Sentiments have improved after all the measures taken, but fundamentals have not changed," he said referring to liquidity-boosting measures taken by central banks in many countries.

Citigroup said corporate India had posted its lowest earnings growth in four years in the September quarter, as high interest rates and input costs hit demand, and Kohli said the current quarter could be even worse as firms could not raise prices.

Data showed foreign funds were net sellers of $23 million of stocks on Tuesday, in a market that had risen 2.8 per cent, after buying nearly $500 million worth shares in the previous two sessions. (With agencies)

Heading: Vasundhara pits her state against Centre - Indian Express
Content:
AICC general secretary Margaret Alva, who created a flutter by alleging sale of party nominations in recent assembly polls in Karnataka, could be in for trouble.

Party sources on Friday said that Alva's case could be referred to the Central Disciplinary Action Committee of the party headed by Defence Minister A K Antony.

Alva, who has been sulking since her son Nivedith was not given nomination in Karnataka elections, had created an embarrassment for the party on Thursday as she alleged adoption of "different yardsticks" in deciding party nominations for upcoming elections in six states.

She had wondered why her son and grandson of former Union Minister C K Jaffer Sharief were not given nominations while relatives of two dozen leaders were given tickets in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan and Jammu and Kashmir.

"Were my son and Jaffer Sharief's grandson anti-national, terrorists or smugglers?" Alva had asked. She is also apparently upset over the appointment of her bete noire R V Deshpande as state party chief.

AICC general secretary Prithviraj Chavan, who is in-charge of party affairs in Karnataka and who appeared to be in Alva's firing line, has already dismissed her charges as 'unsubstantiated and born out of frustration'.

Chavan had said "as long as Alva is general secretary, I will not comment on her unfortunate statement. Since she is general secretary of the party, any decision on it will be taken by the Congress high command and Central Disciplinary Action Committee".

Congress disapproved of party general secretary Margaret Alva's charges that election tickets were sold in Karnataka but remained silent on whether it was a fit case for disciplinary action.

"We do not agree for sweeping statements and grievances ought not be aired in public," AICC spokesman Abhishek Manu Singhvi said.

Singhvi described Alva as a seasoned and senior leader of the party but said for all her grievances, there are established and ample fora within the party.

"We have no doubt that such outburst would recur again," he said.

Heading: MNS attacks: we are all Indians, says apex court - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP on Thursday organised a mammoth booth-level workers' rally in Jaipur to kickstart the party's campaign for the Assembly election.

Organised under the ongoing "Vijay Sankalp" series, the meeting underlined the significance of the "Gujarat model" in the party's scheme of things, as it fights to retain the three BJP-ruled states of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. "I have been touring the country for various Vijay Sankalp rallies, but they were meant for the masses. Never ever did I come across such a huge turnout of party workers," said the party's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani.

Taking a leaf out of her Gujarat counterpart's book, Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje said "Rajasthan had been repeatedly let down by the Centre in the last five years". "The coming elections would be a fight between Rajasthan and the Congress," she added.

The "Jai Jai Rajasthan" slogan released on the occasion, similarly, retained the flavour of the "Jeetega Gujarat" slogan, so cleverly used by Narendra Modi in his re-election campaign.

While Vasundhra stressed "development" as her main election plank, Advani repeated another lesson drawn from Gujarat that "anti-incumbency was a phenomenon directed essentially against the incumbent MLA/MP, making it imperative that candidates for elections be elected judiciously".

"The biggest lesson from the US election is that the people yearn for a change when their expectations are not fulfilled by the Government of the day. The aam aadmi who was the Congress's main election plank, feels most betrayed today. So it's time for a change at the Centre as also in a host of states. But in states where the Government has performed, like in Rajasthan, we will buck the trend to come back to power," added Advani.

Vasundhara cocked a snook at the Centre's developmental claims, including the Congress's flagship programme NREGA.

"The Congress says it's sending money for the NREGA programme. But whose money is that? Isn't it our, and your money? And how come a BJP-ruled state like Rajasthan beats other Congress-ruled states like Maharashtra hands down in its implementation? It only shows that our state's delivery mechanism is far more superior to others," she said.

Party president Rajnath Singh added the twin phenomena of the constitution of "booth-level committees" and the "BJP emerging as the biggest party in the country" were "milestones in the party's trajectory". The workers, numbering around three lakh according to Advani, were drawn from over 40,000 booths all across the state.

While Modi had prepared a huge database of booth-level members in the run-up to the Assembly election, the Rajasthan BJP, too, released a database of the state's booth-level committee members. Each 15-member booth- level committee has two women and two youth representatives each. In the ongoing exercise to declare party candidates for various states, the BJP has been dropping as many as one-third of the sitting MLAs, something that is likely to be repeated in Rajasthan.

Senior party leaders like M Venkaiah Naidu, Jaswant Singh, Gopinath Munde and Om Mathur also spoke on the occasion.

Heading: Sedition case: Vaiko out of jail - Indian Express
Content:
SP general secretary Amar Singh has revealed that he and his family members have movable and immovable properties and valuables worth around Rs 37 crore.

Singh, who has filed an affidavit on his properties and other assets along with his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha elections, said he had already paid income tax of Rs 1.99 crore during the current fiscal year along with Rs 60,735 as wealth tax.

However, income tax of Rs 11.93 lakh was yet to be paid by Singh, the affidavit said. Singh does not have any valuables or funds in the name of either of his twin daughters, Disha and Drishti, except for a LIC policy of Rs 2.5 lakh each in their name.

According to the affidavit, Amar and his wife, Pankaja, have Rs 10 lakh in hand. While Amar has bank deposits worth Rs 3.47 crore, his wife has Rs 2.25 crore. The family has bonds, debentures and shares worth Rs 16.60 crore while they have PPF, NSS and LIC policies of Rs 7.06 lakh.

The SP general secretary owns two vehicles and jewellery, including diamonds, worth over Rs 3.32 crore. The family has got watches, furniture, mutual funds and other items amounting to Rs 8.23 crore. According to the details about the immovable assets given in the affidavit, they have agricultural land worth Rs 50 lakh, a plot worth Rs 1.75 crore in Noida's Sector 44, two flats worth Rs 1 crore each in Greater Kailash, one flat each in Bangalore and Kolkata valued at Rs 7 crore, a commercial building in Delhi's Kasturba Gandhi Marg valued at Rs 1 crore, a bungalow in Lucknow valued at Rs 2.8 crore and a house in Azamgarh worth Rs 9 lakh.

Ram Gopal Yadav, another SP general secretary who is the first cousin of party president Mulayam Singh Yadav, has properties and valuables worth over Rs 71 lakh only. Ram Gopal possesses land worth Rs 32.43 lakh, a plot in Lucknow's Vrindavan housing scheme and a house each in Sefai in Etawah and Agra, having a total worth of Rs 23.69 lakh. He also has three firearms worth Rs 1.20 lakh and air conditioners valued at Rs 2.83 lakh.

Heading: Cabinet nod for integrated checkposts - Indian Express
Content:
Two weeks after being arrested on sedition charges, MDMK leaders Vaiko and M Kannappan were released from judicial custody by a magistrate court here on Thursday. When the case came up for hearing on Thursday, the state did not seek an extension of custody, submitting in the court that investigations into the complaint were over.

Vaiko was arrested from his residence by the Q branch of the state police on October 23, two days after making an allegedly seditious speech at the height of a pro-Lankan Tamil wave in the state in which he supported the proscribed LTTE in their war with the Sri Lankan forces and threatened to carry arms to fight the war.

Continuing his tirade against the Centre and state, Vaiko told the media after being released that Tamils in Lanka were losing lives to the arms and ammunition and other strategic support provided by the Indian Government and was being betrayed by the UPA Government of which Chief Minister M Karunanidhi was a partner.

"Collecting money and materials in the name of the poor Tamil families in Lanka is merely an eyewash. The Indian Government has already given Rs 2,000 crore to Sri Lanka to equip itself with weapons in their war to eliminate the Tamils," charged Vaiko.

Clarifying his stand on the sedition charges against him, Vaiko said while he was firmly committed to the unity and integrity of the country, he was equally concerned that the Government helping the genocide against Tamils in Sri Lanka could affect the fabric of unity.

Heading: Gates in Pune on ‘learning visit’ - Indian Express
Content:
In order to step up its vigil along the international border, the Government has decided to set up Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) at 13 identified entry points along the land border. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh here on Thursday, also decided to introduce a Bill to establish a Land Port Authority of India for the management of these ICPs.

"The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved setting up of the ICPs on the land borders of the country at a total cost of Rs 635 crore," Minister of State in PMO Prithviraj Chavan told reporters after the meeting. In the first phase, the ICPs would come up at entry points at Attari-Wagah on the Pakistan border, Raxaul on the Nepal border, Moreh on the Myanmar border, and Petrapole on the Bangladesh border, he added.

Like airports, the ICPs would house all regulatory agencies such as immigration, Customs and border security, apart from having support facilities such as parking, warehousing, banking and hotels in a single complex. The Land Port Authority of India would be responsible for overseeing the construction, management and maintenance of the ICPs.

In another decision, the CCEA also approved a Centrally-Sponsored Scheme to set up 6,000 model schools at block-level across the country. Announcing the decision, Chavan said in the first phase, 2,500 such schools would be set up in educationally backward districts with a total cost of over Rs 9,000 crore of which over Rs 7,000 crore will be provided by the Central Government during the current plan period. However, Chavan said the scheme would not be rolled out in the six poll -bound states till the election process got over.

The Union Cabinet also approved the National Biodiversity Action Plan (NBAP). Chavan said the NBAP would aim for development and integration of biodiversity databases; building national capacity for biodiversity conservation; assessment of vulnerability and adaption to climate change and regulation of introduction of alien species in indian system among other things. The Cabinet also approved a new scheme on Bio-Technology Industry Partnership Programme, which will seek to forge new partnership between the Government and industries for high risk discoveries and futuristic technology development in this sector on cost sharing basis. The CCEA earmarked Rs 350 crore for this scheme during the Eleventh Plan period.

Other decisions

• The Cabinet approved a combined project to build Afghanistan's Parliament building and Indian Chancery complex in Kabul at a revised estimate of Rs 950 crore. The Chancery complex was expected to be completed within 16 months and the Parliament building within 36 months.

• The CCEA also approved construction of a new broadgauge line from Sivok to Rangpo at a cost of over Rs 1,300 crore to provide rail connectivity to Sikkim.

• The CCEA also approved implementation of the 110-MW Pare Hydroelectric Project in Arunachal Pradesh by North Eastern Electric Power Corporation Ltd (NEEPCO) with an estimated cost of about Rs 600 crore. The power generated from the project, which is scheduled to be commissioned within 44 months, will be utilised within the northeastern region itself.

• The Cabinet also approved payment of a productivity linked bonus reward to over 66,000 port and dock workers as per the increased ceiling limit of wage at Rs 3,500 per month from 2006-07 till 2009-10.

• It also approved signing of the agreement on transfer of sentenced persons between India and Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), which would enable the sentenced persons to be near their families and help in the process of their social rehabilitation. The HKSAR's convicted prisoners can now be transferred to their home country and prisoners of Indian origin can be brought to India to serve the remaining part of their sentence.

Heading: Centre to raise border fencing with Dhaka - Indian Express
Content:
Manju Kamble possibly did not realise the significance of the visit she was being paid on Thursday afternoon. She shyly offered tea and water to the third richest man in the world and then settled herself at the window of her kitchen. When her visitor left after spending ten minutes at her one-room home, she waved goodbye.

Manju Kamble (40) has been a sex worker for years. Her visitor was Bill Gates, Microsoft founder, who was in Pune on Thursday. Among the questions Gates asked her was, "How many clients do you get everyday? Do you use condoms?"

Manju and her housemates had a few clients a day, a translator informed Gates, assuring him about the use of condoms. Each client pays us Rs 60 or Rs 70, said Gauri (name changed), who like Manju has sent her two children to a village in Karnataka. Business is not always good, the women grumbled, sometimes as low as one or two clients a day.

Gates is carrying out a crusade against HIV. He was on a "personal learning visit" planned by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

It was a tightly packed schedule, with television and newspaper journalists turning up in huge numbers and occupying vantage positions at different locations for a photo-op and some sound byte.

For Gates, however, it was a purely personal visit that was not to be affected by the huge media presence. His guards ensured that Gates, his father and two sisters were not shoved and pushed by the huge crowd that surrounded the two Mercedez Benz cars that pulled into the narrow lanes of Budhwar Peth, where Gates interacted with the commercial sex workers at Manju Kamble's house.

Gates and his family also visited the Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) project of Vanchit Vikas, a clinic funded by the foundation, on his hour-long visit to Budhwar Peth. According to Darshana Vyas, project director of Pathfinder International, an NGO whose 'Mukta' project works in ten districts in the state to reduce the prevalence of STIs, Gates seemed to be happy with the work at the clinic.

Meena Kurlekar, director of the Vanchit Vikas project, said that the foundation has provided funds for the last three years and helped them reach out to over 4,000 commercial sex workers. "We have 35 to 40 women visiting our clinic daily and the level of STI infection has considerably reduced among them," Kurlekar said.

Heading: Mirage upgrade shouldn’t wait till LS polls: France - Indian Express
Content:
With fencing along the Indo-Bangladesh border once again coming under focus following the recent serial blasts in Assam, the Centre is now planning to take up with the Bangladesh Government the matter relating to doing away with a 33-year-old understanding between the two countries which prohibits raising of structures of permanent nature within 150 yards of the Zero Line.

The Joint Indo-Bangladesh Guidelines for Border Authorities, 1975, stipulate that both sides will not allow any construction of permanent nature within 150 yards of the Zero Line on both sides. According to senior Home Ministry officials, India has not been able to erect fences at around 265 points along the Bangladesh border because of this rule.

"The topography of these border areas often throws up scenarios where fencing within these 150 yards is considered imperative to stop infiltration," said a Home Ministry official. "However, the Bangladesh authorities have often opposed any moves to erect fences within 150 yards in some places saying fence is a defensive structure and violates provisions of the Joint Indo-Bangladesh Guidelines for Border Authorities, 1975," the official added. In fact, there have been instances where Bangladesh Rifles (BDR) troops have fired at Indian personnel involved in fencing on the border. Officials said the Indian Government, for long, had argued with the Bangladesh authorities that erecting a border fence did not violate the 1975 guidelines since fencing was not a structure of permanent nature and hence should be allowed within 150 yards of the Zero Line, wherever required.

However, with the Bangladesh Government not appreciating this reasoning, the Home Ministry is now considering getting a Cabinet nod for amending the 1975 guidelines so that the matter to remove the 150-yard rule can be taken up with the Bangladesh Government.

Out of the 4,096-km-long border India shares with Bangladesh, around 2,626 kms have been fenced since 1986. Also, around 3,300 kms of border roads have been constructed to enable the maintenance of border fencing.

Heading: CBI: declare Todis proclaimed offenders - Indian Express
Content:
With the Indian Air Force combat operational strength dipping to dangerously low levels — the fleet strength is down to 32 squadrons from 39 — and the induction of 126 new aircraft to replace its ageing fleet unlikely to happen in the near future, French avionics major Thales said on Thursday it was waiting for an early nod from New Delhi to go ahead with upgradation of the IAF's existing Mirage 2000 fleet "to bridge the gap between current and future generations" of combat aircraft.

Thales Airborne Systems CEO Pierre-Yves Chaltiel told a group of visiting Indian journalists that France was ready to upgrade the IAF fleet of 51 Mirage 2000 to the Mirage 2000-5 level. "This will significantly enhance the IAF airpower potential and give it a coherent platform-system combination for the next 20 years at a far lower cost than acquisition of new aircraft capable of equivalent performance," he said.

Gerard Christmann, General Manager, Business Line, Electronic Combat Solutions in the Thales Aerospace Division, said they were counting on an early Indian go-ahead for the upgrade programme. "We hope a decision comes through this year and the programme becomes effective before general elections in India. Otherwise, there is a big risk of at least a two-year delay because a new government in place could well mean that the whole process starts all over again. But from the talks that we have had, we get the impression that the IAF wants to move on this quickly," Christmann said.

According to Chaltiel, the upgrade programme is led by the French Government in association with the three original equipment manufacturers — Dassault Aviation (system integration and aircraft modification), Thales (equipment, subsystems) and MBDA (Mica missile). This partnership is able to guarantee state-of-the-art equipment including the RDY3 radar, ICMS Mk 4 integrated countermeasures suite and the modular data processing unit.

The programme is intended to be conducted in two phases — Phase 1 under French responsibility and Phase 2 under Indian charge to complete physical modification of the aircraft and develop locally a national standard with technical assistance from French industrial partners.

Francois Quentin, Senior Vice President of Thales Aerospace Division, said "an upgraded Mirage 2000 is the ideal candidate to bridge the gap between current and future generations".

Indian plans to induct 126 new aircraft could take a while and the dwindling fleet strength has been causing concern in the IAF. Thales has recently upgraded 30 Mirage 2000 of the United Arab Emirates to the Mirage 2000-9 standard. A contract with Greece saw Thales involved in the supply of 15 new Mirage 2000-5 aircraft and 10 Mirage 2000 retrofitted to Mirage 2000-5 standard.

(The writer is in France as part of a media group invited by Thales)

Heading: Panchayat polls: SC questions OBC quota - Indian Express
Content:
After getting their passports cancelled, the CBI has approached a court in Kolkata to declare industrialist Ashok Todi and his family members, charged with abetment of suicide of Rizwanur Rehman, as Proclaimed Offenders.

The CBI counsel also moved an application for attachment of their properties, to which the court said it would give Ashok Todi, his brother Pradeep and his brother-in-law Anil Saraogi time till November 10 to appear before it or CBI. Sources said an application was moved under Section 82 (proclamation for absconding persons) and Section 83 (attachment of property of persons absconding) after the Todis failed to surrender either in the court or before the CBI by October 27. All petitions moved on behalf of Todis in the trial court of Metropolitan Magistrate Bhivas Chatterjee and sessions court for staying of arrest warrants were dismissed.

The CBI has been carrying out raids at various places in Kolkata and Chennai to find the Todi brothers who began to face the heat after the metropolitan magistrate issued non-bailable warrants against them as they failed to appear before it. The passports of Todis and Saraogi have already been cancelled for their alleged role in inciting Rizwanur Rehman to commit suicide last year, a month after his marriage to the industrialist's daughter. Rizwanur's body was found on railway tracks on September 21, 2007. He had married Priyanka on August 18 last year.

Heading: ‘Curfew’ in Valley to check separatists’ protests - Indian Express
Content:
Enraged about a delay in serving paan, a constable allegedly shot a handicapped vendor dead near the Hardoi bypass crossing here on Wednesday evening.

Constable Rajiv Mishra fired five bullets at Kaushal Asthana, who died on the spot with two bullets lodged in his chest. Mishra was accompanied by Sanandan Mishra, son of another policeman, when the incident occurred.

Talkatora Station Officer Sanjay Pandey denied his role in the incident till Mishra was arrested late in evening after the intervention of the police top brass.

Lucknow DIG Chandra Prakash said: "Initially, the SO, Talkatora, tried to suppress the details of the incident. But eyewitnesses told us the truth. Pandey has been sent to the Police Lines and we have initiated the process to terminate Mishra's service."

Mishra was posted as the Criminal Intelligence Officer in the Talkatora police station. After the incident came to light, the post was scrapped from Lucknow Zone with immediate effect.

Inspector General A K Jain said each member of the Lucknow district police will give a day's salary to Asthana's widow.

In another incident which surfaced on Thursday, a 46-year-old woman has accused a head constable of raping her in his official residence adjacent to the police station. Tejpal Singh (59), was posted at the Tilhar police station in Shahjahanpur district.

"The woman has filed an FIR at Tehesil Diwas on Tuesday. She has accused the policeman of raping her on October 15 when she had come to the police station to file a complaint," said SP Shahjahanpur, Ejil Arsan. The accused policeman, who had only five months of service remaining, is absconding, he added.

The incidents fly in the face of Chief Minister Mayawati's strict order to discipline the police. Four months ago, after the Hazratganj Station House Officer openly thrashed two brothers, Mayawati had asserted: "There should not be a repetition of Hazratganj and the culprits should be dealt with severely and even jailed, if necessary."

On the occasion of Police Day on October 20, she had reiterated: "The police should be humane while interacting with the public to improve their indecent image that prevails in the mind of people."

But despite the warnings, few policemen have been penalised. Either the people have been absolved following a departmental inquiry or reinstated within a short period after minimum disciplinary action.

In the Hazratganj incident, the erring SHO was suspended, but within a month he was given charge of a police station in Agra.

IG Lucknow Zone AK Jain said: "It is not possible to monitor the activities of each and every constable in such a huge department."

Claiming that proper action has been taken against the culprits, the IG said: "The department does not have any policeman who had been involved in any criminal activity and no action has been taken against him".

Heading: Assam blasts: car trail leads to arrest of 5 men in Nalbari - Indian Express
Content:
With Assembly elections just 11 days away, the J-K Government on Thursday imposed an undeclared curfew across Kashmir valley to thwart the separatists' plan to take out protest marches towards Srinagar's grand mosque.

While the curfew did manage to halt the separatist protests, it added to the woes of mainstream political parties, which are yet to initiate election campaigns and approach people for votes.

The separatist-sponsored Co-ordination Committee which spearheads the protests and poll boycott campaign, meanwhile, repeated the call for the march on Friday. The Committee also called for similar protests on the election days. "We will go ahead with march on Friday," said a Committee spokesman .

However, IG, Kashmir range, B Srinivas said they had not imposed any curfew. "People were put under friendly confinement to avoid harassment from separatists," he said, adding the separatist calls for protest marches and subsequent police restrictions would not hamper the poll process.

In Srinagar, J-K Police and CRPF personnel were deployed in heavy numbers and the troops had sealed off all the entry routes into the city. People were not allowed to move out of their homes, and security barricades had been erected everywhere.

In the downtown localities, securitymen had warned people to stay inside. A heavy police and CRPF cordon had been put in place around the Jamia Mosque, and the roads were sealed with barbed wire spools. "There were police and CRPF men everywhere in our locality and nobody was allowed to venture out," said Mohammad Shafi, a resident of Nowhatta.

In other districts of the Valley, too, undeclared curfew was imposed. In Sopore, the curfew announcement was made early in the morning.

Hurriyat chairman Mirwaiz Umer Farooq, placed under house arrest, criticised the Government decision to impose curfew. "The Government is trying to crush the voice of people in Kashmir by using force," he said.

The mainstream political parties are worried but hope that the intensity of the separatist call will diminish as the poll date approaches. "This situation is more likely to affect Srinagar city. We hope the rural areas will not be affected much," said NC leader Ali Mohamamd Sagar.

Heading: Blasts don’t affect tourist flow in Kaziranga - Indian Express
Content:
A week after the serial blasts in Assam, the police are yet to come up with anything worthwhile to solve the riddle.

The police, however, picked up five persons from Nalbari district in Lower Assam on Thursday in connection with one of the three blasts in Guwahati.

The arrested persons have been identified as Chandra Boro, Bhola Boro, Arabinda Boro, Bhupesh Boro and Raju Boro. Sources in the police said they were picked up following a clue linked to a Maruti car used in the blast at Panbazar here last Thursday.

Nalbari SP Jitmal Doley said the five persons were picked up and handed over to Guwahati City Police on Thursday. An official here said the persons were being interrogated by an IGP-level officer. With this, the total number of persons detained or arrested by the police has gone up to eight.

The other three include one Nazir Ahmed of Moirabari in Morigaon district, from whose mobile phone an SMS was sent to a local television news channel as well as a number in New Delhi in the name of an organisation called ISF(IM) on Saturday. The police had suggested that the acronym when expanded was Islamic Security Force (Indian Mujahideen).

The police, meanwhile, have found out the chassis numbers and engine numbers of two of the three Maruti cars used as car-bombs by the terrorists. Police have also revealed that the car used in the Panbazar blast was originally registered in Delhi.

The car used in the Ganeshguri blast on the other hand had an Itanagar registration.

Police have also claimed having identified the owner of the car used in the blast outside the DC's and CJM's courts in Guwahati.

The registration number on the number plate of the car used as a bomb however was fake. While it was a number from Sonitpur district (AS-12N-1025), the authorities have confirmed that the registration series currently in use in that district is AS-12F.

Heading: Rs 60,000-cr scam in 2G spectrum allocation: CPM - Indian Express
Content:
The serial blasts of October 30, despite the devastation wreaked by it, seem not to have deterred tourists from coming into the northeastern state. Even as the United States issued a travel advisory to its citizens against visiting Assam, dozens of foreign tourists including Americans are in the state, taking safaris through the Kaziranga National Park, home to the one-horned Indian rhinoceros.

"Tourist flow to Kaziranga has already begun, and at least 700 tourists including 150 foreign tourists have already visited the national park since it reopened for this season on November 1," Dibyadhar Gogoi, divisional forest officer told The Indian Express.

In the last season, Kaziranga, home to over 1800 rhinos, had over 87,000 tourists, of which about 6,300 were foreigners, Gogoi said. "We are expecting a bigger rush this season, especially in view of more tourist arrivals to the country as a whole," he added.

The blasts also do not appear to dissuade those in the tourism industry. "We have already brought in several groups of foreign tourists even after the October 30 serial blasts. Even today I am taking around a group of 18 Japanese tourists in Kaziranga," said Ashish Phukan of Jungle Travels India, which handles about 50 per cent of foreign tourists in northeast India. He said an 11-member group of Americans had left Kaziranga on Wednesday, while a Taiwanese group is arriving Friday. "We are getting queries following the October 30 blasts, but not one group has cancelled their trip or changed their itinerary."

"There were obviously a lot of cancellations on the first three or four days, but those can be considered only as immediate reactions. One week after the blasts, the tourist flow appears to be normal again," said S M S Bordoloi of Hiuen Tsang Travels.

Four other national parks in Assam — Manas, Orang, Dibru-Saikhowa and Nameri — have also opened their gates for tourists last week, after having remained shut for the monsoons until October 30. Tourists have also started visiting Pobitora, a wildlife sanctuary 50 km east of Guwahati.

Heading: NGOs to state Govt: check illegal Bangladeshis - Indian Express
Content:
The already troubled relations between CPI(M) and DMK nose-dived further on Thursday with the major Left party alleging a scam running into crores in 2G spectrum allocation by the Telecom Ministry held by DMK's A Raja. The CPI(M) demanded an inquiry into alleged discrepancies in the spectrum allocation process, saying the faulty method had cost over Rs 60,000 crore to the national exchequer.

The party pointed out that Swan Telecom which had bought a licence for 13 circles, along with the necessary 2G spectrum, for a paltry Rs 1,537 crore subsequently sold 45 per cent of its stake to Etisalat for $900 million, taking its book value to $2 billion. Similarly, Unitech sold 60 per cent of its stake to Talenor for Rs 6,120 crore while paying only Rs 1,651 crore as licence fee.

The Government has actually got only one-sixth of what it should have got, had it gone through a fresh auction route. It has incurred a loss of Rs 10,000 crore on Swan and Unitech licences alone, the statement said.

The deal between UAE's telecom operator Etisalat and Swan Telecom, and Unitech and Talenor (of Norway) had brought out the magnitude of largesse that had been doled out, it added. The CPI(M) said "Instead of redressing what has become an open scandal, the Government has dealt with the question as to whether these companies can sell their shares legally".

Heading: The train from Deoband - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty NGOs met Meghalaya Chief Minister Donkupar Roy on Thursday and demanded that the Meghalaya Progressive Alliance coalition Government must immediately introduce a three-tier identity card system to check illegal Bangladeshi migrants in Meghalaya.

After the recent Assam blasts, NGOs in Meghalaya have been stressing the need to put in place a mechanism to stop influx of outsiders and illegal Bangladeshis migrants.

Joint Committee of NGOs chairman H P Oflyn Dohling said the Government must immediately operationalise the inner line permit and work permit to contain the unabated illegal migrants. He said the Chief Minister assured the NGOs that the Government would do the needful.

The Government is putting in place a mechanism like the work permit which prevents labourers from outside to get voting right in Meghalaya. The permits will also be issued to inter-state migrants.

Heading: Army: prestige hurt by arrest of officer - Indian Express
Content:
The excitement and confusion at the platform in Deoband is usual. People scurry around looking for their coaches, some managing to hop on as the train pulls out and others missing it altogether as it pulls out of the station at 12 pm. But this is no ordinary train. Decked with posters, the 18-coach Sheikh-Ul-Hind Express is a special train that's carrying about 2,000 clerics to Hyderabad for the 29th conference of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind that will be held on November 8 and 9. It's also carrying a message of peace and national integration and with it a hope that people will see them as men of peace and not supporters of terror.

The train is named after Maulana Mehmud Hasan or Sheikh-Ul-Hind, who was the guiding force behind the formation of the Jamiat that went on to become one of India's leading Islamic organisations. At present, it has 10 million primary members and a notable presence in towns and villages across India.

Abdul Wajid has come to Deoband to board the Sheikh-Ul-Hind Express from Rampur, some 200 km away. The madrasa teacher has attended many conferences of the Jamiat but realises the importance of the Hyderabad meet in these times. And so do the hundreds of clerics who have boarded the Aman Ekta Karwan from neighbouring Muzaffarnagar, Bijnore, and other western Uttar Pradesh towns and from Uttarakhand.

The organisation, that was founded in 1919 and led a prominent role in the freedom struggle, last held its conference in 2005. The issue it debated then was reservations for Muslims, now it's terror.

"One of the issues that we will discuss is, 'Can terrorism ever be jehad?'. The Darul Uloom at Deoband had recently passed a fatwa on terrorism but ordinary people are still not clear on this. Jehad is a term used in the Quran against zulm (atrocities) but terror itself is a zulm. So these two things are separate, they cannot be one. We want to make this message clear," says Jamiat leader and Rajya Sabha MP Mahmood Madani.

The delegation will also discuss the related issue of community profiling. "In the name of terrorism, the way investigation is often carried out and the way a community is profiled is not right. The third issue is that there is one force that is threatening the minorities in the country and there is another that is provoking them. We have to deal with both," adds Madani.

However, Madani admits that there is a need for the community to introspect. "We should introspect. Not just us, everybody should look within themselves. We will not let our youth go astray. If someone is wrong, he should be punished. There was (Mansoor) Peerbhoy who confessed to what he did. There was also Peerbhoy's mother who withdrew the lawyer the family had hired to defend him when he told her of his involvement," says Madani.

Peerbhoy, the Pune techie, was arrested by the Mumbai ATS on September 29 on charges of sending terror emails and for his alleged involvement in the Indian Mujahideen plot.

In the coaches, the passengers are settling down slowly. The aisles are busy with people carrying and stocking water bottles while others have got comfortable enough to read newspapers and pull out rotis and paranthas from tiffins.

America's president elect Barack Obama is the obvious topic of conversation and his message of change appears to have struck a chord here too. "By sending a Black to the White House, the American people have shown that there can be change, there can be progress. Change is good. We should learn from that," says 32-year-old Tafzil Ahmed. "Who knows? Maybe some day India will elect a person from the backward class as its prime minister," adds another.

For many, it is their first visit to Hyderabad and once they are done with the conference, they plan to take time off to visit the Charminar and Mecca Masjid. Quari Mohammad Shoaib is one of them.

An alumnus of the Deoband madrasa, he now teaches in his hometown of Najibabad in Uttar Pradesh. "This conference is important. Many young people like me are scared to even travel these days. I feel scared that the police may harass me because of the way I look." Shoaib, who spends a lot of time among young students, says he has seen a slight inferiority complex creep amongst them.

"They seem more hesitant to go out, to travel. They think people stereotype them because of their beard and topi," he says.

But this one time, they are not scared to step out and travel. At the next stop, Meerut, about 200 clerics get on the train, some get off to offer namaz at the platform while others take a hurried tea break. The stops are limited on this train. After Meerut, it stops at the Nizamuddin station in Delhi, then Bhopal. And finally when the Aman Ekta Karwan stops at Hyderabad on Friday evening, its passengers hope it will be the beginning of a peace process.

Heading: HRD ministry, V-Cs to discuss improving ‘teaching standards’ - Indian Express
Content:
Admitting that the arrest of a serving officer for his involvement in the Malegaon blasts has dented the Army's image, the Deputy Army Chief has said that strictest action would be taken against the officer if he is found guilty.

Sticking to the Army's line that the incident is a one off 'aberration', Lt Gen S P S Dhillon said it has nonetheless hurt the image and prestige of the armed forces.

"Indian Army's prestige has been hurt after our officer's name came up in Malegaon blast case," Lt Gen Dhillon told reporters at the sidelines of UN peacekeeping function in the Capital. This is the first official reaction to the arrest of Lt Col SP Purohit by the Mumbai Police for allegedly supplying money to the main accused in the Malegaon blasts.

However, the officer said the involvement of a serving officer was a 'freak' occurrence and several checks were in place to keep an eye on such things. "This is a freak incident. We have our own mechanism in place for keeping a check on these kinds of things," Lt Gen Dhillon said.

The Deputy Chief said that while the incident was an aberration, the strictest possible action would be taken against the serving officer if he is found guilty. He added that the Army will take the next action only after receiving a report from the Mumbai Police.

Heading: Autopsy report points at fake encounter: Rahul Raj’s father - Indian Express
Content:
When the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry holds a conference of Vice-Chancellors and heads of Central Universities next week, one of the key issues on the agenda will be improvement of 'teaching quality' in the light of the recommendations made by the Pay Review Committee (PRC).

The PRC, headed by Prof G K Chadha, has proposed that while teachers must get a good pay hike, they should also be able to ensure accountability under the new 'strong recommendations' on teacher assessment and workload system. A student evaluation element has been recommended for the teacher assessment process, besides self-assessment and institutional assessment. Recommendations on the need for teachers to spend time outside the class as well in tutorials and so on to assist students are also included. Teachers will also be evaluated on the number of research papers they publish and whether these appear in quality journals to ensure a constant upgradation in teacher skills, as per PRC recommendations.

Heading: Parties steer clear of Maoist Bastar - Indian Express
Content:
The father of Rahul Raj, the Patna youth who was killed after attempting to hold a BEST bus hostage, said on Thursday that his son's autopsy report confirmed his doubts that Rahul was "murdered" by the Mumbai Police on October 27. Meanwhile, a complainant has lodged another case regarding the incident against Raj Thackeray and others in a Patna court.

An enraged Kundan Prasad Singh told reporters that the autopsy report confirmed that bullets were fired at his son from a distance of less than 2 feet. "How can an encounter take place from such a close range? He was shot at almost point blank range," said Singh.

Mumbai doctors said there were five entry wounds in Rahul's chest and head. There were only four exit wounds. A senior doctor had interpreted that the bullets were fired from close range, causing gunpowder to burn the skin around the wound.

Singh, who has decided to meet the President of India shortly to demand justice for his son, said: "My son was overpowered by the police and shot dead so that it would look like an encounter."

He added that the "fair report" prepared by medical experts of JJ Hospital, Mumbai, should open the eyes of the Maharashtra Government to the "bestiality" of its policemen. "I have been also seeking legal opinion to move the Supreme Court," he added.

Meanwhile, complaints continue to be filed against MNS chief Raj Thackeray in Bihar. One Vinay Kumar alias Bihari Bhaiya on Thursday filed a case against Raj and nine others accusing them of murder, criminal conspiracy and tampering with evidence in a Patna chief judicial magistrate court.

Heading: 1 more killed by leopard, villagers protest - Indian Express
Content:
With Maoists calling for a boycott of the Assembly polls on November 14, candidates belonging to various political parties, with the exception of the CPI, are refraining from campaigning in sensitive Naxalite areas in Chhattisgarh's Bastar region.

Parts of Dantewada, Bijapur and Narayanpur districts in south Bastar fall in the so-called "liberated zone of the Maoists' Dandakaranya state" where the civil administration does not have any visible presence. Few elected representatives or other political workers — including political heavyweights and senior leaders of both the ruling BJP as well as the Congress — dare to even venture into many of the villages in the 12 constituencies falling in Bastar region.

The situation is worst in Dantewada-ST, Konta-ST, Bijapur-ST,Chitrakote-ST and Narayanpur-ST where candidates avoid travelling along village roads, given the threat of landmine blasts and attack by the Naxalites. Paramilitary personnel keep a close watch even at the corner poll meetings of different political parties in the entire region.

Veteran tribal leader Mahendra Karma, who is also Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, candidly admits, "There are many villages in my Dantewada constituency where I cannot go to seek votes because of risks involved. It's a similar case with other candidates here".

Karma, who has been a prominent anti-Naxalite leader since 1989 when he headed the Jan Jagaran Abhiyan — a movement to raise awareness about the ills of Left extremism — is among the frontline leaders of the controversial Salwa Judum movement, which began three years ago in order to isolate the rebels. But even though he has been provided with 'Z' plus security cover, he baulks from visiting remote areas.

"It's a fact that candidates avoid visiting many places not only during the polls, but also after getting elected. I am already in the Naxalite hit list, so I only stick to the main roads during campaigning," he told The Indian Express.

Similarly, candidates of the ruling BJP, which gave its open support to Salwa Judum campaign, also steer clear of certain areas as a precautionary measure. "Even though rebels do not have much influence in this constituency, we avoid sensitive areas and are cautious during campaigning," said BJP candidate from Chitrakote-ST, Baidumram Kashyap.

Even those who oppose the anti-Naxal movement are apprehensive about venturing too far into Maoist territory. For example, Congress legislators Kawasi Lakma and Rajendra Pambhoi, representing Konta and Bijapur constituencies respectively, have admitted that are not in a position to launch an intensive campaign in many villages.

The only party that has some visibility in such regions is the Communist Party of India (CPI). Its flags are conspicuous in a number of remote villages in Konta, Dantewada, Bijapur and Chitrakote, leading Congress and BJP leaders to allege that the CPI enjoys the tacit support of the Maoist rebels.

"See the manner in which CPI candidates are touring sensitive and hypersensitive areas to canvass support. The local CPI is functioning as the 'dalal' (agent) of the Maoists," said Congress leader Mahendra Karma. "Mass-based parties like the Congress and BJP could not even hoist their party flags in many of these areas," he added. "Is it not indicative of a political nexus?"

However, Dantewada segment's CPI candidate Manish Kunjam described the charge against his party as baseless, alleging that the CPI's presence only highlights how the Congress and BJP have alienated the people, despite being in power for many years. Kunjam, who is also president of the Adivasi Mahasabha, a tribal organisation, said the CPI had always shown stood up for the rights of tribals in the area. "It's reflecting during the election campaign," he added.

Heading: HJM activist detained in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The man-animal conflict in Chandrapur district of Vidarbha deteriorated into a law and order problem in Vesgaon village of Gondpipri tehsil today, when security forces had to be called in to control villagers protesting against the death of a man in a leopard attack.

Abaji Deogade, 28, was killed by a leopard near his house at about 6 am. "I head loud screams, so I ran out. A few other villagers also came out. The leopard had grabbed Abaji by the neck. For about 15 minutes, he held on. But when more villagers joined us, he retreated. However, Abaji was dead," said Subhash Deogade, the victim's cousin.

This is the second leopard-related death in the village in the last one month. The angry villagers first staged a chakka jam and then attacked five vehicles of top forest officials who reached the village after a few hours. The officials, including Conservator of Forest Mahip Gupta, Divisional Forest Officer Rama Rao, Range Forest Officer V M More and two beat guards, were locked up by the villagers in the gram panchayat building.

With the situation taking a serious turn, police forces were called in from Chandrapur. The villagers finally freed the forest officials and allowed Abaji's body to be taken for post-mortem.

"The leopard has killed two people, injured three and eaten about 10 goats, 20 dogs and a lot of hens. This has been going on for more than a month, and the forest department has done little," said a villager, Ramu Raspalle.

Heading: Sangh Parivar blames RSS man’s death on ‘soft’ Orissa Govt - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai ATS officials on Wednesday picked up an active member of Hindu Jagran Manch (HJM) from Vapi, who was earlier associated with Swami Ashimanandji Maharaj in his ashram at Subir village in Ahwa Taluka of Dangs district.

Sunil Dhawade, 30, was picked up from a packaging factory in Vapi GIDC. A resident of Ambapada village in Ahwa Taluka of Dang district, he earlier worked at Sabrikumbh with Swami Ashimanandji Maharaj who runs Vanvasi Kalyan Ashram at Subri village in Ahwa taluka.

Sunil left his job with Swamiji and started working in a packaging company in Vapi GIDC three months ago.

Sunil is an active member of HJM and Vishwa Hindu Parishad in Dangs. Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur stayed for some days at Sabrikumbh fair in 2005. Pragya was close to Swamiji, who had gone underground after her arrest, and Sunil used to drive her around, said sources.

Valsad District Superintendent of Police D J Patel said, "Our officials assisted Mumbai police in picking up Sunil as they had approached us for help. We are trying to find out Sunil's antecedents and contacts."

However, Sunil's father Arjun Dhawade said, "We have not been informed of my son's whereabouts. We don't even know for what reason he has been picked up. The police officers contacted me identifying themselves as hotel businessmen and they took his phone number and address."

Heading: Dalai Lama’s envoys back from China - Indian Express
Content:
A day after an RSS activist was shot dead by three unidentified gunmen in Kandhamal district, the Sangh Parivar alleged that the murder was a result of Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik's soft corner for Christians in the state.

On Wednesday, Dhanu Pradhan, a mason at Kumbharigaon village of Christian-dominated Brahmanaigaon area, was shot dead by three persons from their 9 mm pistols from close range. Kandhamal Superintendent of Police Praveen Kumar said at least five rounds were fired at Pradhan's head and chest, some of which exited through his body. Pradhan along with other workers had been engaged in the construction of a school since early morning and the assailants fired at him soon after other workers left for lunch. "We are looking at all possible angles, including the Maoist one. Nothing has been proved as yet. Though there is some tension, the situation is under control," said Praveen Kumar. A combing operation has been launched to nab the assailants.

The Sangh parivar, which of late has become a bitter critic of Naveen Patnaik, said the murder of Pradhan showed that the CM was indifferent to the plight of tribals.

"Naveen Patnaik is acting as a sympathiser of Christians rather than the majority Hindus. The administration is blind and, as in the Laxmanananda case, it is blaming the Maoists without any proof. Within a few days of killing of Laxmanananda, wall posters sprang up in Brahmanigaon which spoke of killing Kandh tribals Dhanu Pradhan, Vikram, Arun Karji and Chitrasen," said Dr Laxmikanta Dash, state secretary of Vanvasi Kalyan Ashram, a body of RSS that brings the tribals into the Sangh fold.

"Though police knew about the threat, still no security was provided to Pradhan. A peace committee meeting was scheduled for today, but a few local Christians sent a message that the four Kandh youths have to be eliminated after which they can talk about peace. This shows that they wanted to disrupt today's scheduled peace meeting," he added.

Ashok Sahu of Hindu Jagaran Sammukhua, another RSS organisation, said the murder was pre-meditated. "The killers have challenged the state police who have proved their incompetence by failing to nab the killers of Swamiji. The Kandhs are assisting in the state-sponsored peace efforts for restoration of normalcy while militant Christians are stoking communal tension," he added. The Sangh has demanded a compensation of Rs 10 lakh for the family of Pradhan and proper safety and protection for the Hindus in Brahamonigaon.

Heading: Our MPs won’t resign, says Sushil Modi - Indian Express
Content: "We presented a memorandum to the Chinese leadership asking for genuine autonomy for the Tibetan people," Dalai Lama's special envoy Kasur Lodi Gyari said after returning from Beijing on Thursday. "As a special general meeting of the Tibetan people is being convened later this month at the suggestion of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, we have been advised not to make statements about our discussions before this meeting," said the statement. The Dalai Lama's envoys had gone to Beijing to hold eighth round of talks with the Chinese officials for finding a solution to the vexed issue of Tibet.

Heading: India, China must work together: envoy - Indian Express
Content:
On a day when its ally in Bihar, the JD(U), declared that all its Lok Sabha MPs would resign to protest against the anti-north Indian attacks in Maharashtra, the BJP clarified that it has no intentions of following suit. Talking to The Indian Express, senior BJP leader and Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Sushil Kumar Modi said his party has decided that its MPs will not resign. Excerpts from an interview:

•JD(U) has said its MPs will resign on Friday over the anti-north Indian attacks. What is the stand of your party?

The BJP has decided that its MPs from Bihar will not resign. We are against the politics of resignations. We feel that RJD, LJP and Congress ministers from Bihar in the UPA Government should resign and not the MPs. It does not make any sense.

•w Don't you think that it will come as a jolt for your ally, the JD(U) and will show a rift in the alliance?

No, I don't think so. Like the JD(U), the BJP too is independent to take its stand over an issue. This will not affect our alliance. Our strategy is to put pressure on the Centre to act. After all it is a Congress Government at the Centre and in Maharahtra too. Everything is in the hands of the Congress.

•w It is being said that the BJP is in a bind, caught between its two allies, the Shiv Sena and the JD(U).

No, this is not true. I had personally demanded action against Shiv Sena leader Uddhav Thackeray when he spoke against Bihar leaders meddling in Maharashtra. But it is notable that the Shiv Sena so far is not responsible for any attack against Biharis in Mumbai. Every report has held the MNS responsible for it.

•w But the Shiv Sena mouthpiece Saamna took credit for the attack on students appearing for the Railway exam?

They may have. But we so far have not received any report in this regard. Moreover, on the issue of preference to locals in jobs, all parties including the Congress and the NCP are of the same opinion.

•w Do you support the JD(U)'s demand that Raj Thackeray should be arrested under MCOCA and a CBI probe should be ordered in the killing of the Patna youth by the Mumbai Police?

Why only MCOCA? The Centre and the state are free to arrest Raj Thackeray under the most severe law. Why should we be against it? After all, the BJP also was part of an all-party delegation to the Prime Minister demanding stern action. Everything is in the hands of the Congress. It is responsible for patronising Raj Thackeray to weaken the Shiv Sena. Lalu and Paswan should resign for sitting in the lap of such a party.

Heading: 5 JDU MPs to quit today - Indian Express
Content:
Limited to the realm of religion so far, India's largest Muslim outfit, the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, has decided to chart out a new course by launching a political party. However, as forming a party is a lengthy process, its strategy for the upcoming Assembly and Lok Sabha elections is to back non-Congress secular parties where the Congress has little or no presence.

"We have decided to launch a party, but the details have not been worked out yet. One thing is clear — the party will take up issues of the Muslim community and other backward and weaker sections," Jamaat-e-Islami Hind president Syed Jalaluddin Umari told The Indian Express. Jamaat leaders added Muslims are in a majority in at least eight Lok Sabha seats, while they are a deciding factor in around 80 constituencies.

Umari said his advice to Muslims for the coming elections is to vote for the Congress where it is engaged in a direct fight with the BJP and to choose other secular parties where Congress is weak. "It could be the BSP, SP or the Left parties," he said.

"I don't think the plans to float a Muslim party can materialise before the coming Lok Sabha elections."

He said while the BJP is implicitly anti-Muslim, the Congress has also failed to address the concerns of the community adequately. According to Umari, other parties have also paid only lip service to the community, using it as a vote bank. "It's time to change," he added.

The way the rise of Mayawati empowered Dalits and the Mulayam Singh Yadav rule in Uttar Pradesh proved to be beneficial for the Yadavs, "a Muslim party is needed to effectively raise the issues faced by the community," said Umari, although he insisted that the party would not be "communal" as it would address "the concerns of Dalits and other marginalised sections of society".

He added that Jamaat is discussing the matter with the Jamiat-Ulema-e-Hind, the Majlis-e-Mushawarat and the All-India Milli Council to seek their participation. Umari said the outfit will also get in touch with Muslim MPs and parties like the Muslim League and All Indian Majlis-e-Ittihad-al-Muslim.

Heading: Day after euphoric victory, Obama team puts leash on expectations - Indian Express
Content:
Janata Dal (United) parliamentary party leader Prabhunath Singh on Thursday declared that five MPs of the party in the Lok Sabha would resign from the House on Friday.

"All five MPs of the JD(U) in the Lok Sabha will resign tomorrow. We have secured an appointment with Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee on Friday morning," Singh told reporters. The declaration comes after the autopsy report of Rahul Raj—shot dead by the Mumbai Police—reportedly said he was shot from a very close range.

JD(U)'s move, aimed at scoring political points, is sure to put pressure on rivals RJD and LJP from Bihar who are part of the UPA Government at the Centre. The resignations are sure to be played out in Bihar, as the death of two Bihari youths in anti-north Indian attacks in Maharashtra has struck an emotional chord in the state. Bihar was also rocked by violent protests from students demanding stern action against Raj Thackeray or resignation of leaders from the state.

"The autopsy report of Rahul Raj who was shot dead by the Mumbai Police clearly shows he was murdered in cold blood. So far the UPA Government at the Centre and in Maharashtra have not taken any concrete step. It seems they are supporting forces out to break the country. In such a situation our MPs are resigning in protest," said JD(U) spokesman and MP Shivanand Tiwary. He said UPA heavyweights Lalu and Paswan should use their clout and do something or else they should also quit.

Days after an all-party delegation from Bihar met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh urging him to intervene in Maharashtra, JD(U) president Sharad Yadav declared that party MPs would resign if Raj Thackeray was not arrested under MCOCA and a CBI probe ordered into the killing of the Patna youth by the Mumbai Police. Caught unawares, Railway Minister Lalu Prasad tried to counter the move by declaring that not only his MPs but MLAs and MLCs from Bihar would also resign over the issue and dared the JD(U) leadership to do the same. However, Nitish countered by saying such a move would lead to imposition of President's Rule in Bihar. "There is demand for imposition of President's Rule in Maharahstra. But Lalu's formula will lead to President's Rule in Bihar", he remarked.

Heading: Preparing for Washington - Indian Express
Content:
Her last ride on the McCain-Palin campaign plane ended here, back home in the cold and the snow and the familiar.

"We are Alaskans!" Sarah Palin, standing with her husband Todd, told scores of cheering supporters who showed up to greet her upon her return to Alaska late on Wednesday.

Standing on the icy tarmac on a subfreezing night, Palin said she had learned much about America in her time on the campaign trail with John McCain. She also said she looked forward to getting back to her day job. She promised to work to expand development of Alaska's oil and gas resources and also to be a voice for families, like her own, that have children with special needs. She said she would "reach out" to Senator Barack Obama, the president-elect, on these issues and more.

"I just thank God for this opportunity that I have to be your governor," Palin said.

"You did so great out there," one woman in the crowd said. "We are so proud of you," read one sign. A chant gained volume, encouraging Palin to return to the national stage: "Two thousand twelve!"

Then Palin turned to speak to reporters. Once again, she asserted that the rumors of tension between her and McCain were not true. In fact, she said, they spoke by phone today during her layover in Seattle.

"We had a great relationship," she said, adding, "I love him."

One tough lesson she said she learned Outside, as Alaskans often call the rest of the country: the media is not always fair. She mocked the notion that she had, as some have claimed, "gone rogue" while running for vice president.

Palin faces some complicated political dynamics now that she has returned. Some state Democrats, often her allies in the past, have been angered by her aggressive partisanship on the campaign trail. Then again, Palin has criticized some important local Republicans, too.

Last week, after Senator Ted Stevens was convicted on federal charges that he failed to disclose gifts and free home renovations he received, Palin joined McCain and other top Republicans in calling for him to resign. Yet while Palin lost her bid for the vice presidency, Mr. Stevens, the longest-serving Republican in Senate history, holds a narrow lead in his bid for a seventh full term.

Asked Wednesday whether she still believed that Mr. Stevens should resign, Palin was circumspect, saying only that the people of Alaska "just spoke" on the issue at the ballot box and that "they want him as their senator." She said Stevens should decide "what happens next." (Stevens could still be forced to step down, and Palin is widely viewed as a potential candidate for his seat if he does.)

The governor took a few more questions, then turned back to the crowd of supporters and worked her last rope line under the supervision of media advisers to the McCain-Palin campaign and the Secret Service.

"This is the last time they'll be doing this for her," said Taylor Griffin, a spokesman for the campaign, gesturing toward the wall of agents at Palin's back. "But for right now, she's still under protection."

Heading: ‘Knew very little, spent too much, resisted coaching’ - Indian Express
Content:
Move over, Carla Bruni, there's a new fashion first lady on the scene.

The black-and-red Narciso Rodriguez dress that Michelle Obama wore in Chicago Tuesday night was another daring fashion choice, a straight-from-the spring-runway style that she paired with a black cardigan. And the blogs are burning up with opinions about it. (most of them negative)

But the symbolism of patriotic red bursting out of black like a firecracker out of the night sky was attractive. And next to Jill Biden in her skirt suit, Obama looked like a breath of chic air. There are indications that Washington is about to become a very stylish place indeed.

The comparisons between Michelle and Jackie Kennedy are really off the mark. Kennedy's style was rooted in Paris, in the haute couture dresses she worked with Oleg Cassini to replicate.

Obama may know how to rock a strand of pearls, but she has her own approach to style. Over the past few months, she has mixed designer dresses from young American fashion talents such as Rodriguez and Thakoon Panichgul with cheap-chic finds from J Crew and H&M, which is a much more modern way to dress than wearing head-to-toe designer. Even if you could afford to spend $1,50,000 in one month on a designer wardrobe, would you want to?

Heading: 106-year-old Atlanta woman basks in Obama tribute - Indian Express
Content:
Sarah Palin left the national stage on Wednesday, but the controversy over her role on the ticket flared as aides to John McCain disclosed new details about her expensive wardrobe purchases and revealed that a Republican Party lawyer would be dispatched to Alaska to inventory and retrieve the clothes still in her possession.

Tensions have simmered for much of the last month between aides loyal to McCain and those loyal to Palin, but they erupted in the wake of the Republican nominee's defeat, as both sides spoke freely — but anonymously — about the wardrobe controversy and other conflicts.

Two aides to McCain and two to Palin discussed the tensions but asked that their names not be revealed, saying they were not comfortable speaking openly about internal operations.

The miscommunication and quarrels between the two camps continued as late as Tuesday night, said McCain aides familiar with the situation. Palin arrived at the Arizona Biltmore planning to deliver her own speech before McCain's concession speech, they said, but was told by McCain's senior aides Steve Schmidt and Mark Salter that would not be appropriate.

Fox News reported on Wednesday that Palin's lack of knowledge on certain topics also strained relations. Carl Cameron reported that campaign sources told him she had resisted coaching before her faltering Katie Couric interviews; did not understand that Africa was a continent, not a country; and could not name the three countries that are part of the North American Free Trade Agreement — the United States, Canada and Mexico.

For weeks, the McCain-Palin campaign has been dealt with the fallout from the disclosure that the Republican National Committee was billed for $1,50,000 in wardrobe purchases for the Palin family — a discovery that was widely ridiculed and undercut Palin's hockey mom appeal.

Several McCain aides said they had recently discovered that Palin's traveling staff had used their personal credit cards to spend as much as $20,000 to $30,000 more on wardrobe items for Palin as she has campaigned around the country in recent weeks.

Palin and many of her aides were traveling back to Alaska Wednesday afternoon and could not be reached for comment.

McCain aides said on Wednesday that spending on Palin's wardrobe continued well after the convention, with one custom-made outfit showing up around the time of her Saturday Night Live appearance.

As first reported by Newsweek on Wednesday, McCain aides said some of that money was spent on clothing for Palin's children and husband Todd, who may have received between $20,000 and $40,000 in wardrobe purchases, including thousands of dollars in shoes. Several aides also said the items included jewelry, but a Palin aide disputed that.
