Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Sabarmati jail undertrial attempts ‘suicide’ - Indian Express
Content:
Two subadult lions, aged about three years, died after falling into a parapet-less well on the outskirts of Mitiyala village near Mitiyala sanctuary under the Gir East forest division. Their carcasses were fished out on Friday.

Premji Delwadiya, owner of the agriculture land, spotted the carcasses floating in his well in the morning and informed the forest officials. Foresters rushed to the spot and pulled out the carcasses and sent them to the Jashadhar Animal Care Centre for postmortem.

Maneshwar Raja, Deputy Conservator of Forest (Gir East), said, "The lions died due to drowning. The postmortem report confirmed this." According to Raja, the well was 40 feet deep with a water level of 15 feet. He said the big cats might have fallen in the well at least 24 hours before the incident came to light. He ruled out any possibility of foul play as all the claws and bones were found intact.

"Even as the state government is providing a subsidy of Rs 4,000 to cover the wells surrounding the Gir forest, farmers do not seem to be interested in this, creating a trouble for the wildlife," Raja said.

The Gir East forest division has been given a target of 4,000 wells to be covered with lid during the current financial year. "Till date, we have covered around 1,500 wells," he said.

Heading: Forest Dept takes Dashmool project forward but minus the phytochemical laboratory - Indian Express
Content:
An Under-trial prisoner at the Sabarmati Central Jail allegedly attempted suicide by consuming sleeping pills in the high security jail premises on Friday evening. The inmate, Naresh Solanki (24), was immediately rushed to the civil hospital where his condition is said to be out of danger.

The Sabarmati police said, around 5 pm, Solanki swallowed the pills prescribed to one of his fellow inmates. About an hour later, he fell semi-conscious and other inmates intimated the jail authorities.

"We are yet to record Solanki's statement, as we are awaiting permission from the doctor. It will be only after talking to him that we can ascertain the cause behind the incident. As of now, we are relying on what some of the inmates told us that Solanki accidentally swallowed the pills," said Sub-Inspector G B Vaghela.

This is the second such incident reported from the jail in a week. On October 31, a murder convict, Mayabhai Kapadbhai, had allegedly committed suicide by hanging himself in a jail lavatory. Investigation suggested that the suicide was a fallout of a court refusing to grant him furlough to celebrate Diwali with his family.

Heading: MGVCL’s kite twine excuse false, say Ambikanagar residents - Indian Express
Content:
For the second consecutive year, the state Forest Department has embarked on a tree plantation mission under the Centre's five-year Dashmool (ten roots) project. The drive has been launched as the Medicinal Plant Board, Government of India, sanctioned Rs 5 crore to encourage medicinal herbs plantation.

Ironically, even as the Department aims to create a market of medicinally important Dashmool concoction for pharmacists, the foresters do not have any account of phytochemical (chemical contents present in the plants) contents present in the roots of these herbs. The exact amount of phytochemical elements is important to show the quality standards of medicinal important herbs thereby facilitating to create an individual market of the product.

Responding to a query on the method undertaken to find out the exact phytochemical contents in the herb roots, R V Asari, Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forest, said: "The foresters don't have that information. It is the work of the pharmacists to find out the extent of medicinal contents in the plants." He added that the Forest Department's main aim is to popularise the raw materials of Dashmool among the forest dwellers.

Forest officials have been planting 10 medicinal plants whose roots have medicinal importance in the Valsad and Surat forest circles for the last one year. Interestingly, the basic initiatives that should be taken to create a market for the medicinal plants seem to be missing.

Seeking anonymity, some forest officials said that though the Dashmool project has been taken up, there is no phytochemical laboratory available with the Department as of now.

Refusing to comment on the availability of phytochemical laboratory, he said, "There should be initiatives to find out the compounds in the roots which are medicinally important. The institutes can approach the Forest Department on this issue."

He further said: "Ayurvedic scriptures show that Dashmool has medicinal importance and they are useful in toning systems." Asari said the project aims at availing raw materials of Dashmool in the forest areas for pharmaceutical companies. "We are conducting workshops to rope in more pharmacists in this project," he said.

Dashmool is an amalgam of roots of 10 different plants, used as an analgesic and also for treating migraine.

Heading: Education office receives 22 proposals for new schools - Indian Express
Content:
A day after over 100 refrigerators and 50 television sets burst due to high voltage supply in 274-odd households at the Ambikanagar Society in the Gotri area, beelines of residents were seen outside repair centres.

Residents said the Madhya Gujarat Vij Company Limited (MGVCL) authorities' claim that the incident was the fallout of a kite twine was false. "The excuse of kite twine is false. The electric poles in the area are in a bad state. Even as new electric meters are being installed, the wiring is very old," said Ambikanagar Housing Association secretary Bhagwandas Rana. He said the society, which mostly has middle class families, suffered a loss of nearly Rs 1.5 lakh.

Bakul Patel, a resident whose TV set and refrigerator got defunct on Thursday, said: "The incident occurred due to MGVCL's negligence. MGVCL authorities also admitted to this during our conversation with them."

Patel said the voltage was excessively high on Thursday, adding that MGVCL should have blocked the feeder line, which kept on functioning even as a repair work was on. This led to more damage, he added.

Society members have now met MGVCL authorities and have demanded installations of new wire system.

K I Dalwadi, Junior Engineer, Gotri zone, refused to comment on this issue.

Heading: City’s wi-fi networks now under police scanner - Indian Express
Content:
The district education office has received over 22 proposals for new schools in Vadodara district. While authorities feel that the number of applications to start the new schools is similar to last year, they are waiting for the State Secondary Education Board to give the green signal.

"Almost similar numbers of proposals were submitted to the board last year, out of which 12 were sanctioned," said R K Patel, District Education Officer (DEO). The Board has received application for new schools in Gujarati, English and Hindi medium of education in the city and the rural areas.

District Primary Education Officer (DPEO) Manilal Bhusara said the process is yet to start for the primary schools. "We generally start getting the applications by January. Keeping intact the criteria, we mostly sanction all of them. We had around 20 primary schools that were given sanction last year," he said.

The primary education board looks into the criteria for sanction, including experience in managing schools, teaching staff, permission for land, among others.

Bhusara said: "The processing is done here, and many a times the rejected candidate directly approaches the primary education board for the sanction. This time too, there are two to three such proposals from the previous year, which will be directly applying to the centre after fulfilling the criteria."

Heading: Reasons galore for ban on Friday flea market - Indian Express
Content:
The city's wireless-fidelity networks are now under the scanner of the police departments, after US national Kenneth Haywood's Internet access was hacked into in Mumbai for sending a terror mail after the July 26 Ahmedabad blasts.

The police have now issued notices to wi-fi service providers in the city.

Newsline visited two such hotspots in the city that offer these services to the customers.

Aziz Ahmed, Front Office Manager, Hotel Surya Palace, said they have stopped giving the service to outside visitors. "We have just restricted our services to the guests in the hotel and we issue specific passwords to them," said Ahmed. He said that immediately after the blasts, the hotel had stopped providing the services to visitors who were not staying in their premises.

As per the recent notice issued by the Vadodara police, the records of the users have to be submitted every week to the local police station. "Right after the blasts, notices were issued to all Internet service providers. Since most of them are in the Sayajigunj area, we keep checking their records off and on. For wi-fi networks also, we are now checking their records and are insisting on regular updates," said Sayaji Inspector D L Zala.

Saurav Chaudhary, Manager, Ginger Hotel, said that as per the regulations, they are giving these services to those people who register with them with their server and get their passwords. "We are not giving free service. The client has to register with us," he said.

Sunny Vaghela, a hacker who has been aiding the police across the states in monitoring terrorism, said that wi-fi networks are the most susceptible to hacking, as many of these services do not keep a log of the users (basically a unique number for every new computer that logs on to the wi-fi network).

"Hacking wi-fi networks is easy, therefore what the police can do here is to check if the log data of the servers are intact or not," he said.

Heading: 7 killed, 8 injured in road mishap - Indian Express
Content:
The civic authorities and the city police might have tightened security due to the heightened threat perception after the Ahmedabad bomb blasts, but the casualty has been the weekly flea market, a monumental part of the city's living heritage.

Jumma Bazaar, or Shukarvaari, as Vadodara's Friday flea market in the Walled City area is called, has suddenly been banned by both the Vadodara Municipal Corporation and the police, snatching away the means of livelihood for many.

Newsline begins a series looking at what is happening to traditional market places in the city and how it impacts the life of Barodians.

The vadodara police have a simple rationale to close down the Shukarvaari Bazaar on the Fatehpura stretch that sits every Friday — to solve the city's traffic problems.

According to Joint Commissioner of Police Pravin Sinha, the market was blocking traffic in the area and did not have any authorisation from the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC).

The police also say that articles sold in this temporary market include stolen ones, yet another reason to close it down.

They said there has been an increase in the number of thefts in the area from where the vendors operate. They even surmised that it could be the handiwork of some vendors.

Inspector B N Chawda of the City police said many vendors have a network with small-time criminals and thieves in Mumbai in around the Chembur and Dharavi areas, who act as suppliers to the middlemen who, in turn, sell items to these vendors.

"Many residents in Fatehpura have said that some of the vendors in the area engage in thefts, as there is no regulating authority on the nature of goods being sold here and how they might have been acquired. Of late, the market has become a hub for stolen goods," he said.

The police also said that there have been cases of eve teasing and minor clashes as well, something the vendors have denied outright.

On Friday, about 100 protestors gathered near the Champaner Gate to oppose the ban on the Shukarvaari Bazaar.

The police arrested six protestors including two women vendors and the former Vadodara president of the Janata Dal (Secular), Motilal Kanojia, in this regard.

Besides Kanojia, the others arrested include Jagdish Prajapati, Ganesh Rajput, Master Vishandas Surtani, Laxmi Vaghela, and Saraswati Vaghri.

In the morning, while some policemen were seen picking up a 12-year-old boy and later releasing him after Inspector Chawda intervened, some of the protestors filled the police van themselves.

The police said the protestors had unlawfully assembled and had tried to prevent them from carrying out their duty.

They were booked under Sections 133, 504, 168 and 159 of the Indian Penal Code.

Around 9 am, at least 25 women vendors surrounded Chawda and demanded the immediate release of the protestors.

Heading: Gujarat Maritime Board in Texas Treasure hunt - Indian Express
Content:
As many as seven people died and eight others were severely injured when their public transport vehicle collided with a parked truck near Tankara in Rajkot district in the early hours of Friday.

The accident occurred around 4.30 am when the victims were on their way to Rajkot from Morbi.

Preliminary investigation by the Rajkot Rural police revealed that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver who reportedly fell asleep on the steering wheel.

The Tankara police said that after colliding with the rear side of the truck, the vehicle fell into a nearby pit. They said, one of the injured, who was travelling with her sister, informed them about the incident through a cellphone.

A crane was pressed into service to pull out the vehicle from the pit and extricate the bodies. With the help of the villagers, they shifted the injured to hospitals in Morbi and Rajkot.

The Tankara police further said the truck driver had parked his vehicle with the support of a jack and had gone to Morbi to fix a flat tyre. The cleaner was resting inside the truck when the accident occurred. The police have begun procedures to identify the deceased and have learnt that the passengers belonged to Rajkot, Morbi and Rajasthan.

A police officer said: "It was a horrible sight. Several bodies were stuck inside the vehicle. Some were dismembered."

The police said six people died on the spot while one was declared dead on arrival at a hospital in Morbi. The officer said most of the bodies have been found in a mutilated condition, which has made the identification task difficult.

Heading: Forest officials accused of harassment by Dangs tribals - Indian Express
Content:
A team from the Economic Development Cell of the Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB) has carried out an inspection of the casino cruise Texas Treasure with an intention to buy and refit the vessel as a floating restaurant to promote tourism in the state. Meanwhile, foreign buyers are also known to be in the fray.

The luxury liner, which was converted to a casino cruise in 1998, has been anchored at plot number 11 of Alang Breaking Yard. Although the ship was in good condition, it was sold off to Alang breaker, Samir Bhimani, by the US owners following a dispute with its operators.

The state government, given the good condition of the vessel, has been mulling over the possibility of re-floating it as a restaurant off the Saurashtra coast, probably off Ahmedpur-Mandvi beach.

A team of GMB led by a senior officer, V Devulkar, inspected the hull and engine of the ship. It also checked for certificates and all papers and explored the feasibility of re-floating the vessel. The team is expected to submit its report to the GMB.

Bhimani, who has priced the ship at nearly Rs 25 crore, has been expecting a team of Singaporean buyers on Saturday. "Specific International Group from Singapore will visit tomorrow. Star Cruise and Jumera Group from Dubai have also expressed interest," he said.

This is perhaps for the first time in the history of Alang that any ship waiting to be scrapped is attracting buyers with re-floating plans. "It is not without reason. The cruise, with a capacity of over 2,300 passengers, offers all luxury and comfort with a special casino. Besides, it is still fit to float for another 10 years," Bhimani said.

Heading: Unclaimed bags near Modi’s near Modi’s residence keep cops on toes - Indian Express
Content:
Tribals from several villages in the Dangs district have been complaining of harassment and destruction of their livelihood by foresters. In a complaint lodged with Ahwa Sub Divisional Office recently, tribals from several villages have alleged that their standing crops have been destroyed by foresters.

Levelling allegations of excesses, Gadar Ramubhai Rajubhai and 15 other tribals of Dabhas village said that their standing crops were completely destroyed by the forest beat guards on October 14. In their complaint, they said that farming was the only source of income for them and nothing was left now.

Rakmaben Rameshbhai and half a dozen other tribals of Bhapkal village also alleged that foresters destroyed the standing crops in the village.

As many as 80 files from the claimants for tribal land were also allegedly reduced to ash by some miscreants when they set the hut belonging to one Mangalbhai Amirbhai of Mokhamal village, afire.

Mangalbhai, who is the president of the Forest Rights Committee formed under the Forest Rights Act of 2006, suspected the hand of some forest beat guards and members of the parallel forest committee formed by the Forest Department.

Xavier's Manjooran, whose Adivasi Mahasabha is working among adivasis and assisting the formation of forest committees by involving village panchayats, alleged that foresters, besides harassing the tribals and destroying their livelihood, were also creating division among tribals by forming their own committees.

Referring to Forest Rights Act of 2006, he said that forest committees must be formed by the village panchayats without involving the Forest Department, but the latter were forming their own committees without involving village panchayats with a view to create fissures among tribals.

The forest officials have, however, denied the allegations. District Forest Officer (South Dangs) Bharatsinh Vaghela said that the department had removed encroachments on forest land done after December 13, 2005, the last date for considering claims of the tribals over forestland. He said that the department was allowing cultivation on the land in possession of the tribals prior to December 13, 2005 but was removing the encroachments after that date.

Vaghela categorically denied the allegations pertaining to torching of files for land claims of tribals. "These allegations appear to be motivated by ulterior objectives," he said. But he also added that these allegations are under investigation.

Heading: Surat police get custody of Ahmedabad blasts accused - Indian Express
Content:
The gandhinagar police were on their toes on Thursday when they were informed about an unclaimed travel bag and suitcase near the official residence of Chief Minister Narendra Modi.

Police teams along with experts from the Bomb Disposal Squad and the Dog Squad were immediately rushed to the site, when the Sector 21 police were intimated about "some objects" lying unclaimed near circle 30 on Akshardham Road. The site is barely a few metres from the campus wall of the CM's residence in the Mantri Vistar area in Gandhinagar.

The traffic on the road was stopped as BDS personnel carefully opened the suitcase and the bag after taking them to an open field near the site. A check revealed only some clothes.

Inspector G H Algotar of Sector 21 police said: "It seems that someone must have flicked the suitcase and the travel bag from somewhere in the city and must have dumped them here while fleeing or after finding no valuables inside them. It can also be a prank by some miscreants."

Meanwhile, the Gandhinagar police have made a station diary entry about the incident and are trying to locate the owner (s) of the suitcase and the bag, which are lying at the sector 21 police station at present.

Heading: Govt dons ESMA shield to battle LPG dealers - Indian Express
Content:
The surat police on Friday took over the custody of Sajid Mansuri, Abu Bashar and Tanveer Pathan for their suspected role in planting of bombs here.

Mansuri and Abu Bashar were earlier in the custody of Ahmedabad police for their alleged role in the Ahmedabad serial blasts.

The three were produced before the special court in Ahmedabad today, which ordered them to four days in remand with the Surat Crime Branch.

Inspector P M Parmar (Crime Branch) said: "We have arrested them in connection with the recovery of the live bomb from the City light area in Surat. Mansuri was declared wanted by the Surat police for the last seven years. During his visit to Surat city, he introduced Kayamuddin to Tanveer to execute the plan of blasting the bombs."

The Special Investigation Team (SIT) had arrested Tanveer and Zahir Patel for their alleged role in locating the places where the bombs were to be planted.

The Surat police had recovered 29 live bombs across the city during and in the days following the Ahmedabad blasts, which had failed to go off.

The police had recovered the bombs with the help of local people and later defused them.

The first live bomb was found from Traffic Island opposite Nupur Hospital in the City light area and the complaint was registered with the Surat Crime Branch.

Heading: Central team conducts feasibility survey for Rajkot airport expansion - Indian Express
Content:
Cooking gas distributors across the state have resolved to go on an indefinite strike from November 10

With LPG dealers across the state having resolved to go on an indefinite strike from November 10, the government has decided to invoke the provisions of Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) to deal with the situation with an iron hand.

"The government will not tolerate any attempt by LPG dealers to disrupt the supply of cooking gas cylinders in the state. We will not hesitate to use ESMA if they resort to strike from November 10. There are provisions in the ESMA to issue non-bailable arrest warrants against those who resort to and instigate strike disrupting supply of essential services," said Principal Secretary (Food and Civil Supplies) Rajesh Kishore.

Kishore told Newsline on Friday that the government has been inviting the representatives of LPG dealers for talks to find an amicable solution to their demand for withdrawing the licence system. But they are not prepared to sit across the table and thrash out the issue, he said.

Justifying the licencing system, he said it was mandatory for LPG dealers to obtain a licence under the Gujarat Essential Commodities (Licensing Control and Stock Limit) Order, 1981, which any state is empowered to formulate under the Central Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

The Gujarat government has introduced the licencing system for LPG distributors to curb the black marketing of domestic gas cylinders and check the increasing incidents of harassment of customers by LPG dealers and their staff. "We had done away with the licencing system last year. But, the government was constrained to reintroduce it two months after we started receiving complaints of black marketing and bad behaviour of distributors towards customers," Kishore said.

The LPG dealers want to operate under the Control Order of the Union Petroleum Ministry, where they are not required to obtain a licence. This apparently dilutes the role of the state in dealing with irregularities often committed by LPG distributors. Hence, this licencing system introduced under the State Control Order, explained a senior Civil Supplies official.

The official claimed that the Gujarat unit of the All India LPG Distributors' Federation will have to eat its words and withdraw the call for an indefinite strike, once the department issues orders invoking ESMA provisions against the protestors. "In fact, about 100 of the total 520 LPG dealers across the state have communicated to district collectors that they would not join the strike," he said.

Throughout the day, officials in the Civil Supplies Department were seen busy chalking out a counter strategy and making preparations to meet the situation that may arise out of the impending state-wide indefinite strike by the LPG distributors.

"There is no need to panic. We have already instructed the collectors and the district supplies officers to work out alternate plans to ensure a smooth supply of LPG cylinders in their respective areas. For this, we have also decided to put to use the existing infrastructure of the State Civil Supplies Corporation, besides requisitioning the services of owners of over 16,000 fair price shops (FPS) and 6,000 kerosene licence holders to meet the situation," said a senior official.

Surat
Surat District Supply Officer Sanjay Modi said they have identified 32 Fair Price Shops and 42 other shops to deliver LPG cylinders if dealers go on strike. The civic authorities have also identified twenty FPS in the district so that rural consumers are not affected adversely.

Ahmedabad
Ahmedabad District Supply Officer (DSO) V N Shah said that an LPG centre will start functioning from November 10 at each taluka headquarter under a deputy mamlatdar (civil supplies). Consumers will be given LPG cylinders on a 'cash and carry' basis.Gujarat LPG Dealers' Association president P M Patel, however, said that the strike will begin irrespective of ESMA if their demands are not met.

Vadodara
The district administration on Friday held a meeting with the agitating LPG dealers and asked them not to go on strike, as it would be illegal under ESMA. District Collector Vijay Nehra said the supply would be unaffected should there be a strike, as adequate provisions have been made.

Rajkot
The Rajkot district administration has made a contingency plan to deal with the strike, said Rajkot District Collector H S Patel. The distribution of LPG cylinders will be looked at by the administration with the help of oil companies, he said. "Temporary outlets will be opened at ration shop premises for the convenience of the consumers in the rural areas," said Patel. He said the collectorate will also take help of the Railway Welfare Board and the Police Welfare Board for the distribution. The collector said that a meeting of 140 dealers was called on Friday and they were also warned about the cancellation of their licences should they strike.

Heading: ISRO set to launch country’s first indigenous geomatics software - Indian Express
Content:
A team of the Civil Aviation Department, Government of India, conducted a feasibility survey of three selected places for the proposed expansion of the Rajkot airport on Friday. The international standard airport is likely to be built on a Public-Private Partnership basis.

Rajkot District Collector H S Patel said, "A team led by the civil aviation director checked the feasibility of the project." The three sties are Parapipaliya, Nakarwadi and a location near National Highway 8 B.

The expansion plan has been proposed in view of the future development of the city, as the existing airport on the Jamnagar Road can handle only one Airbus at a time.

Expansion of the same site has also been into consideration. For this purpose, the Civil Aviation Department will have to acquire land from the Indian Railways, which has its staff quarters there. The Indian Railways has shown willingness to transfer 21 acres of land provided it gets land for quarters at some other place.

At present, three flights — two by Jet Airways and one by Indian — operate from Rajkot. They are between Rajkot and Mumbai.

Heading: Siblings believe — ‘yes, she can’ make the world a better place - Indian Express
Content:
Developed by ISRO's Ahmedabad centre, new software to be more compatible with Indian satellites and will cut costs

This is an initiative that could spell a huge technological leap for the country besides saving hundreds of crores in foreign exchange. ISRO is about to launch the country's first comprehensive indigenous software for geomatics — 'Indigenous GIS and IP Software' or IGIS. With this, India is poised to become totally self-reliant in the software component of the Geospatial industry which accounted for nearly Rs 950 million in 2006-07, with much of it going to foreign players like ESRI, AutoDesk, Bentley Systems, Leica Geosystems, InterGraph and PCI Geomatics.

IGIS will be installed in all ISRO remote sensing centres resulting in huge cost savings.

The IGIS software has been developed by ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad along with its J-V geomatics technology partner Scanpoint Geomatics Limited (SGL), an Ahmedabad-based public limited company. It is a seamless Geomatics application, which includes Geographical Information System (GIS), Image Processing with integration with real time information using GPS.

R R Navalkund, Director, SAC said, IGIS will benefit India's research and academic institutions as the pricing of the software will be highly competitive.

Chirag Soni, Technical Director, SGL, said: "ISRO provided the domain expertise while we provided the development expertise to come up with IGIS. Along with the added advantage of having both GIS Processing and Image Processing applications, IGIS will be more compatible to Indian satellites."

An ISRO team member said all preliminary technical evaluation of the software has been very encouraging. "For sometime, ISRO has not purchased geomatics software from any foreign player and the stage is set for achieving self-reliance in every space application," he added.

ISRO sources revealed that Chairman G Madhavan Nair was given a presentation by the IGIS team on his recent visit to SAC this week, adding that the commercial launch will take place any time in December.

SGL Managing Director Ramesh Sojitra, said: "The idea is to have a comprehensive, totally Indian, geomatics application software to geographically visualise both the Raster and Vector data, manipulate the data for standard analysis as well as create maps and images."

He said to work on the pricing issue and to find a suitable Indian name for the software, the IGIS core team will meet tentatively on the 24th and 25th of this month.

Heading: Ahmedabad-based painter brings Obama, Gandhi on same canvas - Indian Express
Content:
Siblings of Sonal Shah (40), who is all geared up to work as an advisor to Barack Obama, believe she can help make the world a better place.

Daughter of Gujarati emigrant Ramesh Shah, Sonal was born in Mumbai and had moved to USA with her family in the early 70s. Before her current appointment, Sonal was working in the US on a global development strategy for Google. Earlier, she has also served as vice president at Goldman Sachs besides co-founding Indicorps, an NGO offering one-year fellowships for Americans of Indian origin to work on specific development projects in India.

After her coursework at the University of Chicago (B.A.), the London School of Economics, and Duke University (M.A.), Sonal worked with the United States Department of Treasury for over seven years on a variety of issues and regions.

Sonal's younger sister, Roopal, and younger brother, Anand, run Indicorps in India. Her parents live in Houston, Texas, where her father is a financial advisor.

Roopal told Newsline: "Sonal has the unique opportunity to serve as a member of Barack Obama's transition team and to make a positive impact on America and the larger world community."

Obama, she feels, stresses on the spirit of service and sacrifice. "Sonal believes strongly in these values, which is why she co-founded Indicorps—to help Indians reconnect with India through service. Obama's transition team is another way for her to give back in service and to resonate the message "yes, we can."

Anand is assisting Piramal Foundation with a new social enterprise named Sarvajal, designed to bring affordable clean drinking water within reach of the greater Indian population.

Heading: Village celebrates Sonal Shah’s appointment as US Presidential advisor - Indian Express
Content:
Ahmedabad-based artist Aijaz Saiyed, who has made two paintings of Barack Obama along with Mahatma Gandhi, is planning to send them to the US President-elect as a goodwill gesture on his win in the presidential elections.

Saiyed, who works with the Directorate of Census Operations in Ahmedabad as an artist, had made the paintings on the eve of the elections.

Saiyed told Newsline: "Obama is quite inspired by the thoughts of Mahatma Gandhi, and the influence was very much evident in his speeches. Apart from that, Gandhi's principles are very much relevant in the present world where terrorism is spreading its roots. So, I made the paintings wherein Gandhi is blessing Obama to spread the message of peace."

On his plans to gift Obama the paintings, Saiyed said he would try to send them through the Government of India.

Heading: Sajjanpur rape and  murder case: Cong, MGJP leaders visit victim’s family - Indian Express
Content:
Gabat is a tiny village in Sabarkantha district. It has suddenly captured public attention after the US Presidential election. The reason: President-elect Barack Obama has appointed Sonal Shah, originally a native of Gabat village, as one of his advisors.

The news has driven the people of the village to a state of Titanic exultation —they have been bursting crackers, and singing and dancing to celebrate Shah's victory. People have also gone nostalgic about the old memories of Sonal when she lived in the village with her family until she was six.

Mukundchandra Shah, Sonal's uncle, who still lives in the village, said: "Since Friday, we are trying to congratulate her over the phone, but in vain, as the phone has been busy all through. Ultimately, we called up my brother, Dineshbhai, to convey our wishes. In our village, people have almost gone mad over the news. In less than 24 hours, the village youths have burst crackers worth over Rs 1,000."

According to Shah, Sonal was born in Mumbai but lived in the village till the age of six. She did her kindergarten in the village school.

Even village authorities are planning to celebrate Sonal's success by organising a rally in her honour in the village.

Deputy Sarpanch Ranjitsinh Zala said: "It is a matter of pride for our village that a girl from here has been so successful that the American President has appointed her as his advisor. We are organising a grand rally in the village to celebrate her success."

Village Talati Sansinh Zala, said: "The villagers are celebrating the occasion by distributing sweets among themselves. A number of media persons have also visited the village."

Heading: Three held for ‘vandalising’ Hanuman idol - Indian Express
Content:
Umiya Sena to go on indefinite fast from Sunday to protest against police's 'inability'

The rape and murder of a mentally challenged teenaged girl at Sajjanpur village of Tankara taluka in Rajkot seems to be getting politicised with leaders from the Congress and Maha Gujarat Janta Party paying visits to the deceased's family on Friday.

This comes after the Patels in the village launched an agitation against local BJP MLA Mohan Kundariya for the 'failure of administration' in arresting the culprits.

Jasdan Congress MLA and Saurashtra in-charge Kunwarji Bawadia visited the family of the 19-year-old girl who was found raped and murdered in the outskirt of the village over three weeks ago.

Hours after his visit, former state home minister and president of Maha Gujarat Janta Party Gordhan Zadaphia also met the family members. However, both the leaders denied that it was a politically motivated visit. "We have come to extend our support. There's nothing political about it," said Bawadia.

Zadafia said: "We would take up the issue with the government to make sure that justice is done to the family." Siddharth Parmar, secretary, Maha Gujarat Janta Party, said the police "have lost their morale" under the Narendra Modi government , which is leading to such incidents.

The police have so far detained seven men in connection with the case. "The detentions have been made on the basis of suspicion. No substantial evidence or clue has been found so far," said a Tankara police official.

The Umiya Sena has, meanwhile, announced to go on an indefinite fast from Sunday to protest police's inability in arresting the accused. The group mainly comprises Kadva Patels, who are traditionally supporters of the BJP. Kundaria himself is a Kadva Patel.

The agitation has refreshed the memory of Chandni rape and murder case, wherein a minor girl from Rajkot was raped and murdered at Datar Hill in Junagadh in 2007.

The incident had led to a widespread protests by the kolis against the Modi government, which left the koli leaders from the region divided on the party lines.

Heading: CAB to fete Sourav on December 7 - Indian Express
Content:
The Songadh police have arrested three Christians for allegedly damaging an idol of Hanuman at a temple in Songadh taluka.

A complaint in this connection was lodged with the Sonagadh police station by the temple priest.

Hindu activists now plan to organise a maha aarti at the Hanuman Temple in Kanara village on Saturday.

The police said the situation is under control as adequate personnel have been deployed in the village

According to the police, Lakha Gamit, a resident of

Kanara village in Songadh taluka had constructed the temple on his agricultural field on the outskirts of the village.

On Wednesday morning, he found the head of the idol damaged. He also found some stones lying in the temple premises. After the incident, Gamit, who is also the head priest, informed the village panchayat and later lodged a police complaint.

In his complaint, Gamit accused Keshya Gamit, Arvind Gamit, Suresh Gamit, all residents of Kanara village, of damaging the idol.

On the basis of the complaint, the police arrested the accused on Thursday.

Senior officers immediately rushed to the spot after learning about the incident and pacified the villagers.

Tapi Superintendent of Police P N Patel said: "The village has Christian and Hindu population. Lakhabhai had a conflict with Keshya, Arvind and Suresh a couple of months ago and he suspects their involvement in the crime."

He added: "We have found that the stones, which hit the idol, were thrown from a distance. We have arrested them and are investigating the case further. We have deployed our staff at Kanara village for the maha aarti on Saturday."

Heading: Deep, Vignesh fined by ICL committee - Indian Express
Content:
The Cricket Association of Bengal will felicitate Sourav Ganguly on December 7 at the Eden Gardens. Though the details of the function are yet to be finalised, the CAB is contemplating it on a grand scale. That the state association will felicitate Sourav was already reported in this daily.

CAB president Jagmohan Dalmiya wanted the southpaw to reconsider his decision though. "We had waited till the last minute and hoped that Sourav would reconsider his decision to retire from international cricket. But during the function at Nagpur yesterday, we saw that he had firmed up his mind. We fully respect his decision and the CAB would felicitate him in a befitting manner," Dalmiya said. He added: "Sourav has continued to inspire and enthrall throughout his long years in international cricket and to win laurels for the nation with amazing alacrity. The CAB, of which he is an integral part, would take this opportunity to honour his contribution."

Heading: Mahindra show promise and profligacy - Indian Express
Content:
The disciplinary committee of the Indian Cricket League (ICL) today took strong action against the two erring players Deep Dasgupta and Ganapathi Vignesh of Royal Bengal Tigers and Chennai Superstars respectively for their involvement in an on-field altercation during their match in the ongoing ICL 20s Indian Championship held at Panchkula on Tuesday. Both the players were docked half their monthly fee as penalty.

"The 30th match of the ICL 20s Indian Championship between Royal Bengal Tigers and Chennai Superstars played on November 4 at Panchkula, saw the two players, Deep Dasgupta of Royal Bengal Tigers and G Vignesh of Chennai Superstars involve in a physical altercation. The match referee Mr Ajit Wadekar took notice of the incident and called for a report from the umpires. Mr Wadekar subsequently summoned the two players with their respective coaches and captains, along with the three umpires for a detailed inquiry on Wednesday.

"Based on his findings, Mr Wadekar imposed a fine, on both of them, amounting to 50 per cent of their monthly fees," said a statement released by the tournament director Kiran More.

Royal Bengal Tigers stakeholder Mithun Chakraborty accepted the decision while urging their opponents not to provoke the Royal Bengal Tigers.

"All players should respect and uphold the spirit of the game. I had been closely following the match and can say that Deep was provoked. It is my opinion that not only the offender but also the conspirator is equally guilty. I am greatly pleased that the ICL disciplinary committee has taken a similar view towards the incident and penalised both players involved, equally. Finally I would like to tell all the other teams — don't provoke the Royal Bengal Tigers or be prepared to face the consequences."

Heading: Govt takes U-turn, says no evidence against accused - Indian Express
Content:
Mahindra United, despite finishing as the stronger team on the night, failed to return with full points in their I-League away match against East Bengal at Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK) on Friday. The 1-1 draw saw the Mumbai outfit move to seven points from as many outings, while East Bengal moved to nine points.

Substitute Paresh Shivalkar scored for Mahindra in the 58th minute only to see Sunil Chhetri negating the advantage three minutes later.

Shivalkar's goal was the result of a lovely off-the-mark manoeuvring as he came from behind to tap home an Edeh Chidi pass. East Bengal defence was disorganised and failed to spot Shivalkar.

East Bengal's goal was set up by Yusif Yakubu who collected a Rahim Nabi through pass just outside the box, created space for Chhetri with a brilliant first touch and timed the release perfectly. Chhetri too was up to the task and scored with a left-footer from a difficult angle.

The goal apart, the red-and-golds, however, had very little to show for, especially in the first half.

They lacked any constructive midfield play, couldn't initiate attacks through the flanks. These rendered Yakubu and Chhetri ineffective upfront.

The visitors, on the other hand, were very compact and pressed the hosts back to the wall with a series of raids. They must rue the lost chances.

India international Sushil Kumar Singh missed a sitter in the 23rd minute. Then Chidi, who otherwise had an excellent game, failed to convert a Sushant Matthew pass from inside the box in the 28th minute. Sushil once again came close to scoring in the 30th minute, but his sharp header from six yards was brilliantly saved by East Bengal custodian Subrata Paul.

The red-and-golds changed their strategy in the second half dropping Yakubu to a withdrawn position. It worked. Yakubu started to conduct the show with his excellent passing skill, and the off-the-ball play in the attacking-third got better.

Chhetri was unlucky not to score in the 52nd minute as his lob from a Yakubu pass rebounded off the crosspiece. A few minutes later, Nabi bungled another opportunity from close range.

Surprisingly, East Bengal surrendered the initiative after the eqauliser and allowed their opponent to come back into the match.

Mahindra accepted the favour and went into attack mode. East Bengal defence looked insecured with Nirmal Chhetri making lots of mistakes. Veteran Suley Musah, however, had a good game. Also, Mahindra strikers lacked sharpness in the penetrative zone.

Heading: Bengal’s lost Nano India’s showpiece in Chile, Peru - Indian Express
Content:
The state government admitted on Friday that the West Midnapore police could not find any evidence against the three arrested students of Lalgarh — accused of Salboni blasts.

The West Midnapore police had arrested the three students — Gautam Patro,Budhadev Patro and Eben Murmu — from Lalgarh on Sunday and the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) court had remanded them in police custody for ten days on Tuesday.

Public prosecutor Ardhendu Saha did not oppose the bail petitions moved by the trio before the cjm court in the district. Saha admitted before the court that the police had arrested them, suspecting their involvement in the blasts. But no evidence was found against them. Subsequently, the court granted them bail.

Home Secretary Ashok Mohan Chakrabarty, however said the students have already been interrogated in the custody and the police felt further remand was not required. "Director General of Police A B Vohra has instructed the police not to harass innocent villagers," he added.

Chakrabarty, however, added: "It is difficult to avoid harassment of the villagers during raids but local police has been instructed to follow the directives."

The home secretary also said the DGP had submitted an interim report on Tuesday on the Salboni blasts, which did not hold any officer responsible for the blast. "Additional Director General (CID) will submit an interim report next week on the security lapses during the chief minister's visit to Salboni," he added.

In a related development, a team of Central Forensic Laboratory(CFL) visited the blast site in Salboni on Friday. The team took soil samples, collected by the district police.

The CFL will test the samples to determine the kind of explosive used in the

landmines.

Heading: Buddha blames Tata exit on Mamata - Indian Express
Content:
Nano, the small car by the Tatas, will be showcased at the India Show 2009 to be held in Santiago and at the Buyer Seller Meet in Peru.

The announcement was made on Friday at a meeting organised by the Bengal National Chamber of Commerce, India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO).

According to ITPO, the purpose of holding the India Show in Chile and Peru is to tap their unexplored automobile markets.

"Tata Motors will display Nano in both Santiago and Peru shows," said the ITPO Executive Director, Rajiv Yadav.

"The exclusive India Show is meant to tap new overseas markets. It will highlight the potential of Indian industries," said Yadav.

The Santiago show, which is to be held from March 18 to March 21, is expected to draw huge crowds. Companies like Reliance, Tata Motors, Bombay Dying, Wipro, Infosys and TCS have already confirmed their participation.

As part of the government's initiative, the agency has been organising a number of exclusive trade shows in various Latin American countries.

Last year, the India Show was held in Brazil, in which 14 Indian companies had participated.

In its effort to address environment and energy-related issues, the ITPO will also organise Envirotech and Energytech exhibitions at Pragati Maidan in New Delhi from December 14 to December 17.

Heading: Bureaucrat’s cash goes missing from Thai Airways flight - Indian Express
Content: Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattcharjee has directly blamed the Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee for the Tata exit from Singur. "They (the Tata Motors) had completed 85 per cent of the work in Singur. The Trinamool is solely responsible for this (Tata's pullout)," he sad. "The Tata pullout in the face of irresponsible and destructive agitation by the Opposition will always be marked as a big loss for industrialisation process of the state," he said. In an interview with the party organ Ganashakti, CM reiterated that the land in Singur will be used only for industry.

Heading: Empty classrooms greet NBA team at BESU - Indian Express
Content:
A top bureaucrat in the state government allegedly lost nearly Rs 50,000 while on an official trip to Tokyo to attend a conference of the Asian Development Bank.

The Principal Secretary of the Environment Department, ML Meena, left the city on November 1 for Tokyo via Bangkok on a Thai Airways flight.

"I was carrying about Rs 10,000 and $700 in cash, which I had kept in a bag," said Meena. However, according to the principal secretary, he discovered the money was missing from his luggage after he reached Tokyo.

"I was shocked to see that the cash was missing from my bag, but the lock was not tampered with," said Meena.

After landing in the city on Tuesday night, Meena lodged an FIR with the airport police station.

Since Air India is the official handling agent for Thai Airways in Kolkata, the airlines officials were quick to point out a few technical errors on the part of the bureaucrat.

"If he was carrying the cash in a registered baggage, he should have declared it with the airlines. Moreover, he was traveling via Bangkok and the money could have been stolen anywhere. The safety strap on the luggage was also intact," said an Air India official.

Officers at the airport police station confirmed that Meena had lodged an FIR on Tuesday. "We have forwarded a request to Air India and the airlines officials have assured us their full cooperation in investigating the case," a police officer said.

Heading: Manipur extortion module busted, 8 held - Indian Express
Content:
With the Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) authorities suspending undergraduate classes a day earlier, empty classrooms, laboratories and workshops greeted the 14 members of National Board of Accreditation (NBA) team, who were on a visit to the university to conduct an inspection on Friday.

The NBA team, headed by Prof N R Dave, inspected the  infrastructure of the university like its libraries, workshops, auditoriums and hostels. Later, the team surveyed every department and interacted with the faculty members. However, the team couldn't find any undergraduate students in the classrooms.

With the team expressing its desire to watch a cultural programme, the authorities had to ask students residing in the nearby areas to perform in the evening.

"The NBA team interacts with students to get feedback on teaching-learning process at universities. This time, however, this will not be possible. We do not know how the team is going to react over this issue," said a teacher.

On Saturday, the inspection team is scheduled to interact with the alumni of the university and various representatives of the companies hiring students.

"NBA accreditation is like an audit for technical universities. It is necessary for students opting for higher studies as well as jobs abroad. Funds for the Technical Education Quality Improvement Plan are also given to only those institutes that have NBA accredition," said registrar Biman Bandopadhyay.

In the last accreditation, the university had scored less than 750 points on a scale of 1,000 and was given an accreditation for three years.

Even as the NBA team inspected the university, eight students arrested by the police in connection with Thursday's violence at the campus were produced in the Howrah court and remanded in judicial custody till November 11.

Heading: NGO demands compensation from Tatas for pullout - Indian Express
Content:
In a joint operation, the Special Task Force of the Kolkata police and the Eastern Command's military intelligence unit arrested eight alleged militants from Manipur. They included senior members of militant outfits, the People's Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak (PREPAK) and the People's Revolutionary Army (PLA).

Additional Commissioner of Police Rajiv Kumar, who heads the STF, said: "They were arrested from an auction house, Parekh House on Lenin Sarani near Jyoti Cinema on Friday, where an auction was in progress."

He added: "We have informed the Manipur police and are awaiting information from them. Only then we can claim that the arrested persons are militants."

Police sources said the arrests are a major setback for extortion modules of Manipur militant groups operating in the city.

Sources said those arrested included PREPAK's lieutenant K Kanta Singh and member of its finance department Achom Jagat Singh, and PLA's finance department member M Chittaranjan Singh. They were present at the auction of old vehicles of the Border Road Task Force (BRTF) deployed in Manipur, to extort bidders from Manipur.

A cash amount of Rs 15 lakh was also recovered from them.

"A group of nearly 15 Manipuri militants had come to Kolkata in response to an open tender from the BRTF for auctioning old vehicles worth crores of rupees. The militants usually operate in two modules. The first actually participates in the bidding. The other waits on the sidelines for the bidding to finish and then extorts at least 20 per cent of the final bid amount from the bidders," said STF sources.

"Both the PREPAK members belong to its "Shanti" faction. They have recently rechristened their faction as the United People's Liberation of Kangleipak (UPLK) and Kanta Singh is one of its founder-members," STF sources said. They added that the militants were living mostly in Madhyamgram in North 24 Parganas, close to the Dum Dum Airport. Chittaranjan Singh was staying in Room No 312 of the Manipur Bhawan on Rowland Road, sources said, adding that a team has been dispatched to Madhyamgram to conduct further raids.

The background of the five others, Chirom Iboyaima Singh, L C Deben Singh, Soram Tomba Singh, Koijam Ibomcha Singh, is yet to be confirmed but the security forces believe that they belong to the UPLK.

Their network is so wide that they track every tender and deal originating from Manipur and extort bidders, they added. Intelligence sources claim that similar extortion modules existed in Shillong, where Assam Rifles auctions are held; New Delhi, where Ministry of Home Affairs deals related to Manipur are finalised and Guwahati, the transit point to Manipur.

Heading: Morcha asks Tamang to quit politics - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another case regarding the small car factory in Singur, a Delhi-based NGO — Human Rights Law Network — has filed a PIL on Friday in the Supreme Court.

The NGO filed the petition seeking an order that Tata Motors should pay compensation to the state government and West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation, as the government had to face huge losses due to the pullout.

The state government had acquired 997.11 acres for setting up the Tata small car plant for Rs 119 crore. According to the NGO, there is a legal compulsion for the Tatas to pay the compensation to the state government and WBIDC to cover the losses.

A senior counsel of the state government said that the Supreme Court has directed the state government last week to file an affidavit regarding its stand on the return of land to the farmers. Now, the state government is preparing its reply according to the direction of the Apex Court.

In another development, Tata Motors filed a fresh petition in the Supreme Court for withdrawal from the legal battle on the land acquisition issue in Singur by the state government, which is pending before a bench.

This after Joy Deep Mukherjee, one of the petitioners, had challenged the land acquisition process by the state government in the Supreme Court.

Delivering the final verdict, the Calcutta High Court in January 2008 held that the land acquisition was legally valid. Then Mukherjee, one of the petitioners, had filed a special leave petition in the Supreme Court in February challenging the order of the High Court.

In the petition, the Tatas pleaded that the company was not involved in the land acquisition process in Singur anymore.

Tata Motors only took the possession of 645 acres by lease. As the company decided to pull out from Singur, Tata Motors was not involved anymore with the issue, the company contended.

Heading: Turin keen on educational partnership with state - Indian Express
Content:
The Gorkha Janamukti Morcha (GJM) has demanded that the All India Gorkha League (AIGL) president Madan Tamang resign from his political career.

The Morcha, which had set November 7 as the deadline for Tamang to prove his allegations made against GJM president Bimal Gurung, said it would launch an agitation against Tamang from Saturday.

GJM spokesperson Binay Tamang said the AIGL chief had failed to substantiate his charges. Madan had alleged that Gurung had held a secret meeting with state Home Secretary Ashok

Mohan Chakrabarty on October 11 at Tinchulay, in which the decision to suspend the non-cooperation movement launched by the Morcha was taken.

The AIGL leader had hinted that Gurung had sold out the movement to the state government.

Binay Tamang said: "We gave him time till November 7 to prove where and when the alleged meeting was held, and who were present therein. But he could not prove the charges."

The GJM spokesperson said: "We demand that Tamang quits his 40-year political career as he has made baseless remarks. We will not force him to leave Darjeeling, but his false allegations can make the public angry. If violence is reported, the Morcha will not be responsible."

He added: "We have asked our students' wing, Gorkha Janamukti Bidyarthi Morcha, to launch an agitation against him, which will include dharna, rallies and gherao of his house."

The AIGL chief told The Indian Express that the Morcha's stand against him was an assault on democracy. "This is against freedom of expression. I'm fully prepared to face the GJM. I am willing to die tomorrow but such strong-arm tactics cannot be tolerated," he added.

"I met the National Human Rights Commission team, which is at present in Darjeeling, and submitted a memorandum to them, mentioning the threats and anti-people activities of the GJM. How can the state government allow this to happen?" he said.

Darjeeling District Magistrate Surendra Gupta said the administration was aware of the situation.

"Though we are not providing any security to Madan Tamang, to prevent any untoward incident on Saturday, we have deployed adequate security cover."

He added, "Tamang has not approached us for help or lodged any complaint with the police."

Heading: Cancer survivors: Emotional counselling a must for patients - Indian Express
Content:
Soon, information technology and automobile sectors could be the two possible areas of partnership between West Bengal and the city of Turin, Piedmont region in Italy, said the Mayor of Turin on Friday.

"We will explore other possibilities but research will be the driving force of the partnership," said Mayor of Turin Sergio Chiamparino, who was in the city to promote the partnership between Turin and the state.

The Mayor, who is on a two-day visit, is accompanied by a team comprising representatives from universities, Turin Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Centre for Foreign Affairs of Piedmont and Turin municipality.

On Friday, they met Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya and seek a meeting with the chief minister and the Governor.

According to Sabyasachi Sen, Principal Secretary, state Commerce and Industries Department, West Bengal and Italy have gone a long way in developing their relationship, undertaking a number of diplomatic and bureaucratic exchanges between the two.

"West Bengal has a strong background of tanning industry and there is immense scope for trading. We would like to seek support from their government in developing and upgrading the tanning technology," said Sen.

On the academic front, the representatives of 11 Italian universities have signed a memorandum of understanding with four universities of West Bengal.

Calcutta University, Jadavpur University, Burdwan University and Rabindra Bharati University have entered into an agreement with various universities in Italy like University of Rome, University of Turin, University of Naples and University of Venice.

Heading: PTTI students attack school education minister’s car - Indian Express
Content:
Rekha Das still remembers the trauma, when she first learnt about her breast cancer. "When the doctor told me about it in 2005, I felt I would die soon," said Das.

November 7, on National Cancer Awareness Day, as she recalls the developments since then, she realises she it was her never-say-die spirit that kept her going through the tough times.

Rama Majumdar was diagnosed with breast cancer in 1997. Gritty enough to survive the disease, she discovered with shock that she was diagnosed with spinal cord cancer in 2006. She did not give up though. An employee with the West Bengal government, Majumdar left her job after being diagnosed with cancer the first time and decided to counsel other cancer patients.

Many survivors like Das and Majumdar, however, say there is little emotional support for cancer patients in the city.

Kalyan Roy, another cancer survivor, spends his time counselling cancer patients and helping them fight the battle. He also denies that Kolkata does not have good treatment facilities for cancer patients. "A place like Tata Memorial in Mumbai undoubtedly has better infrastructure but Kolkata has equally qualified and competent doctors," he adds.

Roy, however, says: "The city needs awareness about the disease. People spend Rs 30,000 on a treatment that can be undertaken for Rs 3,000. To combat cancer, one needs strong emotional support, from family and other cancer survivors."

To celebrate the Cancer Awareness Day, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Cancer Reserch Institute and the Kolkata Police inaugurated a mobile cancer detection unit at the Police Bodyguard lines to help people diagnose the disease in early stages.

Two more such units will be posted at BT Line and 2nd Battalion, Cossipore. "Such units should be set up at several places so that cancer can be detected at the earliest stage," said Ashish Mukherjee, a member of the institute.

Heading: All for one - Indian Express
Content:
State School Education Minister Partha De was attacked by the students of the Primary Teachers Training Institutes (PTTIs) at Bishnupur in Bankura on Friday.

The minister was on his way to Bankura to attend a programme. "The students had not taken permission from the police to hold the protest. When the minister's car arrived, the students blocked it. The window panes of the car were broken by the protesters," said Bankura Superintendent of Police Vishal Garg.

The police said that De was not hurt in the attack and left after attending the programme. "The police have arrested 10 students," Garg added. "We condemn the incident. But the students were protesting peacefully when the police provoked them and the situation turned violent," said Ashok Rudra, a PTTI students union leader.

Heading: Tech talk - Indian Express
Content: The employees of Citi India Chandigarh branch will join thousands of their colleagues worldwide for the company's third annual 'Global Community Day' on Saturday, November 8. More than 1,500 employees across 28 towns and cities, including that from the City Beautiful, will dedicate their time and talents to a wide spectrum of community development initiatives addressing specific needs including education, housing, environmental protection, child welfare, senior citizen support, disaster relief and healthcare. Citi India, in association with Youth Technical Training Centre, will spend quality time with children in various slum areas and invite them to share their dreams. Avdhesh Mahajan will lead the social activities on behalf of Citi India in Chandigarh. Recognising that many Citi employees volunteer year-round in their communities, Global Community Day celebrates Citi's volunteer spirit through a one-day global campaign. "Volunteerism is a key aspect of our corporate citizenship globally and in India. Global Community Day is a great opportunity for our employees to actively engage and make a difference in their communities. In the current environment, our support is especially relevant," says Sanjay Nayar, CEO, Citi South Asia.

Heading: The curtain rises - Indian Express
Content:
What an idea!

Remember the Abhishek Bachchan ad where he reaches students in far off areas through the mobile? Well Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) is making it come true. Teaming up with Communication and Manufacturing Association of India (CMAI), IGNOUE will provide textual, audio and visual educational content to students on cell phones. Word is that even appearing for examinations may go mobile. The mobile education campaign hopes to reach 29 million students in 2009 and double the number in the following year.

Serve it right!

Nokia has introduced seven new mobile handsets along with two new services. Amongst Nokia 1202, 1661, 2320, 2323, 2330, 5130 XpressMusic and 7100 Supernova, Nokia 1202 and 1661 are claimed to be their lowest cost mobiles that will offer flashlight, extended battery life and multiple phone books. Nokia has also introduced two new services - Mail on Ovi and Nokia Life Tools. Mail on Ovi is enabled on Nokia's Symbian 40 series based phones will offer easy to set-up and use email access. Nokia Life Tools aims at providing agricultural information and education knowledge, and is targeted at the rural and small town sections in the emerging markets.

Get chatty

Google has recently launched SMS service for its popular GMail chat courtesy Gmail India labs. Users will soon be able to send messages from the left navigation pane on the Gmail chat window. For this the user will be issued a resolute pseudo phone number. Google has made it quite a functional computer to phone SMS feature. This will also be accompanied by a host of other features like emoticons, gmail gadgets that were released by google a while ago.

Mapping India

Microsoft has announced a 'Made in India' product to cater to the locals. The new Live Search maps for India is developed by the Microsoft India Development Centre (MSIDC) based in Hyderabad. It will give users access to detailed business listings across 29 cities and street maps for nine cities. The Live Search Maps is powered by Nokia owned NAVTEQ and pits against the likes of Google maps and Yahoo maps. Live Search Maps has a subtle and fast user interface with a 'Suggestion Box' appearing unobtrusively to enhance user search. Live Search Maps is accessible from mobile phones as well.

Heading: Poetry in Motion - Indian Express
Content: The third annual Chandigarh Theatre Festival organized by the Chandigarh Sangeet Akademi is back and six plays will be staged this year, five of them by the city's own theatre groups. The festival begins on November 10 at the Tagore Theatre and the first play is Chhaledda, a Punjabi play written by S Bhag Singh and directed by Kuldip Sharma of Ajnabi Rangkarmee. The production is a statement on human relationships, social values, message of rural development and condemns drinking and drugs. Produced, directed and adapted in Hindi by Zulfikar Khan, Charan Das Chor, a play by Habib Tanvir is a story of a thief who becomes a legend simply by sticking to the vows that were taken by him in a jiffy before his guru, without caring for its implications. Loot, written by Joe Orton and directed by Nima Dandona of Studio Challenge and deals with crime and punishment. Aadhi Raat Ke Baad by Shankar Shesh and directed by Sudesh Sharma puts a question whether there will be a dawn of justice after the episode. Baawli written by Asif Ali deals with the loneliness of the old, while Balwant Thakur's Mere Hisse Ki Dhoop Kahan Hai, subtly showcases the hazards of population explosion.

Heading: Art for all - Indian Express
Content: Verse by verse, thoughts translated into feelings and words changed into emotions. Sublime, sensuous, sensitive...the evening was all about poetry that made you laugh, cry, feel and transcended you to another world. The evening, thought of by Yashovardhan Saboo had poetry in motion, with many reading the poetry of their favourite authors, from Pablo Neruda to Gulzar, Roald Dahl to Tennyson. Fantasy met reality, love collided with hate, death met life, as the poets reached out to your senses. The highlight of the evening were the fresh and original verses by young poets from various schools, including St John's, where The Crucible, a creative writing endeavour to nurture an appreciation of the written word is taking shape. Nature, death, humanity, love, longing...the budding poets explored it all, with passion.

Heading: The original - Indian Express
Content: The Chandigarh Lalit Kala Akademi has planned to invite a galaxy of artists, art historians, curators, conservators, filmmakers, theatre personalities, dancers, musicians, writers and art critics of national and international repute for delivering lectures in the city. The idea is to involve art lovers of Chandigarh into an ongoing dialogue with the best in the country and creating a knowledge pool to inspire and sustain them in their pursuits. As part of this endeavour, Muzaffar Ali, internationally renowned filmmaker and painter will present a lecture on Art Binds Us All and the audience will also get a chance to view a short film Breathe Into Me made by him on Sufism. Join Muzaffar Ali on November 8 at the Auditorium of Government Museum and Art Gallery at 5.30 pm.

Heading: Movie Magic - Indian Express
Content:
BR Chopra's Mahabharat makes a timely re-run

The man who gave the greatest televised epic of our times may have fallen silent but his legacy continues. And just as news of B R Chopra's passing away comes in, Star Utsav brings in a timely re-run of the original 'Mahabharat'. After the successful launch of the 'Katha Band', the channel is set to bring for its viewers yet another classic 'Katha' from the history of Indian television. Maintaining the classic splendour of the '90s, B R Chopra's Mahabharat is back to enthrall Indian audiences. This incredibly successful TV show has left an indelible impression in the hearts and minds of viewers worldwide with its timeless values and teachings. The 94-episode series, which originally ran from 1988 to 1990, is known to have created a voluntary curfew on the roads, just to get hooked to this classic tale of the victory of good over evil. Commenting on the re-launch of the show, Ravi Menon, EVP and GM, Star Utsav said, "Star Utsav has been an undisputed leader in the Katha slot. B R Chopra's Mahabharat is the finest Katha ever told on Indian television and we want to bring it back to the new generation through this slot and help relive its classic splendour." You can revive the magic of B R Chopra's 'Mahabharat' starting November 10 at 6 pm on Star Utsav.

Heading: Swiss Connection - Indian Express
Content:
Chandamama's iconic folk and adventure tales will now adorn the silver screen

If you are Indian and over 20, you will probably know these characters well: Vikram and Betal, Supandi, Uncle Pai and Shikari Shambu. Over years, we have connected with these eminent animated characters, and the comic books in which they appear. But these characters are now transforming. Amar Chitra Katha, Tinkle and Chandamama went online a few months ago; and now Chandamama, the iconic children' magazine looks to add yet another feather in its cap. One of the legends from the Chandamama library of 15,000 stories will be made into a full-length animated feature film by Technopark based Toonz Animation. "Both of us are in a complementary business. We are in the business of creating content and Toonz in the business of rendering it in the audio- visual format. It is a natural fit," says L Subramanyan, CEO of Chandamama.

Chandamama was first launched by legendary filmmakers B Nagi Reddi and his friend Chakrapani to familiarise the post-Independence generation with Indian tradition, folklore, mythology and history in the form of stories. After a successful print edition and rapidly going web portal, it was a natural choice to make it popular through the audio-visual medium as well. "The beauty of these stories lies in their simplicity and the socio-cultural values they try to communicate. The animated film will be a platform to provide the youth with both engaging and educative entertainment," feels Jaya Kumar, CEO, Toonz Animation Limited.

With the release date slated in 2011, work is on in full swing. "We have short-listed six stories from the library. They are a mix of humour, adventure and folklore. Ideally we want to select just one story, but we might take references from other stories as well," states Kumar. Toonz will undertake the entire production based in its state-of-the-art studio in Technopark and will finance 100 per cent of the production cost. "In its nascent stage it is really difficult to say but the estimated budget of the film is pegged at around 20 crore," confirms Kumar.

Although the cast and crew for the film is yet to be finalised, Toonz seems sure about hiring foreign scriptwriters and directors, while also taking help from their Indian counterparts. "It is important to have a mix of both worlds. The final product will appeal to the world audience and in the bargain not lose the Indian flavour." Also, as the trend is today, they are looking to rope in Bollywood actors to lend their voices for the characters in the movie.

Published in 14 Indian languages, will the movie be also dubbed in various languages? "It's primarily going to be in Hindi and then will dub in English for the world audience. Besides, it will be dubbed in four to five vernacular languages as well," states Kumar.

Heading: Small is big - Indian Express
Content:
For Lasserre Olivier, ideas are waiting to be found, handpicked and put to optimum use. And for this, nature is his bounty. "I live in it and with it," he says, as he takes seat at the UT Guest House, snaps open his laptop and clicks into his work — landscape masterplan of Rhone Alpine Valley, Switzerland, and Coupvray, Paris, the lighting plan in Geneva and regional project of Nyon District, Switzerland, among others. Interestingly, each highlights a conversation between human and natural structures. "I like to keep the virgin greens intact, just the way it's here," for Olivier, Chandigarh has a complete blend of human organization and raw wilderness.

"The strong relation between landscape structures and landscape quality of the two places is hard to miss," Olivier feels that an aerial view of both would reveal a similar territory structure. "Both have a valley in the back drop, a cone shaped structure (Panchkula in Chandigarh's case) and a fluid body (read Beas), though it's subject to different types of vegetation, surfaces and functions," he emphasises that treatment of the place is what marks the difference. "The placement of elements like path, plot limit, wall, hedge, fence, infrastructure, river, tree alignment and forest edge, along with political inclinations define the uniqueness of both the places." What's also of importance is the mindset of people and how they preserve it. "More than the design, it's how the people respond to it that shapes a city and Chandigarh's doing just fine," Olivier wraps up the conversation.

Lasserre Olivier will present 'Emerging Trends in Landscape Architecture' on November 9 at 10:00 am at Government Museum and Art Gallery, Sector 10.

Spaces in between
