As we speak of landscape design, voids cannot be left behind, says architect Andy Schonholzer, also a part of the conference. He has designed and redefined public spaces in Switzerland. " Last time, I visited Sector 17 and the plaza with its horizontal structure reminded me of shopping complexes back home," he says though Switzerland is pretty what it misses is Chandigarh's greenery. "Besides, Chandigarh has an edge - it was designed as a planned green city."

Heading: Govt takes steps to make road travel safe - Indian Express
Content:
The latest Bollywood actor to hop on the TV reality-show-judge bandwagon is the very charming Mahima Chaudhry

With all those big stars making their presence felt on television, it would be unfair to still refer to it as the "small" screen. While last year television saw the likes of Urmila Matgaonkar, Shilpa Shetty, Farah Khan slip into the shoes of a reality show judge, the new arrivals this season have been Karisma Kapur, Sushmita Sen to now the charming Mahima Chaudhry. The latter makes an entry into 9X's all-new reality show 'Jalwa Four 2 Ka 1' as a judge along with actor-director Satish Kaushik. What made her switch screens? "Today, Bollywood is the essence of entertainment everywhere. If you notice even television actors are dancing like their big screen counterparts complete with the filmi naach-gaana," tells Mahima, speaking to us from Mumbai. And more than her, you can hear the actor's 14-month-old daughter in the background. "She's dancing to the Ellen DeGeneres show," laughs Ariana's actor mom who is making the most of her new found role. In fact, as Mahima tells us, family is priority now. "I had been acting for almost a decade and there came a time when all I wanted was a baby. That's when I decided to take a family break," Mahima makes a candid confession. Now with Ariana padding around the house, Mahima's taken on one assignment. "I decided to step on the sets of 'Jalwa Four 2 Ka 1' as it requires me to be present only on one day of the week and that suits me brilliantly," shares Mahima whose role on the show is pretty well defined. "I am supposed to judge the most entertaining team. Other aspects such as dance, acting are secondary," she lists out.

For those who haven't got a clue on the show's format, here's a quick take. Hosted by versatile actor Ali Asgar and popular TV star Divyanka Tripathi, 'Jalwa Four 2 Ka 1' brings together four opposing captains - singer Mika, actors Rakhi Sawant, Shakti Kapoor and Shweta Tiwari. These four will "battle" for the title of the wholesome entertaining team. And it's a unique format which demands that team captains 'trade' team members amongst one another for further twists. Team members in the fray include the likes of Kashmera Shah, Rajeshwari Badola, Khayali, Twinkle Bajpai...to name a few.

As for Mahima's own career graph, this pretty lady is in no tearing hurry. "Everyone's asking me about future projects, films and the likes. Well, I am reading a few scripts but nothing is finalised. I don't want to do anything just for the heck of it and moreover it should leave me enough time to be with Ariana," she signs up saying.

'Jalwa Four 2 Ka 1' goes on air from November 9 on Channel 9X at 9 pm.

Heading: Designer deals - Indian Express
Content:
Learning bitter lessons from the Kufri road tragedy, Himachal Pradesh government today announced a total ban on use of mobile phones by the drivers, removal of music systems including CD and DVD players from all passenger vehicles, and installation of speed governors in buses.

Senior officials say that those found indulging in rash driving, endangering the lives of passengers, and driving transport vehicles without valid licences and certifications by the local transport authorities, will be dealt sternly under law. Private operators will lose licences to ply their vehicles if found indulging in illegal practices, or employing drivers without official verifications.

These steps are part of the drive announced by the state's Transport Minister Krishan Kapoor today morning for checking road accidents, and to make travel safe. "Some of the measures were already in force. But private bus operators and drivers did not adhere to them, resulting in the loss of valuable lives. The government will not spare such negligence anymore," Kapoor told mediapersons.

Kapoor admitted that after he attempted to check these violations by the transporters in the township, they resorted to a 'chakka jam'.

Later, when officers of the Transport Department held talks with them, the transporters agreed that adhering to safety rules was essential, and said that these would be followed.

"We have analysed the factors responsible for major road accidents, and drawn up a plan to address the problems. No operator will be allowed to have an unauthorised person on the driving seat. Only a duly licenced and trained professional will be allowed to drive a passenger vehicle. The government will issue a special badge, and it will be mandatory for such drivers to wear it on duty," said the minister.

He pointed out that buses will be fitted with speed governors, which will check overspeeding and ensure that the vehicle is driven at a safe speed. Habitual violators will lose their licence if they are found to be involved in three road accidents.

Overloading will be effectively curbed and all buses which have cassette, CD or DVD players will lose route licences.

Private bus operators have been told to provide shutter doors in buses instead of folded doors, which pose a danger to the passengers. He claimed that since the BJP government has come to power in the state, the number of fatal mishaps has gone down. The Kufri accident, Kapoor said, was a case of rash driving, since the driver was changing the CD with a remote control. The driver died in the mishap too.

Heading: Mock drill to deal with earthquake - Indian Express
Content:
Ralph Lauren, Versace, Jasper Conran & Sabyasachi - big names with big designs come knocking on city doors

Retail therapy couldn't get better than this. Trickling out of the wardrobe, international brands are making their presence felt in your room, den, kitchen, in short, every nook and corner of the house. With Rosebys draping poster beds and French windows, biggies including Ralph Lauren, Versace, Jasper Conran and Sabyasachi Mukherjee too have pitched their extravagant tents here, successfully teasing the rich bored house(proud)-wife

"With fashion spinning into a lifestyle, designers are all set to break into your homes," says architect Annu Bains, who's been juggling with big names for over a month now. The house-proud consumer, she adds, with wads of disposable income is ready to invest in a home dripping in design. Take Hotel Mountview. It's amongst the first few to flaunt a Ralph Lauren - a cream striped wallpaper with a touch of gold.

From fabrics to tiles to wallpapers, furnishings and accessories, international design houses are on a roll. Housing a two tile pattern from Versace Ceramic Design project and making space for more, Rohit Sehgal of Ganapti in Manimajra flaunts the brand in his show window. "It's complete with mosaic, logo and insignia and is priced at Rs 1,200 a square feet," he tells us. Wow! In cream and grey, the next in the line is a collection from Tommy, says Sehgal, getting out Swarovski accessories to enhance floorings and walls. "It's marketed through Gardenia Orchidea, and we are looking forward to furnishings from Versace soon," Sehgal's hopeful.

Meanwhile, Sabyasachi Mukherjee has tied up with Bombay Dyeing and is making its way into our rooms. Bed sheets, comforters, duet covers and towels, Dharam Chand Aggarwal (DCA), Sector 26, is expecting the first lot to arrive this week. "Blending prints, dots, stripes and checks with motifs from around the world, Sabyasachi has created an eclectic 'Art in the Bedroom' bed and bath line that can eventually be expanded to cover the entire household,"

Rajesh Goyal of DCA tells us as he hands out a brochure full of the collection in earthy shades and soft designs. Known as Bombay Dyeing Sabyasachi Signature Line, "the bed sheets have four pillow covers and start at Rs 2,200," adds Goyal. Exuding an image of comfort, the Sabyasachi collection gives you an opportunity to mix and match your linen, just the way you mix and match your clothes.

Though designers have dabbled in homes before, but never have such big names come knocking on city doors. "Since they have set foot in Chandigarh, the design element has increased manifold," nods architect Ranjot Singh, who has elaborately used Ralph Lauren designs in Shelton Resort along with city ventures. A walk across the city decor scene and fabric coordinates by UK fashion designers Jasper Conran are hard to miss. "They are amongst the first ones to hit the city," says Rajan Sankalp of Floors & Furnishings, as he opens Conran's designs that bring in a signature mix of classic British elegance and a cheeky irreverent attitude. "Sackville Street is Jaspers latest collection for Designers Guild," Sankalp shows us another collection that is inspired by men's wear and highlights relatively dark colours and fabrics. "Designs of classic suiting and tie like flannel, pinstripe, birds-eye spot and windowpane checks are accentuated with an elegant colour palette and counter pointed by zingy silks," he says.

Using the runway appeal to sell home accessories, designers will soon be seen strutting their home collections, reads the fashion forecast. Probably twice a year presentation to tell us exactly the trimmings and length of the curtain hemlines stop. Keep the doors open!

Heading: Man found murdered - Indian Express
Content:
In order to prepare the community and the government machinery in the event of a an earthquake, the Shimla administration will undertake a mock drill in the two most thickly-populated areas of the town - Lower Bazaar and Sanjauli.

The drill will be conducted under the guidance of National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). It is the first effort of its kind in the region. Shimla lies in seismic zone IV, and any high intensity calamity can cause heavy loss, in light of the haphazard construction on the hills.

Brig BK Khanna, Senior Specialist in training and capacity building, will monitor the drill involving the police, fire and medical agencies.

Deputy Commissioner JC Rana said efforts are on for improving the logistic support like setting up new rehabilitation centers at the sub-division level and special 'Apda (disaster) Sadan' at various places in the district.

Heading: Bungling: Official asked to pay up - Indian Express
Content:
A labourer from Uttar Pradesh was found murdered near police lines on Friday morning.

The victim, aged around 35, was identified as Jhhagdu Prasad alias Gajjar. He hailed from UP. Police said six persons have been rounded up for interrogation. These are Ram Dhiraj, Mukesh, Ganesh, Rampal, Chhotu and Kanhaiya.

Five of them used to stay with the victim at the HPCA stadium. The victim had been working here for two-and-a-half months, and had come back from home only recently, after being with his family for Diwali. He was married.

SSP Atul Fulzele said that police have registered a case of murder. Jhhagdu Prasad was working as a labourer at the stadium, where construction work is on.

Police got information about the murder at about 7.30 am. SHO Rajiv Attre reached the spot with his team and started investigation. The body was lying in a pool of blood. Police have recovered a can of kerosene, and half a bottle of country-made liquor from the spot.

Heading: Demand for Sirmour’s development - Indian Express
Content:
After the detection of a case of blatant misuse of official position in the withdrawal of honorarium, the acting secretary of Arki Nagar Panchayat has been asked to deposit Rs 1.49 lakh as recovery amount.

The directions have been given by the Joint Controller (Audit) of the Department of Urban Development. Following the order, the Nagar Panchayat today passed a resolution, urging the government to initiate the process for the recovery of the amount from the erring official.

The bungling came to light after a team of audit officials raised objections concerning the withdrawal of money in violation of laws. Sources in Nagar Panchayat reveal that on the demand of members of the Nagar Panchayat, the government had given additional charge of Secretary of the civic body to Naib Tehsildar Keshav Ram, in 2003.

It is learnt that the Nagar Panchayat House also passed a unanimous resolution, seeking permission to pay honorarium and fixed telephone expenses to the Naib Tehsildar. Following this, the official allegedly started withdrawing Rs 3,000 per month as honorarium, in addition to Rs 500 as telephone expenses.

However, the Nagar Panchayat's proposal was rejected by Director Urban Development Department in June 2004. Despite this, the Acting Secretary allegedly continued withdrawing the honorarium and the telephone expenses.

In 2006, the Director of the Department wrote to the Naib Tehsildar to deposit the recovery amount immediately. Despite this, the withdrawal continued every month, till it was detected by the auditors a few months ago.

The Naib Tehsildar has now been asked to deposit Rs 1.38 lakhs for the honorarium withdrawn by him, and Rs 11,000 for the telephone expenses. When contacted, Joint Director Vinod Gupta said that following the detection of financial irregularity, the erring official has been asked to pay up.

President of the Nagar Panchayat Satish Kashyap said that following the failure of the acting Secretary in depositing the amount, the House today passed a unanimous resolution urging the government to initiate action for the purpose.

Heading: Bhiwani killing:ASI arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Various volunteer organizations of Sirmour today protested the state government proposal to shift the steel plant unit of Steel Authority of India from Nahan to Kandrori in Kangra district.

The residents met under the banner of Nagrik Sabha. Those present on the occasion included Chairman Anjuman Islamia Yaqub Beg, president Vaishia Sabha PC Aggarwal, Chairman Koli Sabha Dalip Singh Verma, president Brahman Sabha Nardev Sharma, Rajput Sabha's Naresh Kumar Solanki and Member Mahila Sabha Dayavanti. They said an agitation would be launched if the government did not take major efforts to develop Sirmour.

Challans for violation of traffic rules

Chief Judicial Magistrate Nahan today challaned more than 58 vehicles for various violations of motor safety rules and other regulations, like driving without helmet, without a Pollution Control Certificate etc. He said that the vehicle drivers must adhere to traffic rules in order to ensure their safety.

Heading: Recommendations of reforms commission likely to remain on paper - Indian Express
Content:
ASI Ramkumar, an accused in the alleged fake encounter that claimed a life of a college student, Kuldip, was arrested yesterday. Constable and driver Balraj, whose name also figured in the FIR managed to flee. Police have also claimed to have recovered the revolver used in the shooting. Sources said Ramkumar was arrested yesterday night but Balraj managed to escape from the police custody. Six police officials are still absconding. Meanwhile, women of different communities of Bhiwani and nearby areas observed two-minute silence in memory of the deceased. Expressing sympathy to the bereaved family, they demanded immediate compensation of Rs 50 lakh and a government job to one member of the family. A mahapanchayat will be organised on November 16 where future course of action will be decided, they said in a voice vote.

INSO protests

Activists of Indian National Students Organisation (INSO) submitted a memorandum to Governor A R Kidwai asking to him order a probe by a sitting High Court judge into the killing of 22-year-old Kuldeep. INSO chief Vikas Rathee, who led the protest, said the students would continue their agitation until the Congress is thrown out of power. They shouted anti-government slogans in protest against the killing.

Heading: I would like to contest against my brother, says Partap Chautala - Indian Express
Content:
The Hooda government may have shown alacrity and zeal in setting up the Haryana Administrative Reforms Commission, but the same zeal seems to be missing when it comes to implementing these recommendations. The commission, which was set up under the chairmanship of Karan Singh Dalal, has handed over its first report on the subject-district administration. The recommendations may remain on paper and not get implemented, with less than one and a half years of the tenure of the present government remaining. On asking when the recommendations will be implemented, Hooda said the government will first wait for the commission to present all its reports before studying and implementing the relevantsuggestions.

The Administration Reforms Commission was set up in November 2007. In one year it has presented only the first of the several reports. Other reports, including those on elementary education, public health, Panchayati Raj Institutions, Police department etc, are in the pipeline. By the time the Commission finishes presentation of the remaining reports assembly elections would be due in March 2010. Even if the government tries to implement the recommendations next year, it would just have a few months left.

Talking to The Indian Express, Karan Singh Dalal, Chairman of the Commission, said the first report may have taken a year's time, but he would bring out the other reports soon. "I may present two reports at one time next month and follow up with other reports one after the other,'' he said.

However, senior leader of the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) and former finance minister Sampat Singh called it a futile exercise. "The government is not serious about it and is trying to hoodwink the people. Why would it hold back the administrative reforms commission's suggestions?" he asked.

"The government should table the report in the Haryana Vidhan Sabha at the earliest and allow debate and discussion on the provisions. Let the House take a decision on the suggestions," he added.

BJP leader Gyan Chand Gupta was also critical of the government's attitude. " It is all an eyewash. The government is whiling away time. When will the government find time to study the report?" he said. "We will consider the necessary reforms if our government comes to power in the next elections,'' he added.

Heading: HC orders completion of vigilance enquiry - Indian Express
Content:
Back in the Congress after a brief stint with the Haryana Janhit Congress (BL), Partap Chautala said he would remain in the party as long as he was alive. Addressing a press conference here today, Chautala said if the Congress gives him a ticket in the 2010 Vidhan Sabha elections he would like to contest against his brother Om Prakash Chautala.

Chautala said he was attracted by Kuldeep Bishnoi's stand on the SEZ and had joined the HJC last year. He was soon disillusioned by his lies on the resignation issue "Later the Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee nailed his lie and said Bishnoi had never sent his resignation to the Lok Sabha. His stand on the SEZ was dithering too. Therefore, I resigned,'' he said.

Chautala, 70, has had a chequered career. He began his political career in 1968 and has won just one assembly election till now.

He was with the Lok Dal, before joining the Congress party in 1982. A few years later he quit the Congress, but joined it again in 1991.

Heading: Power station synchronised after renovation - Indian Express
Content:
A PIL filed by P P Kapoor, convener of Haryana State unit of "Indian Federation of Trade Unions (IFTU)", seeking inquiry into allotment of residential plots meant for industrial workers at Panipat by Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA), came up for resumed hearing today in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

The petitioner had alleged that HUDA had allotted many residential plots to ineligible persons. He had leveled allegations against 17 persons.

The counsel for HUDA pointed out that a vigilance enquiry which was ordered by the Haryana government in 2005, is still on. At present it is being conducted by Sajjan Kumar, DSP.

Advocate H C Arora, counsel appearing for petitioner, brought it to the notice of the Bench that HUDA is protecting the persons who have been wrongly allotted the plots.

The High Court has directed the investigating officer to complete the investigation within two months and submit a report.

In case the report is not submitted by the officer within the stipulated period, he would be asked to be present before the Court on the next hearing. Orders against him for breach of directions will be issued by the Court.

Taking umbrage at the stand taken by HUDA, in its written statement, the Bench observed in its order, "We are prima facie of the view that only those persons employed in the industry, who come within the definition of workmen under the Industrial Disputes Act would be entitled to allotment of plot as industrial workers."

Heading: Punjab farmers reap rich profits - Indian Express
Content:
The 110-MW Unit-I of Panipat Thermal Power Station was synchronised today after renovation, modernisation and upgrading.

Giving details, a spokesman of Haryana Power Generation Corporation (HPGCL) said the generation capacity of the Unit had been upgraded from 110 MW to 117.8 MW, thereby increasing the availability of power for the consumers of the state.

The unit shall now be more efficient as the worn out components of the boiler have been replaced.

The existing impulse turbines have also been replaced with state-of-the-art reaction turbines which are based on the latest technology. The work of renovation and modernisation was started by BHEL in September 2007 and has been completed at a total cost of around Rs 160 crore. With the completion of renovation this old unit of PTPS, which was commissioned in 1979, is expected to generate maximum cost effective electricity for the state.

Heading: Badal to take up Rajasansi issue with Manmohan Singh - Indian Express
Content:
Bumper crops: Estimates say Rs 15,000 cr earned by farmers from paddy alone

After a profitable wheat season and bumper paddy crop, farmers in Punjab are reaping good profits. Rough estimates say farmers in the state will be selling paddy worth Rs 15,000 crore this year. The total income from sale of all the crop from Punjab this year, including wheat, paddy and cotton, will be around Rs 30,000 crore, Rs 2,000 crore more than last year.

For a section of economists and agriculturists, the diversification dream may have taken a beating, but delay in sowing time of paddy has helped save the depleting water table of the state.

While floods this monsoons may have creased the Punjabi farmers' brow for some time, the bumper paddy crop, a handsome minimum support price of Rs 930 per quintal and PUSA 1121 being finally declared as basmati variety had all the worries vanishing. The government is expecting 150 lakh metric tonnes of paddy to be purchased in Punjab mandis this year, which is almost four lakh metric tonnes more than last year.

Gurinder Singh, a farmer from Moga, says, "I may not be able to quantify in rupees, but our profit margins for both paddy and wheat this year have been good. On an average, after both the crops, I would say that my profit margin is about 50 per cent."

Ravi Inder Singh, another farmer from Patiala, who had stacked away his basmati at the beginning of procurement season due to low prices, is now shuttling his 800 bags to the Rajpura mandi, where a part of his harvest has been priced at around Rs 3,300 per quintal.

Ajmer Singh Lakhowal, president of Punjab Mandi Board, is also a happy man these days. As he puts it, "When the farmer is happy, I am also happy, as all this will make my department richer."

Punjab Mandi Board collected market fees worth Rs 355.77 crore this year, almost Rs 30 crore higher than the same corresponding period of wheat last year. Lakhowal says, "The paddy season will help take our collections even higher, as the volume of paddy purchased is higher than wheat."

Helped by a handsome rise in the minimum support price (MSP) of wheat by almost 25 per cent this year, the Central government picked up around 100 lakh metric tonnes of wheat this season, while the market arrival was around 105.9 lakh metric tonnes.

Similarly, the market arrival of paddy is expected to touch the 150-lakh metric ton mark this year and the government purchase is expected to be around 136 lakh metric tonnes.

Director (Agriculture) B.S. Sidhu says, "The delay in sowing of wheat till June 10 has helped us salvage the depleting water table. While procurement season became a little longer than usual, it was manageable keeping in mind the costs we were otherwise paying. Moreover, a handsome return to farmers always translates into more investment into the agriculture sector, which is a major need of Punjab."

Sidhu added, "At the same time, we are also looking at varieties that will need even less time to ripen, use lesser water. To help farmers quicken the process of transplanting paddy from nurseries to fields, we have trying to popularise the use of transplanters and other such machinery."

Heading: ...urges Praful to bail out Rajasansi - Indian Express
Content:
Business at Rajasansi Airport, Amritsar, has suffered a lot following the decision of many airline companies to reduce their flights. This is a setback for Punjab and the matter will be taken up with the Prime Minister, said Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, on his visit to the city today.

About eight international flights have been reduced per week from Rajasansi Airport. The airlines, however, point out that they are not able to get enough business class customers from this airport and preferred to reduce the air traffic rather than suffer losses.

Badal was in town to attend a sangat darshan in Cabinet Minister Hira Singh Gabria's constituency. Contradicting the airlines' stand, he said, "The Central government will be apprised of the details of the business from Amritsar airport so that they can convey the message to the airline companies as well."

Meanwhile, it needs to be mentioned that the decision of reducing the number of flights from this airport has meant a major setback to the projects coming up in and around Amritsar in the form of hotels and shopping malls, which were eyeing NRIs and foreigners as their primary clients.

Heading: Kalia woos IT industry in Bangalore - Indian Express
Content: Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today wrote to Union Minister of State for Civil Aviation, Praful Patel, urging him to take immediate remedial measures to not only retain but improve the passenger traffic at Amritsar. The CM asked him to direct all the airlines flying to Amritsar to maintain their normal schedule. Badal said it was a matter of great concern for Punjab that certain airlines had decided to curtail their flights from Rajasansi International Airport. Already, flights from Rajasansi airport have been reduced from 89 international and domestic flights per week in November 2007 to 61.

Heading: Moga sex scandal: Barjinder surrenders, in CBI custody - Indian Express
Content:
A high-level delegation, headed by Punjab Industry Minister Manoranjan Kalia, engaged in one-to-one discussions with H.R. Binod, head of Infosys India business unit, and Chandraketu Jha, head of Infosys commercial unit, both of whom are also on the Infosys Board of Directors.

The Minister was accompanied by Principal Secretary, Industries and Commerce, Dr S.S. Channy; Punjab Infotech Chairman H.S. Grewal and Managing Director, Punjab Infotech, Rakesh Verma. Earlier, Kalia, in his inaugural address at the three-day ICT flagship event held in Bangalore today, said Punjab has come up with a slew of incentives that would help the IT sector's growth.

He said Punjab had led the Green Revolution when the country needed food security and that it would rise to the occasion again to contribute to the IT sector's growth in the country.

Highlighting the initiatives, including the 380-acre Knowledge City at Mohali, the new IIT at Ropar and the Industrial Facilitation Act, he invited industry representatives to visit the two proposed project sites - the 100-acre site at Kapurthala for IT projects and the 280-acre site at Ropar for high-end software development projects.

'Support Obama to fight terrorism'

AMRITSAR: All India Anti Terrorist Front chairman MS Bitta has urged the political parties across the nation to support US president-elect Barack Obama to enable the country to eliminate the terrorist training camps being run in Pakistan. He also sought release of a white paper on various bomb blasts and communal clashes in the country. Addressing mediapersons on Friday, Bitta said Obama's statement against terrorists training camps being run in Pakistan indicated his resolve to deal with terror organisations with an iron hand. He said the wrongful policies of the government had forced people to take to arms.

Heading: Cheating menace at GNDU: 26 to appear before UMC panel - Indian Express
Content:
Barjinder Singh, son of former education minister Tota Singh, was remanded to four days' CBI custody by the Special CBI Court here today.

He was produced before the court of Special CBI Judge H.S. Madan, after the Punjab and Haryana High Court had said on Thursday that the CBI court would decide on the issue of his custody and reserved the verdict on his bail plea till November 11. Barjinder is one of the prime accused in the infamous Moga sex scandal.

The CBI had sought a five-day police remand, which was objected to by the defence counsel, who pleaded for a day's police remand for the accused.

The defence counsel said the accused was a patient of asthma and required medical aid, so the judge allowed a medical examination before taking him into custody and one before producing him in court after the end of the custody period.

The judge also allowed the defence plea of allowing a meeting of the accused with his lawyer for 10 minutes during his custody. The alleged sex scandal, involving police officials, local politicians and other influential persons, came to light in June 2006 on the complaint of one Ranjit Singh and in February this year, the CBI arrested former Moga SP Davinder Singh Garcha and Ropar SP (headquarters) Paramjeet Singh for their alleged involvement in the scandal. The two have been reinstated after their initial suspension following their arrest.

Heading: 5 pc reservation for poor in housing projects - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another incident that has exposed the menace of cheating in Guru Nanak Dev University, 26 cases of use unfair means of copying (UMC) have come to the fore in the supplementary tests conducted for various streams in September. They would be summoned before the UMC committee of the university on Saturday.

The copying had been noticed during the coding of the exam results. The students had allegedly left identification marks on their answer sheet, which is not allowed. Those found guilty are likely to be disqualified for a minimum of two years. Sources said these students were from varied educational streams, including commerce, electronic maintenance and computer applications.

Sources added that this is not the first time that such a thing has happened, as UMC cases are reported almost every year in the university.

Confirming these cases, Dr Gurnam Singh, professor incharge, examination, at the university, said, "Some of them had even written their names, roll numbers and telephone numbers on the cover pages of the answer books, which is prohibited."

He added that the details of these students had been sent to the UMC committee. "The committee, headed by a judge, would decide the matter," he said.

Registrar Dr R.S. Bawa said stern action would be taken against students found guilty. "The punishment in such cases amounts to disqualification for a minimum period of two years," he said.

Heading: Historic gurdwara in PoK converted into police lines - Indian Express
Content:
In a move that could go a long way in providing affordable housing to the economically weaker sections, the housing and urban development department today notified a policy under which 5 per cent area has been reserved for the poor in all mega housing projects, both public and private, coming up in the state.

It has been mandated that the applicant must be a resident of Punjab for the last 10 years and the applicant must not own residential property in Chandigarh or Punjab.

The cut-off income limit has been kept at Rs 10,000 per month for one room tenement and Rs 15,000 for two room set, said a spokesperson.

The cost of the tenements would be determined by the local development authority concerned in consultation with the promoters.

The policy encourages use of the latest low-cost technique so that the housing needs of the poor can be met at affordable rates.

Allotment of houses shall be made to the eligible applicants through a computerised draw.

Heading: Arrest of cop, trader in graft case sparks tension in Sector 17 - Indian Express
Content:
Claims Sikh jatha that visited PoK last month

The historic gurdwara of Guru Hargobind, the sixth Sikh Guru, near Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), has been partly demolished and converted into police lines.

This was claimed by Sarwan Singh, president of Central Committee of All Jammu and Kashmir Refugees (1947), after a six-member delegation of the Committee led by him visited

Muzaffarabad (PoK) from October 9 to October 23. He also claims that this was the first Sikh jatha to visit PoK after partition.

Sarwan Singh, originally a native of Kotli in Muzaffarabad district in PoK, said he was just 24 when he came here after partition.

The other delegation members who visited the place included Gajinder Singh, Saran Singh, Rajinder Singh, Kulwant Singh and Kartar Singh. All of them said they were shocked to see that the historic gurdwara had been converted into police lines.

Kartar Singh, whose great-grandfather Suba Singh was the mahant of the gurdwara in 1831, disclosed that the then governor of Jammu and Kashmir, Kanwar Sher Singh, had visited the gurdwara and transferred 100 bighas of land in the name of the gurdwara, along with other offerings.

All the six members of the Sikh jatha were guests of a relative, who has converted into Islam. The neo-converts in PoK are now called Sheikhs.

Sarwan Singh said at the time of partition, the population of Sikhs in PoK was 70,000, but a majority of Sikhs migrated, while the remaining were either converted or killed by Muslims.

He said they all met PoK president Raja Zulqarnain Khan during a dinner hosted by him at the President's House there. He said they demanded that the Government of Pakistan and PoK should give back the land and building to Sikhs and the gurdwara would be constructed as Gurdwara "Chatti Padshahi" in the memory of Guru Hargobind.

Heading: Family of victim moves HC - Indian Express
Content:
The Sector-17 Plaza witnessed a commotion on Friday after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Neelam police post in-charge Sub-Inspector Sanjeev Kumar and Sector 17 Traders' Association president Subhash Kataria for allegedly demanding and accepting Rs 50,000 as bribe from a shopkeeper. Local traders vandalised the police post in support of the SI, claiming that the CBI had forcibly made him hold the marked currency notes.

Scores of people gathered outside the police post after Sanjeev and Subhash allegedly walked into a trap laid by the CBI and were taken to the post. The agitated mob smashed the walls of the pre-fabricated police post by pelting stones and raining kicks and blows.

Sources said Manoj Pandey, owner of Pandey Book Shop in the Anand Theatre Complex, had approached the SI to get another shop of his in the area vacated by a tenant. The officer had allegedly demanded Rs 50,000 for the job. "I went to the CBI and lodged a complaint," said Pandey.

As directed by the CBI, he called up Sanjeev in the morning when the latter allegedly asked him to hand over the money to Subhash Kataria. "We have recorded the conversation. This is a proof that the SI had demanded the bribe," said a CBI official. The CBI laid a trap at Kataria's shop, Delhi Jewellers, and caught him red-handed while accepting the money.

"We then came to the police post where the SI was waiting for Kataria. We never tried to put money in his hand," the official claimed. The protesters, however, claimed otherwise.

They shouted slogans against the CBI for allegedly implicating Sanjeev. More than 20 sub-inspectors gathered outside the post as the news of his arrest spread. People climbed on trees to witness the drama. A few of them even entered the post and tried to set free Sanjeev. Reinforcements were called in, which took almost two hours to control the agitated mob. A police van had to be called to the parking area adjacent to Neelam Cinema to take away the accused.

Speaking to the media, Sanjeev claimed he never demanded any bribe.

Heading: Kharar: all six ‘rapists’ in police net - Indian Express
Content:
Panchkula gangrape: Police officers threatened us, says family; petition claims father of an accused is using Deputy CM's influence

The mother of the 17-year-old gangrape victim in Panchkula approached the Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday, seeking an order to get the case probed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or to change the officers investigating the case at present.

The name of Haryana Deputy Chief Minister Chander Mohan, too, figures in the affidavit that claims the father of one of the main accused (Chhavi) in the case is a close friend of his and is using his influence to evade arrest.

The petitioner also claims that her daughter was forced to discontinue her studies as the culprits were roaming scotfree. The petition says: "DSP (City) R C Rathi and Sector 14 SHO Inspector Surjit Kumar visited the house of the girl last night and asked her to join them for investigation and later threatened her to reach a compromise and change her earlier statement recorded before the magistrate under Section 164 of the CrPC."

It adds: "Before September 16, the victim was raped six times (on July 22, 26, 28, August 5 and 26 in 2007 and on September 4, 2008) by the accused, in connivance with two girls — Tanu and Chhavi. Since the boys and the girls belong to influential families, the local police are shielding the accused. While the father of Aman Ahuja is a senior executive officer in the Transport department, Jitesh's father is a prominent businessman. The local police are out to help the culprits as the father of one of them has close ties with Chander Mohan."

The petition also highlights the "shoddy investigation" conducted by the police. It says: "The police have not collected even the clothes worn by my daughter when she was raped. Instead, they took the clothes that she was wearing when she went to lodge a complaint with the police." It adds: "The police exerted pressure on the medical staff to misrepresent the real facts. Besides, the family named Aman Ahuja as an accused several times, but his name was deliberately omitted from the FIR. It served as a vital ground for him to apply for bail, which he eventually got."

Police 'inaction'

The Panchkula police have failed to even establish the identity of the two accused named as Jatin and Chhavi. This, after the victim's family procured Chhavi's photograph from her school records and gave it to the police. While Superintendent of Police Sandeep Khirwar has proceeded on a 15-day leave to Mauritius, Haryana Director General of Police Ranjiv Dalal refused to answer his phone. DSP (City) Ram Chander Rathi said: "We have been trying our best to crack the case. Every time the victim is taken anywhere for investigation, women constables accompany her. There is no question of anyone threatening the victim."

Heading: Jan Shatabdi to stop at Mohali from today - Indian Express
Content:
The Kharar police claimed a major breakthrough on Friday after they arrested four more people who had allegedly raped a minor girl in Kharar village on Diwali night last month. They have also recovered the swords, iron rods, batons and the other weapons allegedly used by the accused to scare the girl and her family members.

With two of the accused already in their custody, officers claimed that all six youths who had allegedly committed the crime had been arrested.

The six are accused of raping the 15-year-old girl of Bhagomajra village for over two hours, after assaulting and gagging her and holding her two elder sisters and an aunt hostage. The two main accused — Kamaljit Singh alias Kamal and Fateh Singh alias Titu —who were named by the girl, were arrested on Thursday.

During their interrogation, the names of the other four surfaced, the police said. The four were identified by the girl, her aunt and sisters after their arrest.

According to the police, the six have confessed to committing the crime.

Acting on a report published in Chandigarh Newsline on November 6, highlighting the gangrape incident, the Punjab State Human Rights Commission (PSHRC) had on Thursday taken a suo motu notice and sought report from the state government through the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) of Mohali.

Sub-Inspector Dalbeer Singh, the Kharar Station House Officer (SHO) who is the investigation officer in the case, said Mandeep Singh alias Rosy, Kulbeer Singh alias Nana, Sukhwinder Singh alias Ladi and Mohan Singh were arrested from a forest area near Bhagomajra village. They were allegedly planning to flee the area.

A local court, meanwhile, sent Kamaljit Singh alias Kamal and Fateh Singh alias Titu in police remand till Monday. All six accused in the age group of 22-28 years are residents of Bhagomajra village.

The SHO said barring Titu, a beldar with the Agriculture department in Sector 70, Mohali, and Mohan, member of a family of agriculturists, all other accused were unemployed.

On Diwali night, when the villagers were busy bursting crackers, the teenager was picked up from her courtyard around 8.30 pm and allegedly raped by the six accused. They allegedly raped her till 11 pm when her parents arrived and raised an alarm.

The accused were accompanied by six others who are yet to be arrested.

Heading: PGI launches body donation helpline - Indian Express
Content: The Nangal Dam-New Delhi Jan Shatabdi will have a two-minute stop at the Mohali station from Saturday. The Delhi-bound train (2058 up) will reach Mohali at 7:07 am and leave at 7:09 am. On its way back from Delhi, the train (2057 down) will reach and leave Mohali at 7:41 pm and 7:43 pm, respectively. After Annadpur Sahib, Morinda and Ropar, Mohali is the fourth station to be added to the route.

Heading: HDFC to pay up for snatching car from loan defaulter - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Anatomy, PGIMER, Chandigarh, has created a helpline with regard to donation of bodies. The phone numbers are 9914208201 and 9914208202.

According to the department, a person in his life can express in writing his will to donate his body — form can be downloaded from the PGI website, www.pgimer.nic.in — and can convince his next of kin that after death his body may be donated.

The body, along with the death certificate/declaration of death certificate, should be transported within three to five hours to the department (or to any other nearby medical college/institute).

In case of any difficulty in transportation, the department will provide a vehicle within the tricity. If the body is brought during non-working hours, it can be kept in the cold chamber of the PGI mortuary, which is open 24 hours on all days.

Heading: Best Students - Indian Express
Content:
Upholding an order of the district forum, the UT State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the HDFC Bank to pay Rs 4 lakh as compensation to the complainant whose car had been allegedly snatched by the bank's musclemen.

"They cannot use force like this. Musclemen have no place in a civilised society," said the commission, dismissing an appeal filed by the HDFC.

The commission also directed the bank to pay Rs 5,000 as costs of litigation. The district forum had earlier directed the bank to pay Rs 10,000 as costs on August 28 this year.

Balwinder Singh had purchased a Tata Indica DLS Car in 2006 by raising a loan of Rs 2,16,500 from the bank. The amount was to be repaid in 48 monthly instalments of Rs 6,248 each. After he had paid two instalments, a crisis in the family reportedly kept Balwinder from making the next five payments. He paid the last instalment on June 2, 2007. On July 20, 2007, the complainant said, he was going to the Sector-11 rehri market when five recovery agents stopped him and took possession of his car.

He went to the district forum after his requests to the bank to release the vehicle on payment of the due instalments fell on deaf ears.

In its reply, the bank said the vehicle had been taken over as per the agreement reached between HDFC and the complainant when he took the loan. They said the respondent was a chronic defaulter and a sum of Rs 2,47,335 was due on him, and that he had voluntarily surrendered the vehicle. The bank also said an inventory of the vehicle was prepared, for which Balwinder was issued a letter which he signed later.

The commission said it had gone through the copy of the inventory. "No evidence has been led by the bank that it was signed by the respondent. There are no signatures under the said endorsement. This means the bank had tampered with the letter, which was signed by the bank at the time of advancing the loan. This letter cannot be relied upon. It further amounts to unfair trade practice," said the commission, adding that there was no evidence either that any notice was served on the respondent for repossessing of the vehicle on account of default of payment.

The commission said it could not be proved that the respondent had surrendered the vehicle voluntarily. "There is no affidavit of a responsible officer of the bank that says the respondent had voluntarily surrendered the vehicle and no force was used."

Heading: More CCTV cameras, wire-fencing at PU - Indian Express
Content:
Changing 4 schools in 9 years has made me more adjusting

"Taking up new challenges is always exciting. I love to leave my comfort zone and carve my own identity wherever I go. Changing four schools in nine years has made me more adjusting," says Abhivyakati Saxena, a student of Carmel Convent School. She has travelled to different parts of the country and studied in various schools, thanks to her father's job. But all this travelling, as she says, has shaped her into a better human being. 

This thirteen-year-old girl has an excellent academic record with an aggregate of 95 and above and has always been among the top three students in her class. Her favourite subject is Mathematics and why other children her age dread it is a mystery to her. "Instead of finding the subject to be a burden, I find solving sums to be very relaxing. Maths is the only subject which completely tests one's mental ability," she says. 

Other than academics, Abhivyakati is also adept at a number of extra-curricular activities. She is a good orator and has represented her school at various declamation contests at the district and state level. "Participating in such competitions has improved my public speaking skills. I feel that I am able to put forward my opinion more easily and clearly," she states.

She represented her school at the WORDZ MUN held in the city recently, where she was given the commendation award. She was also selected to participate in the Aryabhatta examination, a national-level test of one's mathematical ability. She is also the founder member of her school's Reporters Club.  

Her hobbies include reading books and giving words to her thoughts in the form of poetry. "I am very fond of reading and can read anything I can lay my hands on. But detective novels and thrillers are my preferred genre, with Agatha Christie being my favourite author," she says. Abhivyakati is a trained Bharatnatyam dancer and has also learnt Hindustani Classical music. She feels that the current breed of music is not as soulful as it used to be. "Music is one thing that soothes your senses. But the kind of songs that are composed today are crass and sound like cacophony," she shares.

She aspires to be an aeronautical engineer when she grows up as the universe and stars fascinate her no end, she admits. She says her father is her inspiration. "I would like to be as tactful as he is. I find him to be extremely calm even in the toughest of situations," she says.

Heading: PUSU denies involvement of law student in clash outside V-C’s house - Indian Express
Content:
The battering of a Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) member outside the vice-chancellor's residence at Panjab University has prompted the authorities to devise additional measures to strengthen security on the campus.

The authorities have decided to install more closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras for which an estimated budget of Rs 34 lakh has been announced. The officials plan to place wires on the boundary walls of the campus.

Private security on the campus was, earlier, sought to be replaced by hiring trained individuals.

The university has also decided to close the gate from the PGI as well as the one from Sector 25 after 6 pm every day.

While gate number 2 will remain open, every vehicle entering the campus would be checked.

Members from the Students' organisation of India (SOI), meanwhile, submitted a memorandum to the vice-chancellor questioning the security of students on the campus.

Talking to Newsline, president of Students' organisation of India, Paramvir Sunny said, "The number of such incidents has risen in the past and the authorities must take steps to curb the same. We appeal to the students to join hands in maintaining peace on the campus."

Heading: Two-day mental health fest starts at GCG-11 - Indian Express
Content:
In a press conference held in the Panjab University on Friday, under the leadership of PUSU President Tejpal Singh Cheema, it has been demanded that the security on campus be tightened. A member of Students of Panjab University (SOPU), Barinder Dhillon, was beaten up by nine youths outside PU Vice-Chancellor RC Sobti's residence late on Thursday evening.

Speaking about the incident that left even the V-C injured, Cheema said, "If the V-C is not safe, then how can the students be assured of their safety." 

A case of assault, rioting and intimidation has been registered against three youths, Simranjeet Singh Sandhu (a law student in PU), Narinder Gujjar and Sanjay Kumar (members of Haryana Students Association (HSA), and other unidentified accomplices.

Supporting Sandhu, whose name appears in the FIR, Cheema said, "Sandhu is still recovering from the attack he had suffered at the hands of SOPU campus president Barinder Singh Dhillon last year".

He further claimed, "Dhillon is on bail in the attack case against Sandhu. Sandhu has also applied for the cancellation of his bail. Last night's incident is being used by the SOPU president as a pressure tactic against Sandhu so that he takes his application back and his bail may continue."

Chema also alleged that the V-C has a soft corner for Barinder and he was allowed to campaign in the campus during elections even though he was an outsider then. It was further demanded that the V-C should issue a statement denying Sandhu's involvement in the incident.

Heading: ‘Virtual schools are the future of education’ - Indian Express
Content:
A two-day mental health fest was inaugurated at the GCG in Sector 11 on Friday. An inter-college declamation contest, psychological testing and a slogan writing competition marked the first day of the fest.

G K Singh, the founder of the Psychology department in GCG-11, was the chief guest on the occasion.

Amrita Pathak of GCG-11 won the first prize in the declamation contest while Karubaki from MCM DAV College came second and Pallavi of GCG-11 was declared third. Consolation prizes were given to Neha from SD College and Yuvika from MCM DAV College.

The team from GCG was adjudged as the best team, but being the host team, they gave away the trophy to MCM DAV College. 

Psychological testing of college students on different parameters of mental health was also undertaken on the occasion.

Students also participated enthusiastically in the slogan writing competition. Kanika Bali, Swati and Balkiran were awarded the first, second and third position respectively. Former HODs of the department of Psychology, GCG-11 were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Set up to create awareness, NGO passes ‘illegal’ orders - Indian Express
Content:
Moving with the changing times, we must realise that education too needs to be reformed. We cannot ignore the role technology plays in the current education scenario," said Jairaj Kataria, the resource person at a seminar on the role of technology in education on Friday. 

Talking about the dominance of technology in the field of education, Kataria said that if progress is to be made, schools should adopt IT and multimedia ways of learning. "Virtual schools are the future of education. With more and more schools adopting the smart way of teaching, the face of classroom teaching is changing. Apart from making academics interesting for students, smart classes have various advantages to it," he stated. 

He, however, maintained that smart classes were not a replacement for teachers; but just a tool to assist in teaching. "Nothing can replace the utility of teachers. IT aids empower them with lots of resources within the classroom. Following the footsteps of digital learning will also improve the academic performance of students as multimedia presentations help generate their interest. It also increases their grasping power," Kataria said. 

Advocating the use of technology, he said that it also enables parents to assess their ward's performance and improves the teacher's effectiveness at the same time. "Technology works in the favour of both students and teachers. As it helps decrease the teachers' workload, their productivity increases. Since virtual schools work on the concept of pictorial learning, the child learns more and retains more," he concluded.

'Quality of research more important than quantity'

PATIALA: A three-day national seminar on Ferroelectrics and Dielectrics was inaugurated at the Thapar University on Thursday. The seminar is organised biannually and is being hosted for the first time in Punjab by the School of Physics and Materials Science (SPMS) of Thapar University. The seminar has been held at different IITs and other universities in the country in previous years. The seminar was inaugurated by educationist and scientist, Kamal Singh, who is the vice-chancellor of SGBG Amaravati University, Maharashtra. In her inaugural address, Singh said, "The quality of research is more important than the quantity in the form of publications, patents and devices. We need young researchers to come up with modern devices based on ferroelectrics and dielectrics." Director of Thapar University Abhijit Mukherjee, also spoke on the occasion. Conference convener KK Raina said about 200 participants were attending the seminar from India and other countries.

Heading: High Court pulls up ‘consumer forum’ - Indian Express
Content:
The role of a non-government organisation — Consumers Forum, Chandigarh — which has been working to create consumer awareness in the city since 1981, has come under the scanner with the UT Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum accusing the body of tarnishing the image of the original forum and misleading the public.

The UT consumer forum in Sector 19 has declared illegal the orders of the NGO in four separate cases this month and issued notices to them to explain how can the organisation mislead the people and even 'threaten' the opposite parties by passing fake orders. The NGO authorities, however, say it has been highly successful in its relentless efforts to create consumer awareness in the 27 years as it has been functioning in the city even before the Consumer Protection Act came into effect in 1986.

In an order passed by the UT Consumer Forum today, Air India has been directed to pay Rs 10,000 compensation to a Sector 27 resident, Rajiv Gupta, after a delay in flight to London in February this year caused him 'huge mental and physical harassment'. While passing the order, president Jagroop Singh Mahal ruled that the NGO, which was approached by the complainant for his grievance before he approached the forum, illegally directed Air India to pay Rs 1.5 lakh compensation without even hearing the opposite party.

"It is not understood as to how the Consumers Forum, Chandigarh, exercised the powers of calling the opposite party to pay such a huge amount. They are misusing the name by issuing baseless letters, they have no authority and are just meant to create awareness," said Mahal.

President, UT State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Justice K C Gupta, when asked about the functioning of the NGO said a lot of confusion arises because of the similar name of the body. "People are mislead by the NGO leading to utter confusion. We have no problem if they create awareness, but it has been increasingly seen that they are passing orders to which they are just not authorised at all," he said.

On the other hand, the NGO runners in Karuna Sadan take huge pride in the fact that they have been spreading huge consumer rights' awareness by guiding the distressed consumers to approach the consumer forum. "We have catered to as many as 10,000 consumers all these years. We have no legal authority to pass orders and just forward the grievance of the opposite party to them. In our every order, it has been specifically written that the consumer is free to approach the consumer forum," said H S Ahluwalia, secretary general of the NGO.

When asked about the order directing Air India to pay Rs 1.5 lakh besides other orders of compensation, Ahluwalia admitted it was inadvertently done and they have amended their 'mistake'.

Nothing new

* On October 31, 2008, the UT consumer forum said the Consumers Forum, Chandigarh, acted in a careless manner when they asked a newspaper agency to refund the amount of an advertisement which was wrongly published. The UT Forum then dismissed the complaint as no deficiency was found on part of the agency.

* On October 21, 2008, the UT consumer forum accused the NGO of threatening the SDO of Municipal Corporation to pay arrears of a water bill of Rs 7,951. The forum said the NGO adopted an illegal method.

* A notice was also sent to the NGO by the UT consumer forum on October 15 after they wrongly impounded Rs 50 as 'out of pocket expenses' for a case in which an insect was found in a cold drink bottle. They were directed to produce the record of the complaint and to show what action was initiated.

Heading: Lobbying for the post of Mayor begins - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday summoned two principal office bearers of the Consumer Forum Chandigarh, a society located in Karuna Sadan in Sector 11.

The directions were passed in the wake of a public interest litigation filed by Advocate H C Arora.

The petitioner sought directions to the Chandigarh Administration and the Registrar of Societies, Chandigarh, for further directing the 'Consumer Forum, Chandigarh' to change its name as it resembles that of the district level Consumer Disputes Redressal Forums.

The petitioner had submitted that the identical names are creating confusion for the public.

The UT Administration had also filed a reply on its own and also on behalf of the Registrar, Firms and Societies. Stating that the "consumers cannot be misled by virtue of the names of the two entities" the Society justified its existence.

The reply filed by Administration also came under criticism from the court, but the counsel appearing for UT Administration owned up to the mistake in drafting the reply.

Coming down heavily on the Society, the Bench asked: "Tomorrow you may register a society in the name of High Court of Judicature? Can you pass orders giving directions to the PGI for alleged deficiency in service?"

The Chandigarh Administration also earned the wrath of the High Court.

"Are you totally helpless in checking such society using the name of Consumer Forum?" the High Court asked the counsel appearing on behalf of Chandigarh Administration.

The Division Bench then directed the complaints manager and the general secretary of the Society to appear in person.

Making its intentions pretty clear, the Bench clearly directed the petitioner to "examine whether the Society has committed any criminal offence by conducting in the above manner, and whether criminal prosecution can also be directed to be initiated against it."

Heading: High Court holds foster mother guilty of ‘wilful disobedience’ - Indian Express
Content:
As the term of the present Mayor comes to an end on December 31, political parties have started the exercise of wooing councillors.

This time, a Scheduled Caste (SC) candidate will be selected for the post and political parties are doing everything possible to see their candidate taking over the reigns.

While councillor Ram Lal is the candidate for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), former mayor Kamlesh, current deputy mayor H C Kalyan and councillor M S Chohan are the frontrunners for the post from the Congress. The BSP, meanwhile, has no SC candidate who can contest for the post.

The House has 35 councillors of which nine are nominated. Among the elected councillors, Congress has a majority with 14 councillors. The BJP-SAD has 8 seats and the BSP 4 seats. The local MP also has one vote.

The votes of the BSP councillors as well as the nominated councillors would be instrumental in deciding who the next Mayor would be.

The BSP is yet undecided about the support to the candidates. Jatinder Bhatia, leader of the BSP in the House, said: "In the coming days, a meeting would be held with the leaders of the party. A decision would then be taken on who the party would support."

A BJP leader said the party is making all efforts to ensure support of the BSP councillors. The party is, at present, preparing for the visit of L K Advani on November 16.

The elections for the post of the Mayor are important keeping in view the impending Lok Sabha elections. The candidate who is finally elected would play an instrumental role in the elections, sources say.

Heading: Reduced lending rate raises hope in realty sector - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has taken strong note of 'wilful disobedience' of court orders by one Seema Kapoor, a resident of Hoshiarpur. The court had issued showcause contempt notices to Kapoor, asking her to explain as to why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against her.

The directions were passed in wake of a petition filed by Deepak and Jyoti Kapoor, residents of Hoshiarpur and natural parents of Aishley Kapoor, a minor.

The parents had moved the High Court demanding custody of the minor. Seema and her husband, Surinder Kumar, had contended that the minor had been given to them in adoption. The parents and guardians kept battling for her custody. Demanding back the child later, the parents had filed a case in a lower court, which had directed the foster parents to hand over the custody to her natural parents. Challenging the order, Seema moved the High Court, which granted stay on the orders of the lower court. The case was pending ever since. On the last date of hearing, however, the court had directed Seema to appear in the court along with the minor. Seema, however, went to the UK along with the minor without seeking prior permission from the court.

A case was also registered on charges of illegally taking the child on August 12 by Hoshiarpur Senior Superintendent of Police. Taking a dig at Seema Kapoor, the High Court observed: "She spirited away with the minor to the United Kingdom under the guise of a stay order granted by this court and failed to make an appearance. She is guilty of gross and deliberate violation of orders of this court and in my considered opinion, has also committed offences under the Indian Penal Code (IPC)."

Heading: Reprieve to Sanjeev Bansal - Indian Express
Content:
The reduction in benchmark prime lending rate (PLR) by 50 to 75 basis points (bps), announced by the banks has inspired optimism among both the sellers and buyers who expect a revival of the real estate business.

"The impact of this reduction in rates could be seen immediately as developers have started receiving queries from prospective buyers for home purchase," says developer of Dee Ess Associates, Zirakpur, R P Malhotra.

State Bank of India (SBI), had cut their benchmark PLR by 75 basis points (bps) from 13.75 per cent to 13.00 per cent per annum, effective from November 10, 2008.

With the reduction of 0.75 per cent in home loan rates, the buyers would be directly benefited with reduced equated monthly installment (EMI). For instance, the EMI of a home loan by the SBI on a floating rate of 11 per cent would be Rs 1032 per lakh. With the reduction of 0.75 per cent, the EMI would be reduced to Rs 982 per lakh. For a home loan of Rs 25 lakh for 20 years, the EMI would be reduced to Rs 24,550 from the current Rs 25,800.

The Union Bank of India, the United Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Bank of India, Allahabad Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Syndicate Bank and Dena Bank, among others, had already cut their PLRs by 0.75 per cent.

Allahabad Bank and Oriental Bank of Commerce have reduced their PLRs by 75 basis points from 14 per cent to 13.25 per cent. The banks also said they would be reducing interest on term deposits by 50 basis points from December 1.

"Now the prospective home buyers would like to cash on the reduced interest rates. Though, it will take some time for the high value sector like real estate to revive, the developers are hopeful about the movement in the market," says vice-president, ATS Infrastructure Ltd, Ratan A S Bhullar.

It is expected that the remaining PSU banks and leading private sector lenders — ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank — would also announce reduction in lending rates in the coming few days.

Citibank, meanwhile, became the first foreign bank to cut PLR by 50 basis points to 15 per cent.

The reduction was made possible after the Reserve Bank India (RBI) announced to reduce the repo rate - the rate the RBI charges on borrowings by commercial banks - by 50 basis points to 7.5 percent recently.

Heading: Warm Gesture - Indian Express
Content:
The Bar Council of India (BCI) has stayed further proceedings initiated by the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana against Sanjeev Bansal, former Haryana Additional Advocate General and an accused in the cash at judge's door case.

The BCI also issued notices to the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana which has taken suo motu notice of the case and cancelled the licence of Bansal.

The directions were passed today on a transfer petition filed by Bansal in the BCI. Accusing the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana of having a predetermined approach towards him and being biased, Bansal sought transfer of petition from the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana.

In the petition, he submitted that since the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana itself has taken suo motu notice of the issue, it cannot preside over it and decide it. It cannot be the judge of its cause, the petition reads. It was further stated by Bansal that the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana has relied upon irrelevant material while taking suo motu notice of the case. He further stated that rather than relying on any material evidence, the Bar Council has relied upon news item. The Bar Council didn't even touch the FIR, in which my name is not mentioned, the petition reads. Bansal has demanded that the complaint filed by the Bar Council itself should be transferred to the BCI.

Bansal was to file a reply in the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana on November 8 but all the proceedings have now been stayed. Speaking to Newsline, Bansal said that he will soon be filing a revision application challenging the suspension of his licence.

Heading: Beaten in 2007, MC chief in 2008: Sukhwant’s journey to the chair - Indian Express
Content: This World Kindness Day, BIG 92.7 FM have kickstarted 'Raahat Abhiyaan' through which they are requesting city folks to donate old woolen clothes and blankets for slum children. "The day falls on November 13, and so, our RJs suggested that we should collect woollies and give them to those who need the most," said Siddharth Bhardwaj, Regional Director, North - I, BIG 92.7 FM.

Heading: Snatcher held while trying to escape - Indian Express
Content:
For the Kharar Municipal Council (MC) chief Sukhwant Singh, it has been a journey from defeat to victory.

The 35-year-old law graduate was defeated from Ward 8 in the MC by-election on August 8, 2007, only to emerge victorious with his pharmacy postgraduate wife Paramjeet Kaur in the MC General elections on September 14 this year.

While Sukhwant won from the same constituency, which he lost earlier, his wife became the councillor from Ward 11. Riding high on his good fortune, Sukhwant was elected the new president of the Kharar MC on Thursday.

The couple had contested on the symbol of the SAD-BJP combine, with whom Sukhwant's elder brother — Charanjit Singh, an independent MLA from Chamkaur Sahib — had joined hands to contest the polls.

While the couple registered themselves as the only "councillor couple" in Kharar's history, Sukhwant became the second member of the same family to become the Kharar city chief. Charanjit had earlier served as Kharar MC Chief for two terms — 1992 and 2002.

Crediting the entire success to his elder brother, whom he treats as his political "mentor", Sukhwant promised planned and overall development for Kharar with no more illegal colonies and haphazard growth in the area.

Talking to Chandigarh Newsline, the new Kharar city chief said he will strive for the early preparation of the Master Plan of Kharar local planning area, which has already been assigned by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) to the Singapore-based Jurong International Consultants.

Safe drinking water supply and cleanliness along with the provision of better basic civic amenities top Sukhwant's agenda.

"An accountable, responsive and transparent municipal administration with restored dignity and honour of the local residents will be my priorities," says Sukhwant, who runs an LPG agency in Ropar.

Charanjit, meanwhile, is upbeat with his brother's success. "Sukhwant's victory shows that city residents have reposed faith in us after my three consecutive terms," says the proud brother.

Charanjit announced that the new civic body will function under the patronage of the ruling SAD-BJP combine and will impress upon the state government to release maximum funds for putting Kharar on the path of development, which, he said, had stopped after his resignation as MC Chief in March 2007.

Lal takes charge as senior vice-president

Roshan Lal took charge as senior vice-president of the Kharar MC on Friday. Lal is the senior-most councillor in the current MC House after being elected for the fifth consecutive time since 1979. "I will continue serving the public with power and confidence," said Lal after taking charge.

Second stint for Singla as junior vice-president

Jai Bhagwan Singla was elected junior vice-president of Kharar MC for the second consecutive time. In the previous house also, Singla had served on the same post. "My hard work and social service has paid off," says a jubilant Singla, while offering the public his round-the-clock services as before.

'Civic body heads have Congress background'

Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu claimed the new president, senior vice-president and junior vice-presidents have a Congress background. "He miserably failed to accommodate any traditional Akali councillor on any of the three top MC posts," said Sidhu while accusing the Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh for bringing the Kharar MC under the SAD-BJP combine rule.

Heading: Chief Justice inaugurates conference on vascular diseases - Indian Express
Content:
The police arrested a snatcher who had fallen off a speeding motorcycle, which he was riding along with his accomplice after snatching a purse from Phase IV in Mohali late on Thursday night.

Raj Kumar of Gajewal village in Patiala sustained serious injuries from the fall while his accomplice managed to run away, Sub-Inspector Baldev Singh, who is investigation officer in the case, told Newsline.

A purse with Rs 2,200 cash, which the duo had snatched from one Kamaljeet Kaur of Phase IV, was recovered from Raj Kumar.

Around 8.15 pm on Thursday, when Kamaljeet was returning home along with her father Beant Singh, two motorcycle-borne youth intercepted them. Brandishing a knife and a rod, the duo asked to hand them over whatever valuables they were possessing, the police said.

The two snatched away the purse and some important documents from Kamaljeet before fleeing away.

The victim noted down the Chandigarh registration number of the bike and called the local police, which immediately swung into action and sealed all exit points of the city. "In a bid to crash over a checkpost near Madanpura Chowk, the motorcyclists lost control and the pillion driver fell off while the driver managed to speed away," the IO said.

The arrested youth, reportedly unemployed, was remanded to one-day police remand by a local court while a hunt has been launched to track down his accomplice.

"We hope to crack several other cases of snatchings in the area with the help of this breakthrough," Superintendent of Police (City) Varinder Pal Singh said.

Heading: Tagore Theatre to have a director soon - Indian Express
Content:
The 15th annual conference on vascular diseases, VSICON 2008, was inaugurated at the Government Medical College Hospital, Sector 32, by Justice Tirath Singh Thakur, Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. The conference is organised yearly by the Vascular Society of India (VSI).

The meet was presided over by Dr J S Gujral, former HOD, PGI, and saw the presence of Dr K R Suresh and Dr V S Bedi, president and secretary of VSI respectively. The opening of the three-day conference was marked by paper presentation by various experts.

Dr Vinod Bhan presented papers on thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysm repair while Dr H S Bedi presented papers on infrarenal aortic occlusion and catastrophic aortic diseases. The session was jointly chaired by Dr Sunil Aggarwal and Dr Ashish Johari. This was followed by a special session on vascular imaging which saw Dr Anil Hindorani, Dr Prakash Madhavan, Dr S A Hussein and Dr D B Dekiwadia presenting papers on topics including duplex ultrasonography, triplex USG, replacement of a CT scan by duplex scan and DSA as a gold standard diagnostic tool.

Dr Gurjit Singh and Dr Arvind Kohli, president and secretary of VSICON '08 respectively, said that vascular diseases would be discussed threadbare in the course of the conference as an emerging medical stream. "Efforts to enhance awareness within the medical fraternity and among common people will be the key agenda for the experts who have gathered here," they said.

Heading: Two years on, ‘dog bylaws’ still await notification - Indian Express
Content:
Expressions of interest would soon be invited for the appointment of a director at Tagore Theatre. The decision was taken in a meeting of the managing body of the theatre held on Friday. The revised rates to be charged for organising events were also finalised in the meeting.

UT Home-cum-Cultural Secretary, Ram Niwas, proposed that a professional with a background in theatre, art and other cultural activities should be appointed as the director of the Tagore Theatre. "The person should be someone who could envisage, visualise, conceptualise and work out various programmes and promote the theatre as a fulcrum of social, cultural and literary activities," he suggested.

Till a full-time director is appointed, the UT Director of Public Relations (DPR) and Cultural Affairs would look after the additional charge in addition to his own duties.

Members, during the meeting, were in favour of a rate revision citing the reason that the theatre has been renovated and revamped recently involving a huge amount of resources and professional expertise.

It was decided that the rate for functions held by government organisations and amateur artists would be Rs 3,000 excluding service tax of 12.36 per cent and education cess.

For non-government cultural programmes like mushaira, kavi samelans and musical events, which are neither sponsored nor tickets are issued for them, would be charged Rs 10,000 excluding 12.36 per cent service tax and education cess. Tariff for private and public schools, colleges, semi-government organisations, autonomous bodies, NGOs and charitable organisations will be Rs 15,000 excluding taxes.

Meanwhile, for commercially sponsored events or for events having entry by tickets, the charges are fixed at Rs 50,000 excluding taxes.

Booking for the rehearsal hall equipped with an AC would cost Rs 3,000 while a rehearsal hall without AC would cost Rs 1,000. The rates would be applicable for a show of 4 hours and extra charges would be levied on an hourly basis.

Heading: Decomposed bodies found near Panchkula IT park - Indian Express
Content:
It has been two years since the Municipal Corporation (MC) formulated bylaws for managing dogs in the city. Termed as "dog bylaws", these were specific guidelines to be followed for tackling both pet and stray dogs.

In an MC meeting held recently, councillor Brig K S Chandpuri (Retd) raised the issue of the delay in the notification of these bylaws.

The MC had instituted a committee for the formulation of these bylaws. After the committee formulated the detailed rules, residents of the city visited the office of the then mayor, Surinder Singh, requesting that the laws be made less stringent. While these were passed without amendments in the House, they are yet to be notified.

Some of the guidelines entailed in the bylaws include: more than one pet dog not to be allowed in houses up to 5 marlas, pet owners not to be permitted to take dogs to the Sukhna Lake or any other public garden maintained by the MC, pet dogs not to be allowed to defecate in public places like parks and owners to bury their dogs at any barren place, among others. A violation of these rules would invite a penalty upto Rs 500, mandated the rules.

With an aim to check the growing population of dogs, the bylaws also contain specifications on sterilisation and vaccination of stray dogs.

Councillor Dr A P Sanwaria, who was part of the committee that formulated the bylaws, states that these should be implemented at the earliest. "It has been two years since the bylaws were formulated. These would help maintain the beauty of the city and also save residents from the menace of stray dogs," says Sanwaria.
