Heading: Daddy Dearest - Indian Express
Content:
From radio jockeying to television, this live show host is busy juggling tasks

From radio to television, is switching medium a difficult task?
I would say it has been hectic. One live show in the morning on radio and another one on television in the evening have been quite a juggle and struggle. I have been with radio for five years and I have gotten into the flow of things. But TV is new to me. It has a different kind of buzz and it involves greater interaction with the audience.

What is the format of Bindass Live?
This show can best be described as a platform for youth to speak out their minds and voice their grievances. It is a daily show and each episode targets issues like homosexuality, smoking, child rights and many other issues. Every day, we also have artistes from various fields coming on the sets, like DJs, tattoo artists and models.

What was it about the show that appealed to you?
The best thing about youth-based talk shows is that the younger crowd is never diplomatic and very straight forward. They have definite opinions. It is a lot of fun interacting with them because even I get a chance to be myself.

How's the experience of hosting a live show on television?
Live shows are always more difficult, but being an RJ helped me. There are no retakes here, hence you have to do your homework well and have a good presence of mind. If you are going to attempt live television, make sure you are at ease with the idea first.

What according to you are the essentials of being a good host?
I am pretty new to this medium and so talking about the essentials would be tough. But I guess being confident and not feeling distressed helps one in the long run.

Who are you favourite anchors on television?
Internationally, I have always admired Jay Leno in The Tonight Show. I think anyone who is aspiring to become a host has a lot to learn from him. Closer home, I admire Vir Sanghvi. He is spontaneous and has a brilliant screen presence.

What's next on the agenda?
Becoming an actor is definitely on the cards. But right now I am concentrating on radio and TV. Two more production houses have already offered me a couple of assignments on TV, but I am too tied up to commit. I want to grow in my profession at the moment and eventually make it to Bollywood.

(Bindass Live airs on Bindass TV every Monday to Thursday, 7.30pm)

Heading: Bubble Bath - Indian Express
Content:
My Daddy the Crocodile Hunter
Animal Planet
Sunday, Nov 9, 8 pm
Rating***

What's it about? On September 4, 2006, crocodile hunter Steve Irwin died an untimely death in the oceans while filming for his show, when he was speared through the heart by a sting ray. The world lamented the loss of a naturalist who had brought glamour to khaki shorts and had made reptiles and creepy-crawlies seem lovable. This show is a dedication to that man and features his daughter, nine-year-old Bindi Irwin. The special one-hour long programme will take viewers behind the scenes and will show them what it was like to grow up with her famous father.

Who's in it? The show is very ably hosted by a young and charismatic Bindi Sue Irwin. Bindi, who was named by Steve after his favourite crocodile, has spent practically all her life in front of the camera — right from the moment she was born. She's very much at ease and for those worried whether she'll overplay the sentimental card; there's nothing to fear as Bindi manages to keep the mood upbeat; although, fans of Steve, will occasionally feel choked up at the sight of the old Crocodile Hunter footage. Steve's widow, Terry Irwin, gets her few minutes before the camera too, as she talks about her daughter, but essentially the show belongs to little Bindi

What's hot? Steve, Steve and more Steve. The Crocodile Hunter may have died, but his charisma and mystique live on in the behind-the-scenes and home-video footage that his daughter shows. Bindi herself is well on her way to becoming a star in her own right and it shows in the panache and confidence with which she hosts the show. Also, watch it to know why Bindi's tribute to her dad at his funeral received a standing ovation and went on to be declared the TV moment of 2006. The girl speaks from her heart and thankfully, avoids th saccharin sweetness that afflicts so many TV tributes Also, like her father, even bestows goodbye kisses on the little creepy-crawlies that she handles at Australia Zoo. Cute.

What's not? This is not a show for initiates into the world of wildlife conservation, but for confirmed Steve Irwin fans who miss the naturalist and his famously zany ways with animals. Some might also find Bindi a little precocious, as she talks nineteen-to-the-dozen about her dad and sings about how "To you he's the Crocodile Hunter, but to me he was always Dad."

Should you be watching it? Definitely. This is a tribute to one of the TV legends of our times, touchingly told by his daughter. And even of you were never a Steve Irwin fan, do tune into the show to see why he appealed to so many all over the world.

Heading: Bharathi Nrityanjali in Mysore - Indian Express
Content:
With every new soap, half-a-dozen new faces are launched. If we go by the average — five new soaps a month — 2008 alone has seen over 250 new actors on television. The astounding statistics compel one to ask how does the industry absorb so many actors?

Part of the answer lies in the launch of new channels. But the main reason is the dynamics of the industry where a fresh face is preferred over an established name. The known actors then rarely return in lead roles, acceding to play supporting cast in a soap or participating in reality shows.

Often, 'big' faces go obscure once the soap's off the air or the script changes track. They age off, die, get kidnapped or undergo plastic surgery. Sumeet Sachdev, Gautam in Kyunkii Saas Bhi Bahu Thi, was once the lead but generation leaps ate into his role. He's not been part of another show. Now, with Kyunkii's doubtful future, he too may become invisible unless he reinvents himself. Instant recollection yields other such names — Preeti Amin of Jhoom Barabar Jhoom, Poorva Gokhale of Kkoi Dil Mein Hai, Vikas Manaktala and Priyanka Bassi of Left Right Left.

The word in the industry is that the new-face phenomenon is the offshoot of the tantrums the actors throw after tasting success. The producers however, deny this. "The characters on the small screen are more memorable than the actors who play them. So it's difficult to launch, say, a Rajshri Thakur as the lead in another show as people still remember her as Saloni of Saat Phere. Moreover, even though I wish to hire her, I can't, unless I have a script where her character will override Saloni's popularity," explains Sunjoy Wadhwa of Sphere Origin Productions. One can recall how Sakshi Tanwar's role as Ganga in

Kahaani Hamaarey Mahabharat Ki didn't go down well with the audience because they couldn't think of her as anyone but Parvati of Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii.

Rajan Shahi of Director's Kut feels that time commitments also contribute to the strain. "To play the lead is as much a drawback as an advantage. If an actor is shooting for me 10 hours a day, they don't have time to do much else," he remarks. "Besides, soaps are driven by scripts — new faces bring freshness to new characters." Citing an example, he points out that there are hardly any faces in the industry that could have done justice to the four young characters in the new show Miley Jab Hum Tum.

It leads to fierce competition, but these days, with the advent of reality shows and experimentation with scripts, a la Balika Vadhu, the actors have more options. Karan Panthaky, the lead in Jhoom Barabar Jhoom, points out, "Reality shows like Nach Baliye require many senior actors, which paves the way for new ones on other shows." Panthaky has not been seen after his show went off air two months ago. "I'm open to doing non-lead roles; after all, these days, villains are more important."

But Sanjeeda Sheikh disagrees that the career scope of an actor is limited after having played the lead. "My role as a vamp in Kayamath became more popular than my lead character in Kya Hoga Nimmo Ka." Sheikh will soon be seen in a film but says she's happier doing TV. "There's so much to do. I have no complains."

Heading: Rs 10-lakh dream comes crashing down - Indian Express
Content: For the first time, Bharathi Nrityanjali, a unique Bharatnatyam recital based exclusively on Mahakavi Subramanya Bharathi's works, was presented by senior artistes of the Sri Rajarajeswari Bharatanatya Kala mandir on Friday at the Mysore Association auditorium, Matunga. The dance recital was choreographed by Guru Kalaimamani K Kalyanasundaram.Hosted by the Bharathi Medical and Research Foundation to commemorate the 126th birth anniversary of the poet, the dance repertoire depicted select patriotic and devotional  songs and scenes from the immortal Panchali Sabdam.

Heading: Illegal hawkers pose security threat - Indian Express
Content:
17-year-old who used to give hefty tips using stolen money caught

The Mumbai police on November 3 arrested a 17-year-old youth from Ahmedabad for stealing Rs 10.35 lakh from his employer in Borivali. The police said that Raju Sharma (name changed) had stolen the money from one Sanjeev Khurana, owner of the Sawariya Enterprises, on October 27.

According to the Borivali police, Khurana who deals in mobile phone services had approached the Borivali police a day after the theft when he realised that his money had been stolen. He also informed the police that Sharma who had been working with him for past two months was missing . Borivali police registered a case of house-breaking and theft and initiated an inquiry to trace Sharma."During investigations, we came to know from Khurana that Sharma had seen him keeping Rs 11 lakh in the safe. After keeping the money, Khurana had locked it . In the parking lot, Khurana had also handed over his bag with keys, to Sharma so that he could get his car.

According to Khurana, Sharma might have probably stolen the key while he was busy trying to get the car and used the key to open the safe when the office was deserted," said Assistant Police Inspector Prakash Ramgude of the Borivali police station. The police said Sharma's parents had died when he was a child and he was staying with his elder brother and grandmother at Dahisar. He had been staying on his own at Amboli for a couple of years now, said police.

"His grandmother told us that Sharma had gone to visit her at Dahisar and also given her Rs 50,000. He told his grandmother that he had won a lottery and was going to Ahmedabad for some work," said Ramgude.

A police team sent to Ahmedabad nabbed him and brought him to Mumbai. "During interrogation, we found that Sharma had come to Ahmedabad in a luxury bus and spent days staying in luxurious hotels. He also spent Rs 2 lakh on sex workers and was well-known among the hotel staff for handing out tips to the tune of Rs. 500 for room service. We recovered expensive clothes and mobile phones from him. He had only Rs 4.13 lakh remaining with him when we arrested him," said Ramgude. Sharma was produced in the court and remanded to juvenile custody till November 10.

Heading: HC dismisses Balaji’s plea, Kyunki goes off STAR - Indian Express
Content:
Even after the Railways has installed CCTVs at stations and foot over-bridges (FOBs) to ensure round-the-clock security, presence of unauthorised hawkers is becoming a growing concern for the authorities. According to the railway sources, these hawkers, who pose security threat, are convicted every year but resurface after sometime. "The CCTVs have been installed at FOBs for security purpose. At every station, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) has a monitoring cell so that they can keep a watch on the activities going on in the stations. So why can't they remove illegal hawkers?" asked a railway official.

However, Shyam Sunder Gupta, chief public relations officer, WR, said, "We initiate action against hawkers as per the law. After the blast, we have carried out a drive to remove unauthorised hawkers for ensuring safety at railway stations, but they have not been wiped out completely. The drives against them are being carried out continuously to control the increasing number of hawkers."

In 2007, as many as 4301 hawkers were caught on central line and penalties amounting to more than Rs 17 lakh have been imposed on them. In 2008— between January and October— over 3727 hawkers were caught and fined. An amount of over Rs 20 lakh had been collected from them too. Similarly in 2007, in Western Railway, 5281 hawkers were caught and 96 of them were jailed. In 2008, 3177 hawkers were caught and over Rs 11 lakh was collected as penalty.

SC Parhi, senior divisional security commissioner, RPF, Central Railway's Mumbai division, accepted that RPF did not have detailed records of the evicted hawkers. He said, "We only maintain records of place from where these hawkers were caught and not their details. But, the chargesheet submitted to the court contained every detail."Besides this, the commuters also have to face inconvenience due to the presence of hawkers on FOBs.

Heading: Fire at Deonar dump yard sets residents, corporators fuming - Indian Express
Content:
Mega soap Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, whose last episode was aired on Thursday night, failed to get any relief from the Bombay High Court after a vacation bench dismissed the appeal filed by its producer Balaji Telefilms.

The appeal had sought to stay the termination notice served by television channel Star TV, that airs the serial. Balaji, headed by Ekta Kapoor, filed the appeal after a single judge bench of the High Court rejected its petition on November 3.

On Friday a division bench comprising of Justice J P Deodhar and Justice S J Kathawala also denied relief to the production house. Balaji Telefilms had contended that the agreement between the two parties provided that the show will run at least upto March 2009. They also argued that the channel did not fulfill their obligation of promoting the serial through advertising.

However, senior counsel Ravi Kadam, appearing for the channel, contended that they have advertised adequately and that the contract was a terminable one.

He argued that the programme had 'outlived its life' and it had to be taken off the air because the channel was losing viewers and the TRPs had slipped. Star's lawyer Ravi Kadam contended, that the agreement provided that the serial could be stopped if its TRP fell by 20 per cent vis-à-vis the TRPs in June 2008.

Balaji's lawyer Janak Dwarkadas said that it was a 'flagship' programme for both his client as well as Star. He also mentioned that the serial was popular even in Afghanistan. "It made Star what it is today," he said. However, Kadam argued that the serial was not being taken off air because of any malice and contended that fall in the TRPs were hurting Star's advertising revenue. He further argued that the serial had fallen out of the top 10 serial rankings and was lying at the 15th place in October. With the dismissal of the appeal Balaji will either have to move the SC or wait for arbitration proceedings. The agreement provides for appointment of a arbitration panel in case any dispute.

Heading: Six held for attempting to burn Sena office - Indian Express
Content:
A fire raging at the city's largest dumping ground at Deonar has added to the woes of residents in the surrounding areas. While the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation(BMC), despite all its efforts has failed to douse the fire which began early this week, corporators have asked the civic body to carry out a health survey and set up an air monitoring committee to keep a check on the pollution.

There are complaints that the waste from left over Diwali firecrackers which was dumped at the ground resulted in a fire. But Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak claimed that the fire was caused by ragpickers. "Ragpickers set the fire so that biodegradable waste gets burnt and they can easily segregate solid wastes and sell them in the market," he said. "We have asked the fire brigade at Zone 5 to douse the fire as soon as possible. We will also utilising water from the Thane creek to douse the fire."

Corporators said nearly 300 to 400 people from the nearby areas are falling prey to respiratory problems like asthma, acute bronchitis, chronic infection and throat cancer due to the air pollution caused by fire at the dumping ground. "The BARC submitted a report stating that more people are affected adversely owing to a large amount of gases like sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and carbon monoxide which are emitted from the dumping ground," said Shiv Sena corporator and standing committee member Rahul Shewale in a special committee meeting held on Friday.

Corporators have urged the civic body to set up an air pollution monitoring committee and demanded health check-ups in the area. "There should be a door-to-door health check up programme in surrounding slum areas to identify exactly how many people are falling sick due to air pollution," said Shewale. He also said that the committee would help check and control air pollution.

According to the sources, almost 6000 metric tones of solid waste are dumped to the Deonar dumping ground every day. This constitutes around 70 per cent wastes from the city, said sources. The Deonar dumping ground is spread over 110 hectres of land and has been operating since 1927. The civic administration will soon table a proposal of Rs 5,000 crore to develop sanitary landfill and waste processing plant to scientifically dispose of the waste so that the civic body can partially shut down the dumping ground.

Heading: A project caught in legal tangle - Indian Express
Content:
Accused include practising lawyer, cops allege they adequately planned, executed crime

Six persons including a practicing lawyer were arrested by the police on Thursday night for plotting to set afire the Shiv Sena branch office in Bhandup. The accused have revealed that they were acting on the orders of dreaded gangster Bunty Pandey, and that the lawyer was planning to float a party in opposition to the Shiv Sena and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS).

The incident occurred in the wee hours of November 2, when unidentified miscreants poured petrol on the main door of the office and set it on fire. However, a police patrol van passing the area saw and extinguished it. About a week later, the police arrested the accused.

"We have arrested Lala Bhaleram Kagda (21), Manikumar Vincent (28), Santosh alias Satya Dilip Ingle (19), Gautam Govind More (22), Murugesh alias Murugan Kuppuswami (35) and Avinash Ramchandra Rasal, who is a practising lawyer. Except Rasal, the other accused have admitted that they were paid to carry out the act," said Bhandup senior police inspector Prakash Jadhav.

The accused have been booked for arson and criminal conspiracy and were produced at the Mulund Sessions Court. While Rasal has been sent to judicial custody, the other five accused were remanded to the police custody.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone VII) Rajkumar Whatkar also said that during interrogation, "the five accused have admitted that they committed the crime because Pandey had asked them to". "Rasal, who was planning to float a party by the name of Rashtriya Sena, has also admitted that he has represented Pandey in some cases. The party was being planned to combat the Shiv Sena and the MNS' drives against the North-Indians, and Rasal was presently engaged in enrolling members," said Whatkar.

Rasal's lawyer Dinesh Mota argued that his client was being made a scapegoat, just because he was planning to launch a party. "The police have alleged that Rasal was the office bearer of Rashtriya Sena and had paid the other five accused to perform the arson. However, the fact is though Rasal was contemplating launching a party by that name, it is in an embryonic stage at present and yet to be registered," said Mota.

The police have also alleged that the accused would often visit Rasal in his office and the money for performing the act had exchanged hands there last month. "While initially we assumed it was a case of personal animosity or spontaneous vandalism, investigations have revealed that the act had been adequately planned and executed," said Jadhav, adding that "further investigation is underway".

However, Mota refuted the allegations saying 'professional rivalry' may have led to his client's implication in the case. "Rasal has been practising for around 30 years and is a respected lawyer. The police have acted under some political pressure and don't seem to have any evidence to prove their allegations against Rasal," said Mota.

Rasal is a defence counsel who has represented Arun Gawli in 1995 Jayant Jadhav murder case and accused in 2002 Ghatkopar blast case. He has also held the vice-president post in the Bombay City Civil and Sessions Court Bar Association.

Heading: A renovation on fast track... - Indian Express
Content:
Middle vaitarna Bid challenged, project now awaits court nod

Two months after it was cleared, work on the Middle Vaitarna Project to augment water supply for Mumbai's rising population, is yet to begin. Construction of the state's largest dam is already running a month behind schedule and further delays could be likely as the project is in a legal tangle.

The joint venture contract for the Rs 490-crore construction work, was awarded to China International Water and Electric engineering company (CWE), a largescale enterprise under the Chinese government and Soma Enterprises, an Indian firm, for the construction of a vital installation.

But the second lowest bidder, Patel Engineering moved court and the hearing is scheduled for November 11.

"We cannot start the work as the case is in court. The work order has been given to the contractor and we are seeking legal approval whether we can start constructing the approach road to the project site," said deputy municipal commissioner, (water supply) Pramod Charankar.

"If the High Court issues a stay, the project will be further delayed. Otherwise, work will begin by next month," said another civic official.

Work on the project was scheduled to begin on October 1. The dam is set for completion by 2011.

The 105-metre-high dam will be constructed about 145 km north east of Mumbai at Mokhada in Thane district. It one of the most ambitious and costly projects, worth a total Rs 1,600 crore, undertaken by the civic authorities which aims at plugging the water shortfall in Mumbai.

Once completed, the dam will supply an additional 450 million litre of water per day to the city. The dam will be constructed using advanced Roller Compacted Concrete (RCC) technology.

The project had already run into opposition over the award of contract and environmental issues earlier.

Heading: Flats for the poor by lottery on Monday - Indian Express
Content:
Taraporewala aquarium: Taraporewala Aquarium to go fifth-generation

Almost a decade after the efforts to renovate the Taraporewala Aquarium fizzled out, the idea finally got a push on Friday with Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh approving a Floor Space Index (FSI) of 4 for the project.

In 1998, a Singaporean company was roped in to renovate the aquarium, which was started in May 1951 by the fisheries department. But it withdrew from the joint venture as it did not find the government's terms acceptable. The renovation project got stuck in litigation between government and the Singapore company till 2000.

Since then, the aquarium has been in dire straits.

Today, after a presentation by urban development secretary Manu Kumar Srivastava, the government gave its go ahead to increase the FSI from 1.33 to 4. The renovation will be on BOT basis, on a concession period of 25 years.

"Work is likely to start in three months and the entire construction period is two years," said U P S Madan, Project Manager, Mumbai Transformation Support Unit. Four companies from Singapore and Malaysia and two from Australia have been shortlisted.

The city can now look forward to a fifth generation aquarium, like the one in Beijing and Singapore.

The Taraporewala aquarium will then have close to 150 exotic species of aquatic animals in addition to 50 Indian species. Some of the species expected to be displayed include the whale and the shark. The aquarium now has 55 species.

"It will be a fifth generation aquarium. The final design will be decided after the final bidder is chosen. It could even be a seven-storey structure," said Madan. "The new aquarium will obviously be costly and may be out of reach of the lower middle-class. The older building will have an aquarium, to be kept open for visitors at a lower cost, for them."

According to Madan, there is a provision for a dolphin show pool, though it's not mandatory. The new aquarium will have restaurants, an interactive section and educational sections. It will have a 50-metre-long 180 degree tunnel.

Officials admitted that footfalls at the aquarium had decreased over the last decade. In 1992-92, 13 lakh tourists visited the aquarium which dropped to 3 lakh in 2006-07. A survey showed that Mumbaikars wanted the aquarium to be renovated.

Heading: Plea to cancel Raj’s bail adjourned - Indian Express
Content:
870 houses, worth Rs 4 lakh each

The Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) will allot about 870 flats meant for the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) on Monday through lottery.

Since the time MHADA announce the scheme, it drew a tremendous response with over 65,000 people submitting applications for the affordably-priced flats.

On Monday, lots would be drawn wherein a little more than one-tenth of the applicants would be allotted the flats.

"Our lottery system will be completely transparent and it will be conducted using a software certified by the National Industrial Engineering Institute. Those selected, will have to submit necessary documents within 15 days. If they are found to be ineligible for some reason, the flat will go to the next person on the waiting list," said H K Javale, chief officer of the authority's Mumbai board.

The EWS flats, priced at Rs 4 lakh for a 180 sq-ft apartment, are meant for those drawing a monthly salary between Rs 8,000 and Rs 12,000.

The chairman of MHADA's Mumbai board, Amarjit Singh Manhas, said another set of newly-constructed flats in low, middle and high income group colonies would be released by January next. By March next year, the board will complete its ongoing projects in Chembur, Ghatkopar, Dahisar, Chandivli and Sion. These are in addition to the already completed projects in Ghatkopar and Goregaon, while the HIG colony in Versova would create a stock of 3,561 affordable flats in Mumbai by the next year.

"We are also hoping to generate much more housing stock once the policy for granting 2.5 Floor Space Index (FSI) for redevelopment of the MHADA colonies gets final

approval from state government," said Manhas.

At present, there are 1.16 lakh rooms across 56 MHADA colonies in the city. If the proposal is passed, private developers involved in the redevelopment process can use 50% of the rehabilitation area as their sale component. The extra flats through the increased FSI will have to be handed over to MHADA for public housing.

Heading: ‘He dragged me, tied me to pole... iron chain wound around my neck’ - Indian Express
Content:
Hearing an application for cancellation of MNS chief Raj Thackeray's bail granted to him after his arrest in February, a court in Vikhroli on Friday adjourned the matter to November 18, even as the prosecution pressed hard for his personal appearance in court during the hearing.

The bail had been granted to Raj in February, after he was booked under section 153-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) on the charges of inciting enmity between communities.

He was arrested from his Mumbai residence in February after a series of attacks by MNS men on north Indians in Mumbai and other places in the state.

The Vikhroli court had granted Raj bail on the same day but the magistrate, while granting the bail, had imposed a condition that Raj should not indulge in similar acts or give any provocative speeches.

The state had once again acted against the MNS chief in October by arresting him, this time from Ratnagiri (he was granted bail later), after supporters of his party went on the rampage at several centres where examinations were being conducted for recruitment to railway jobs.

The state had thereafter sought the cancellation of the bail granted in February, as he had violated the magistrate's order and the Vikhroli court had slapped a showcause notice on Raj asking him why his bail in the February case should not be cancelled.

While the prosecution tried hard to ensure Raj's presence in the court, Raj's lawyer, Harshad Ponda, argued that he had been exempted from personal appearance.

Heading: Ghaziabad NRI ‘abducted’ on way back from party, ends up in hospital - Indian Express
Content:
BUS DRAMA: Passenger injured in shootout recounts horror

Manoj Bhagat, the passenger injured in the shootout inside a BEST bus, remembers being hit by a bullet in the thigh but cannot say whether it came from Rahul Raj's gun or from a police weapon.

Bhagat is in the medical intensive care unit of Rajawadi Hospital in Ghatkopar, the same hospital where Raj was declared dead. Newsline spoke to him a day before he was to undergo a surgery.

Still in a trauma, Bhagat tried to reconstruct the events of that day. A clerk in a financial company in Belapur, he had boarded the bus from Sakinaka. "The events unfolded so fast that none of us in the bus knew what was happening," he said.

According to the police, there were at least 12 passengers on the upper deck and they were all made to crouch in the three rows in front. Raj asked all the passengers for a phone to talk to the police commissioner; Bhagat threw his mobile beneath his seat, a relative said.

Bhagat said, "I was seated in the fourth seat on the upper deck. He (Raj) was somewhere at the rear end. He first tried to tie the conductor but later let him go.

"He then dragged me till the pole used as a support to climb the stairs. He tied me to the pole. An iron chain, which Raj was carrying, was wound around my neck. I was facing the driver's end and held on to the chain because I was scared that if I was pushed down, I would choke.

"Within minutes I heard firing from both sides. I felt something hit me and when I touched my left thigh, I saw blood and that's when I realised one of the shots I had heard had hit me. I don't know where the bullet came from. The last I saw was policemen rushing up. By then I was barely conscious."

"A surgery will be performed on Saturday by a team of orthopaedic doctors," said Dr Ashok Khankal, the hospital's medical superintendent.

Dr Atul Shah, head of the orthopedic department, said, "He has fractured the upper end of the femur. There is one entry and exit wound. We had to wait for the wounds to heal before surgery as there was the risk of the infection going to the bone. He is now ready for proximal femoral nail (PFN) surgery, where in a rod will be placed on the fractured part that will support the bone."

The family is tense about the hospital bills. "We come from a very humble family. Though he is not the sole earning member, he shoulders the responsibility. We have not yet got the compensation money (Rs 50,000) promised from BEST. Only today the BEST committee chairman came and assured help in two days," said Revanand More, Bhagat's brother-in-law.

Heading: Tatas slapped with Rs 2.5 lakh compensation for selling faulty car - Indian Express
Content:
In a bizarre incident, a Non-Resident Indian was mysteriously abducted from Ghaziabad while he was returning home after attending a get-together, only to end up at a city hospital in a critical state later. The police confirmed that he was admitted to a city hospital but refused to divulge details on where he has been admitted.

According to the case registered at Massoori police station, Ramesh Singhal, an NRI, who owns a departmental store in the US and is a resident of Modinagar, Ghaziabad, had gone to meet few of his friends on Thursday. "He hired a car from Charu Travels to go to Sangam Hotel to meet his friends," said Vijay Bhushan, SP (City), Ghaziabad. According to the police, on his way back home, a Santro stopped near Singhal's car and allegedly abducted him and the driver.

"The police managed to trace the car and the driver, but till late in the evening, Singhal could not be traced. We have just received information that he has been admitted to a city hospital in a critical state," added Bhushan.

According sources in the police, however, the driver and Singhal were allegedly beaten up by goons and robbed near Massoori. Senior police officials, however, maintained that Singhal was abducted. "There was no ransom call made to the family. We are interrogating one Ramveer Singh, who was there with Singhal at the party," said Bhushan.

Heading: Batla encounter: Jamia resident draws ‘vague’ replies on RTI - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Consumer Commission has ordered Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co. Ltd to cough up Rs 2.5 lakh as compensation to a consumer who underwent immense harassment after buying a brand new Tata Indica car, that turned out fraught with numerous manufacturing defects.

Subhash Ahuja, the owner of a furniture shop in Kirti Nagar, had purchased the Indica car in May 1999 for Rs four lakh. The vehicle, however, started giving trouble from the very first day and Ahuja was subsequently forced to take it to the company's service station 36 times in the next six months.

According to Ahuja, the car was at the workshop for repairs even on the date when he filed the complaint against the company. Seeking damages, he adduced various documents and service cards recording all kinds of major and minor faults in the vehicle, including a defective engine that needed replacement.

"There is no worse case than a brand new vehicle verging on a large number of manufacturing defects that is bound to cause mental agony, emotional suffering, harassment, loss of business and expenses incurred for taking the vehicle time and again to the garage," held Commission president Justice J D Kapoor in a recent decision.

According to the consumer panel, the vehicle manufacturer could not be allowed to wriggle out of the liability of selling a defective vehicle by shifting the onus on a consumer to prove his allegations. The culpability would instead lie on the company to establish that the problems were not manufacturing in nature.

"To expect a consumer who has already been wronged by the manufacturer or trader to incur expenses on obtaining expert opinion of automobile engineers and others to prove that the defects are manufacturing or inherent, is neither the object of the law nor the import of the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act," said Justice Kapoor.

Defending itself, Tata alleged that there were no inbuilt defects in the car and the problems occurred due to constant and continuous use of the vehicle for commercial purposes. The defects were merely trivial adjustments and the replacement of the engine was done as a goodwill gesture, it claimed before the Commission.

Justice Kapoor while adjudicating the matter, said he could not lose the sight of the fact that the list of problems, numbered around 30, comprised a full page of his order, displaying that each and every part of the car created troubles.

Holding the company guilty of selling a faulty vehicle, the Commission observed that since no useful purpose would be served by asking Tata to replace the car, a compensation of Rs 2.5 lakh to Ahuja would meet the ends of justice.

Heading: Ghaziabad woman alleges rape by inspector from Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
Says Supreme Court, Delhi Police, NHRC and AIIMS gave out little information

A jamia Nagar resident has drawn a blank from all quarters — Supreme Court, Delhi Police, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and AIIMS ¿ on his RTI application seeking information on the September 19 encounter at Batla House in South Delhi.

According to Afroz Alam Sahil, he had filed four separate applications under the RTI Act on September 25, and the replies, he claims, are vague at best.

The apex court and city police replied 40 days after he filed the RTI, Sahil says.

Alam said he had posed six questions, of which the police submitted answers to just three. The police ignored questions related to the number of arrests and detentions made after the serial blasts in the Capital on September 13.

Alam had also asked for a copy of the postmortem reports of the two alleged militants and Inspector M C Sharma, all killed in the encounter, and the copy of the FIR lodged afterwards. While the police refused to part with copies of the autopsy saying "disclosure of the information may impede investigation", they said "the copy of FIR can only be provided to the complainant".

In the RTI application filed to the Supreme Court, Alam had asked how many cases had been filed against people or organisations in blast cases, and punishment meted out to those convicted. Alam also asked whether there were any cases in which Delhi Police had made arrests but could not provide evidence.

Supreme Court replied that "cases against terrorists are not directly filed in the court", and "it is beyond the jurisdiction and scope of duties of the CPIO (Central Public Information Officer) under the RTI Act to interpret law and judgments of the Supreme Court."

Alam had requested AIIMS to give a copy of the postmortem but the hospital said it could not give out a copy since it was related to the medico legal records (MLC) under Sections 8(1)b and 8(1)h of the RTI Act. These sections are meant for information expressly forbidden to be published by any court. NHRC was asked about the number of police encounters the Commission is looking into, and how many of them were found to be fake. The Commission's reply said it had received 2,560 cases of encounters, of which it granted compensation in 16 cases. But the NHRC did not give details of these 16 cases.

"It is sad that these institutions turned a deaf ear to the power of RTI," Alam said.

Heading: BJP yet to lift veil on Burari candidate - Indian Express
Content:
QUANTUM OF SOLACE
CAST: Daniel Craig, Judi Dench, Mathieu Amalric, Olga Kurylenko, Gemma Aterton;
DIRECTOR: Marc Foster
This 007 had everything going for it: Daniel Craig, who wowed audiences and critics alike in his first outing as Bond, not a mean feat considering how long the hunt was for the new MI6 agent; Judi Dench in a meatier role as M; Paul Haggis (Crash, In the Valley of Elah) as writer; and Marc Foster (Monster's Ball, Finding Neverland) as director.
However, Quantum of Solace ain't no Casino Royale. That film gave us a Bond we had never seen before: a bruised and confused 007, as capable of getting hurt as hurting. He found and lost love in the film, going through a betrayal in the middle.
Though Quantum of Solace picks up from there, with a Bond determined to avenge that love, against unknown forces who killed her, it eventually turns out to be just an excuse to hang two hours of uninterrupted— interchangeable with convoluted— action and some great actors on (including the two Bond women, with not a decent cocktail dress between them).
The plot, moving from Rome to London to Haiti to Austria to Bolivia, back to Italy, then to Russia, is so complicated that you better give up pretending you care. Greedy dictators, compromised governments and oil politics are thrown about.
It doesn't help that the villain apparently running circles around half the world's governments is an effete pretender (Almeric) who probably won't be able to convince a classroom of kids of his eco-friendly intentions. To dress him up in Hawaiian shirts and a languorous gait is an insult to our intelligence.
Craig looks great and, once in a while, still uses those piercing blue eyes to good effect. But he has none of the spark, wit or wisdom to transcend him above the other J B — Jason Bourne.
As boats crash into ships, planes collide into mountains and entire hotels go up in blasts, we are left looking for precisely the same thing as Bond apparently is: some quantum of solace. None of us is getting it, at least in this film.

2 DAYS IN PARIS
CAST: Julie Delpy, Adam Goldberg, Albert Delpy, Marie Pillet;
DIRECTOR: Julie Delpy
IN Julie Delpy's Before Sunrise and its sequel Before Sunset, a couple find love that comes once in a lifetime in a few brief, hastily snatched hours before they part. She also wrote the screenplay of the latter. Here, Delpy, writing, directing, editing, starring and singing, catches up with a couple who have spent two years together but take just two days in Paris to realise that they really don't know much about each other.
Does time make love stronger, or does familiarity erode romance? Does love happen at first sight, or need love be blind? Does past not matter, or is it the future?
Delpy explores all of this, pointing out how definitions are pointless when love is all that, and more — before sunrise, before sunset, in the darkest hours of the night, and the hottest hours of the day. The beauty is her manner: insightful while being quirky and funny. Here is a film that keeps its eyes open and also its heart, generous to all that it touches, including the five odd drivers of the taxis the couple take.
Semi-autographical, 2 Days in Paris stars Delpy as a French photographer Marion, who has flown in to the French capital with her American boyfriend, interior designer Jack (Goldberg). The reason is partly to see Paris, and partly to visit Marion's parents (played delightfully by Delpy's real-life parents Albert Delpy and Marie Pillet).
Jack is the clichéd American tourist, shocked by a Paris that is cliché tres francais. What he doesn't bargain for, however, are Marion's ex-lovers, who seem to be crawling out of everywhere into their lives. As says the film's tagline: "He knew Paris was for lovers. He just didn't think they were all hers."
In its humour, quirkiness and observations, 2 Days in Paris has flashes of Woody Allen. However, there's one significant difference. Delpy brings to this film what Allen wouldn't: in this Obama season, may we say, the audacity of hope.

FLASHBACKS OF A FOOL
CAST: Daniel Craig, Harry Eden;
DIRECTOR: Baillie Walsh
HERE is a project apparently hoping to ride on Craig's Bond shoulders, not to mention the rest of his nicely-taut and nicely-on-exhibit body.
However, don't be fooled. Just as you are getting used to the fact that he is a Hollywood star fast burning himself up on drugs and sex, and has a tormented past to boot, Craig disappears for almost the rest of the film.
It's, after all, about the flashbacks of a fool. And in flashback, Craig is played as a 15-year-old by this short, skinny blonde guy (Eden) who could have been endearing in his nervous teens but is, at best, irritating. The film is about one hot summer where things came together and then fell apart for this teen, Joe.
As summer-coming-of-age films go, Flashbacks of a Fool has little new to offer in terms of story, mood or even the setting — three lonely cottages by a rocky seashore. What it does have is a surprising amount of nudity. But in a film playing so hard for effect, even that gets barely a raise.

EMI
CAST: Sanjay Dutt, Arjun Rampal, Malaika Arora Khan, Urmila Matondkar, Ashish Choudhary;
DIRECTOR: Saurabh Kabra
There are two films in EMI — one, in which Malaika Arora Khan comes on every 10 minutes shaking her booty, in clothes getting skimpier by the minute, and another, in which four old men have a genuine conversation about their children in which the latter are allowed to have ambitions and to travel abroad without breaking their parents' hearts.
The sad part is that while Kabra could nicely shake and mix up the two, he makes no effort to. The two films run parallel in EMI, the good parts being interspersed with the truly appalling.
And Kabra is working with a nice idea here and a fairly good script involving four different families who have all taken loans and are now defaulting on their EMIs for varied reasons. One a newly married and quickly separated couple; another a DJ who spends more than he earns; the third a father who has borrowed to send his son abroad; and fourth a woman paying off the mob to get her husband's suicide turned into a murder to claim the Rs 2-crore insurance.
There are some very funny moments, like the smooth-talking personal bankers who won't be fazed by lecherous customers or cautious ones; the innovative gangsters who help you in getting bank loans so you can pay up their money, in installments; Sanjay Dutt, who can now do these roles of a kind-hearted gangster in his sleep and who here, in the placement of his expensive dark glasses a little too unevenly down his nose, conveys both his ambitions and limitations; and his gang of small, Munnabhai-esque lumpens.
And there are some very unfunny ones: Rampal, confusing himself once again as a serious musician (in a tweed hat, for God's sake); Choudhary's twitching moustache that has more emotion than the rest of his face combined; Urmila's grieving-widow act dressed in expensive saris, including a transparent red piece, designer suits and twirling wine; and Malaika's ever-shortening wardrobe.
Please, for our sake and yours, get a makeover.

SHALINI LANGER
shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Rajendra Soni - Indian Express
Content:
Waiting for Congress to spell out their's, says Jaitley

Even three days after announcing the list of candidates from all other seats, the BJP is mum on the name of the candidate from Burari in Northwest Delhi. A Poorvanchali-dominated seat, the decision on it was withheld at the last moment after a late night meeting between the state and the central leadership held on Monday.

Burari has a population of nearly 2.12 lakh voters, with 34 per cent of them belonging to OBC and 16 per cent from the SC. "We're waiting for the Congress to declare their candidate before fielding our choice," said BJP leader Arun Jaitley. The state BJP leadership had already decided upon their candidate although at the last moment inputs came from the central leadership which stalled the announcement.

At present, the sitting MLA here is Zile Singh Chauhan of the Congress. The BJP has never been able to win the Burari seat in any of the past Assembly elections. In the last Assembly polls in 2003, the BJP candidate finished a poor fourth. Although the BJP's situation has improved here in the last Assembly elections when it won a majority of the seats, the Congress is also yet to announce its candidate. BJP insiders claim the party is planning to rope in a Congress dissident here in case the party fields Zile Singh Chauhan again.

Party worker Gopal Jha has been staking his claim over the seat. "I have nurtured the seat and converted it from a Congress stronghold to BJP territory. Jha, however, is on a sticky wicket as he lives in Faridabad. It would be unfair to give it to someone else," said Gopal Jha. Meanwhile, Poonam Azad is also gunning for the seat. Other contenders, including the party's initial choice Vijaya Sharma, are also vying for it.

Meanwhile, BJP has reportedly told Kalpana Jain, the Gandhinagar, to withdraw her nomination because of opposition from party cadres. Education Minister Arvinder Singh Lovely of the Congress is contesting from the seat. On Thursday, Jain was not given the party symbol.

BJP leader Harsh Vardhan said, "She's in a dilemma, but haven't heard anything. The BJP list will be left with only three women if Jain withdraws."

Heading: Prashant ready for the step-up - Indian Express
Content:
It's not the fantasy world of Harry Potter, but the brilliance of its creator JK Rowling that caught Nalini Singh's attention. No magic spells work in golf after all; it's the mind that does the tricks.

"It's amazing what she's done in those books, the way her imagination has run wild," she says, talking to Sportline on Friday.

Nalini wrapped up her rookie season's second win on the women's professional tour on Friday, one off the lead when she started the final round at the fifth leg at the Golden Greens club in Gurgaon, but a winner by four in the end. "My game was really steady today. I was a little off the lead, but I knew that if I didn't make mistakes early on, I would be in with a chance. That's exactly how I played," she says.

Her first win, at the Delhi Golf Club in the season's opening leg, had come in much different fashion, as she led from the first day to the last. She's hasn't gone out of the top three in the five tournaments till now: Two other second places (at the second leg at the Qutab Golf Course and the third in Panchkula) and a third place at Chandigarh.

The 19-year-old turned pro in November 2007, and watching the pros in the Indian Masters and the Indian Open, she knew there was work to be done on her game to make a mark in the professional grind. So in the off season, it was back to the drawing board, tweaking the swing with coach Anitya Chand, polishing the putting, and making sure that translated into a more controlled game when on the course.

"I know I have the technique. But golf is so much of a mind game, and that is the aspect I really want to strengthen now," she says.

The third-year Mathematics Honours student at Venkateshwra College makes sure those the numbers on her other scorecard stay in check too; she scored a cool 82 per cent last year.

Heading: Jain’s new rise in the East - Indian Express
Content:
Five Man of the Match adjudications in six outings makes your Man of the Series award a mere formality. With Prashant Bhandari, a similar moment came two years ago when he brought home the Player of the Tournament prize playing for North Zone in the Under-13 category.

2006 was a flop of sorts but this year, Bhandari is looking all set break into the U-15 squad after amassing 629 runs and 12 wickets from six matches in the inaugural School Cricket League, recognised by the Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA).

Bhandari averaged 200-plus with four unbeaten knocks and as many centuries. But among them, his unbeaten 175 against DLDAV tested his character.

"We're (Hansraj School) six down for 91 odd. I really had to apply my mind for each run. I finally remained unbeaten on 175 and we won the match," says Prashant.

Coach Jai Prakash joined the school hand-in-hand with Prashant and has seen the 14-year old right from the time he took his first stance. "I have taught him how to take stance and since then it's been a process of quick learning and quicker application. He's different from others in the way he picks things up. The same thing you would need to repeat to others Prashant will pick immediately. His application is even better. He is a very quick learner," says Prakash.

Talk to him about his idol, Prashant, without a second thought, will name Sachin Tendulkar, but will hit back even on the slightest comparison: "I never copy his (Sachin's) style. I have my own style of play."

After stealing the show with a number of front foot shots, for a moment, he sounded a bit on the backfoot. "I got out in the second delivery in the final for a duck. It's disappointing not to have contributed in the final after making so many runs throughout the tournament," he says.

Father Bhim Singh Bhandari, unlike most other parents, didn't find a reason to pull things back. "He's a 90-percenter in school and the sixth-ranked in the class. As a class IX student, he's doing very well. Education becomes a problem at a certain stage with players continuing with their studies, but it's important for a player as well," says Bhandari senior, adding, "The only thing he needs to concentrate on is his temperament. Whenever, he gets out early, he gets nervous and the frustration shows in his approach as a captain."

Heading: Go Goa - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana pacer finds form with Tripura

Vineet Jain had a dream first-class debut, a five-for for Haryana back in the 1993-94 season. The medium pacer went on to pick 160 wickets from 57 matches before being dropped because of poor form in 2001.

After two years of rag picking, he found a new home in an oblivious corner of the country — Agartala — and hasn't looked back.

"Before the 2004-05 season Tripura were looking for fast bowlers and that was my chance to come back," says the 36-year old.

Coincidentally, his second essay began against Haryana where he finished with six wickets for the match. After five years of flying between Chandigarh (his home) and Agartala, Jain's performance has shown no evidence of age; in fact the average has improved with 78 wickets from 19 appearances.

The challenge of playing with a low profile team helped. "Tripura had been a low-ranked team. The experience is very little, therefore the pressure is there. But if you look at the last three years, their graph is going upwards and they have a very talented bunch of youngsters," says Jain.

Better with age

If he seems to be getting better with the age, there's one more reason to it. "With Pradeep Jain, Pankaj Thakur and I playing for Haryana, the wickets got divided among us. Both of them were spinners (Pradeep and Pankaj), and hence got more wickets than I did. With the Tripura team, I get more chances to have a go at the batsmen," he explains.

He made the most of his chances in the just finished Ranji trophy Plate Division match against Services, bagging the Man of the Match award (64 runs and five wickets).

The majority in team speaks a different language, hasn't it been a handicap? "There's never been a problem of communication. All of them can speak Hindi and I also had to adjust a bit. The time I've spent with Tripura so far, has been the best part of my career," says Jain.

Jain's best first-class batting performance in terms of his runs and the given situation came against Services (58 runs off 61 balls). As he shied away from any further conversation on his performance, opponent coach Jai Prakash Pandey had some observations to make. "It's about his attitude. Look at the way he's chasing the ball just after bowling an over. He's a true team man. This was evident from the way he batted as well," says Pandey, pointing to a boundary saved by Jain at long on.

"He's also one of the most shy players off the field, one of the best behaved. But don't take that for a weakness. You wouldn't find a more aggressive player on the field, even at 36," adds Pandey.

Heading: Striking Home - Indian Express
Content:
All ye trapped in landlocked, wintry Delhi and left longing for the sun, sea and sands of Goa, here's good news. Goa is recreated at the annual festival on the lawns of Goa Sadan on Amrita Sher-Gil Marg. Organised by the tiny Goan community in and around the Capital, the fest promises a good dose of traditional feni cocktails and dishes like chicken xacuti, pork sorpotel and prawn vindaloo. Since no evening in Goa is complete without some great music, there's The Big T, a band flown in to belt out upbeat Konkani and English numbers. Adding to the ambience are the Goan dancers who perform traditional dances such as Ghode-Modnim (horse dance) Divli-Naach (lamp dance) and Corridinho (a legacy left behind by the Portuguese) among the more popular Dekhni and Mando. This year also introduces a painting exhibition by Goan artists. And then there are the stalls selling Goan handicrafts, spices and condiments. Well, asking for the sea would be a bit too much.

The Goa Fest is on till November 9. It is at 18 Amrita Sher-Gil Marg.

Heading: Shushing the Snob Sushi - Indian Express
Content:
It was a subject so disturbing that director Sohaila Kapur waited five years before putting Tattoo, a German play about incest, on stage. "Even then, many actors refused," says Kapur of the Hungry Heart Festival. The play, which premieres on November 7, is "two hours of grim intensity".

Written by contemporary German playwright Dea Loher, Tattoo goes deep into a family where a father has been abusing his daughter over the years. A glimmer of hope emerges when the girl falls in love and makes her bid for freedom, only to be foiled by a weak lover and the ghosts of her past. The names and the costume have been Indianised: Loher's protagonist Mr Baker becomes Mr Waris, played by theatre veteran Ramesh Thakur, while the rebel younger daughter Lulu becomes Lali. The abused daughter, Anita, has been played by Jyotsana Sharma, a far cry from her bubbly persona in Hungry Heart's previous production Ouch. Mr Waris' wife, enacted by Smita Bharti, remains nameless — a symbol of her psychological trauma that reduces her "into an animal that's been beaten into submission". Kapur has added a few strains of music but it only adds to the tension. "There is no comic relief, it remains intense all through," says Kapur.

Produced in association with the Goethe Institute, Tattoo

has been treated like a book, with a screen lighting up

with chapter titles such as "Love", "Marriage" and "Tattoo" before every sequence. As one member of the cast says, "The effect is cathartic."

Tattoo will be staged at 7.30 pm at Akshara Theatre, Baba Kharak Singh Marg, on November 8. Contact: 23329506

Heading: Hips Don’t Lie - Indian Express
Content:
It grills tongues and boils octopuses, but Komachi is essentially about no-fuss, home-style Japanese food

The pellets of vinegared rice would be so perfectly wrapped around a blushing-pink salmon and then twined with a green thread of nori, the whole thing looking like a Hokusai print with not one careless line, that you would think damaging it with chopsticks and dousing it in soy would be sacrilege. Japanese diners in the Capital have always awed you with their snobbish sushi and artistic sashimi that dining at Komachi in Gurgaon, with its no-fuss Japanese cuisine, is a revelation — and a relief.

Komachi, Japanese for beautiful woman, is steadily becoming popular with southeast Asian expatriates who are in search of a quick lunch or a lazy supper without the frills of fancy dining or expensive cheques. Set up by Emi Kanazawa, who has been staying in India for 22 years, the restaurant attempts to provide comfort food to homesick expats. "I settled here after marrying an Indian and spent most of my time looking after his export business. I missed home food since most Japanese diners are terribly expensive and very formal," she says, in between greeting guests who begin to pour in for a midweek dinner. Kanazawa comes from Osaka, a quaintly beautiful town on the mouth of the Yodo River. And for the restaurant, she has brought in three chefs from her hometown to put together a simple, home-style menu

The restaurant has tatami-floored zashiki rooms with low seating and a bar counter that stocks sochu and sake, apart from cans of beer. The walls are lined with beautiful textiles with Japanese prints, mostly images of cherry blossoms. The table is laid out with sashimi, prawn tempura, meat grills and miso soup in beautiful lacquered bowls and stoneware plates. We begin with prawn tempura (Rs 350), served with a heap of crushed radish, wasabi powder and a salty dip. We peruse the menu and are impressed with the unusual items. How about grilled red meat tongue (Rs 350), fresh boiled octopus (Rs 500) and smelt fish served with roe (Rs 350) for a change? And then there is barbecued eel with a tawny glaze — hot and crispy. The menu also, surprisingly, lists mushroom pasta (Rs 380) and steak (Rs 500). "Actually, most Japanese cook these dishes at home and these taste very Japanese," says Kanazawa.

Next we try Temaki sushi (Rs 800) — three big cones of rice and fish in seaweed rolls, not those high-maintenance Hokusai rolls. "At most homes, this is how we eat sushi. It is easy to make and no one bothers about colour-combinations," she says, picking up a pouch and dipping it in soy dressing before biting into it. That is refreshingly raw.

Meal for two: Rs 1,200
Contact: 95124-4363526
Location: Third Floor, MGF Plaza Mall, Gurgaon

Heading: Take One - Indian Express
Content:
A belly-dance workshop gives you tips and tricks to master the seductive moves

If you could never summon up the courage to burn up the dance floor because you simply didn't know how, check out Fayruz Nur, a two-day workshop on Egyptian Oriental Dance that begins this afternoon at the Salsa India Dance Company's main studio at Greater Kailash II. And you can even breathe a sigh of relief if you're not a size zero. The original belly dancers flaunt a luscious shape while moving seductively to a mix of Turkish and Egyptian beats.

"The idea of the workshop is to promote that anybody can belly dance. We want to highlight the liberation associated with the form," says Meher Malik, 20, who has organised the workshop with her Israeli friends, dancers Merav Mizrahi, 34, and Michal Godfrey, 33. The trio rue the status of belly dance in India, thanks to its sleazy misrepresentations in Bollywood. "It's not about seduction. Originally, in Arab countries, where women have been so suppressed, belly dance emerged as a way to express their sexuality and revel in the beauty and the rhythm of their bodies," says Godfrey, who is a personal stylist when she's not putting you through the moves. It's true, in tribal regions in the Middle East, belly dance was the equivalent of Lamaze classes. But what the weekend workshop aims to do is much simpler.

The workshop is divided into different categories to teach eager beavers the art of relaxation and control. "We will experiment with the figure eight, circular movements and movement in flow, focusing on the core area, pelvis and chest. Also, we want to emphasise that one can belly dance to any kind of music," says Malik who is also conducting a workshop on "Belly-popping", a crossover world of belly dance and hip hop with moves inspired from reggaeton, dancehall, American tribal belly dance and hip hop. Mizrahi advises one to wear a skirt and a top and carry a thick and shiny veil, yes, they're teaching you how to reveal only what is essential. But the most interesting part of the workshop is the hafla. "A hafla is the belly dance's equivalent of social dancing. Towards the end of the workshop, students will be invited to do their own thing and share moves with each other," says Malik. Yes belle.

The workshop is at E5 Basement, GK II Enclave, from noon to 8 pm, on November 8 and 9. Rates vary from Rs 600 to Rs 3,300.

For registration, contact 9891257210

Heading: Maya engineering in reverse gear: City youths form party for upper castes - Indian Express
Content:
Model-turned-actor Mugdha Godse on life after Fashion

When director Madhur Bhandarkar came to Mugdha Godse with the script of Fashion, the model was unsure about how her character would make an impact, considering the stronger roles for co-actors Priyanka Chopra and Kangana Ranaut. "But that was before I read the script. Once I was through, I knew Janet's character had as much scope to perform. If

I did it with honesty, it could get me a little appreciation," says Godse.

In the movie, she plays the second-rung model, Janet, married to a gay designer.

It has been a week since the movie released, but the "little appreciation" that Godse had hoped for, has snowballed into generous accolades. "There's been a steady stream of congratulatory messages and phonecalls. Priyanka texted 'Babe, you blew my mind!' at three in the morning, and I was totally floored. The one person who is vindicated is Madhur sir. Everytime he told me I had it in me to make it as an actor, I would tell him not to speculate. Now, with each review that I have received, he has been telling me 'I told you so'," she giggles.

For Godse, the most touching praise has come from her family. "My family is quite critical of me, so I was apprehensive of their reaction. They went for first-day-first-show, when I was still promoting the film in Dubai. My sister later told me they were left speechless by my performance," she says.

There have been quite a few offers since the movie released, but the model-turned-actor says she will only announce them once she signs on the dotted line. "As of now, I have signed with Percept Picture Company for three of their films," she says. Modelling, she says, will definitely be on the backburner for the time being. "Fashion's given me opportunities which I would be stupid to ignore. It's not as if I am giving up modelling completely, but I'll do only select shows," she says.

Heading: Asked to stub it, smokers in Ramjas beat up fellow students inside college - Indian Express
Content:
While the Bahujan Samaj Party struggles to work out a caste engineering formula for Delhi ahead of the Assembly elections here, a bunch of youngsters seem to have taken a leaf out of Mayawati's book while launching a party of their own.

Their formula, though, is the exact opposite to that of the BSP supremo: Rashtriya Sawarn Shakti Party aims to focus on the plight of upper caste poor, and the youth.

Formed by students from various colleges in Delhi, the party is aiming to fight both the upcoming Assembly elections as well as the Lok Sabha elections due next year.

The party recently registered itself with the Election Commission of India. Besides Delhi, the party would also contest the Assembly elections in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, Sanjay Sharma, the party's national president, said.

"Most of the workers in our party are aged between 20 and 30 years," Sharma said. "We are a new party with youngsters and have decided to do what most people (read youths) only discuss."

At 40, Sharma is the oldest member of the party.

He said the party was formed to highlight the neglect by mainstream political parties of "genuine issues" facing the country's upper caste population. "We have at least 10,000 workers in Delhi alone, and most of them have been inspired by the issues that have been ignored by the national leaders," he said.

Sharma had been a part of the protests against the Mandal Commission report on reservations in 1991-92 and said he later decided to quit activism to "pursue my career in business" — he is now involved in the construction trade.

Mohit Bhardwaj, the party's secretary, said: "We have a lot of work to do before people even recognise us nationally. But we have a good base and are hoping to make our presence felt (in the coming elections)."

The other office-bearers of the party are J P Sharma, vice-president; Subhash Sharma, general secretary; and J P Garg. All three are still in their twenties. Sharma said the party is at present finalising the list of candidates who will fight the upcoming Assembly elections in Delhi and other states later this month and early December. "We are aiming to fight about 50 seats in the Delhi Assembly elections," he said.

The party members claim to have roped in some of the big names from among the political circles and say they will be making the final announcements next week.

Heading: Thampu: Rahul feels Stephen’s still needs to improve quality - Indian Express
Content:
Days after the countrywide ban on smoking in public places was implemented, three Ramjas College students were allegedly beaten up by collegemates when they asked the latter to not smoke on campus.

According to sources, the incident occurred last week when five second year BA students — Sandeep Singh, Vineet Kumar, Harinder Singh, Ashwini Pala and Vijay Nehra — left their hostels to have tea at the DUSU office late at night.

"These students left their hostel around 12.30 am when they spotted four other students — Abhishek, Manas, Pranav Shukla and Vijay Nehra — smoking at the college gate," a senior officer said. "Sandeep, one of the victims, asked them not to smoke there as it was a no-smoking zone, and also pointed to a 'smoking ban' poster put up at the gate."

According to the officer, a heated argument broke out between the two groups at this point. But Sandeep and his friends soon left for tea at the nearby late-night kiosk.

Around 1.15 am, when the victims returned to their hostel, they found four students awaiting them, armed with iron rods, grills and sticks, the officer said. The foursome allegedly beat up three students, while the other two escaped and took their complaint to the police.

"Sandeep Singh, Vineet Kumar and Harinder Singh were allegedly beaten up by students while Ashwini Pala and Vijay Nehra managed to escape," the senior police officer said. The victims stay in room 7 of Ramjas College Hostel.

Police officers said soon after they received the complaint, beat police officers rushed to the spot and the three were admitted to hospital. "They were discharged the next day after medical examination," the senior officer added.

Sandeep Singh wrote in his complaint, "I was beaten up by four other students whom I can identify very well. I suffered injuries in my head and my two other friends also suffered injuries."

The officer said an FIR (number 147/08) has been registered at Maurice Nagar police station and investigations are on. The accused have been booked under Sections 308, 323 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code. No arrest has been made yet.

Heading: HC to police: Don’t rush to the TV cameras, get back to work - Indian Express
Content:
Principal Valson Thampu of St Stephen's College and the institution's prominent alumnus Rahul Gandhi had a freewheeling talk a few days ago, on the state of education in the country in general and, more particularly, on Gandhi's recently-aired grouse that his alma mater did not "encourage asking questions".

The Congress leader — during a chat with students of an Uttarakhand school — was comparing the quality of education in India with that abroad, when he had suddenly remarked: "When I was studying at St Stephen's College, asking a question was not (perceived to be) good in our class. You were looked down upon if you asked too many questions."

The comment precipitated a flurry of criticism from other alumni, prompting Principal Thampu to pick up the phone last week to find out what Rahul Gandhi had actually meant — or did not mean. The former student wanted to take it further and invited the principal for a chat. During the meeting, Gandhi made it evident that he "remembers the college with great affection". "But he feels it still needs improvement, particularly in stimulating the spirit of inquiry. He strongly feels education is not just about degrees and employment. He is concerned that education of the kind pursued today in the country promotes intellectual passivity, which is inimical to growth," Thampu said.

Thampu added: "I found him to be a very free and open person. This is positive criticism. I told him the people who are remembered in history are those who bring about change." Thampu remembers Gandhi as a "well behaved, disciplined boy". He taught Literature at St Stephen's when Gandhi was studying History.

The principal had his own criticism for those who lionise St Stephen's — its alumni are particularly known to have a stiff upper lip. He said: "There are those who are irked by any irreverent reference to the college. Ironically, by doing so, they prove Rahul right. There is no harm in cherishing a college's brand value. But it cannot be the only thing... I feel disappointed when St Stephen's — or any institution of excellence — is turned into an idol, as though it has arrived for ever." Some of the criticism, he felt, should egg on the college to grow. "If we have to sustain ourselves, we have to think afresh," Thampu said.

That is a view Rahul Gandhi should agree to.

Heading: Day after, DUSU president backs ABVP vandalism, says: Geelani, a terrorist, shouldn’t have been invited - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday slammed senior police officers for rushing into press conferences to disclose "leads which are not leads at all" in sensational cases with little concern for an "honest" probe.

"Press conferences are hampering your own investigations. As an investigating body, don't you know how to preserve your evidence... these press conferences are giving away leads," a Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar told senior Delhi Police counsel Mukta Gupta.

The court was hearing a petition on the veracity of the police version on the Jamia Nagar encounter. Two alleged Indian Mujahideen militants were killed on September 19.

The judges criticised the conduct of top policemen, drawing from several recent "sensational" cases: the murder of 14-year-old Aarushi Talwar in May, the Jamia encounter in September, and the killing of journalist Soumya Vishwanathan last month.

"Is it a policy to arrange press conferences where your police officers go on to disclose leads which turn out to be no leads at all?" Justice Muralidhar asked. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Alok Kumar and his counterpart in South Delhi Police, H G S Dhaliwal, were present in court.

The Chief Justice said: "Look at what happened in the Aarushi case and the Soumya case... you have not been able to come up with any leads at all. Your officers engage in selective leak of information which surely affects the evidence in hand."

At this point, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Gopal Subramanium intervened on behalf of the police to contend that press conferences are usually held to "appease the public's right to know". The ASG said, "After a sensational event, lack of information causes a certain degree of public unrest. The public wants to know as soon as possible."

But he added that it was indeed pertinent to "draw the line": "We have to strike a balance between informing the public and making police officers accountable for making excessive disclosures... this requires a certain degree of introspection by the probe agencies as there is no existing codification of guidelines on interaction with the media," Subramanium conceded.

The ASG, however, justified the need for press conferences: "We live in times when civil rights activists go to police stations for information and then pass it on to the media. Police at times feel that it is better they call these press meets and brief the media themselves."

Earlier, advocate Prashant Bhushan, who had filed the petition, complained how his attempts to see the Delhi blasts accused in custody were repeatedly turned down by the police. "I and my father, a former Law Minister, visited the Special Cell office and even the Home Minister, who asked us to file an application to see the accused. But still, the police were reluctant to allow us in," Bhushan said.

Heading: Kanpur court receives bomb threat - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi University Students' Union president Nupur Sharma today called S A R Geelani a "terrorist" and gave a tacit approval to the act of violence by ABVP activists against the professor during a seminar on communalism at Delhi University on Thursday.

"No one follows non-violence anymore," Sharma, from the by BJP-backed Akhil Bharatiya

Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), said. "If somebody slaps you on one cheek, you can no longer show them the other cheek."

On Thursday, a group of ABVP activists had protested violently before Geelani could have his say during the seminar, organised at the university's Art Faculty. One activist went to the extent of spitting at Geelani. The row forced the police to intervene and goad away the activists.

Sharma today maintained that Geelani, exonerated by the Supreme Court in the 2003 Parliament attack case, should not have been invited for the seminar. "Geelani is a terrorist and I had politely requested him to leave the venue," Sharma said. "But he refused."

The protest by ABVP activists began at this point.

Meanwhile, the Left-leaning Students' Federation of India (SFI) and All India Students' Association (AISA) protested the incident at the university today. Robert Rahman Raman, a DU student and a member of SFI, said: "Neither DUSU nor Nupur Sharma can decide who can speak in DU and who cannot. If they wanted to protest Geelani's presence in the university, they could have listened to him and then asked him questions."

But the DUSU president said yesterday's protest was fuelled partly because most of those fighting her and other ABVP activists back were from outside the university. "There were a large number of students opposing us who did not belong to Delhi University," she said. "They attacked us first.

"Who has given a right to outsiders to come to DU and conduct a seminar without any permission?"

Sharma said she has shot off a complaint letter to Vice-Chancellor Deepak Pental regarding this.

While Sharma stressed on the need to restrict entry of outsiders in the campus, the rest of DUSU panel belonging to the Congress-affiliated National Students' Union of India (NSUI) refused to comment on the incident.

Heading: The common thread between Lalu and Maya: bindi artist’s canvas - Indian Express
Content:
The Kanpur district court has again received a bomb threat — this is the second in the last 45 days.

On Thursday, a postcard reached the office of District Judge Subhash Chandra, warning of blasts in the court premises within three days.

The postcard, which did not mention the motive of the blasts, was signed by one Ibrahim — who claimed to be a resident of Kanpur dehat.

In September, one Ejaz had sent a similar postcard threatening to blow away the Kanpur court premises on September 26. It, however, proved to be a hoax.

Superintendent of Police (Kanpur East) Manoj Sonkar said: "We have taken the issue seriously and are trying to trace the accused." Additional security has been deployed at the gates of the court and everyone on the premises is being thoroughly frisked, he added. "Anti-sabotage teams are conducting regular inspections of the area and teams from several police stations have been deployed near the court," added Sonkar.

Advocates, however, blamed the police for their complacency.

The General Secretary of the Kanpur Bar Association (KBA), Indeevar Bajpai, told The Indian Express: "No one is concerned about the safety of thousands of advocates and litigants visiting the court."

A delegation from the KBA will soon meet the SSP and submit a memorandum regarding the indifference of the police, he added.

Heading: Sisters consume poison after spat - Indian Express
Content:
After gifting an artwork to the UP chief minister in June, Sheshdhar Pandey hands over another painting to Railway Minister

Sheshdhar Pandey is not much familiar with the particulars of Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav's portfolio and his way of functioning. But that does not stop this Noida artist from admiring the Rashtriya Janata Dal supremo.

"He (Lalu) has taken a lot of initiatives for the poor and is a nice man," says Pandey, as he flips through television channels to point out that the minister was one of the first to comment against the violence in Mumbai. "He feels for the people," adds Pandey.

Earlier this week, Pandey was with the minister at his Prithviraj Road residence, not to discuss politics though. The two talked about art as Pandey gifted Lalu his artwork titled Ardhnageswar, featuring the minister and his wife, former Bihar chief minister Rabri Devi.
