Created using over 2.5 lakh bindis on a 4x4 feet mirror, and priced at an estimated Rs 4 lakh, the artwork depicts Lalu and Rabri in one body and is inspired by the mythological character of Ardhnarishwar that portrays Shiv and Parvati as one. "He (Lalu) is not a God but he has impressive qualities," observes Pandey.

While the artwork is already with Lalu, Pandey hopes to present it to the minister at a formal ceremony over the weekend. "During the brief interaction Laluji told me that he liked the work. He has asked me to keep in touch with his secretary for an appointment during the weekend so that I can gift the work to him in front of a larger audience," says Pandey, as he admirably looks at the image of the artwork on his computer screen.

And he expects something from the minister: "I hope he keeps the bindi work in his office."

His art involves pasting a mirror on an aluminium sheet and then drawing a rough pencil sketch that is to be filled with bindis. The procedure may be tedious, but Pandey does not mind the hard work. "It is the bindis that distinguish my work from others," says Pandey, formerly a clerk in the Indian Army.

This isn't the first time, however, when the 43-year-old has chosen a politician as his protagonist. In June, he had gifted UP Chief Minister Mayawati her portrait.

His studio wall in Noida has an image of Kanshi Ram suspended from the ceiling. "It is difficult to make portraits with bindis but I like the end product on most occasions," notes Pandey.

Next in line is a series featuring Mahatma Gandhi, which the artist promises will be a fitting tribute to the Father of the Nation.

Heading: Rs 1 lakh stolen from Punjab trader on bus - Indian Express
Content:
Two cousins allegedly committed suicide by consuming a poisonous substance at their residence in Nangloi on Wednesday. While one of the girls was declared dead on arrival the same night at the hospital, the other died on Thursday evening.

Police said the deceased, Priyanka (19) and Sunita (19) used to have frequent fights and on the day of incident had another argument after which they consumed poison.

Police said the incident was reported in Arvind Enclave of Kamruddin Nagar village of Nangloi area.

Deceased Sunita's father is an ASI with the Delhi Police and is presently working as security personnel for Vice President Hamid Hansari. Priyanka's father Azad Singh is a farmer in the Jhajjar district of Haryana.

Priyanka had recently come to Delhi from Jhajjar as her father wanted her to study under her uncle's supervision. "Priyanka had failed her Class IX exams quite a few times in the past, while Sunita was pursuing a JBT training course from a private institute near her home. Sunita often teased Priyanka over her failure which resulted in verbal spats. On the day of the incident, their family heard another loud quarrel between them and reprimanded them before leaving the house," a senior police officer said. Later, Sunita's mother Sumesh discovered them unconscious on the floor, with froth coming out of their mouths. Police rushed the two girls to the Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, where Priyanka was declared dead on arrival. Sunita passed away on Thursday.

Heading: Govt-people meeting to plug NREGS holes - Indian Express
Content:
Two pickpockets stole Rs 1 lakh from a 56-year-old businessman as he was travelling in a Blueline in Sarai Rohilla area of the North District in the city. The victim, Avinash Kalia who owns an electrical goods shop in Punjab, had come to Delhi to visit a relative's house.

The police said they received a call about the incident about 1 pm. When they reached the spot, the victim had stopped the bus and had created an uproar in the area.

Kalia is a resident of Paghwara area of Punjab and had come to attend a function in Delhi. "He was to hand over cash worth Rs 1 lakh to one of his relatives, which he was carrying from home," the police said.

He had boarded a Blueline (route number 847 from Seema Puri to Uttam Nagar) from New Rohtak Road. He was robbed on his way to his relatives' place in Uttam Nagar.

Police said Kalia's pocket had been entirely cut through with a blade by the assailants. "The victim, in his statement, said that after he noticed that his money was missing, he raised an alarm and even noticed two youths getting off the bus and running away," an officer said. Kalia then stopped the bus and made a call to the police. A case has been lodged at the Sarai Rohilla police station.

"We are questioning the bus driver and the conductor and have sent out teams to arrest the accused," the senior police officer added.

In a separate incident on Thursday night, two motorcycle-borne youths snatched the bag of a retired MCD primary school teacher, containing valuables and cash amounting to Rs 1.40 lakh, in Vasant Vihar of South Delhi and fled. Police said the victim Manju was headed for her DDA flat residence in Vasant Vihar when the incident took place.

Heading: ‘75,000 voters missing in EC list’ - Indian Express
Content:
* Rajanati, a 29-year-old villager from Badausa in Banda district, worked for 156 days under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS) in the last fiscal year. But when payday came, he was assured half the amount against his total dues of Rs 15,600. Rajanati is still waiting for that money, even though the matter was taken up at the Tehsil Diwas.

* Shakuntala (36), a resident of Barimanpur village of Mahua block in Banda has a job card since March 29, and has been filing regular applications for work in her village panchayat since June 25. But she has not been given any work so far. She has written to the Block Development Officer and even the SDM, but to no avail.

Rajanati and Shakuntala are not the only ones who have job cards under the NREGS but are still waiting either for work or wages.

On Saturday, alongwith Shakuntala and Rajanati, several others from across 20 districts of the state will be talking directly with the state government officials on these issues.

They are part of a Presentation on NREGS, organised by Proact — a professional action group — comprising management consultants for the implementation of PACS (Poorest Area Civil Society) Programme in India.

The meeting will also be attended by representatives of 20 civil society organisations and government officials including Manoj Kumar Singh, Commissioner, Rural Development Department.

Sandeep Majhi of Proact said the aim of the meeting is to bridge the gap between the people and the Rural Development Department — the government agency notified for implementation.

"As a part of the programme, we engaged our civil society organisations for raising awareness on the NREGS. In course of our programme, we found that there were not just successes, but also gaps which needed to be filled," said Majhi.

The successes came in the form of initiatives by gram pradhans and people's groups. "The problems are more or less similar. But while in some places people have managed to find solutions, there are gaps in the rest. So it was necessary to bring them all together," said Aditya Vidhyasagar, communication expert attached with the programme.

The Centrally-funded scheme will complete two years this December.

Heading: Ghaziabad NRI ‘abducted’ - Indian Express
Content:
Azamgarh: HC asks state govt, Election Commission to reply

A Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court has asked the Election Commission, Uttar Pradesh government and the election officer of Azamgarh to explain why names of over 75,000 names were not included in the voters' list of Azamgarh district.

The Bench comprising Justices S Rafat Alam and Sudhir Agrawal passed the order after hearing a writ petition filed by Asad Hayat, the general secretary of Awami Council for Peace and Democracy.

The court has directed the three parties to submit their replies on November 14 — the next date of hearing.

The council's lawyer, S F A Naqvi, submitted that the Election Commission has not complied with the relevant rules applicable in the making of a voters' list.

No intensive survey was conducted in Azamgarh and in the nearby constituencies after the new delimitation of Azamgarh and Lalganj Parliamentary constituencies. This way, over 75,000 voters were deprived of their right to vote, he alleged.

It was argued that the petitioner had conducted an intensive survey and found that in Sagri Gopalpur, Azamgarh, Mubarakpur and Meh Nagar Vidhan Sabha constituencies, names of a large number of voters were either deleted or not included in the voters' list.

The petitioner also submitted that the survey had revealed details, which shows a particular section of the minority community had been deprived of their voting rights.

"These poor citizens were excluded and deprived by this diabolic design to exercise their right to franchise as guaranteed under Article19 (1) (A), 325 and 326 of the Constitution," Naqvi said.

Heading: Ghaziabad woman alleges rape by cop from Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
In a bizarre incident, a Non-Resident Indian was mysteriously abducted from Ghaziabad while he was returning home after attending a get-together, only to end up at a city hospital in a critical state later. The police confirmed that he was admitted to a city hospital but refused to divulge details on where he has been admitted.

According to the case registered at Massoori police station, Ramesh Singhal, an NRI, who owns a departmental store in the US and is a resident of Modinagar, Ghaziabad, had gone to meet few of his friends on Thursday. "He hired a car from Charu Travels to go to Sangam Hotel to meet his friends," said Vijay Bhushan, SP (City), Ghaziabad. According to the police, on his way back home, a Santro stopped near Singhal's car and allegedly abducted him and the driver.

"The police managed to trace the car and the driver, but till late in the evening, Singhal could not be traced. We have just received information that he has been admitted to a city hospital in a critical state," added Bhushan.

According sources in the police, however, the driver and Singhal were allegedly beaten up by goons and robbed near Massoori. Senior police officials, however, maintained that Singhal was abducted. "There was no ransom call made to the family. We are interrogating one Ramveer Singh, who was there with Singhal at the party," said Bhushan.

Heading: UP cops bug phones to forward pvt business - Indian Express
Content:
A Ghaziabad woman has charged an inspector, currently posted with the co-operative cell in Lucknow, and his friends with allegedly gangraping her in Ghaziabad when she was returning to her residence located in Hapur.

A case has been registered on the same at the Kavi Nagar Police Station, Ghaziabad.

Akanksha Malik (name changed) alleged that Inspector Vishesh Kumar Singh had raped her near Hapur Chungi. "On November 3, I was on my way home located in Hapur, when a black Wagon car stopped near me and started honking. When I turned back, the car stopped close to me and the inspector pulled me inside the car. I was raped by the inspector and his friends," alleged the victim.

Meanwhile, Vijay Bhushan, SP (City) confirmed that a case has been registered against the inspector at Kavi Nagar Police Station. "The victim has earlier registered rape cases against the inspector on several occasions in various police stations. As the inspector is posted with the Lucknow branch of co-operatives, we are yet to find out whether he was in town on November 3. We are investigating the matter," added Bhushan.

According to the police, the accused inspector was posted as the Chowki-in-charge, Pilkhuwa in 2005. "The victim and the accused had met each other at Pilkhuwa Police Station, where the victim had gone to file a complaint. They became friendly and were allegedly in a relationship. The victim had earlier filed a rape case against the inspector in 2006 in Bulandshahar," added the senior police officer.

The victim alleged that the police had refused to register a rape case against the inspector on earlier occasions. It took her a meeting with the Senior Superintendent of Police, Ghaziabad, to get a case lodged. "The woman has been sent for a medical examination and we are awaiting the results," said Bhushan. This is not the first rape case reported against the city police. On October 10, a head constable had been charged with raping a minor. He has been absconding since the incident and the police are still looking for him.

Heading: Six BSP candidates file nominations for RS polls - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government has put a stop to the electronic surveillance of conversation between criminals after it surfaced recently that certain police officers were misusing the procedure.

A senior official in the Home department said an officer in the Special Task Force (STF) and an in-charge of the Special Operation Group (SOG) in Varanasi have helped several contractors to grab lucrative business in Lucknow, Noida and Varanasi by prying on the conversations of their rivals through this system.

These cops eavesdropped on tender details discussed by the rivals and alerted their contracted friends so that they could bid less.

The official said the fraud came to light after the harassed contractors approached the Home department and demanded to know how information was being leaked. Sources said they became suspicious after they lost several bids, the latest being one for a private mobile company.

An inquiry was ordered. The department asked the agencies concerned — the STF and the Varanasi Police — to produce records of the mobile phone numbers under surveillance. The phone numbers of the affected contractors popped up on the list, and it was found that these two officers were intercepting calls.

Sources in the Home department said a departmental probe has been ordered against the erring policemen.

The Home department has now decided there will be no sweeping use of the electronic procedure. It will make an exception for the district police — that too, for very special cases.

Besides, the STF has also been instructed to send details about the name and address of the person whose phone will be bugged. The Home Secretary will allow surveillance of only those numbers which carry a letter from the network provider, mentioning their identity details.

The Home department has also wanted to know why different police agencies — the STF, the Anti-terror Squad and the district police — seek permission to scrutinise common numbers.

The Department of Telecommunications allows only nine police agencies across the country to intercept phone calls. Each state is allowed to give the facility to only one of its agencies.

In Uttar Pradesh, the STF, the ATS, the district police and the Intelligence headquarters have the technical expertise to intercept phone calls.

Heading: Catering To Special Needs - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
I have loads of old Hindi film songs.

What's your DVD pick?
All Jackie Chan movies and a movie that I really love — The Pursuit of Happyness.

Your most favourite romantic scene in a movie?
When Dharmendra teaches Hema Malini how to shoot in Sholay.

Which actress you would love to go on a date with and why?
Sridevi. I had a huge crush on her as a kid and in college as well.

Which dialogue have you mouthed in front of the mirror the most?
Kaminey mein tera khoon pee jaungaa.

Who inspired you to become an actor?
Dilip Kumar. When I was in the final year of college, I knew I wanted to be an actor.

The worst film you ever watched?
Gunda.

Which film you wish you could be a part of?
Deewar and Life is Beautiful.

What makes you an actor?
A good director.

Quiz: From which film is this line: Bheegi hui cigarette kabhi jal nahi sakti.....aur yeh tay hai ki teri maut ki taarikh tal nahi sakti.
Mithun Chakraborty said it in the film Gunda (correct).

Heading: After 15 years, police arrests Valmiki - Indian Express
Content:
Perfect Bebo
It takes quite something to impress perfectionist Aamir Khan. So we understand how fit Kareena Kapoor actually is when Aamir compliments her on her great body. Bebo, who is a fitness freak, left quite an impact on Aamir with her well-toned body and her devotion to her workouts. He was also impressed by her professionalism as she shot in Ladakh's cold climate without a single complaint. The two stars are working together on Raju Hirani's Three Idiots. This is their first film together and unit members are already talking about how well the two have hit it off with each other.

Salman on a roll
SALMAN Khan was quite the charmer on the sets of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Challenge 2009, where he appeared with the current love of his life, Katrina Kaif. The picture perfect couple appeared as an 'item' for the first time on Indian television and made everyone's day as they waltzed together to the song Teri Ore, from Kat's hit movie Singh is Kinng. But the star of the day was Khan, who was at his flamboyant best, dancing with the contestants, playing cupid between them.

Heading: Candidates declare assets, Akhilesh Das owns the most - Indian Express
Content:
On the run for the last 15 years, Chandrapal Valmiki — accused in 10 kidnapping cases and seven attempt to murder — was finally arrested on Wednesday night from the Kanshi Ram Nagar district. Valmiki had been first named when he was 14-years-old after allegedly executing a murder in 1992.

Superintendent of Police (SP) Kanshi Ram Nagar Luv Kumar, said, "The criminal had been arrested only once when he was named in the 1992 murder case."

He was later bailed out due to lack of evidence.

Since then, he has been on the run, said Kumar.

Valmiki was orchestrating various criminal activities while staying out of the district. He was arrested in Sahawar while he was returning from his native place at Bagwas village in Sikanderpur. A firearm and cartridges were seized from the possession of the accused. Valmiki was carrying a reward of Rs 5,000 on his head, said Kumar. gangstar.

Heading: Bitten by recession, IIM-L shy of disclosing placement offers - Indian Express
Content:
Going by the assets declared by the candidates for the Rajya Sabha polls, the Bahujan Samaj Party no longer appears a place for the underprivileged and downtrodden.

The collective assets of former Union minister Akhilesh Das — son of the former UP chief minister Banarasi Das — and his wife are worth around Rs 42 crore. A majority of the assets are non-agricultural, running mostly to gold -- and real estate worth over Rs 30 crore.

The BSP leader owns 3.10 kgs of gold worth Rs 37.20 lakh, his wife, Alka Das, has investments worth over Rs 8 crore in bonds and debentures and gold worth Rs 64 lakh.

Das, who has also been declared BSP's Lok Sabha candidate from Lucknow, has around Rs 3 crore in shares, jewellery, bonds and bank deposits. He owns real estate in in Lucknow, Haryana, Noida, Ghaziabad, Khurja, Gurgaon and New Delhi.

The properties listed in the name of his wife are in Lucknow, Noida, Ghazaibad, Gurgaon and on the Delhi-Jaipur highway.

Of the other candidates, Veer Singh, a second-timer for the Rajya Sabha seat, has assets worth around Rs 2 crore.

Former Lok Sabha member from Jalaun, Brij Lal Khabari, has assets worth around Rs 1 crore. He also owns a house in Orai in Jalaun district, worth Rs 50 lakh, jointly with his wife.

Brajesh Pathak and Avtar Singh Karimpuri have announced assets worth less than Rs 1 crore. A resident of Punjab, Karimpuri has assets worth around Rs 52 lakh, of which Rs 41 lakh is the value of a property in Hoshiyarpur which he owns jointly with his wife. Pathak, a Lok Sabha member from Unnao, has disclosed assets worth Rs 60 lakh, which includes Rs 17 lakh which he has taken on loan. Raja Ram owns property worth Rs 38 lakh. It also turns out that most of the politicians have an interest in firearms. While Raja Ram has three, including a rifle and a pistol, Veer Singh has two firearms in his name.

Heading: Teenager raped in Sultanpur, two arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Call it meltdown effect, summer placements at the Indian Institute of Management, Lucknow (IIM-L) began amid uncertainty and utmost secrecy.

While the tension was evident on the campus following global market recession, neither students nor the faculty members divulged any detail about the placement process such as number of companies queuing up, offers on the first day and so on.

The IIM-L administration was cautious in divulging details of this year's summer placement that they have even denied entry of outsiders, especially the media, to the institute for the next six days. "It is a policy decision that no information about the placements goes out of campus till the companies select the students," said Professor Sushil Kumar, the in-charge of the Placement Cell.

Nearly 320 students are applying for the summer placements this year.

Earlier, the IIM-L had decided not to reveal stipend offered during summer placements or salary offered during final placements but for the first time, the institute is not disclosing even the number of companies visiting for the summer placements.

A senior faculty member said: "We have to keep it process a secret because we do not want any negative mindset to affect the placements. We will allow entry to media once the placements are over on November 13."

A student said: "Last year, there were nearly 400 summer placement offers for around 240 students. During the final placements, these companies gave preference to students, who had joined them for summer placements."

He added, "This year, students are preferring Indian companies considering that owing to economic recession, many MNCs may undertake a job cut in future and do not turn up for final placements."

Heading: Woman robbed, stabbed to death in Allahabad - Indian Express
Content:
The Sultanpur police on Friday arrested two persons in connection with a gangrape case lodged at the Jaisinghpur police station in the district.

The victim's father, Bhargav Saran Soni, a resident of Mehmoodpur village, informed the police that three persons of his village kidnapped his 17-year-old daughter while she was on her way to home from school.

The youths took her to a secluded place and raped her.

Jaisingpur police station in-charge, Dhani Ram Verma said: " Following the complaint, we have detained two persons for interrogation. The girl has been sent for medical test and any action will be taken only on the basis of the report."

The arrested persons are Lalji and Satish — both in their early twenties. Lalji owns a shop in the area, Satish is a farmer.

The police, however, suspect that the rape allegations are a fallout of a tussle between two different communities.

Heading: Crackdown on Atiq men: 8 arms licences cancelled - Indian Express
Content:
Unidentified miscreants stabbed a woman to death and robbed her house in the posh Punjabi Bhawan Colony on Friday.

According to the police, Kusham Singh (50), wife of Prithvi Pal Singh, a railway contractor, was alone in the house when the incident took place. While her husband was in Kanpur, Kusham's daughter Manvi was in college.

It is not yet clear on what pretext the miscreants entered the house. Once inside, they tried to lock Kusham in the kitchen. But when she started shouting, they killed her with a sharp-edged weapon. Then they broke the lockers and almirahs in the house and decamped with cash and valuables, the details of which are yet to be known.

The murder came to light when Manvi returned from college around 6 pm. She informed her neighbours who called the police. Superintendent of Police (City) Awdhesh Singh Vijeta and the circle officers immediately reached the spot. "It is too early to comment on the incident but we will soon work out the case," the SP said. Four years ago, Prithvi Pal Singh's son was reportedly abducted from his residence. The police are yet to rescue him.

Singh was on his way to Allahabad at the time of filing of the report.

Heading: Two docs suspended for negligence in UP - Indian Express
Content:
In a move to restrict the activities of jailed MP Atiq Ahmed, an expelled Samajwadi Party legislator, the district administration has cancelled eight arms licenses of his gang members.

District Magistrate Rajeev Agrawal, soon after assuming office five months ago, had initiated an inquiry against all arms license holders to verify their present address and the cases pending against them. There are 244 such cases pending under Section 17 of the Arms Act, said a source. Overall, the administration has cancelled 25 licenses.

Altogether, 28 arms licenses were issued in the name of those belonging to Ahmed's family or his gang. While eight have been cancelled, 20 have been suspended.

The administration has initiated proceedings against the 20, which include two licenses on Ahmed's name, three licenses in the name of his wife Shaista Parveen, one each in the name of his younger brother Khalid Azim alias Ashraf and cousin Hamza.

A decision to maintain or cancel these licenses will be taken after probing each case separately.

According to police sources, Ahmed has 108 criminal cases against him. Ashraf and Hamza are also involved in over two dozen criminal cases, giving enough grounds to initiate cancellation proceedings. While Ahmed has one rifle and a pistol, his wife has a rifle, a pistol and a double barrel gun in her name. The license in her name is issued on a false address, said ADM (City) Pradeep Kumar.

"We are doing what the law says, irrespective of their political affiliations. No one who had obtained license by concealing facts will be spared," said District Magistrate Rajeev Agrawal.

The state government, meanwhile, has decided to transfer some of Ahmed's gang members from Naini jail to others. The office of the senior superintendent of police informed that the police have identified six persons belonging to Ahmed's gang — Ashiq, Ram Lochan Yadav, Ashok Yadav, I B Singh, Ferhan and Pawan Tiwari — for this purpose. While Farhan and Ram Lochan will soon be sent to Mirzapur jail, Ashok Yadav and Ashiq will be transferred to Jaunpur jail.

A report in this regard has already been sent to the state government.

Heading: No corruption in Bundelkhand plantation project, says UP government - Indian Express
Content:
Two doctors of the Uttar Pradesh Provincial Medical and Health Services (UPPMHS) were suspended by the state government on Friday for negligence in performing their duties.

Cardiologist T P Singh of the Balrampur Hospital and Dr Sunanda Verma of the Avantibai Female Hospital were suspended following allegations that they misguided a woman to undergo delivery at the cardiology department rather than a proper maternity ward.

Soon after the suspension order reached the two hospitals, office bearers of the UPPMHS association opposed it and said if the government does not revoke the order within two days, Lucknow doctors will go on a strike from Monday.

Heading: UP to waive off Rs 120 cr loan for small entrepreneurs - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has denied allegations of corruption in the Bundelkhand plantation drive. Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Atul Kumar Gupta said a team of the Union Ministry of Rural Development has inspected the plantation and appreciated it.

"All reports of rampant corruption in the scheme have been proved false and baseless," he told the reporters on Friday.

The project was launched by Chief Minister Mayawati as a long-term plan for the drought-affected Bundelkhand region. But some parties alleged corruption in the project that the state government had siphoned off Rs 219 crore from the allocated Rs 409 crore under the NREGA accounts for the project. They also accused administration of the seven districts, where the project was implemented, of showing irregularities in implementing the scheme.

Gupta, however, said, "The Central team, consisting of retired Colonel HC Jain, retired Brigadier P K Bhatnagar and a few others have investigated the charges and found these to be baseless."

The team has reported that in almost all the seven districts, survival rate of the saplings was 90 to 97 per cent that dismisses all charges of corruption.

Heading: The flame of hope lights up India and Pakistan - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has decided to waive loans disbursed under by the Uttar Pradesh Anusuchit Jaati Vitta Evam Vikas Nigam under various self employment schemes. The loans, running for more than ten years, had become non-performing assets, amounting to nearly Rs 120 crore.

The principal amount provided by the state government as its share as well as the interest rate will be waived off, the state Cabinet decided in a meeting on Friday.

Chief Minister Mayawati has written a letter to the Prime Minister requesting him that the Centre should also waive off its loan share including interest rate so that millions of poor belonging to Scheduled Castes could be given relief from bad loans.

She has also requested the Prime Minister to ensure that the Rashtriya Anusuchit Jaati Vitta Evam Vikas Nigam

takes such step for other states also so that the poor in these states could also be given a loan waiver.

Since 1980-81, the UP Anusuchit Jaati Vitta Evam Vikas Nigam was providing 25 per cent of the project cost as loan to the poor and unemployed SC under various schemes of self employment. The schemes were run in cooperation of the banks.

In course of time most of the beneficiaries could not repay their loans, following which they were unable to get additional loans. Subsequently, the loans became NPAs and the borrowers faced financial difficulties. At present, a large number of project beneficiaries belonging to SCs are burdened with loans.

Heading: Area officer liable if illegal colony comes up, says CM Badal - Indian Express
Content:
Special children from both countries walked together during a torch rally on Friday

It seemed as if India and Pakistan had reunited as over a hundred special children from both the countries walked together during a torch rally at the Eleventh Special Olympics Bharat in Ludhiana on Friday.

Holding banners with messages of communal harmony, such as 'Jive sada Pakistan, aakhi janda Hindustan' and 'Don't laugh at us, but with us', the children marched half-a-kilometre from Guru Nanak Public School to the Satluj Club.

About 500 children from 19 schools will participate in the three-day sports extravaganza to be held at Guru Nanak Public School.

Rukhenaz, a coach from Pakistan, said: "It's like a homecoming for us. We have come here with 37 special children from Lahore, Karachi, Gilgit, Quetta and Islamabad. It is their first visit to India for the kids, who suffer from Down Syndrome and cerebral palsy. I have no words to express the hospitality being showered upon us."

Parmod Kumar, a member of the NGO Bharat Vikas Parishad, said: "This is the first time I am taking part in the Special Olympics Bharat. Earlier, I have participated in the cycling competition at the Kila Raipur Games."

A group of students had a wish. "We hope that all differences between India and Pakistan are resolved and more such events take place."

Ashok Arora, patron of the organising committee, said: "On the first day, athletic skills of the participants will be tested. On the concluding day, participants

will pedal their way

to the podiums in the cycling events. This year's event is dedicated to local lad and singing sensation, Ishmeet Singh, who died in the Maldives recently.

Special Olympics Bharat aims to help people with intellectual disabilities develop self-confidence, social skills and a sense of personal accomplishment.

Started in 1998, Ludhiana is hosting the event for the third time since the first Olympics at Patiala.

Heading: Sutlej Club brawl: two inquiries ordered - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure planned development in the state, the government has issued directions to the local urban development authorities to check the growth of unauthorised colonies in all cities. Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal added that the officer concerned of the area will be held responsible in case any such colony comes up.

Badal was addressing a gathering at a Sangat Darshan programme organised at six places in the Ludhiana Rural constituency, which covers 15 municipal wards, on Friday. The Sangat Darshan was held at Saleem Tabri, Basti Jodhewal, Greenland School, Jamalpur and Jain Public School.

The chief minister asserted that the Sangat Darshan programmes were giving excellent results and helped direct discussion with the residents of the area. He added that the government had chalked out a comprehensive plan for development of both urban and rural areas. The government has already released funds amounting to Rs 350 crore to all Municipal Councils — Rs 3 crore for A class Municipal Council, Rs 2 crore for B class, Rs 1 crore for C class and Notified Area Committees each.

"In the next three years, all basic amenities will be provided to the urban population," said Badal. The government is also laying stress on strengthening infrastructure facilities in the state to boost investment and industrialization, he said.

Minister for Jails, Cultural and Tourism Hira Singh Gabria, MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon, deputy chairman of Punjab Traders' Board Madan Lal Bagga, DIG Ishwer Singh, Deputy Commissioner Sumer Singh Gurjar, SSP R K Jaiswal, MC Commissioner G S Ghuman, Mayor Hakam Singh Gyaspura and councillors Balwinder Singh Bains, Simarjit Singh Bains, Pal Singh Grewal, Tarsem Singh, Daljit Singh Grewal, Gurbax Singh, Balwinder Singh, Gurpreet Rai and Ratanjit Kaur Sibia were present on the occasion.

Grants galore

The chief minister also released grants amounting to Rs 219.81 crore for the development of unauthorised colonies.

Construction of roads Rs 81.85 cr

Water supply, sewerage Rs 74.38 cr

Streetlights Rs 13 crore

Community centres Rs 16.38 cr

Parks Rs 4.72 cr

Other projects Rs 28.67 cr

Entry for VIPs only

It seems Friday's Sangat Darshan was for VIPs only as the common man spent time waiting in the queue. At Salem Tabri, the chief minister left for the second venue after hearing barely 12 to 15 complainants. Similar scenes were witnessed at Greenland School and Jamalpur as well. Balwinder Panesar, personal assistant of Cabinet minister Hira Singh, collected the complaints from those whom the CM could not meet.

Many left high and dry

Baljinder Singh and Omparkash, both of whom are physically challenged, kept waiting in vain to meet the chief minister. Both had hoped for financial help and a job from the CM. Many others were in the same boat and hope their complaints reach the CM for an early solution.

Heading: ‘Not easy to play M F Husain, he is full of contradictions’ - Indian Express
Content:
Two different inquiries have been marked to probe the brawl that took place in the prestigious Sutlej Club on Wednesday night.

While an Additional Deputy Commissioner will investigate the alleged misconduct of the club members concerned, Sarabha Nagar DSP Bhupinder Singh will look into the threats issued by both the parties.

Yogesh Bansal, general secretary of Sutlej Club, said: "Following the incident, Deputy Commissioner Sumer Singh Gurjar, who is the ex-officio president of the club, called me for a meeting and said he will ask an ADC to look into the matter."

On Thursday, two rival groups had submitted separate applications to the club authorities and the police about the incident demanding action against the other party.

On Wednesday night, G S Laddi, former general secretary of the club, and another member, Mahesh Goyal, had a heated argument at club over payment towards a colony development project.

Heading: Diamond jewellery exhibition starts - Indian Express
Content:
The fatigue shows on his face. "I have not slept for days now," says actor Tom Alter, who is in town to act in a play titled 'Pencil Se Brush Tak'. Alter will essay the role of controversial painter M F Husain in the play.

"I always wanted to work with Nadira Babbar. Our friendship goes back many years and when I was offered the role, it was a cherry on the cake. It's not easy to portray Husain as he is full of contradictions — he is passionate about his work, so colourful, so intense and yet possesses a child-like innocence. Innocence is a trait I share with the great painter. He and his family have seen a video of the play and have liked it," he smiles.

On the controversies surrounding Husain, the actor states: "In India these days, you are attacked if you merely disagree with anyone. I am not saying Husain's work has not offended anyone but that does not mean he should be attacked. A dialogue process should be created."

Born to American missionary parents, the actor said: "I share a relationship of ishq and mohabbat with Punjab. Places like Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Batala and Amritsar are very close to my heart."

Alter refuses to be called a Bollywood actor. "I disapprove of this term. I work for the Hindi film industry."

On Husain's love for film heroines, he says: "Every one loves them. I am sure men in Ludhiana too love Madhuri Dixit but then how many people have the courage to declare their love so openly like M F Husain. People are scared of society and their wives."

"Those who say Husain is a rebel are wrong. He is 92 years old now. They have not seen him as a youth, struggling in Mumbai, painting film posters to make a living. This is no rebellion. He has struggled to be where he is today and he deserves all accolades that come his way," says Alter.

I am sure he (Husain) will return to India one day, concludes the actor.

Heading: Grewal demands probe into ‘advertisement tax scandal’ - Indian Express
Content:
A two-day diamond jewellery exhibition, Celestial Jewels and More, started at Dewan-e-Khas of Majestic Park Plaza hotel on Friday. The price of the products range from Rs 10,000 to Rs 10,00000.

This exhibition has brought traditional and contemporary diamond collection. In its first attempt, Celestial has displayed diamond bracelets, rings, chandelier ear-rings and diamond pendants, solitaries, necklace and many other items.

Sheena Dhanda and Anupreet, the organisers of the exhibition, said, "This is our first attempt to introduce our designs as an exclusive brand in Punjab. We are banking on the support of Ludhianvis."

Heading: Slowdown in cycle industry decried - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab state chief of BJP Investor Cell, Sukhminderpal Singh Grewal has urged the Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal to order a CBI or IB inquiry into the alleged advertisement tax scandal by oil companies in Punjab.

Grewal gave an application to the CM in this regard during the Sangat Darshan programme in the city today.

In the application, Grewal said that a major "advertising scandal" of Rs 752 crores by the oil companies in connivance with the officers of Municipal Corporations of Punjab. He said that oil companies across India had installed Flex Hoardings to advertise their products but till date, they haven't paid any advertisement tax applicable on these hoardings.

There are over 68,388 retail outlets all over India, of which 5,226 retail outlets were commissioned in Punjab These retail outlets have erected Flex Hoardings with an average 1000 sq. feet advertising space apart from other advertisement spaces such as Glow Facia and Signages, which meant advertisement tax on 52,26000 sq feet advertisement space was fleeced by these oil companies. This adds up to a whopping Rs 125 crore loss per annum for the Punjab government only. Considering an average age of meagre six years of these hoardings, as most of them were installed during previous government's tenure, this amounted to a loss of over Rs 752 crore to the state exchequer.

Grewal demanded that a CBI or IB enquiry be ordered immediately and responsibility of erring and corrupt officials of these oil companies and Municipal Corporations be fixed and guilty be booked as per law. He alleged that "advertisement mafia" was hand-in-glove with certain officials of Municipal Corporation, and were openly flouting landmark judgments of the Punjab and Haryana High Court wherein the any hoarding within 100 meters from any important road had been banned.

Heading: Mediation centre starts today with promise of speedy justice - Indian Express
Content:
The members of the United Cycles Parts and Manufacturers Association on Friday held a meeting to discuss the slow-down in bicycle sales because of the fall in steel prices. The manufacturers have already reduced the prices of bicycle by about Rs 30 besides giving some offers to woo the customers.

Charanjit Singh Vishvkarma, president of the association, urged the secondary producers of steel to fix the prices of raw material because they are not able to determine the exact cost of finished product this way and hence the clients are not picking the stocks.

He said, "Clients are apprehending that prices of bicycle may fall further and hence they are not picking orders."

Heading: Use Triple, PAU experts tell farmers facing DAP shortage - Indian Express
Content:
District and Session Judge and Chairman, District Legal Services Authority, G.K. Rai today informed that Mediation and Conciliation Centre, Ludhiana, will start functioning on November 8 at the court room no.15-A, New Court Complex here.

Giving details, Justice Rai said that Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ludhiana, Kishore Kumar and Civil Judge, Randhir Verma would be functioning as mediators.

Rai further informed that that Mediation and Conciliation Centre, Ludhiana, was being set up at the intiiative taken by S.B. Sinha, Judge of Supreme Court of India and under the guidance of Justice T.S. Thakur, Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Initially, 165 cases have been referred by the various courts with the consent of the parties to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, which would be taken up.

Justice Rai informed that at this centre, 165 cases in various courts relating to civil suits, matrimonial disputes, MACT cases and cheque-bounce cases would be settled with mutual consent of both parties. He urged the people to bring their cases to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre for the immediate and final settlement.

Rai said that the centre would not only provide speedy justice to the litigants, but also help in reducing the pendency of cases in the courts, he added .

Rai said that 19 mediation and conciliation centres will start functioning on November 8 in Jalandhar, Ludhiana, Sangrur, Amritsar, Hoshiarpur, Ferozepur, Patiala, Faridkot and Moga in Punjab. In Haryana also, mediation and conciliation centres will come on stream on the same date at Faridabad, Gurgaon, Rohtak, Sonepat, Jind, Karnal, Kurkshetra, Rewari and Hisar.

Heading: HCL hires 10 during campus placement drive - Indian Express
Content:
Defending champions New Public School, Sector 18 boys' and girls' teams were dethroned in the fifth Emily Gosain Memorial Inter-School Basketball Tournament held at St Xavier's School, Sector 21 on Friday.

Playing an inspired game, St Xavier's School, Sector 44, Chandigarh wrested the boys' title while St Kabir School, Sector 26, Chandigarh stunned them in the girls' section.

St Xavier's-44 carved out a thrilling 64-52 verdict over New Public School in the boys' final while St Kabir School proved too good for NPS by routing them with an authentic margin of 55-16 in the one-sided girls' final. NPS felt the absence of their star player Smiti who suffered injury in their earlier match.

Defending champions NPS boys began on a whirlwind fashion by winning the first quarter by 18-7. However, St Xavier's boys were not discouraged. They reorganised their game and won the second quarter by 13-6. The half time score was 24-20 in favour of New Public School.

At the conclusion of the third set St Xavier's led by a narrow margin of one point (37-36). The thrilling third set saw both teams equal at 32-all. A three-pointer basket by Stanzin made 35-32 and Xavier's star player Gurjot (18) sunk a basket to give his team a lead by 37-36.

Despite midway through the last quarter Gurjot came out after committing five individual fouls, Xavier's continued to maintain pressure and slowly kept on increasing their margin. Vishwadeep (16), Anmol (12) and pint-sized three-point specialist Stanzin (9) systematically controlled the match. From 45-40 they increased their lead to 64-52. At one stage., NPS' main playmaker Sartaj (30) was rested for some time which gave an advantage to their rivals.

New Public School took the court without injured Smiti in the girls final. Absence of Smiti who had capitalised on rebounds in their earlier matches, was badly felt today. However, credit should not be taken away St Kabir School which played as a joint team. The deadly duo of Naina (23) and Rupandeep (20) demolished the NPS defence.

Results (all finals):

Boys: St Xavier's School, Sector 44 Chandigarh (Vishadeep 16, Anmol 12, Stanzin 9, Gurjot 18, Sanchit 7) bt New Public School-18 Chandigarh (Deepak 2, Gurpinder 2, Dilbag 1, Sartaj 30, Sunraj 2, Gurlovleen 6) by 64-52; Girls: St Kabir School-27 (Naina 23, Rupandeep 22, Kriti 6, Prakriti 4) bt New Public School, Sector 18 Chandigarh (Manisha 2, Neha 14) by 55-16.

Heading: Two held with 8 qtls of poppy husk - Indian Express
Content:
HCL, a leading IT Global Company and Unicon India, an investment solutions company, visited Desh Bhagat Institute of Management and Computer Sciences, Mandi Gobindgarh, under campus placement drive. The company has 120 branches across the country.

Dr Zora Singh, chairman, Desh Bhagat Group of Institutes, while welcoming the officials of the companies said that job opportunities in today's world were increasing for those who were updating their knowledge and polishing their personalities as per the Industry needs. He encouraged the students to prove themselves worthy of the jobs they were being offered by the visiting companies .

Unicon India selected 10 students from BBA (final year) for their various branches across Punjab with minimum package of 1.05 lakh per annum plus incentives. Unicon India informed the students about their businesses, distribution network in India and their mission over the coming years. They focused on the growth of insurance sector in recent times and about the services Unicon provided in insurance sector.

HCL conducted online test for selection in six-month project semester training for MCA (final year) and B.Tech- Computers (final year) students. They informed the students about the latest developments in IT sector, the use of IT in various Industries including Banking, Airlines, Marketing & various fields. The students participated with full zeal and enthusiasm in making this event a grand success.

Later, Prof Shalini Gupta, Director General, Desh Bhagat Group of Institutes, congratulated the selected candidates and said that all the students should develop their personalities as an industry-ready type because soon after completing their studies, they would be taking responsible positions in industry.

Heading: MNS campaign: It’s narrow mindedness, suggests Patil - Indian Express
Content:
The Khanna police on Friday claimed to have arrested two smugglers and recovered 8.74 quintals of poppy husk from them.

The accused have been identified as Tersem Singh, a resident of Garri village near Machhiwara, and Parkash, a resident of Nurpur Mand village. The poppy husk was packed in 23 bags and was placed in a truck.

In press release, SSP Arun Pal Singh said, "The incharge of anti-narcotics cell, Gurmail Singh laid a naka at Neelo bridge on Thursday. The police party signalled a truck bearing registration number PB-11 AG 9575 to stop. After the search, 23 bags of poppy husk were recovered from the truck. Both accused were remanded in police custody by the local court till Monday.

In another case, ASI Sukhwinder Singh of CIA staff arrested a man near Galwaddi village on Thursday and recovered 15 grams of heroin from him. The accused was identified as Balbir Singh of Rohty Chhanna village.

Heading: Black Thursday continues to haunt Guwahati - Indian Express
Content:
Apparently disapproving of the pro-Maharashtrian campaign, Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil said people who ask for preferential treatment within a particular state are 'narrow minded'.

Patil, who himself hails from Maharashtra, suggested that such actions divide and weaken the country.

"At times we find that people say that we speak a particular kind of language, we are born in a particular state and so we should be given preference over others. That approach is really a narrow minded approach," he told a group of girl students from Arunachal Pradesh at his residence.

He made no direct reference to anyone but was clearly talking in the context of the campaign launched by Raj Thackeray's MNS (Maharashtra Navnirman Sena) which has been demanding preference to Maharashtrians in jobs in the state.

As part of their campaign, the MNS activists have attacked several North Indians who went to Maharashtra in connection with employment.

"It cannot help anyone of us. United we are stronger, divided we are definitely weaker," the Union Minister said.

Urging youngsters to explore the country, Patil said, "If you do not go out of your own state, you tend to feel that the place where you are born is the most beautiful and other places are not equally beautiful and attractive and that creates misunderstanding between people living in different parts of the country."

The visiting girls from the North-eastern state, many of whom have come to the national capital for the first time, are on an educational trip organised by the ITBP.

The 21 girls, hailing from West Kameng, Tezu, Lohit, Changlang and West Siang districts of Arunachal Pradesh had earlier visited the Taj Mahal in Agra, Parliament House, India Gate, Lotus temple, India Habitat Centre among others.

Heading: Malegaon probe: 2 more held, CBI assures help to ATS - Indian Express
Content:
Black Thursday's serial blasts continue to take traumatic toll especially wives and mothers, with a woman who lost both her husband and infant daughter hospitalised for trauma, while two grieving ones have both claimed a body as that of their son.

Four year-old Moromi was returning home from the government Junior Basic School at Dispur on fateful October 30 when her father, Sagar Sarma, was struck down by an explosion at Ganeshguri.

Her mother, Sunita, after losing her husband was hoping to at least take her daughter back home from hospital.

Moromi did return, but in a shroud after battling for life for four days from severe burns.

Sunita is now in the psychiatry ward of the same hospital her daughter died in, being treated for acute trauma.

At the Guwahati Medical College and Hospital, the mother of a young man identified the charred remains as those of her son, Santosh, two days ago.

But another mother looking for her son has also claimed the body as that of her missing son.

Both have now to await the result of the DNA test the police subsequently ordered.

In the Uzan Bazar area, a bomb at the compound of the district deputy commissioner's office left a young woman, her child and mother-in-law shattered.

The wife has a vacant look as she hugs her husband, Rana's shirt, while her mother-in-law's tears have not dried up as yet.

Another mother in Barpeta, has not reconciled to her son Manik Saha's death in the blast there.

Heading: Bangladesh authorities encouraging rebels: Aiyar - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were picked up from Vapi and Pune by the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) in connection with the Malegaon blast probe amid concerns that more army officers may come under the scanner.

Leave records of arrested Lt Col P S Purohit, suspected to have masterminded the September 29 blast, have been given to the investigating agencies, official sources said on Saturday.

Two serving Colonels may also face interrogation. There were reports that a retired Lt General could also be quizzed but there was no official word on it.

No details were immediately forthcoming about the two persons picked up from Vapi and Pune. ATS officials said nine persons, including a Sadhvi and a serving army officer, arrested for their alleged involvement in the blast could be booked under the stringent MCOCA act.

"The application of some sections of Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) is being considered presently," they said.

Under MCOCA, those convicted can get a maximum punishment of life imprisonment and a minimum of five years and police can keep the accused in detention for 180 days to file their chargesheet as against the normal 90-day period.

The accused in the blast that left six people dead have been booked under various sections of the IPC including murder and conspiracy, Indian Explosives Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

The ATS officials had said they were still on the lookout for a suspect identified as Ramji, who is suspected to have played a major role in planting the bomb in the town.

A Colonel who may be probed is posted in Deolali in Nashik while the Lt Colonel is based in Pune. According to the sources, Army is contemplating action against Purohit under Section 21 B of the Army Act which prohibits military personnel from having any political affiliations.

The ATS is investigating the possible involvement of some of the accused in earlier blasts like the 2006 Nanded blast in which two persons were killed while making a bomb.

The ATS has taken permission to conduct scientific tests like brain mapping, polygraph and narcoanalysis on Purohit.

However, the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) has not yet given a schedule regarding when the tests will be conducted, ATS officials said.

Scientific tests have been conducted on Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur, former army officer Ramesh Upadhyay and senior member of the organisation Abhinav Bharat Sameer Kulkarni.

A senior CBI official from Delhi of Joint Director rank has met ATS officials, adding another dimension to the ongoing probe.

Government's worries have been voiced by Defence Minister A K Antony who said the alleged involvement of a serving officer (Purohit) in the Malegaon blasts was a matter of "serious concern."

Necessary action will be taken against him by the Defence Ministry on the basis of the Maharashtra police's investigation report in the case.

"On the part of the Army, without any hesitation, they are fully assisting and cooperating with the investigating agencies. We are waiting for a report from the Maharashtra police and I can tell you, we are taking it seriously," he said.

CBI ready to provide all help to Maharashtra ATS

New Delhi, November 8:

After establishing an 'informal' contact with the anti-terror wing of Maharashtra police, the CBI said it was ready to extend all required help to the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS), probing the Malegaon blast.

The CBI has contacted the ATS which have arrested nine persons, including a serving Lt Col of the army, for their alleged role in triggering the bomb in the Muslim-dominated powerloom town.

"We have established informal communication with ATS Maharashtra and are ready to extend all required help," Press Information Officer of CBI R K Gaur said in a statement.

The CBI wanted to probe the links of the arrested accused, including Lt Colonel Srikant Purohit, with the April 2006 blast in Maharashtra's Nanded town.

The agency had investigated the Nanded blast and filed a chargesheet on March 15, 2008 against 10 people which included Sanjay Chowdhury, Yogesh Deshpande, Maruti Wagah, Gunniraj Thakur and Mahesh Pandey. They are allegedly associated to Bajrang Dal. Two people -- Himanshu Venkatesh and Naresh Laxman -- were killed while manufacturing the bomb.

The Maharashtra Police have so far arrested nine persons which include Lt Colonel Purohit, former ABVP activist Sadhvi Pragya Thakur and one Sameer Kulkarni.

Purohit was working with the Army Liaison Cell, a front of Military Intelligence, and was learning Chinese and Arabic in Panchmari in Madhya Pradesh.

Police and security agencies are trying to trace links of one of the accused to Jammu and Kashmir with a possibility that RDX could have been smuggled from there.

Heading: Maha Govt, police harassing Sadhvi Pragya: Rajnath - Indian Express
Content:
"Certain authorities" in Bangladesh are backing Indian rebel groups sheltering in that country and there was urgent need to impress upon them that by doing so nothing would be gained, Union Minister for DoNER Mani Shankar Aiyar said in Shillong on Saturday.

"Certain authorities of Bangladesh are encouraging activities that are detrimental to India," Aiyar told mediapersons in Shillong.

It was also necessary to impress upon Bangladesh to admit that there were anti-India groups on its soil which were not doing any good to them, he said, adding that the situation could be improved if relations between the two countries are moulded.

Aiyar, however, said the insurgency problem was "home grown". "The insurgents grow here and when they are hemmed in they tend to cross the border."

Describing the recent blasts at Agartala and Assam as episodic, the Union Minister said, "It would have been a cause of worry had there been a systematic deterioration of the situation."

He asserted that the northeast was still secure and claimed that the insurgency problem in the region has shown a tangible improvement over the years. "The northeast, barring Manipur, is a secure place for people to come and companies to invest."

Even in Manipur, the gross state product rate is as high as 11.4 per cent, the highest in the NE, and can be compared to that of China, he claimed.

"Of course, the disturbing elements have to be tackled and the Centre is taking measures towards that end," he said.

Heading: Malhotra's assets rose by five times in four years - Indian Express
Content:
BJP chief Rajnath Singh on Saturday accused the Maharashtra government and police of harassing Malegaon blast suspect Sadhvi Pragya Singh in the name of investigation.

"It seems that Pragya Thakur is being harassed in the name of investigation. Not even a terrorist is subjected to tests three to four times as she has been subjected to," he said on the sidelines of a party function.

"There is definitely a role of the Maharashtra government and police in this whole episode," he said.

Nine persons, including Sadhvi Pragya Thakur, having allegiance to a right-wing Hindu outfit, and a serving lieutenant colonel have been arrested in connection with the Malegaon blast.

Heading: Mission successful: Chandrayaan-1 in lunar orbit - Indian Express
Content:
V K Malhotra, BJP's Chief Ministerial candidate for Delhi, and his wife have assets worth about Rs 5 crore, which is a five-fold increase in four years.

However, Malhotra owns only one old car valued at Rs 2.75 lakh, according to the declaration of assets made by him while filing the nomination papers from Greater Kailash assembly seat on Saturday.

The affidavit says they have assets worth Rs 5,003,4350, including two houses in the city valued at Rs 2.5 crore. In 2004, when Malhotra contested from South Delhi Lok Sabha seat, he had declared that they had assets worth Rs 1.01 crore.

Malhotra owns a house worth Rs 1 crore in Nizamuddin area in South Delhi while his wife has a house in Defence Colony worth Rs 1.5 crore, the BJP leader declared in the affidavit before the Additional District Magistrate Bansh Raj.

Malhotra revealed that he and his wife have invested about Rs 1.62 crore in various financial instruments like NSS, LIC, postal savings and policies. His wife's assets are valued at over Rs 2.2 crore.

While he possesses 50 gm gold jewellery worth Rs 50,000, his wife has 960 gm of gold jewellery valued at Rs 10 lakhs, he said in the affidavit.

He also declared that he has Rs 1,75,000 in cash and Rs 19,38,850 as deposits in banks. His wife has Rs 1,15,000 in cash and Rs 8,05,757 as deposits in banks and shares.

In 2004, he had declared that he was co-owner with his wife in one property in K G Marg worth Rs 6.25 lakh.

Malhotra does not have any criminal antecedents.

Heading: Five killed, six injured in explosion in Meerut - Indian Express
Content:
India's maiden moon mission -- Chandrayaan-I — on Saturday entered the tricky lunar orbit after scientists successfully carried out a most critical manoeuvre, 18 days after it was fired into outer space.

Space scientists at the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) carried out the lunar orbit insertion by firing the liquid engines on board the spacecraft for 817 seconds.

"The lunar orbit insertion (LOI) began at 4:50 p.m. and lasted for 817 seconds (14 minutes)," ISRO spokesperson S Satish said. The satellite has been placed in a 7,502 km X 500 km elliptical orbit around the moon, he said.

Heaving a sigh of relief, ISRO chief G Madhavan Nair said Saturday's operation was the 'most critical moment' in the mission.

"We have done it," a visibly happy Nair declared.

"For the last 20 minutes, almost all our hearts were at a standStill," Nair said from a ground centre near Bangalore.

The spacecraft, launched on October 22, had been placed in the Lunar Transfer Trajectory on November 4.

The mission, orbiting the earth at a distance of 3,86,000 km, was commandeered from ISRO's Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) at Peenya on the outskirts of the city with aid from the Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) at Byalalu.

Chandrayaan-I would now be lowered gradually and placed in a circular orbit at a distance of 100 km from the lunar surface.

The successful lunar orbit insertion (LOI) was an important milestone for the Rs 386 crore moon mission whose success depended on Saturday's hit or miss manoeuvre.

According to space experts, the challenging LOI was not without danger because it meant traversing through an area in which the gravitational forces of the earth and moon nearly cancel each other out.

Consequently, even a small deviation could send the spacecraft into a frash course towards the moon or earth—or on a path leading into deep space.

Experts recall that about 30 per cent of unmanned moon missions of the US and former Soviet Union failed during LOI phase.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh,who is now in Muscat on an official visit, congratulated the Indian space scientists for the singular achievement.

"This (today's achievement) will be etched in the history of Indian space in golden letters", Nair said.

In the coming days, the height of Chandrayaan-1's orbit around the moon would be carefully reduced in steps to achieve a final polar orbit of about 100 kms height from the moon's surface.

The spacecraft, launched on October 22, had been placed in the Lunar Transfer Trajectory on November 4.

The mission, orbiting the earth at a distance of 3,86,000 km, was commandeered from ISRO's Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) at Peenya on the outskirts of the city with aid from the Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) at Byalalu.

Chandrayaan-I would now be lowered gradually and placed in a circular orbit at a distance of 100 km from the lunar surface.

The successful lunar orbit insertion (LOI) was an important milestone for the Rs 386 crore moon mission whose success depended on Saturday's manoeuvre.

According to space experts, the challenging LOI was not without danger because it meant traversing through an area in which the gravitational forces of the earth and moon nearly cancel each other out.

Consequently, even a small deviation could send the spacecraft into a fresh course towards the moon or earth—or on a path leading into deep space.

Experts recall that about 30 per cent of unmanned moon missions of the US and former Soviet Union failed during LOI phase.

The lunar orbit manoeuvre was performed from Chandrayaan-1 Spacecraft Control Centre of ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network here, while Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) at Byalalu on the city outskirts supported the crucial task of transmitting commands and continuously monitoring this vital event with two dish antennas, one measuring 18 metres and the other 32 metres.

Expressing happiness that the accuracy that ISRO got in regard to Saturday's lunar orbit is really remarkable, Nair said nobody (space agency) would have secured such a precise orbit in the first attempt.

The achievement goes to the credit of ISRO, which has demonstrated its knowledge base in carrying out long trajectories under the influence of multiple bodies. "We (India) now have a big leadership as far as space is concerned", he said.

ISRO said the performance of all the systems on board Chandrayaan-1 is normal.

Nair said the Moon Impact Probe (MIP) on board Chandrayaan-1 would be released to hit the lunar surface around November 15. "Thereafter, systems (on board Chandrayaan-1) would be switched on one-by-one".

ISRO officials said the primary objective of 29-kg MIP is to demonstrate the technologies required for landing a probe at the desired location on the moon. Through this probe, it is also intended to qualify some of technologies related to future soft-landing missions. This apart, scientific exploration of the moon at close distance is also intended using MIP.

Of the 11 payloads, five are from India, three from European Space Agency, two from the US and one from Bulgaria.

Heading: Advani turns 81, launches website and hopes to do an Obama - Indian Express
Content:
Five persons were killed and six others injured on Saturday when a mortar shell exploded in the crowded Bengali Basti area in Meerut, police said ruling it out as a terrorist act.

"Some rag pickers had found the mortar shells in the Cantonment area while gathering scrap. They struck the shell with a hammer to extract metal and it exploded," Inspector General of Police, Meerut Range, Harbhajan Singh said.

The five killed have been have been identified Omar Dutt, 10, Nizamul Hasan, 12, Sudhiyan, 18, Razakh Ali, 16, and 17-year-old Musharraf.

Six people were injured and two of them were stated to be in critical condition, Deputy Superintendent of Police P V Ramashastri said.

Five more shells were detected and army experts called to defuse them, he said. The explosion occurred at around 3 pm in a slum where mostly Bangladeshi immigrants are residing.

The DSP said it was an 'accident' and not related to any terror activities.

Families of each of those killed will be given Rs 50,000 while the injured with get Rs 30,000, District Collector Kamini Chouhan said.

Heading: Aussies stay in the hunt - Indian Express
Content:
* Harbhajan Singh became the third Indian after Kapil Dev and Anil Kumble and 22nd bowler overall to take 300 or more wickets in Test cricket when he dismissed Australian skipper Ricky Ponting on the second day of the fourth Test match.

* Harbhajan, who made his Test debut against the same opponents at Bangalore in 1997-98, took 10 years and 234 days to reach this milestone.

* Of his haul, 200 have come in 40 Tests at home at an average of 26.74, while the other 100 at 39.69 in 32 overseas Tests.

* Three reasons Harbhajan loves bowling against the Aussies — he's dismissed Ricky Ponting 10 times, Matthew Hayden eight times and Adam Gilchrist on seven occasions.

* The year 2002 has been the best year of his career. In that year, he claimed 63 wickets at an average of 23.22 in 13 Test matches. He took 60 wickets at an average of 25.95 in 12 Tests matches in 2001 and 49 at 32.46 in 11 Test matches this year.

Heading: Ponting invokes 'Sydney Test', blames the Indian camp - Indian Express
Content:
Born to a Czech father and a Polish mother, Jason Krejza's family history is far removed from cricket, and even farther from the occult art of spin. In a country such as India, considered a bastion of slow bowling, with a long list of all-time greats, the chances of success for someone of his pedigree would always be considered negligible.

But on Friday, in the outskirts of Nagpur, this 25-year-old who started his career at the Sydney Cricket Ground before moving to Hobart in order to improve his prospects, became world cricket's the most successful debutant since Lance Klusener grabbed eight wickets for 64 in Kolkata 12 years ago.

Krejza's figures of 8-215 instantly attract attention, not just for his haul but also for the numbers on the other side of the dash. The ignominious double-century against his name could suggest he was simply fortunate, picking up wickets as the batsmen went after him. But watching him rip the ball through the air, make it jump off the surface, made it abundantly clear that the off-spinner had been more than just a beneficiary of providence.

With India rolling along at 422 for five, Australia needed some urgent intervention to stop Mahendra Singh Dhoni and Sourav Ganguly, already together for 119 runs, from running away with the Test. The slide started with the oddest of strokes — skipper Dhoni swiping at a delivery, attempting to hit it fine, almost like a standing paddle-sweep, to see his furniture disturbed.

Indian collapse

After the pair had weathered the storm all morning, surviving until lunch without a mishap, that wicket was all that was needed to open the floodgates, clearing the way for a typically Indian cave-in.

Ganguly's fairytale farewell ended moments later, beaten by the turn as he steered into the hands of slip. Zaheer Khan and Amit Mishra were bowled off successive deliveries, and though Ishant Sharma survived the hat-trick ball, his stay was cut short by a juggling close-in by catch Simon Katich, another Australian with roots in continental Europe.

Krezja had picked up five wickets for 15 runs in the space of 26 balls, but experts thought they saw a silver lining behind the Indian collapse, expecting the local spinners — the "real" spinners — to be unplayable on a track where an Australian had been so destructive.

Harbhajan's 300th

Only mildly surprisingly, Dhoni opened the bowling with Zaheer Khan and off-spinner Harbhajan Singh, but the new ball offered nothing for either — Zaheer having another off day and Harbhajan getting little purchase in comparison to his Australian counterpart.

The first breakthrough came from M Vijay, breaking down the stumps from mid-on to end Matthew Hayden's breezy knock of 16. But Simon Katich relentlessly struck boundaries at will as the visitors seemed determined to score quickly, like Australian teams of old, to give themselves a chance of victory in this must-win game.

Bowlers were switched, fields were changed, and at long last, Ricky Ponting fittingly became Harbhajan's 300th victim in Test cricket while attempting an ill-advised cut against a delivery that turned more than expected. He celebrated with a flourish, but India would celebrate no more on Friday, Katich standing firm on a fiery 120-ball 92 and Michael Hussey playing the perfect sheet anchor on 45.

At 189 for two from 49 overs, Australia have flung the gauntlet and the Test is suddenly up for grabs again. Harbhajan and Amit Mishra, who was too slow through the air to be any sort of threat, will have a lot of thinking to do overnight.

Heading: State associations in player dilemma - Indian Express
Content:
MS Dhoni and Kevin Pietersen might enjoy different statures in their captaincy but their achievements have been remarkable in a similar sort of a way. Their batting is defined by aggression, but they are calm on field.

The two have become 'Superstars' in their respective countries, yet both appear to be soft-spoken leaders. In many ways, Pietersen is travelling the same path that Dhoni has traversed. Like Dhoni, Pietersen was handed a team which needed some imaginative navigating during their series against South Africa at home after Michael Vaughan quit.

"Dhoni has been the key player in both the Test and ODI sides in the last 12 months," said England coach Peter Moores. The one thing that differentiates the two is Dhoni's achievements as captain. He won the T20 World Cup, a series against Australia and Sri Lanka in their backyard. Dhoni has done what many couldn't, while Pietersen, handed the reins only recently, is still finding his way around, though South Africa's 4-0 drubbing was an impressive start.

Strapping and well-built, neither has been averse to lending their batting the sort of excitement that makes them crowd favourites. Dhoni is known to send yorkers for six, while Pietersen's switch-shot won unprecedented fame as the decade's smartest innovation. "I'm here for six weeks, let's see if I use it," he hinted cheekily.

Dhoni has remained unprovoked during his team mates' impetuous moments, and Pietersen doesn't intend to turn into a class-monitor either. Asked whether they are under pressure to behave well in India, he quipped, "Absolutely not! We'll behave as well as we did when we were ambassadors of the game in Antigua. But we have to be our own persons, not someone you are not," he added.

Both brought a sense of newness to captaincy. "What I bring to England is freshness. The boys have accepted the new set-up. I like to give my players the confidence to know they can go out and perform without worrying about anything. They know they have the backing & support of captain and coach," the 28-year-old said.

Heading: Reversal of fortunes? - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai's middle-order batsman Rohit Sharma and Baroda all-rounder Yusuf Pathan's inclusion in the India squad for the one-day series against England has put their respective cricket associations in a dilemma.

With India scheduled to play their first ODI at Rajkot on November 14, Sharma and Yusuf's absence from the next Ranji Trophy game — against Gujarat at Surat and Uttar Pradesh at Vadodara respectively (November 10-13) — looks certain. Sharma's batting against Rajasthan had played a big role in Mumbai's win in the first match and the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) has written to the BCCI, asking permission to play him in the next outing. Baroda Cricket Association (BCA) is planning to do likewise.

MCA joint-secretary Hemant Waingankar said it won't be an easy decision, especially when there is no gap between the Ranji final day and the one-dayer. Mumbai coach Praveen Amre had requested the MCA to seek BCCI permission. Rohit's scores against Gujarat — 201, 92, 148 and 101 — prove that he has been brilliant in every outing.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Baroda coach Paras Mhambrey said it will be hard to get Yusuf for their first Ranji match. "Yusuf has played a crucial role for us in the last two years, we are definitely going to miss him. We are planning to write to the BCCI requesting to play Yusuf," he said. With the ODI venue at Rajkot not too far from Surat and Baroda, the officials are keeping their fingers crossed. While chief selector K Srikkanth is said to have given green signal, the final call will be taken by skipper MS Dhoni.

Heading: Steyn's pace sinks fighting Bangladesh - Indian Express
Content:
Their media man Andrew Walpole and captain Kevin Pietersen sat scrutinising a bottle of mineral-water — both smiling broadly — even as coach Peter Moores took the first set of posers during England's inaugural press briefing at the Cricket Club of India on Friday, kickstarting their winter-tour to India. Then without further fuss Pietersen took a quick sip, and got down to the job of saying the nice things visitors say after being welcomed. Waters will be tested in a different fashion over the next six weeks.

Now, this is a side which touched down in Mumbai after just a 12-hour stop-over in London, and some hectic travelling from Antigua where a spectacular bruising of Stanfordesque proportions was inflicted on them. Plus, the phantom-feeling of having lost a million in a winner-takes-all roulette which panned out in the Caribbean. But Pieterson didn't look terribly jaded.

Their impending seven-match criss-crossing of India can be easily shrugged off this time, for this tour provides this bunch of Englishmen the perfect opportunity to strut their stuff and get noticed in the land of another Twenty20 spectacle — come as it does ahead of the IPL auctions, exactly three months from now. Hence, a routine one-day series will take off, preceded by England's lessons from Stanford which Pieterson admits the team has learnt, but with bright prospects of catching the eye of Indian franchises and becoming IPL signings at the February 6 auctions. The eagerness to play in India just got a shade keener.

Off to the right start

"We are always looking forward to India," insisted coach Peter Moores of his squad, adding, "We didn't play as well as we should've in the big game (in Antigua) but we know that we've a very tough one-day series against India and then a Test series and everyone is looking forward. You arrive in India and there's so much passion for cricket. There are 10 stations showing it on TV, and it's a different experience."

Enthusiastic opening-odes then followed from coach and captain — to the revered status the game enjoys here, to the great wickets on which runs can be plundered, to Dhoni — India's superstar captain on the steady rise, and effusive congratulations to VVS Laxman on his century of Tests and to Sourav Ganguly on the completion of his fantastic career. The itinerary — with Rajkot, Indore, Kanpur and Cuttack — rest assured won't be much of a drudge, though it's learnt that the visitors have requested replacing Guwahati as a venue, with Mohali likely to get the honour.

Pieterson apart, there are the Ashes heroes — the original star Andrew Flintoff back to the game after a long layoff, and Steve Harmison — who'll be out to prove their resurgence. India had drubbed England 5-1 the last time they toured here in 2006, while England won a close contest at home, but this one-day series promises to be different with the stakes considerably higher and wider.

Lessons learnt

The Stanford Super Series might have been the richest of the lot, but it shouldn't be difficult for England to move on. Move on to India, at that. Pietersen, who left Indian shores last time as the highest run-maker from the visiting side, will perhaps deem this one more crucial. Addressing his first media-interaction as captain here, the dashing batsman was all heedful and alert. Leaning forward, listening carefully, there was a clear effort to understand the accent, as much as to be understood.

Stanford games, he reckoned, were an experience from which England could only take some new lessons. "We went into the Stanford game not knowing what was going to happen. We dived into depths of uncertainty but found out and learnt a lot of things. Maybe we made some mistakes, but I'm not scared to try new new things. You bump your head once or twice but you learn. But the boys are keen to play here now," he said.

India, under Dhoni have been in rampaging form, while England will bank on their 4-0 drubbing of South Africa earlier. "As a team we are very confident because we've been playing some very good cricket. The key now is to get most out of the practice this week," Pieterson added. The Stanford loss won't be difficult to erase from their minds once India's own rich IPL radar starts beeping names of Englishmen. This is one 50-over series with T20 implications.
