It doesn't help that the villain apparently running circles around half the world's governments is an effete pretender (Almeric) who probably won't be able to convince a classroom of kids of his eco-friendly intentions. To dress him up in Hawaiian shirts and a languorous gait is an insult to our intelligence.

Craig looks great and, once in a while, still uses those piercing blue eyes to good effect. But he has none of the spark, wit or wisdom to transcend him above the other

J B — Jason Bourne.

As boats crash into ships, planes collide into mountains and entire hotels go up in blasts, we are left looking for precisely the same thing as Bond apparently is: some quantum of solace. None of us is getting it, at least in this film.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Lok Sabha election may hit hard on Right to Education Bill - Indian Express
Content:
CAST: Julie Delpy, Adam Goldberg, Albert Delpy, Marie Pillet; DIRECTOR: Julie Delpy

In Julie Delpy's Before Sunrise and its sequel Before Sunset, a couple find love that comes once in a lifetime in a few brief, hastily snatched hours before they part. She also wrote the screenplay of the latter. Here, Delpy, writing, directing, editing, starring and singing, catches up with a couple who have spent two years together but take just two days in Paris to realise that they really don't know much about each other.

Does time make love stronger, or does familiarity erode romance? Does love happen at first sight, or need love be blind? Does past not matter, or is it the future?

Delpy explores all of this, pointing out how definitions are pointless when love is all that, and more — before sunrise, before sunset, in the darkest hours of the night, and the hottest hours of the day. The beauty is her manner: insightful while being quirky and funny. Here is a film that keeps its eyes open and also its heart, generous to all that it touches, including the five odd drivers of the taxis the couple take.

Semi-autographical, 2 Days in Paris stars Delpy as a French photographer Marion, who has flown in to the French capital with her American boyfriend, interior designer Jack (Goldberg). The reason is partly to see Paris, and partly to visit Marion's parents (played delightfully by Delpy's real-life parents Albert Delpy and Marie Pillet).

Jack is the clichéd American tourist, shocked by a Paris that is cliché tres francais. What he doesn't bargain for, however, are Marion's ex-lovers, who seem to be crawling out of everywhere into their lives. As says the film's tagline: "He knew Paris was for lovers. He just didn't think they were all hers."

In its humour, quirkiness and observations, 2 Days in Paris has flashes of Woody Allen. However, there's one significant difference. Delpy brings to this film what Allen wouldn't: in this Obama season, may we say, the audacity of hope.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Andhra plans loan insurance for rural poor - Indian Express
Content:
While the Right to Education (RTE) Bill finally got the Cabinet go-ahead last week, the path to the implementation of the legislation is still far from clear. General Election proximity may hit the fate of the legislation that seeks to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged between six and 14.

Though the Cabinet approval has ensured that the Bill is ready to be introduced in the Parliament when it meets in December, the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry is worried that if the Lok Sabha fails to clear it within the short span for which the session is expected to be on, the legislation would lapse in the event of elections. The Ministry is, therefore, hoping that the legislation will be taken up by the Rajya Sabha first.

The only surefire way to ensure the Bill stays afloat as Government changes hands is to introduce it first in the Rajya Sabha. The HRD Ministry has done its bit to ensure that the legislation goes first to the Rajya Sabha and is not read as a money Bill. It is compulsory for all money Bills to be first introduced in the Lok Sabha, so the HRD Ministry has added no financial implications and cost factors to the Bill.

"While there is a mention of state-Centre fund sharing to meet the cost of the Bill's implementation and of seeking the Finance Commission's help on this issue, no cost figures have been put into the Bill. It will be the finally the discretion of the Law Ministry and Parliamentary Affairs Department to decide under which category the RTE Bill falls — money or non-money Bill," added the official.

"The HRD Ministry's job is over with the Cabinet finally approving the RTE Bill. However, there is a concern about its actual implementation and enactment. The reason is that if the Parliament meets only for a short period next month and if the RTE Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha first, there is a strong possibility that it will be referred to the Select Committee for a detailed examination. In that case, it will not be possible to enact the Bill in such a short period and the legislation will lapse as the Lok Sabha will dissolve. So, the whole process will have to be repeated. That will be bad news for the Bill," top government officials said.

In the works since 2002 when the 86th Constitutional amendment was effected, the Bill will come with a decentralised district level grievance redressal system, a broad spectrum National Advisory Council of experts to help implement the legislation's provisions and a clearly spelt out role for the Finance Commission to ensure a controversy-free state-Centre fund sharing formula. The Bill will apply to all private schools stipulating 25 per cent reservation for needy children.The long awaited legislation was first taken to the Cabinet in August only to be referred to a Group of Ministers (GoM) after funding-related questions cropped up at the meet. The Bill finally passed muster when the GoM headed by Union HRD Minister Arjun Singh gave it a go ahead and said that the funding issue was no longer a problem. While Singh headed the GoM, others on board were Finance Minister P Chidambaram, Science & Technology Minister Kapil Sibal and Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia. The GoM was unable to meet for two months after it was first formed on August 8 to resolve all outstanding issues because Singh had taken ill. However, the Ministry was at the job, trying to build consensus on the issue between concerned ministries and examining the role of the Finance Commission.

Heading: All In The Family - Indian Express
Content:
In A first-ever move, the Andhra Pradesh Government has decided to launch an insurance scheme to cover loans taken by women and rural poor. This scheme will come to the rescue of all those families which are caught in debt traps and vicious loan cycles, in case the borrower dies.

"The insurance scheme is being launched from November 19, late Indira Gandhi's birth anniversary," informed R Anitha, director, Self-Help Groups.

In the next one year, loans to the tune of Rs 10,000 crore, being provided to the rural poor, would be insured through the scheme.

"Right now we are covering 8.1 lakh Women's Self-Help Groups (SHGs) working in Andhra Pradesh under this insurance scheme, but we plan to extend it to households of all SHG members, which means loans taken by their spouses would also be covered soon," said Chinna Thatiah, regional project director, Rural Development, who is anchoring the scheme.

Under the scheme, a person taking a loan will have to pay 0.5 per cent of the loan amount as premium to insure his loan. Of this 0.5 per cent, the Government will pay 50 per cent of the amount under the Janshri Bhima Yojana. For example, if a person takes a loan of Rs 30,000, the premium to insure this loan at 0.5 per cent will be Rs 150. Of this Rs 150, the Government will pay Rs 75 as subsidy, so the borrower will have to pay only Rs 75. In case, the borrower dies or is unable to repay the loan, the insurance company, Life Insurance Corporation (LIC), will pay the insured amount to the SHG which will settle the outstanding loan amount and give the remaining amount to the family.

If an SHG member wants a loan above Rs 30,000, then he will have to pay a premium of Rs 5 per Rs 1,000. The 50 per cent subsidy will be applicable only on the first Rs 30,000 of the loan amount. "If a woman pays the premium for a loan of Rs 50,000 or Rs 60,000, that entire amount is like a sum assured. In case she dies, the LIC will pay back the loan to the bank through the SHG," Thatiah explained.

The state Government thought of launching the scheme after it was observed that many SHGs were breaking apart or members were at loggerheads after the death of one of the members, as the onus of repaying the loan fell on them. "It gets worse if an SHG member, who took a hefty loan, expires because the responsibility of repaying the loan falls on the remaining members of the SHG. Often members have to take money from their husbands or relatives to clear the loan. There was discord among the SHGs due to this," Thatiah said.

After the state Government launched the 'Pavla Vaddi' (25-paise interest) scheme a few months back, there had been a spurt in the number of people availing loans. Defaulters and number of borrowers expiring before clearing the loans had also gone up correspondingly.

"Banks were wary and rethinking whether to give loans to the SHGs. This scheme has infused new confidence in the banks, and loans are being provided now without any hassles. In the next one year, we aim to provide loans amounting to Rs 10,000 crore to SHGs under the 25-paise interest scheme and provide insurance cover on the loan amount as well," the regional director said.

Going a step further, the Rural Development Department is creating an extensive database of SHGs with personal details of members and their families, addresses and contact details. While this process is on, 24-hour call centres have been started in all the 23 districts. These call centres are community-based and maintained solely by them.

Heading: CPM, Sangh Parivar watermarks on Kannur terror tag - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP has declared candidates for 217 out of the 230 Assembly constituencies in Madhya Pradesh, and seems to be following the Congress formula of fielding relatives of leaders.

Wifely duties

* Former education minister Laxman Singh Gaur's wife Malini will contest from Indore-4 constituency. The minister died in a road accident early this year. This is Malini Gaur's maiden election.

* Former forest minister Prakash Sonkar's wife Nisha will contest from Sanver. The minister died a natural death. During the bypoll, the party had ignored Nisha's claim. She will contest for the first time.

* Rajya Sabha MP Vikram Varma's wife Nina will contest her maiden election from Dhar.

Sons of the soil

* Both the sons of former Congress chief minister Govindnarayan Singh — Harsh and Dhruvnarayan — will contest on BJP tickets. While Harsh was elected on the Rashtriya Samanta Dal ticket, his brother will contest for the first time.

* Senior leader Kailash Sarang's son, Vishwas, will contest his maiden Assembly election from Narela constituency in Bhopal.

* Former chief minister Kailash Joshi's son Deepak will contest for the second time from Hatpiplya.

* Former minister Kishorilal Varma's son, Devendra, has been fielded again from Khandwa. His father was murdered following a dispute over non-payment of wages.

* Former chief minister Virendra Kumar Sakhlecha's son, Omprakash, has been fielded again from Javad.

* Former chief minister Sunderlal Patwa's nephew, Surendra Patwa, will contest from Bhojpur. He had lost the last election.

Can the Congress catch up?

The Congress has declared only 117 candidates so far, but a family presence is already in evidence.

* Vibha Patel, sister-in-law of former minister Rajkumar Patel, will contest from Govindpura.

* Leader of Opposition Jamuna Devi's nephew Umang Singar will contest from Gandhwani-ST seat.

* Union minister of state for agriculture Kantilal Bhuria's niece Kalavati Bhuria will contest from Jhabua.

Heading: BPL scheme: EC reply sought - Indian Express
Content:
With the police unravelling the terror network in the state, this communist bastion in north Kerala, notorious for decades of recurring political violence between the CPI(M) and the Sangh Parivar, has emerged as a hotbed of religious extremism. If "party villages" — so named for their distinct political allegiances — in the northeastern belt of Kannur district were battlegrounds for communist versus saffron clashes, terror recruiting has been mainly from Muslim patches in the coastal villages, infested with organisations that operate covertly in the region.

Kannur city, 3 km from the district headquarters, now sports a terror tag thanks to the death of two local youths in Kashmir, the arrest of three alleged terror recruiters and a couple of absconding leaders, including their operation commander Tadiyantavide Nazeer. In addition, many Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and National Development Front (NDF) operatives in the region are under police surveillance.

Religious indoctrination camps and conspiracy sessions were held at Maithanappally and Neerchal that are part of the city region, while the terror mission to Kashmir, comprising recruits from elsewhere in the state, was flagged off from Kannur city, according to the police.

But now the blame game has begun, with the saffron camp alleging that the CPI(M) has played a considerable role in enabling the growth of radical Muslim parties like the PDP and the NDF in its bid to counter the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), an ally of the previous Congress-led United Democratic Front government in Kerala.

The coastline here, which houses several historical mosques and an impressive palace, is known as a bastion of the IUML, which always represented the region in the local municipal council. Incidentally, League leader and Union Minister of State for External Affairs E Ahamed's ancestral house is located in this area.

Clashes between Hindu fishermen on the northern side of the city and Muslim communities on the other extreme have been frequently reported for many years now. These incidents strengthened the position of the NDF in the region and it came to be regarded as a protective force against the Sangh Parivar. Middle-class Muslims here, too, financially supported NDF and PDP for the same reason.

In the meantime, the CPI(M) jumped into the fray as well. The party wanted to see fringe Muslim outfits — the PDP, the Indian National League (INL) and the NDF — pose a serious challenge to the IUML.

"The NDF and the PDP have grown with the support of the CPI(M), which hoped that these two organisations would help weaken the IUML. When an NDF activist was killed, allegedly by RSS men, near Iritty in Kannur in 2000, senior CPI(M) leaders had paid homage to them. The CPI(M)-NDF affair is a common thing in Kannur," said IUML district president Abdul Khader Moulavi.

The CPI(M), however, begs to differ. Says its district secretary P Sasi, "The IUML's anti-Marxist line has helped the growth of the NDF. To ward off the threat from the RSS and other Hindu outfits, the IUML supported the NDF. The CPI(M) has never supported the NDF."

According to BJP district president P P Velayudhan, the CPI(M)'s disavowal of its association with the PDP and the NDF does not mean much. "The CPI(M) had used the NDF and the PDP to defend Hindu outfits. Now, the communists are worried over the unexpected outcome," he said.

The fact, however, is that though the NDF had enjoyed the tacit support of the CPI(M) in Kannur, the relationship between the two soured about two years ago when a CPI(M) defector-turned NDF activist was killed in Thalassery, allegedly by CPI(M) men. Since then, there has been several instances of clashes between the NDF and the CPI(M).

Interestingly, what is common between the 'hit squads' of political parties and terror recruits in Kannur is their criminal background. To keep in leash the hitmen that had been deployed to finish off their rivals, the CPI(M) and the saffron camps had locked them away under various criminal cases. The story is more or less the same with the suspected slain militants and their arrested leaders. All of them were involved in fake-currency rackets and other criminal cases before they became terror recruits.

Red versus Saffron

* The history of violence between CPI(M) and BJP-RSS cadres — with the Congress and smaller outfits pitching in as well — in the district goes back three decades.

* The latest National Crime Records Bureau says this district logged the country's highest number of riot cases in 2006 — 737 cases — averaging more than a couple every day. Every once in a while, Kannur throws up an equally telltale statistical symptom of what goes on. Consider this: At the fag end of its tenure, the last Left Government of E K Nayanar read out in the state Assembly Kannur's record for the four preceding years. In 2001, over 200 bomb explosions, 180 killings (the government claim that only 26 of these were certified political murders, was soon discounted), besides over 1,000 cases of attempted murder.

Heading: ‘Cannot direct BCI to defend blast accused’ - Indian Express
Content:
The future of the implementation of Rajasthan Government's Bhamashah Yojana — a scheme for providing monetary assistance to 50 lakh women in the below-poverty-line (BPL) category — will be decided on November 17. A Supreme Court order on Friday directed the Election Commission (EC) to furnish its response to the appeal filed by the Vasundhara Raje Government against a Rajasthan High Court order staying the implementation of the scheme.

The HC had made its decision on October 21 after hearing a petition filed by one Mohan Lal Sharma, who accused the Government of violating the model code of conduct by bribing the poor, as polls had been announced in the state. Senior advocate Mukul Rohtagi, appearing for the Raje Government, objected to the High Court's decision, arguing that it had no right to exercise jurisdiction in what was the EC's domain. "How can the high court step in? Why should there be a duplicate order, when the EC is seized of the matter?" said Rohtagi. The EC on October 18 had asked the state Government not to enroll new members for the scheme.

Heading: No lead on threat letter to judge - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Friday took note of the worrying trend of Bar Associations passing resolutions prohibiting advocates from representing those accused in terror cases. The apex court, however, refused to issue directions to the Bar Council of India (BCI) in the matter since the Council is a statutory body.

Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice C K Thakker while perusing the submissions of senior advocate Colin Gonsalves appearing for those advocates who refused to abide by the 'diktat' of their Bar Associations said that directions to a statutory body like the Bar Council of India could not be passed. "How can this sort of a prayer be entertained? BCI is a statutory body. How can this court issue mandamus for BCI?" it asked, suggesting that the counsel amend the petition and approach the court again. Mandamus is a writ commanding a public official or authority to perform its duty, and it is a discretionary power of the court to issue such a writ.

The petitioner's counsel submitted that a standard policy had to be laid down by the BCI since State Bar Associations in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Maharashtra had passed resolutions that members of the Bar would not defend the accused in terror cases.

Heading: Rizwanur case: Todi challenges NBW - Indian Express
Content: The police are yet to come up with leads on the origin of a threat letter delivered to Seventh Metropolitan Magistrate Bibhas Chatterjee on Thursday. Chatterjee had issued an arrest warrant against Ashok Todi. The letter warned the judge that his "rigid attitude" towards the Todis "might cause his own harm".The letter, written in English on a postcard, allegedly threatened that he should step down or would have to pay the price as all his decisions were going against the Todis. After receiving the letter at his office, Chatterjee got in touch with the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate who immediately informed the police.

Heading: Jamiat anti-terror meet to start today - Indian Express
Content:
Ashok Todi, the Kolkata-based industrialist accused of abetting the suicide of his software engineer son-in-law Rizwanur Rehman last year, approached the Supreme Court on Friday seeking an urgent intervention as he challenged the issuance of non-bailable warrant (NBW) against him by a Kolkata trial court judge following his failure to appear in court.

Senior advocate Harish Salve, making an urgent mention of the application before a Bench of Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice C K Thakker, urged the court to stay the NBW against Todi.

The Bench suggested at the beginning that the accused must cooperate with the investigations, but later realised that the accused was actually seeking a review of an earlier order passed by the apex court. On October 13, the court had said that trial in the case would not proceed till the Calcutta High Court decides on a petition filed by Todi challenging the CBI's decision to chargesheet him in the case.

Salve argued that if Todi surrenders before the police, he would be arrested immediately and all proceedings pending would be rendered infructuous. The Bench conceded to this plea and posted the matter for hearing on November 10.

Apart from Todi, six others were also chargesheeted by the CBI on September 22 for alleged abetment of Rizwanur's suicide. A Metropolitan Magistrate in Kolkata had asked the accused to appear before it on October 27, but they had failed to abide by the order leading to the issuance of the NBW.

However, Todi, his brother Pradeep and brother-in-law Anil Saraogi have been avoiding appearance prompting the CBI to cancel their passports last month. The chargesheet also names the then deputy commissioner of Kolkata Police Ajoy Kumar, then assistant commissioner of police Sukanti Chakraborty, Sub-Inspector Krishnendu Das and S M Mohiuddin alias Pappu, a family friend of the victim.

Rizwanur's body was found on railway tracks on September 21, 2007. He had married Todi's daughter Priyanka on August 18, 2007.

Heading: HC reserves order on Sec 377 - Indian Express
Content: A two-day national conference of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind will begin here on November 8 at Omar Function Hall at Shaheen Nagar. At least 2,000 clerics from across the country are expected to attend the conference which will discuss 'anti-terrorism and national integration'. CM Y S Rajasekhara Reddy, popular Maoist Balladeer Gaddar, Swami Agnivesh and several Muslim leaders will attend the conference which will also discuss Dalit-Muslim unity and several socio-political issues confronting it.

Heading: Pranab never said China was a threat: MEA - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday concluded the marathon hearing on the decriminalisation of Section 377 of the IPC even as the Centre on Wednesday had maintained that "homosexual sex is against the order of nature". A Division Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar reserved the matter for final judgment.

Even as the Centre submitted in the court that Section 377 IPC ought to prevail to "protect the human race", a bunch of NGOs fighting in favour of gay rights argued to amend the provision by decriminalising gay sex among consenting adults in private.

The hearings saw the Government resort to religious literature to explain public morality in India, while the court sought an explanation on a National Aids Control Organisation report pointing out that men who have sex with men fear persecution to such extent that they deny medical care for themselves, thus adding to the fear of contracting HIV/AIDS virus.

"Section 377 IPC throws a stigma on these people. They live in fear. So tell me what compelling interest you have for allowing this law to remain?" the court has asked the Centre.

Heading: Rajiv’s killing distanced DMK from Tigers, hints Karuna - Indian Express
Content:
The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday sought to downplay External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee's comments earlier this week that "coping with the rise of China" was foremost in the immediate challenges which India is facing and that China was furthering its interests "more aggressively".

An official statement by the MEA spokesperson said, "At no point in his speech did the Minister use the word 'threat' to describe China. There is thus no cause for misinterpretation and the kind of negative gloss that has been put on the speech by certain elements in the media."

The spokesperson said, "It is clear that in his speech, he recognised that there is enhanced engagement with China and as a result of our engagement we have today a completely different situation; economic development has given both our countries new capabilities and that it is our belief that there is sufficient space for both India and China to grow together and build a cooperative relationship in the new architecture."

It is learnt that the Chinese diplomats in New Delhi took up this matter informally with the Indian diplomatic establishment, following which the MEA put out a statement to salvage the situation.

Speaking at the National Defence College on "India's security challenges and foreign policy imperatives", Mukherjee had said, "What are the immediate challenges that we face. To my mind, the foremost among these would be (a) to cope with the rise of China; (b) maintenance of a peaceful periphery; and (c) managing our relations with the major powers."

And then, he elaborated, "China as India's largest neighbour and as an emerging power is both a challenge and a priority. As a result of our engagement with China over the last 30 years we have now reached a somewhat normalised relationship."

"Of course there are some unresolved issues between us. However, we need to factor in the fact that as a result of our engagement we have today a completely different situation than when we started,'' he said.

Heading: BJP defends ABVP attack on Geelani - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister and DMK patriarch M Karunanidhi struck a diplomatic note on Friday by distancing himself from the LTTE, even as he expressed doubts about the chances of peace without both sides laying down weapons.

After the recent political flare- up following the intensification of war in Sri Lanka, Karunanidhi has been under fire on the one hand from the Congress, for the unhindered pro-LTTE wave in the state, and on the other, from pro-LTTE parties like MDMK, PMK and others who have been criticising his Government for "not doing enough" on the issue.

Responding to PMK founder S Ramadoss's and president G K Mani's taunts that DMK had no connection with the LTTE, Karunanidhi said the DMK's relationship with the LTTE has two phases: before and after the assassination of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi. Though he did not elaborate further in the article, written in party organ Murasoli, Karunanidhi indicated that the assassination had put a wedge between the two. As if to answer angry Congressmen from Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, he added that this stand vis-à-vis LTTE was made known inside the Assembly two years ago.

"I wonder how effective it will be if only one side is asked to lay down their weapons," said the senior leader, adding that in his opinion, ceasefire was possible in Lanka only if both parties put down arms and negotiated to arrive at a solution that was acceptable to all neutral countries including India, followed by a permanent cessation of hostilities in the second phase.

Several Congress MLAs, whose outside support the 'minority' DMK Government is dependent on, came out against the state government for its alleged soft approach towards Tiger supporters in the state and threatened to take it on inside the Assembly once the session commences from Monday.

While the CM cleared the air for the sake of agitated Congressmen, he also sought to consolidate the support base for the pro-Eelam cause in the state, even if it includes once-bete noire S Ramadoss of the PMK. Union Minister and senior DMK leader T R Baalu called on Ramadoss at the latter's residence in Tindivanam earlier this week as Karunanidhi's emissary to explore a possible patch-up between the erstwhile allies who were together when the alliances at state and Centre, DPA and UPA, were floated. Sources said Baalu suggested to Ramadoss that the leaders should have a meeting to solve the issues, to which the PMK leader sought time to consult with his partymen. Sources said the meeting may take place before the Assembly session on November 10.

This is a surprise move by Karunanidhi, as the DMK and PMK, though together in successfully contesting the Parliament and Assembly elections, had separated after frequent spats.

Meanwhile, LTTE sympathiser Vaiko, who was released on Thursday after two weeks of judicial remand for sedition, said collecting relief material for the Tamils in Lanka was a fraud as the Indian Government, of which the DMK was also a part, was providing arms to the Government forces in their war against the Tamils.

Heading: BJP’s bid to please rebels: Koshiari for RS seat - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP has defended students' body ABVP over its protest against S A R Geelani at a seminar here on Thursday.

"The charged emotions of patriotic students can't be ignored," said party spokesperson Rajiv Pratap Rudy. "His (Geelani) association with militants can't be denied and one can simply say that he was just saved by the skin, and the shroud of mistrust still prevails about him," Rudy added.

"The BJP has taken note of the protest by ABVP activists at a Delhi University seminar and we certainly feel that the nature of protest should be more hygienic," Rudy said.

Heading: BSP nominees for RS: Akhilesh Das’s assets worth Rs 43 cr - Indian Express
Content:
Attempting to stem dissidence against Uttarakhand CM B C Khanduri, the BJP high command has decided to nominate former CM Bhagat Singh Koshiari to the Rajya Sabha. A sitting legislator from Kapkot constituency, Koshiari has been the face of rebellion in the state for the last three months. According to BJP sources, the decision to nominate Koshiari was taken at a meeting of the party's parliamentary board at its headquarters in Delhi on Thursday evening. Koshiari will be replacing Congress Rajya Sabha member Harish Rawat whose term ends on November 21.

In August this year, under Koshiari's leadership, more than 20 legislators from Uttarakhand had camped in Delhi seeking a change in the state leadership. At that time the party high command had rejected the demand, asking the rebels to work for the party's victory in the ensuing parliamentary elections.

In October again, 17 legislators had approached the party with the same demand. This time again, the crisis was defused with the intervention of party president Rajnath Singh and other leaders.

These leaders had held a series of talks with Koshiari, some of the state ministers and Khanduri.

Talking to The Indian Express, Koshiari said that he would follow whatever the party high command asked him to do.

Heading: Obama effect on Advani’s website - Indian Express
Content:
The BSP is far from being the "party of the underprivileged" if the assets of its Rajya Sabha nominees are anything to go by.

According to the mandatory affidavit on assets filed by the six BSP men, along with their nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha on Friday, Akhilesh Das Gupta, BSP General Secretary and son of former UP chief minister Banarasi Das, is the richest of the lot.

A former Congress Union Minister, Das has, along with family members, declared wealth and properties over Rs 43 crore. The major portion of the assets comprise non-agricultural land worth around Rs 40 crore and include plots, flats and bungalows in Lucknow, Haryana, Noida, Ghaziabad, Khurja and Delhi. Das, former mayor of Lucknow, owns gold worth Rs 37.20 lakh, while his wife owns gold worth Rs 65 lakh. He owns a residential plot in South City and Sushant Lok in Gurgaon worth Rs 2 crore and Rs 1.5 crore respectively. He has two plots in Khurja worth Rs 40 lakh and Rs 36 lakh respectively and owns two bungalows in Lucknow worth Rs 1 crore and Rs 4.5 crore respectively. He also owns a residential flat worth Rs 80 lakh in Delhi.The property listed in the name of his wife is 1.106 acres of land in Lucknow worth Rs 4.8 crore, a commercial plot in Lucknow worth Rs 8 crore, one plot in Noida's sector 92 worth Rs 1.5 crore and one plot in Vaishali, Ghaziabad worth Rs 1 crore along with a residential plot in Sushant Lok, Gurgaon, worth Rs 1.5 crore. His wife also owns a commercial plot of 3,619 sq meters in Gurgaon on the Delhi-Jaipur highway worth Rs 3.5 crore.

In stark contrast, another RS candidate Raja Ram declared wealth to the tune of Rs 38 lakhs only. Raja Ram had been in the news when his name figured as Mayawati's successor in the party. Other candidates of the BSP — Brajesh Pathak and Avtar Singh Karimpuri - have properties worth less than Rs 1 crore. Veer Singh, a second-timer for the Rajya Sabha seat, has properties and valuables worth around Rs 2 crore while former Lok Sabha member from Jalaun, Brij Lal Khabari, has assets worth around Rs 1 crore.

Heading: Uma files papers from Tikamgarh - Indian Express
Content:
After a website on his book My Country My Life, BJP prime ministerial candidate L K Advani will on Saturday unveil a personalised, interactive website that the BJP has described as the "country's largest political website".

Impressed with Barack Obama's ability to use the Internet as an effective campaign tool, Advani's campaign managers have incorporated features from barackobama.com in Advani's site — lkadvani.in. While the Internet penetration and tele-density here may be insignificant when compared to the corresponding figures in the USA, the BJP, nevertheless, hopes to use the Internet as a tool to target Young India that will have a decisive say in the 2009 Lok Sabha elections.

A dedicated blog on the site will encourage "a free flow of views" on issues ranging from economy to defence. The website, having sections in English and Hindi, will ask the users to send in their feedback and suggestions, some of which could be incorporated into the party's election manifesto. The website would also invite volunteers to work for Advani and the party.

Aiming to be the first off the block on every nugget on Advani's campaign, the site hopes to make conventional campaign tools redundant. "Whether it's press releases, or videos; campaign schedules or speeches, the Advani site will be most comprehensive. A search engine will facilitate the user's search on every aspect of Advani's life and politics," said a BJP leader. The site has about 150 videos and 700 pages of text, including speeches and interviews.

In an obvious attempt to target the youth, the site's homepage has pictures of Advani interacting with youth representatives and N R Narayanmurthy releasing the Kannada edition of Advani's memoirs, My Country My Life.

Heading: Vice-President to go to Maldives for swearing-in of new President - Indian Express
Content:
True to her unpredictable nature, Uma Bharti filed her nomination from Tikamgarh on Friday, less than 36 hours after announcing that she won't contest the November 27 elections. The Sadhvi's move took some by surprise, more so because she had claimed that if she herself took the plunge she would not be able to devote much time to guide the candidates of her fledgling Bharatiya Janshakti, which is yet to open its account.

Given her constant flip-flops in the past, party sources admitted that they would not be surprised if she pulled out from the fray on November 10, the last day of withdrawal of nominations.

The BJP, which Bharti had led to an astounding victory in 2003 as its chief ministerial candidate, knows her well enough to anticipate such last-minute surprises. Her party had earlier indicated that she might contest from Dhar, where the disputed Bhojshala is located and where she had succeeded in whipping up communal frenzy ahead of the last elections. But the ruling party was more prepared for Tikamgarh, considered to be the former chief minister's home turf. When the party sensed that she could file nomination from Tikamgarh, they released the name of Akhand Pratap Singh, her adversary who also hails from the region.

Singh was food and civil supplies minister in the BJP Government and was sure to get the axe, but has benefited thanks to Bharti's anticipated candidature. His name was finalised, along with 12 others, well past midnight.

Singh, who was with the Congress till 2003, had become a major embarrassment for the Government, often rubbing it the wrong way. Just ahead of the elections, he had walked out of the Cabinet meeting to protest allotment of land to a trust headed by BJP vice-president Anil Dave.

Heading: BJP destroying Army’s secular image: Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Vice-President M Hamid Ansari will represent India at the swearing-in ceremony of the new President of the Republic of Maldives, Mohamed Nasheed, on November 11.

Nasheed was elected President in the first-ever multi-party Presidential elections held on October 28, ending the 30-year reign of incumbent Abdul Gayoom.

Dr Mohamed Waheed Hasan will also be sworn in as Vice-President at the inaugural ceremony. During the visit, Ansari will call on the new President, the Vice-President and outgoing President Abdul Gayoom in addition to meeting members of the Indian community in the Maldives.

"India welcomes the successful conclusion of the first multi-party Presidential elections in the Maldives. As the Maldives enters a new era in constitutional reform, democracy and development, India looks forward to strengthening its relations with the Maldives and assisting it in its various developmental efforts," the MEA said here on Friday.

Heading: Immolation bid against Prabhunath’s acquittal - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress on Friday demanded immediate dismissal of Lt. Colonel Prasad Shrikant Purohit who was arrested for his alleged involvement in Malegaon blast, even as the party sought to put the blame on the BJP for infiltrating "secular institutions".

"Prima facie, a case has been established against Lt Col Purohit as the Army has allowed the civilian administration to make further inquiry. The Army should dismiss the officer immediately. Secular character of the Army has to be maintained and that is why exemplary punishment is the need of the hour," said AICC secretary Praveen Davar, who is also secretary of the AICC Ex-Servicemen Cell.

Chairman of the cell K P Singh Deo said the Armed Forces should do some "serious introspection" on whether there was an attempt to undermine the unity of the Armed Forces or something else. "It is a shocking thing how a military officer can be involved in this. In the Armed Forces, we are taught secular values," he said.

Blaming the BJP and its allied organisations for trying to impose their "exclusivist agenda" on institutions that have been the backbone of Indian democracy, AICC spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi said, "We are proud of our Army but ashamed of the acts of omission and commission of those who seek to infiltrate, influence and convert established secular institutions for divisive agenda and ideology."

Heading: Check ‘Hindutva infiltration’ in Army: CPM - Indian Express
Content:
The Patna police on Friday averted immolation bids by Lalmuni Devi's relatives, who had been protesting against the recent acquittal of Maharajganj's JD(U) Lok Sabha MP Prabhunath Singh in the 1995 murder of Devi's two sons. Devi, a key witness in the case in which Singh and six others were the main accused, had threatened self-immolation outside the Patna High Court on Friday.

Although Devi did not accompany them outside the court, her son Kishori Roy (45) and six immediate relatives along with 13 other protestors, gathered near the main gate at around 12.15 pm with paper and match boxes.

But before anything untoward happened, the police arrested seven of the protestors and chased the others away.

"We have arrested Lalmuni Devi's son Kishori Roy and six others for attempting suicide and abetting others for the same under IPC sections," Kotwali police station in-charge Mudrika Prasad told The Indian Express. Prasad said there had been no law and order problem outside the court with policemen being stationed there to avoid any immolation bid.

Lalmuni Devi's son Darogo Rai was killed near an election booth in the Masrakh Assembly constituency on March 25. His brother, Rajendra Roy suffered grievous bullet injuries in the incident and died six months later.

Heading: Shiv Sena to target taste buds with ‘vada pav sammelan’ - Indian Express
Content:
With a serving Lt Colonel arrested in connection with the Malegaon blasts, the CPI(M) on Friday asked the Government to take reports of "Hindutva infiltration" into the Army "seriously" saying such incidents had raised questions about the sanctity of the Armed Forces.

"So far there was a sanctity about the Armed Forces and that sanctity we maintained and upheld. Now, that is clearly breaking down. So there is a requirement for immediate attention and correction," said CPI(M) Politburo member Sitaram Yechury, adding the arrest of former and serving officers of the Army in cases of bomb blasts had "disturbing implications" for national security.

Demanding that the "new dimension" to the growing terrorist threat must be fully investigated and the entire network and persons involved uncovered, the CPI(M) leader said, "What needs to be recognised is that some extremist elements both amongst the Muslims and Hindus are resorting to terrorist violence. Terrorism by itself is anti-national and the state should move against it irrespective of which quarter it came from."

Attacking the BJP for dismissing the serious development as a "sponsored investigation" instead of coming out against such extremist groups, he said "the RSS and its outfits are making absurd statements that Hindus cannot be terrorists. These are the same people who go on talking about Islamic terrorism".

"Now the VHP, Shiv Sena are talking about giving legal support to Hindutva terrorists, but there is a big hue and cry when the Vice-Chancellor of Jamia Millia University talks of legal aid to his students, against whom charges have not been proved, just because they are Muslims," Yechury said. "So it is clear that even in the manner in which this issue is being tackled, there is a communal bias. Therefore, we have said that without prejudice and discrimination, the same yardstick should be applied to both kinds of terrorism."

The role of the Bhonsala Military School in Maharashtra should be probed, he said, adding that "no private educational institution can be allowed to provide military training".

Heading: Polls just 10 days away, voters yet to get I-cards - Indian Express
Content:
While the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) continues with its sons-of-the-soil campaign, rival Shiv Sena appears to be trying to win the hearts of voters through another tried and tested route — their stomachs.

On November 24, the Shiv Sena will hold a vada pav sammelan in the city to standardise the taste of the popular Maharashtrian snack that will be sold in its fast-food chain to be launched on the eve of the forthcoming elections.

To be hosted at the Shivaji Park grounds in Dadar, the programme will see eminent vada pav sellers setting up stalls to serve their fare to the Shiv Sena's panel of chefs as well as other visitors.

The party plans to launch the scheme from January 23 next year — party supremo Bal Thackeray's birthday — with 100 stalls being set up in Mumbai in the first phase, with other cities like Pune, Thane and Nashik being targeted later. The party has tied up with fast food giant McDonald's to help in standardising the size and taste of the vada pav and chutney and in marketing the venture, Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP and Saamna executive editor Sanjay Raut told The Indian Express.

The names of the chefs who will be part of the panel to select the taste of the branded vada pav are likely to be announced soon. Sanjay Gurav, who heads the Maharashtra Vada Pav Vikreta Sena, said they would invite around 25 famous vada pav sellers to set up stall at the sammelan and also inaugurate a vada pav stall with the Shiv vada pav logo, which will be part of the 100 such kiosks to be set up across the city.

These kiosks will be manned by vendors who will don a uniform of saffron shirts paired with blue trousers, added Gurav. A credit society to ensure that the vada pav sellers save money at the end of the day is also on the cards and centralised kitchens would be set up to serve hot vadas to the clientele.

The Shiv vada pav scheme is seen as an effort by the Sena to strengthen its organisational network and provide livelihood to its cadres. Shiv Sena executive president Uddhav Thackeray had earlier met McDonald's CMD Amit Jetiya and roped in the fast-food giant to participate in the venture. Raut, who is supervising the exercise, had also organised a vada pav party in New Delhi recently.

Heading: RSS-backed statehood parties to scuttle BJP plan - Indian Express
Content:
Many voters in J-K are yet to receive new electoral photo identity cards (EPICs) though the first phase of the Assembly polls is only 10 days away.

The state Election Commission says that they are running out of time and there is now little chance that the digital election I-cards will be issued to all the voters before the polls. Ten assembly segments including three in the Valley will go to polls in the first phase on November 17 and not a single EPIC has been issued to the voters in these constituencies so far.

"We are running short of time and may not be able to issue new voter I-cards to all voters," J-K Chief Electoral Officer B R Sharma told The Indian Express. "We are trying our best to provide cards to as many people as we can."

"All those possessing the old voter cards will be allowed to vote. And for first-time voters, there are other alternatives. All other relevant documents will be valid for voting in the state," Sharma said.

Heading: AI plane tilts while landing, passengers safe - Indian Express
Content:
In the 2002 Assembly elections, candidates owing allegiance to various RSS-backed outfits fighting for separate statehood for Jammu cut into the vote bank of BJP, ensuring that the latter ended up with just one seat in the recently-dissolved Assembly. That the groups demanding statehood for Jammu could win just one seat — Jammu State Morcha MLA Ashwani Sharma from Bishnah — is another story. However, on many seats, including the prestigious Jammu (West), the combined votes polled by the BJP nominee and the candidate fielded by those for separate statehood was more than the votes secured by the eventual winner.

This time too, despite efforts by senior BJP leaders to enter into some kind of understanding with these RSS-backed groups, they are all set to upset the BJP's applecart by fielding "strong, winnable" candidates in a majority of seats in the Jammu region. Buoyed by the support that the recent Amarnath Yatra "struggle" received in the entire Jammu region, these groups feel their chances are pretty good.

Leading the pack is the Jammu State Morcha (Progressive), headed by Prof Virender Gupta, who has already upped the ante against the BJP. "The BJP wanted to have its way by forcing an agreement that suited it down our throats. This was not acceptable to us," Gupta said, adding that this was the main reason why his party decided to have no truck with the BJP.

Heading: 80,000 J’khand contract teachers strike work - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 161 passengers and crew on board an Air India Airbus A 310 had a narrow escape on Friday when the right wing of the aircraft (on a flight from Jeddah) tilted and grazed the runway while landing at the Karippur International Airport at Malappuram in Kerala.

According to airport sources, the pilot managed to bring the aircraft (Flight AI 962) to a quick halt before any damage could occur after he saw the right wing rubbing the runway.

The incident occured at around 9.15 am.

All passengers were safe and the aircraft did not suffer any damage except for some paint on the wing getting scraped, the sources said.

A senior airport official said prima facie there was nothing abnormal with landing parameters like weather, wind speed and visibility.

Only a detailed probe including the examination of the Flight Data Recorder could give clues on why the aircraft tilted while landing, the official said.

The aircraft has been grounded and engineers from Mumbai were expected to arrive here for a detailed check, he further said.

Heading: Petrol pump scam: SC okays 112 allotments - Indian Express
Content:
Around 80,000 teachers who were working on contractual basis are up in arms against the state Government and are demanding regularisation of their jobs.

These teachers — officially called 'para shikshaks' — are organised under the banner of two separate bodies.

While the Jharkhand Shiksha Mitra Sahyogi Sangh (JSMS) launched a nationwide strike on November 1, the Jharkhand Sahyogi Shiksha Mitra Para Shikshak Sangh (JSSP) joined them this Friday.

While regular teachers are permitted to take leave and get transferred every three years, para-teachers work without these service conditions.

In addition, para-teachers receive only about Rs 3,000 per month as salary, while regular teachers earn Rs 15,000 per month.

"To get our salary, we had to grease the palms of officials," says Dhanjay Manjhi, a para-teacher.

On Friday, these teachers took out processions and burnt effigies of Chief Minister Shibu Soren and Education Minister Bandhu Tirkey.

"We had submitted a number of memoranda highlighting our grievances, but the Government did not act on them. Fed up, we had no choice but to start a strike," said JSMS secretary Binod Behari Mahato.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Shibu Soren has said that his Government is considering the demands of the para-teachers.

However, Education Minister Bandhu Tirkey has adopted a harsher stance.

"If they don't call off their strike before November 10, we will invoke the appropriate law to deal with them," he said.

Heading: Bhutan King talks of change in first speech - Indian Express
Content:
Six years after The Indian Express carried a series of reports bringing to the fore a scam of irregularities in the allotment of retail petrol pumps and LPG distributorships by the previous NDA Government, the Supreme Court on Friday brought long-awaited relief to 112 such cases, judging that their "selection was based on merit".

However, the apex court upheld the cancellation of 93 petrol pumps in different parts of the country.

Tracing the history of the scam, the Bench of Justices C K Thakker and R V Raveendran recalled how questions were raised in Parliament after this newspaper carried reports in August 2002, alleging that the BJP-ruled government allotted petrol pumps and LPG distributorship to relatives and associates of political functionaries.

The then prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee was forced to order the Petroleum Ministry to take steps to cancel all allotments made on the basis of recommendations of Dealer Selection Boards from January 2000 till that date. This resulted in the cancellation of 3,760 allotments, but several allottees challenged this decision in different high courts.

All these cases were eventually transferred to the apex court which on December 20, 2002, quashed the government order, except in regard to 413 cases, which were named in newspaper reports as being mired in irregularities.

On Friday, accepting the report of a court-appointed committee set up to examine the remaining 409 cases (five were repetitions), the Bench said, "The approval by the Committee with respect to 112 allotments is accepted and the cancelling of allotments in those cases is set aside."

However, 297 cases were not found to be allotted on the basis of merit but due to political favouritism. The Bench proceeded to cancel 93 such allotments spread across states including Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

Some other cases were found to be on the "borderline" by the court, and taking a lenient view of about 40 such allotments, the apex court ordered the setting aside of their cancellation.

Heading: Will quit politics in 5 years: Rane - Indian Express
Content:
"Destiny has put me here. I will protect you as a parent, care for you as a brother and serve you as a son. I shall give you everything and keep nothing. This is how I shall serve you as King."

These were some of the most inspiring and animated words of the speech, the newly crowned fifth King of Bhutan, Jigme Khesar Namgyei Wangchuck, gave in his first public address to the nation, on Friday morning at the Chaglimithan stadium.

The stadium was packed with 25,000 Bhutanese. Several thousands waited outside and roared and waved at the new King.

The Bhutanese, many of whom had trekked for days to turn up at the venue were ecstatic. Each one of them carried the Bhutanese national flag.

The King reminded the Bhutanese people of changing times. But any change devoid of peace, security and happiness had little significance, he said and added that change should not destabilise the fundamental qualities of Bhutanese society.

Recalling that the essence of Bhutanese philosophy was 'gross national happiness', the King said, "Our generation of Bhutanese have been gifted a strong and dynamic nation by our forefathers. I am confident that as long as we are willing to work with their commitment and dedication and follow their example, we can bring peace, happiness and prosperity to our country."

Heading: Deshmukh wants central exams in Marathi also - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane, who has made several attempts to dislodge Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, has offered to quit politics in five years. Rane was speaking at a function to felicitate Sindhudurg District Central Cooperative Bank Chairperson D B Dholam on Thursday when he made the surprise statement. He is touring different parts of the state to gain a pan-Maharashtra identity to outgrow his image as a Konkan strongman.

In his speech, he said he would not remain in politics beyond four or five years. He told the audience that his wife had asked him how long he would continue to be in active politics and had pointed out that Dholam was active at the age of 76. He did not cite any particular reason for this but rued that values had deteriorated in politics.

The minister pointed out that politics, which once used to be equated with selfless service, had now been reduced to just a tool for self-gain and was being exploited by unscrupulous people from all sections of society.

Meanwhile, Rane's remarks have raised eyebrows in Congress circles. "It is an outburst from a desperate leader who has lost patience and is in a hurry to become chief minister," quipped a senior Congress functionary. "Look at the way he is going around in the state, addressing public meeting in which he is criticising the same Government of which he is a part."

However, a Rane supporter said the outburst indicated his anguish over the poor quality of governance in the state. "He is disappointed with the way the state is being governed and his remark indicates his anguish over the fact that despite repeated requests to the high command to intervene in Maharashtra'a politics, nothing is being done."

Rane had offered to quit his Cabinet post about three months ago and had submitted his resignation to Congress chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

Heading: Denied ticket, former J-K Cong chief to contest as Independent - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of the 'sons of the soil' agitation launched by the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh said that the state Government would write to the Centre requesting permission for Maharashtrian students to give the examinations for their recruitment to the Central services, like the Railways, in Marathi, in addition to English and Hindi. He was addressing a felicitation function organised by the Mumbai Regional Congress Committee (MRCC) here on Friday on the occasion of the State Government completing four years in office.

Deshmukh said that he had sought information about the recently conducted Railway recruitment exam where MNS members had beat up North Indian candidates who had appeared for the exam at a Mumbai centre. Around 19 per cent of the applicants were Maharashtrians. He stressed the need for the exam to be simultaneously conducted in Marathi as it was the official language of the state and also the mother tongue of the locals. Such a facility for writing exams in the regional language is already available for the UPSC examinations.

Stating that the Congress wanted to take all sections of the society forward, Deshmukh added that they had issued a Government resolution as far back as 1972 asking for priority in job recruitment for locals in at least 80 per cent of the jobs. Deshmkuh said that the state had invited Rs 1.30 lakh crore FDI and these companies would also require local talent in their projects.

However, Deshmukh hastened to add that contrary to the popular perception that outsiders were snatching away the jobs of locals, his visit to a plant run by an automobile major in Pune had revealed that over 80 per cent of the people employed there were Maharashtrians. While attacking the anti-outsider campaign, without naming either the MNS or the Shiv Sena, Deshmukh said that his government was working to ensure that all people of the state got equal opportunities and stressed that it was necessary to maintain the cosmopolitan and inclusive character of Mumbai.

He said some organisations were exploiting the youth and were creating a law and order situation without addressing the real issues concerning Maharashtra. Pointing to the arrest of activists of Hindutva outfits in connection with the Malegaon blasts, Deshmukh said that once investigation progressed, 'Many people would have to cover their faces while moving around'.

'People safe in Maharashtra'

Making an indirect reference to Friday's resignation of Janata Dal (United) MPs from the Parliament over the anti-outsider campaign launched in Maharashtra , Deshmukh referred to the huge turnout at the Chhath puja celebration this week and said that it was necessary for these people to come to Maharashtra and see how safe people were. Speaking to reporters later Deshmukh dismissed the resignation as indicative of the personal agenda of the party.

Heading: Cash to voters: Cong leader gets EC notice - Indian Express
Content:
Having lost the tussle for the party ticket in north Kashmir's Sopore constituency, Ghulam Rasool Kar, the senior-most member of the J&K Congress on Thursday announced that he would be contesting the polls as an Independent candidate, making him the first dissident from the party.

The Sopore ticket has been given to Abdul Rashid Dar. Kar had been hopeful that he would be given preference, and had presented his case to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, who heads the screening committee for the state.

"I am the senior-most leader in the state. My party ditched me by choosing a junior worker over me," said Kar. "Dar had secured only 2,000 votes in 2002 elections. When, I contested Parliament elections in 2004, I bagged 10,500 votes from the same constituency. Still my name was dropped."

According to Kar, former J&K chief minister Ghulam Nabi Azad and JKPCC president Saifuddin Soz are responsible for denying him mandate. "Both Azad and Soz are afraid of me, as I would have been the chief ministerial candidate of the party. To keep me away from the Assembly both Soz and Azad joined hands," he said.

However, senior JKPCC vice-president Muzaffar Parray said that Kar was mistaken in his assumption. "He could have never been a party's chief ministerial candidate. Neither former chief minister Ghulam Nabi Azad nor PCC president Soz conspired against him."

Heading: Meltdown on mind, PM heads for Oman, Qatar today - Indian Express
Content:
The election authorities have issued a showcause notice to leader of the Opposition in Assembly Mahendra Karma as an FIR was registered against him following a report that he had distributed money to voters during the campaign for the next week's Assembly polls in Chhattisgarh.

The District Returning Officer for Dantewada, from where Karma is contesting the November 14 polls, has served a notice on the Congress leader, seeking his explanation on the charge against him that he had distributed money during the campaign, said Joint Chief Electoral Officer Gaurav Dwivedi.

The District Returning Officer was investigating the matter. Appropriate action would be taken according to the provisions of law, Dwivedi added.

Heading: Bihar Cong chief slams Deshmukh for ‘inaction’ - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of global financial crisis, India will look to the Gulf countries and their surplus funds to be leveraged for the country's developmental requirements.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, who will be leaving for Oman and Qatar on Saturday, said, "The current international economic and financial situation provides a unique opportunity for India to leverage the surplus funds in the Gulf for our development needs, and to accelerate trade and investment flows into each other's countries." Singh will be travelling to Oman and Qatar from November 8 to 10.

In Oman, the Prime Minister is expected to sign MoUs on cultural cooperation, standardisation, and cooperation between diplomatic institutions in both countries.

"We hope those would be signed once finalised by both sides," Sheikh Humaid Almaani, Oman's ambassador to India told The Indian Express.

On the visit to Oman, Manmohan said that it would give him an opportunity to "renew with the leaders and people of Oman the very special affinity" that has existed between the two countries through centuries. During the visit, he will meet Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Said and will hold detailed discussions on bilateral relationship with Oman's Deputy Prime Minister Sayyid Fahd Mahmoud Al Said.

On his Qatar visit, Singh said India attaches great importance to its ties with Qatar, which is one of the largest and most reliable suppliers of energy. "Given the complementarities that exist between us, I am confident that we can build a mutually beneficial strategic partnership in this sector," he said.

With Qatar, a defence cooperation agreement is expected to be signed. If the agreement goes through, Qatar would be the second country in the Gulf region — after Oman — to have such an agreement with India.

In Qatar, Manmohan will meet Emir of Qatar Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al Thani and will hold discussions with Prime Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassam bin Jabor al Thani. "I will discuss with them ways in which we can further strengthen our relations and move forward in all dimensions," Singh said.

He will also take up the issue of safety and welfare of the Indians living and working in these two countries. "We have a large number of Indians working in Oman and Qatar. Their contribution to these countries is widely acknowledged and appreciated by the authorities. I am grateful to both the countries for the very warm welcome that has been accorded to them. During my discussions in Oman and Qatar, I shall also discuss ways in which we can better assure their safety and welfare," the Prime Minister said.

Heading: Cong sops: rice at Rs 2 per kg, free power - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Friday came in for flak from the Bihar unit of the Congress for failing in his duty to protect north Indians in Maharashtra.

"If any constitutional head is not able to discharge his responsibility, he should resign on moral grounds or else the party leadership should intervene," Bihar PCC chief Anil Sharma said at a press conference here.

According to him, the Maharashtra Government was "not as tough" as it should have been on the MNS. "The Chief Minister said the National Security Act count not be invoked against Raj Thackeray. We disagree with it," he said, adding that it was evident from Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's letter to the CM that the Congress leadership is "not satisfied" with the functioning of the Government in Maharashtra.

"The CM is not doing what is expected of him. Being the CM, he must implement law and order. Had he done it, Raj Thackeray would have been behind bars under the NSA," Sharma said.

He accused the JD(U)-BJP regime in Bihar of destroying the evidence. "The Bihar administration immediately cremated Rahul Raj because of which facts could not come out. Now we know from autopsy report that Rahul Raj was caught and then shot from a very close range," said the Bihar PCC chief.

Heading: Doctor’s prescription wrong, says CPM - Indian Express
Content:
Steering clear of the contentious issue of Naxalism, the Opposition Congress on Friday released its election manifesto and announced a slew of populist measures for the coming elections in Chhattisgarh. The schemes include subsidised rice, free power and interest-free loans to farmers, 50 per cent reservation for women in government jobs and a law to enforce restrictions on purchase of agricultural land in the state.

The manifesto for next week's Assembly polls, released by party leaders here, promises to launch a scheme to provide 35 kg rice to all sections, except those paying income tax, at just Rs 2 per kg, countering the BJP Government's current scheme of providing rice at Rs 3 per kilogram to more than 36 lakh families living below the poverty line.

Taking its cue from an existing law in Maharashtra, the Congress promised to enact a law to ensure that only farmers belonging to Chhattisgarh could purchase agricultural land within the state. State Congress President Dhanendra Sahu told The Indian Express that this was included in the manifesto as it had come to light that in many cases agricultural land was being purchased for investment purposes. He sought to assure the people that the Congress would provide a "guardian government" which would be clean, transparent, development-oriented and accountable.

Farmers would be provided free electricity and interest-free short-term loans, a one lakh grant for purchase of tractors, a 75 per cent subsidy for borewell digging along with a reduction of the irrigation cess to Rs 10 per acre. Besides, the party also sought to assure the electorate that no land belonging to farmers would be acquired for any purpose without their consent. Moreover, farmers would get free treatment for all ailments at government hospitals within the state.

Heading: Indian in Obama team: Gujarat village celebrates - Indian Express
Content:
Holding that the Manmohan Singh Government's prescription to protect India from the global financial crisis was wrong, the CPI(M) on Friday came out with a charter of suggestions, including demands for a special fiscal package, to increase public expenditure and a moratorium on job or wage cuts in the organised sector.

The party claimed that the paradigm of neo-liberal economic policies, propagated by the shenanigans of the capitalist order, had failed and said it was strange that when the vision of "trickle down economics" was getting discredited across the world, the economic managers of the UPA Government were clinging to it.

In the charter, the CPI(M) sought a special fiscal package directed at increasing public expenditure to boost income and consumption of the working people to ensure broad-based growth, expanding of fiscal deficit by the Centre as well as states, scrapping of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act and putting in place a debt relief scheme for states to encourage them to adopt an expansionary fiscal stance.

According to senior CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury, the Manmohan Singh Government has once again made a wrong diagnosis of the genesis of the crisis and hence suggested a wrong prescription. "The Government refuses to accept that the crisis reflects the bankruptcy of the ideology of neo-liberalism," he added.

He said the world over leaders had admitted that it was time to restructure capitalism but in India, the Government was relying upon only one policy instrument — the interest rate — to control inflation as well as reverse the growth slowdown.

"Using one instrument for achieving two policy goals is illogical," Yechury said.

The broad suggestions of the CPI(M) are: undertake massive public investment directed at sectors which are capable of creating employment demand, strengthen and extend NREGA to urban areas, extend the period of guaranteed employment beyond 100 days, encourage food grain production and expand public procurement operations for all major crops and step up investment in irrigation.

It also mooted universalisation of the public distribution system, regulation of domestic corporate retailers to ensure that small and unorganised retailers are not hit, increasing customs duties to protect Indian industries and sector-specific relief packages to bail out small-scale industries.

Heading: Orissa invokes ESMA against agitating docs - Indian Express
Content:
Gabat is in a garba mode these days. Ever since US President-elect Barack Obama appointed Indian-American Sonal Shah, who heads Google's philanthropic arm, an advisory board member, celebrations have not stopped in this tiny village. With good reason, as Sonal, 40, is a native of Gabat village of Sabarkantha district.

There is a festive atmosphere as people are bursting firecrackers and dancing to the drumbeats. People have gone nostalgic about the days when little Sonal lived along with her family here.

"We tried in vain to congratulate her as her phone remained constantly busy. Ultimately, we called up my brother, Dineshbhai, there to convey our wishes," said Mukundchandra Shah, Sonal's uncle.

"In the village, people have almost gone mad in celebrating Sonal's success. The youth have been bursting firecrackers ever since the news of Sonal's appointment came in."

According to Shah, Sonal was born in Mumbai but she lived at Gabat till she was six. She did her kindergarten at the village school.

The village authorities are also planning to celebrate Sonal's success by organising a rally in her honour. Deputy Sarpanch of the village Ranjitsinh Zala said, "It is a matter of pride for us that one of our village girls has been so successful that the American President has appointed her his advisor. We are organising a grand rally to celebrate her success."

Talati of Sansinh Zala village said, "The villagers have gone mad since yesterday and are marking the occasion by distributing sweets among themselves. Mediapersons have also visited the village in search of Sonal's roots."

Heading: MNS attacks: 5 JDU MPs quit - Indian Express
Content:
Refusing to bow down to the demands of agitating doctors, the Orissa Government on Friday invoked the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) and threatened them with arrest and transfer to the remote districts if they ceased work from Sunday.

Peeved at the dismissal of Bibek Swain, an anaesthesiologist, Santanu Sahu, a surgeon, and Anup Nath Sharma, an orthopaedic specialist working in Jajpur district headquarters, for allegedly chopping off of the palms of five deceased tribals in the Kalinga Nagar firing case, 2,400-odd doctors working in various government hospitals, primary and community health centres of the state had resigned en masse.

Though Health Minister Sanatan Bisi said he was prepared for a discussion, the doctors turned down the offer demanding an audience with the CM. The Government hopes that since most doctors leading the agitation work in the Capital Hospital of Bhubaneswar, they would yield in at the mention of transfer.

Heading: Show cause notice to Yousuf - Indian Express
Content:
The Stanford Twenty20 may have been organised in far-away Antigua, but one man who was in the thick of the action was left-arm spinner Murali Kartik, the lone Indian in the extravaganza and member of the Middlesex squad, the England domestic Twenty20 champions.

Kartik played in two of their three games, including the money-game against Trinidad & Tobago (T&T), but couldn't help them rake in the $280,000 at stake in that contest. But the 32-year-old believes a tournament of such magnitude could have been handled better.

"There wasn't an opening ceremony which I think was certainly warranted. We just went there and started playing straight," he says. He adds that even the fixtures were designed oddly, as Middlesex's only meaningful game was sandwiched between two 'warm-up' games against England and the Stanford Superstars. "The match against T&T was crucial for us. And even though we were playing to win in the other two games, the fact that they didn't have any significance was there in the back of our minds," he admits.

The pitch at the Stanford Cricket Ground in Antigua also came in for severe criticism. "It was very slow, and the ball wasn't coming onto the bat, as was very evident from all the games," he says.

The quality of cricket during the tournament was not of the highest standard, and all the teams were guilty of dropping a number of catches. But Kartik reveals that the lights at the ground were not great, and that it was difficult sighting the ball. "It was like catching a half-moon at times. You simply couldn't spot the ball. Even the West Indian cricketers who have played here before struggled," he explains.

Apart from the Stanford Series and the Twenty20 championships in England, Kartik also played in the IPL as part of the Kolkata Knight Riders. And he believes that the quality of competition during the first season was the best of the lot. "It was fantastic. I also expect the Champions League to be very well organised and for the cricket to be of the highest standard," he says.

Heading: Serena pulls out of Doha, Ana follows - Indian Express
Content:
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has served a show-cause notice to star batsman Mohammad Yousuf demanding return of $124,000 it spent on his legal case in India involving his controversial contract with the ICL. "Today, we have served him a show cause notice and if he doesn't return the money, we will file a lawsuit in a civil court to recover money," PCB lawyer Shan Gul said.

Meanwhile, Yousuf told Geo News that the attitude of Pakistan captain Shoaib Malik and the PCB were responsible for his joining the ICL. "I was not given the respect a senior player deserves in the team. I was fed up with the attitude of captain Shoaib Malik and the cricket board," Yousuf said.

Malik was surprised by the allegations. "He never came to me and talked about any issue. I had a perfectly normal relationship with him and we practised together regularly," Malik said.

Yousuf denied money was the motivation for his defecting to the ICL. "Money was never an issue for joining the ICL. I was getting paid by the board for not playing in the private leagues," he said.

Heading: Form-struck and injury-hit, Arsenal face big United test - Indian Express
Content:
World number three Serena Williams and fourth-ranked Ana Ivanovic withdrew from the WTA Championships on Friday.

Williams, who also pulled out last year after playing just one set, blamed a sore stomach muscle.

Ivanovic, who is suffering from a virus and after losing her first two matches could not qualify for the semi-finals, defaulted her last match against Russian Svetlana Kuznetsova.

Although Serena won just one game in the last two sets of her defeat by sister Venus on Thursday, the American said she only felt the problem develop back at her hotel.

"I felt I didn't serve well, I had a lot of double faults," Serena told reporters. "Looking back I think maybe that's why I was doing it because I didn't feel it (the injury) at the time."

Olympic champion Elena Dementieva now joins Venus as a qualifier from the maroon group while Jelena Jankovic and Vera Zvonareva progress from the white group. Zvonareva remained undefeated on Friday, adding a 2-6, 6-3, 6-4 victory over Jankovic to two previous wins.

In Saturday's semis, Zvonareva meets Dementieva and Jankovic faces Venus

Heading: Pitcher Perfect - Indian Express
Content:
Arsenal are going through a sticky patch, goals and points are drying up and injuries are mounting, so it is not the best time to entertain Manchester United on Saturday.

A home defeat by Hull City and last week's shipping of two late goals to allow local rivals Tottenham Hotspur to grab a famous 4-4 draw both undermined the "Fortress Emirates" mentality.

That was followed by another defeat at Stoke City and Wednesday's goalless home draw with Fenerbahce in the Champions League, a team they thumped 5-2 away last month.

Striker Emmanuel Adebayor will miss Saturday's game with an ankle injury, winger Theo Walcott is doubtful with a shoulder problem and Robin van Persie is suspended. Without their first-choice strike duo, Wenger is likely to turn to 19-year-old Carlos Vela, who played the last 30 minutes on Wednesday, and Nicklas Bendtner, hardly ideal against the Champions of Europe.

Lack of depth

That lack of depth has left Arsenal exposed a little but Wenger, instead of looking to his own selections and dealings, or otherwise, in the close-season transfer market, has chosen to look elsewhere for blame.

Increasingly frustrated by the way more physical teams have been able to negate his slick-passing but lightweight side, the Frenchman this week claimed that Stoke's players had set out to deliberately hurt his players. However, he is refusing to panic. "We want to be guided by the way we want to play football, our spirit and not to go over-board," he said.

"We lost a game (against Stoke) but we are six points behind the leaders. It is the start of November and we have plenty of quality to get it back.

"United is always a massive game and Saturday is no different. But they drew also against Celtic so maybe that shows you how demanding the Premier League is."

Another defeat could stretch that gap to nine.

Dimitar Berbatov, Wayne Rooney and Cristiano Ronaldo are all starting to find the net regularly for United and Carlos Tevez is also showing some sharpness after spending time on the bench.

United have managed an away win at Arsenal in the league just once in the last 10 years.

Heading: Harbhajan bags 300th wicket - Indian Express
Content:
Squinting into the desert sun, the scouts huddled behind a screen, their radar guns cocked. The catcher went into his crouch as the lanky pitcher pawed at the mound, then rocked and fired. The only sounds were a grunt and the pop of the ball in the mitt.

At first glance, it looked like any other big league tryout. But this one had a twist: The pitcher, Rinku Singh, had never picked up a baseball before May.
